## One set of tabs, buttons and status parts for every page (branch `ds-one`, 29 Oct 2026; DS1-DS6)

The owner, 29 Oct 2026, looking at the item page's design: "tab change follow this design pattern and button all design follow this". The
reference is the parts board (`TP_Parts.dc.html`, and `IT_Item.dc.html` for tabs in use) of the canvas "CW Daily Screens". This runs before
the page-by-page waves, so each later build inherits the parts. CSS and view markup only: no route, rule, permission, form field, version
check, FormOnce or CSRF changed; every link and current-page mark of a tab row is the one it had.

**DS1. One buttons component.** Every button is a `.btn` (a `<button>`, a link or a summary): plain white with a hairline, 600 14 px words,
10 px corners, 40 px high. A variant says what kind it is, and there are only five: `.primary` (the main action, magenta), `.soft` (a helper
attached to a field: the pink tint with its own edge, `--accent-line`), `.ghost` (quiet: Leave, Change, Clear, Export; muted words, no
edge), `.ok` (the answer "all fine": the green tint), `.risky` (red words on white). Sizes: `.sm` 34 px, normal 40 px, `.lg` 48 px; on a phone
every normal or large button is 48 px and a small one 44 px, 44 px on a touch screen. Disabled: faded (.45), the reason in plain words beside
it (`.btn-why`). The variants are keyed on `.btn` only, so every button of every template now carries it (a bare `<button>` keeps the plain
look as a fallback). The mapping:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `.btn.primary`, `button.primary`, `a.button.primary-link` | `.btn.primary` |
| `.btn.secondary`, `button.secondary`, a `<button>` with no class, `a.button` | `.btn` (plain) |
| `.btn.danger` / `button.danger` (solid red), `.btn.danger-outline` | `.btn.risky` (red words on white) |
| `.btn.ghost` (accent words), `.btn.quiet`, `button.link` | `.btn.ghost` (muted words) |
| `.btn.success` (unused) | `.btn.ok` |
| `.btn.big` (two lines, full width) | `.btn.lg`; a button holding `.btn-title` + `.sub` is laid out on two lines across its row |
| `.btn.xs`, `.btn.dark`, `.btn.dashed` (unused), `.btn.full` (sign-in) | removed (the sign-in page's own rule makes its link full width) |
| `.split` + `.split-main` + `details.split-more` (an accent arrow) | `.btn.primary` + `details.more` (DS4) |
| `details.doc-more` + `.doc-more-menu` (a document's More) | `details.more` + `.more-menu` |
| `.bulkbar .btn` (translucent), `.bulkbar .btn.primary` (pink), `.bulkbar .btn.danger` | the plain, main and risky buttons on the dark bar |
| app.js's password "Show" (`.reveal`) | `.btn.ghost.sm.reveal` (`.reveal` only places it) |

Kept as controls of their own, not button variants: `.icon-btn` (the shell's bell, menu and help), `.grp-toggle` (a group's fold),
`.side-link` (the person's menu), `.bulkbar-close` (the bar's x), `button.po-default` (the editor's hidden default), `.add-item` (a board's
dashed "+ Add" row), `.pager a`, `.menu-item` (a row of More), `details.lq-menu` (a Lines to place row's "⋯").

**DS2. One tabs component.** Every tab-like control is a `nav.tabs` of `a.tab`: 14 px semi-bold muted words, the open tab (`aria-current`,
as before) in the dark accent with a 3 px accent bar under it, a count as a bubble (`.count`) that turns accent on the open tab, 44 px to
tap. The row never wraps: it scrolls sideways inside itself and app.js fades the side that has more (it already marked every `nav.tabs`). A
second row sits right under the first. A class after `tabs` only names the row for the tests and the spacing:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `nav.tabs` > `a.tab` (2 px line, 500) | the same classes: the 3 px bar, 600, the bubble |
| `nav.seg` > `a.seg-item` (the black pills: a tab's segments) | `nav.tabs.seg` > `a.tab` |
| `nav.seg` on the reports (Show) | `nav.tabs.show-tabs` |
| `nav.seg.store-seg` (the store choice) | `nav.tabs.store-seg` |
| `nav.pills.show-pills` (the queue's Show, with an "Show" label), `nav.pills` (barcodes), `nav.pills.dispatch-pills` | `nav.tabs.show-tabs` (the visible label dropped: the row's aria-label says it) |
| `nav.pills.state-pills` (Store Products, By Item, New variants), `nav.pills.period-pills` | `nav.tabs.state-tabs`, `nav.tabs.period-tabs` (the state's dot kept) |
| `strong.tab-count` | `span.count` (the bubble) |
| `nav.legend` (the match strengths under their bar) | `nav.tabs.legend` (each list's colour key kept) |
| `p.seg-links` (the count sheet's Show, New items' All / waiting) | `nav.tabs.show-tabs` (New items' one toggle link is now its two tabs, the same two addresses) |
| `.filters-on ul.pills`, `.pills-label` (the filters that are on) | `ul.filter-chips`, `.filter-chips-label` (removable chips, not tabs) |

Not tabs, kept: the buying flow (`ol.flow`, numbered steps), the phone's bottom bar (`.tabbar`), the pager, `nav.rows-choice` (rows per page,
a size picker like the pager), the spot check's 20 blocks. The item page's parts and the settings sections have no tab row yet: their
waves draw them with these classes.

**DS3. Status: three parts, one set of colours.** `.chip` is the solid status (8 px corners now, was 6); on a record (any page heading, its
state line, not only a document's) it is the 32 px block; `td.doc-st` stays the solid cell of a board; `.tag` is the soft tag: its tone's
tint and words, 12 px (was 11), grey when it names no tone, and it never takes the tone of a row around it (`.tag:is(<tones>)`). The seven
colours are the tone classes, as before: grey `waiting` (a draft), blue `info` (sent, new), purple `review` (waiting for someone, being
checked), amber `needs` (needs a look), green `done`, red `blocked` (late, refused), navy `off` (closed). Mapped: `.tag.ok` / `.warn` /
`.bad` → `.tag.done` / `.needs` / `.blocked` (the invoice list's match tag too); `.tag.band <tone>` → `.tag <tone>`; removed (no page used
them): `.status`, `.status-*`, `.tag.mine`, `.mark`. One colour moved: a closed purchase order is navy (`PO_STATE closed` → `off`), as the
approved canvas draws "Closed"; a delivery's draft stays amber (its work is waiting) until the goods-in wave redraws that board.

**DS4. The page's create button and More.** The section's create button is the page's main action at the normal size (was small, and a
split button with an accent arrow when the section has several "New …"): `.btn.primary`, then the other "New …" under a plain "More"
(`details.more`, Words `UI more`, its name "More to create"). More is one component for the page and for a saved document's bar (the order's
and the invoice's other steps): a `<details>` that needs no script, a drawn arrow, a menu of rows (links, a form's button, a fold's summary;
a risky step in red words), in the flow under its button on a phone. app.js closes an open More on Esc or a click elsewhere, as it did the
split menu, but never one that holds an open step (a reason being typed, or a step the server refused and opened again). The document bars'
buttons are the normal size too (they stand beside the create button's place in the head). On the Dashboard (no section) the create
buttons are plain (`split.php`'s `main` false): its main action is the person's first job, as the Dashboard design (HM_Home) draws it.

**DS5. One main action per page, or one per form where a page holds several.** The parts board: "One main button per page. The rest are
plain." Applied:
- a form that only filters or searches (a GET form: every toolbar's Apply, the search page, the audit search) is never the page's main
  action: its button is plain (24 templates);
- a button repeated on every row of a list is plain and small (`.btn.sm`): Open, Receive, Review, Choose, Check & match, Book invoice,
  Make final on a row, Match on a candidate (GI_List draws "Receive" so); the exception is a work queue whose rows are each one small form
  answered in turn (Lines to place's Place, as LP_Queue draws it; Simple matching's Apply) and a record's decision (OK / Not OK) where a
  page lists several records;
- the saves of a settings page with several small forms are plain (TP_Settings draws them so): a warehouse, a reason, an approval rule;
- on a record page the page's job keeps the colour and an edit beside it is plain (the item's selling mode, the supplier item's "make main",
  the company's Change);
- a helper on a field inside the main form is soft (the delivery editor's scan Add, beside "Save and book in");
- the empty state's next step is plain (the page's create button is its main action);
- a list's bulk bar has one main action: the first action offered as `primary` (`bulk_bar.php`); the others are plain (New variants'
  "Confirm match" beside "Create as new items", Store Products' "Create new warehouse products for these" beside the list's own action).

Where a page had two magenta buttons, demoted (listed for the owner in the build's report): the toolbar's Apply on 22 list pages and the
audit and search pages' Search; the Dashboard's create buttons beside the first job's button; the bulk bar's second positive action; Arriving's Receive per row; the bench list's Open; By Item's Review and the picker's Choose and quick Match;
Check & match per row and the match lists' Open (`CheckMatchScreenTest` now pins them plain); By store's Review; To check's Open; Repack's
Make final per row; the not-invoiced list's Book invoice; a delivery's Book invoice and Claim beside its review answer; an approval rule's
Save; a warehouse's three saves; a reason's three saves; the hand-over and account balances' Pay; a count's "Recount them all" beside "Make
the count final"; the delivery editor's Add (now soft) beside "Save and book in"; the item's "Save selling mode" beside "Confirm the card";
the supplier item's "Make this the main supplier" beside "Save price"; the company's "Change" beside "Confirm"; Settings' "Edit company";
the landing page's "This is a real product" fold; the staff set-up sheet's incidental "New user" (the page after the form shows no create
button, as the new invoice page: `side: ''`; "Done: back to …" is its main action); returns' quick "Return from a delivery" beside the create drawer; the empty state's button.

**DS6. The tests.** `UiUnitTest::testTheOneTabsButtonsAndStatusPartsFollowThePartsBoard` pins the CSS of the three components (and the
seven tones' colours). `UiTemplatesTest::testNoViewUsesARemovedClass` scans every template (the classes in the markup, between PHP blocks
inside an attribute, and in PHP-built strings), the classes the controllers hand a template, the classes app.js sets and the stylesheet's
rules: no removed class, every button a `.btn` with at most one variant and one size, every tab row a `nav.tabs`, a soft tag names only a
tone, and the stylesheet names no button variant but the five and two sizes. `UiTemplatesTest::testEveryPageHasAtMostOneMainButtonPerForm`
counts the main buttons of each template's forms (a button inside the form or naming it with `form=`; the branches of one if as the largest,
a loop as many) and the main links and fold buttons outside them, at most one each; a class that names `primary` only under a condition is
left to `tests/Support/MainButtons`, which `KernelBrowser` runs on every HTML page a kernel test opens (a failure names the page and the
buttons). The pins that named the old classes follow (`KernelUiTestCase::segments`, the pill and legend helpers of the matching tests, the
reports' Show, the More xpaths of the invoice tests, the item cards' filter chips).

## Stock counts, one way in and one way out (branch `counts-one-page`, 29 Oct 2026; CV1-CV12)

The owner approved the count screens of the canvas "CW Daily Screens" on 29 Oct 2026 (relayed by the coordinator with the static mockups
`CT_Board`, `CT_Sheet`, `CT_Final`, `CT_Phone`): one way in (the board's bar) and one way out (the sheet's "Save and review", the final page's
"Make the count final"), monday.com's board look, one main action a page, no help paragraphs. Built from main `24b474a` (OV, the order and
invoice boards, DS1-DS6) in `/root/cw-ctone`. Layout and navigation only: no migration, no new route, no new permission, no service rule
changed (`Counts\*` untouched). Code: `src/Ui/Controller/CountsController.php`, views `stock_counts`, `stock_count`, `stock_count_before`,
`src/Ui/Words.php` (`COUNTS`, `COUNT_GROUP`; `COUNT_HOW` removed), `src/Ui/Html.php` (`clock()`), `public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`.

**CV1. The board's groups.** Overdue (red, `blocked`: counted, but longer ago than the plan), Never counted (purple, `review`), Inside the
plan (green, `done`), in the design's order; the list under them is `CountPlan::next` as before (the first N, never counted first). The four
figure tiles went into the headings: each heading carries the plan's figure for the warehouse (the plan's own "overdue" counts the never
counted too; on the board they are apart, so Overdue's figure is overdue minus never; "items in the plan" is the sum), and "· k on this
list" when the list shows fewer. A group with nothing on the list is a heading only (no fold); a search counts what it found. Inside the plan
starts folded: the page draws its toggle with `data-folded` and app.js folds it with the toggle's own code, so without the script every group
is open. A row: the tick box (section 21's `td.c-pick` + `label.pick`), the item, its status as the solid cell (`td.doc-st`), last counted,
sold a day. The shared board classes (`.doc-group`, `.doc-board`, `.doc-list`); a ticked row keeps its cell solid.

**CV2. One way in: the bar.** The board sits inside the "open a count sheet" form, and its bar is the shared `.doc-bar` (sticky in its
form): "N ticked" (app.js, from `data-words`; hidden without the script, where nothing would keep it true), ONE "Count" menu
(`select name=mode`: The ticked items / The next N due / Everything found (k) / An empty sheet: scan as you go), the shelf menu (the
warehouse's places, when it has any), the note, and ONE "Open count sheet" (primary). The four open buttons and the "how many" box went.
"The next N due" sends a hidden `n` = the board's Show choice (50, 100, 200; the brief's "existing setting": no new setting): the list on
the board is exactly the next N, so what is opened is what is seen. With a search the menu offers everything found instead of the next N
(as the buttons did). The route, its four modes and checks (`bad_next` 1 to 200, `nothing_ticked`, `bad_mode`), FormOnce, CSRF and the
500-line limit are unchanged. A refused open now comes back with the ticked boxes (they were lost), the menu's choice, the shelf, the note.

**CV3. The board's head and toolbar.** The Filter pop-over went: one search, the warehouse and the Show choice side by side, and a plain
Show button (a GET form is never the main action, DS5). The head's right holds "Open sheets (N)", a plain link to Count sheets
(`state=draft`, the warehouse; N read by the record index (doc_type, status, id): drafts are sheets), instead of the create button, which
pointed at this same form; nothing when no sheet is open. The "How counting works" fold, the board's notes and its foot line went; the plan's
one line with its setting link stays.

**CV4. No stock figure on the board.** The board showed "Stock now" on every row: with a blind count (`counts.sheet_shows_stock` off) that
told the counter the figure before the count. The design has no such column; it went.

**CV5. The sheet's head.** The status block in the heading (`div.doc-head`): an open sheet is "Counting" (blue `info`, as the design
draws it; the Count sheets list's rows and their "Open sheets" heading say it too); the other states as before. Under it one line: where
(the warehouse, its shelf), "opened <when> by <who>", the note; a blind count adds the tag "Blind count". At the head's right "N of M
counted" with its bar (a `progress`, section 13), instead of the create button. Every other view (a final sheet, a record that puts a count
back, someone else's open sheet) keeps its facts list.

**CV6. The sheet's lines and the line to count now.** The scan box is a card of its own, 48 px with 16 px words ("Scan a barcode or type a
CW number"; Find it); what it finds is CT4's (a barcode or a CW number; a name is not looked up). The lines are a board in a card with the
blue edge: the item (line, CW number, brand, selling mode; its barcodes), Stock now (only when the setting shows it: CV8), Counted (the big
box, 18 px), Saved ("✓ Saved 10:15": the line's own count time, CT2's moment per line, in UK time with the day when it is not today:
`Html::clock`; else "Not yet"). app.js's "not saved yet" mark finds the Saved mark in the box's row. The line to count now (`tr.now`: the
line a scan or "Save and next item" marked, else the first one on the page not counted) has the accent's tint. On a phone (CT_Phone) it is
the one big card, first (`order: -1` in the cards' grid), with "How many did you count?", a 64 px box and "Save and next item"; the other
lines are small cards (the name and its Saved mark, then the box: the design's done cards have no box, but a wrong figure must stay
correctable on a phone). "Save and next item" (`next` = its line) is a soft button of the quantity form (the main button stays "Save and
review"); wider than a phone it is not shown. It saves exactly as Save, then opens the next line not counted after it (else the first one
before it), marked and its box ready, read after the save by the line key; with none left, the sheet as after Save. Enter in any box still
saves only: the form's first button is a hidden Save (`button.po-default`, the order editor's), so Enter never reviews and never moves on.

**CV7. The sheet's bar.** The shared `.doc-bar` at the bottom, after the quantity form, its buttons naming it (`form="count-lines"`): More
(DS4's one More; in a bar at the bottom its menu opens upwards and scrolls when tall) with two folds (`details.doc-act`): "Count on paper:
download and upload" (the download link, the upload form) and "Stop this sheet" (the reason, the button); then Save, and "Save and review"
(primary, `then=review`: OV6's button, renamed). The "When you have counted" card and the folds under the page went. After an upload's
preview, a refused upload or a refused stop, More comes back open with that fold open (PV26's rule); the preview is a card in the page above
the bar. With no line on the page (a filter, an empty sheet) the bar's main action is the link "Review the differences" (OV6 kept a link).

**CV8. A blind count never shows the stock figure on the sheet.** CT4 showed it once a line held a quantity, so a counter could read it and
type it again to make the line agree. With `counts.sheet_shows_stock` off the sheet now has no Stock now column at all (the brief: "blind
counts never show the stock figure"); the download leaves it out as before. "Before it is final" still shows what CW holds (that is where the
differences are decided), and a final sheet what it booked; someone else's open blind sheet says "not shown: a blind count".

**CV9. Before it is final: the strip and the two boards.** The four tiles became the shared strip (`section.doc-progress`): Counted (of M on
the sheet), Same as the system (green), Different (amber), A reviewer checks (the lines above the limits: they wait on Differences once the
count is final, CT6). Then the board "Different from the system" (amber): every line with a difference, left out by a later count, whose stock
moved after the count, kept, counted too long ago, marked by too many count times, or above the limits; the biggest difference first as before.
Then "Same as the system" (green), folded at first by the script. A line: the item, with what moved, what keeping the count does and the
limits it is above under its name (as before); Counted; System (what CW holds now); Difference; What happens (the solid cell: Booked as
counted, green; A reviewer checks it, amber; Left out, navy; red where it stops the making final: Count again: too many count times, Counted
too long ago, Stock moved: choose); and the answers: "Count again" (plain, small) on every line (`/recount` empties any counted line:
`CountSheets::recount`), "Keep my count" (quiet, small) where stock moved, as before. The too-many-times message and its one button stay above.

**CV10. Before it is final: the bar.** Back to the sheet (quiet, left), and ONE "Make the count final" (the post form: csrf and version,
unchanged). While a marked line waits for its answer the button is drawn switched off with the reason beside it (`.btn-why`, DS1) and there
is no post form, as before; the service's own refusal (409 `moved_since`) is unchanged. The help paragraph about making it final went.

**CV11. Words.** New (`Words::COUNTS`): the group headings' figures, "Open sheets (%s)", "%s ticked", the Count menu and its four choices,
Shelf, "Open count sheet", Counting, Blind count, the head's line, the scan box's hint, Saved / "Saved %s" / "Not yet", "How many did you
count?", Save, "Save and next item", "Save and review", "Review the differences", the strip's four labels, the two groups, System, the four
line states. Changed: the scan box's label, `blind`, `recount` ("Count again", as the too-many-times words already said), the open sheet's
intro. Removed (no page uses them any more; the owner's "no help paragraphs"): `COUNT_HOW`, the tiles' words, the four open buttons', the
board notes and foot, `save_page`, `save_hint`, `final_*`, `paper_text`, `stop_text`, `holds_now`, `over_chip`, `make_final_title`,
`make_final_text`, `retime_all_text`, `mode`, `no_mode`. `COUNT_GROUP` is in the design's order.

**CV12. Kept, and the tests.** Every rule: blind counts (stricter, CV8), later-count protection (a line left out says so; Differences'
"counted again since"), the changed-stock choices (warn first: both answers, no post form until answered, the 409), the warehouse scope
(the board, the open sheets' figure and link are the chosen warehouse's), the sheet limits (500 lines, the next 1 to 200, refused in
words), duplicate-open protection (FormOnce), CSRF on every POST, the opener alone, versions, the count time per line (`at_<line>`) and the
changed boxes only (`was_<line>`). Tests (red first: `runs/ctone_red.log`, 9 failures on `24b474a`): `CountsScreensTest` (new: the one Count
menu opens each kind of sheet and a refused open keeps the choice; "Save and next item"; changed to the new pages: the groups with their
figures and folds, the solid cells, the bar's one button, the head, the Saved mark, the bar's More and buttons, the strip and boards, the
switched-off button, a blind count never shows the figure, the preview opens More), `OpFinalScreensTest` (the review button's words, Enter's
hidden Save, no stock column on a blind count), `UiUnitTest::testTheCountPagesFollowTheApprovedDesign` (CSS and JS pins; the three count
templates close every tag they open), `CountWordsTest` (`COUNT_HOW` gone, the group order). app.js checked with `node --check` on cw-test;
not seen in a real browser.

## Goods in on one page (branch `gi-one-page`, 29 Oct 2026; GV1-GV10)

The owner's request of 29 Oct 2026, approved design (the canvas "CW Daily Screens": `GI_List` the Goods in board, `Main` one delivery on one
page, `GI_Phone` checking at the bench on a phone): Goods in on ONE page, monday.com board style, like the purchase order and supplier
invoice one-page work (PX, PV). Built from main `24b474a` in `/root/cw-gione`. Code: `ReceivingController` (the board, the one page, its one
form), views `receipts` (the board), `receipt_edit` (the one page), `gi_more` (new: its More), `doc_bar` (an optional note), `bench_list` (its
links); `receipt_bench` removed; `Words` `GI`, `GI_STATE`, `GI_CHECK`, `GI_DUTY`, `RECEIPT_ERROR`'s `saved_not_booked*` and `fine_*`, `NEW
receiving` ("New delivery"); `app.css`'s block "gi-one-page"; `app.js`'s Goods in block (the old bench page's find, fill and tick code gone
with it). No migration, no permission, no service change: `GoodsReceipts`, `ReceiptPlan`, `GoodsReceiptHandler` and their tests
(`tests/Integration/Receiving`) are unchanged; every route stays.

Before: Goods in, Start, the editor (save), attach the invoice (its own form), the bench page (save), the delivery's page, Book in: 7
presses, 4 forms sent, 7 pages. Now: "Receive" on the board's order (or "+ New delivery"), then on one page "All fine" per line (with the
script nothing is sent; without it each press saves) and "Book in N items", which sends the paperwork answer, the invoice number and its
copy with it: 2 forms sent, 3 pages.

**GV1. The board.** `GET /ui/receiving` is a board (PV18's shared pieces: `.doc-group` headings with their count, `.doc-board` cards with a
6 px coloured edge, `td.doc-st` solid status cells): Arriving (blue: the open orders, approved, sent or part received, that still expect
items and have no delivery being checked; the order's number and "N still to come", its state's own colour, the supplier, Expected (red
when today or passed), the items to come, and for someone who receives goods a plain small "Receive": the new-delivery form's own POST with
the order and "copy its lines", FormOnce), Being checked (purple: not started (grey cell), part checked, paperwork not right (red cell);
"Checked" as a purple bar and "4 / 6 lines"), Ready to book in (amber: checked at the bench; "N problems" under the status when lines
were found short, over, damaged, wrong or without a stamp), Booked in today (green; Booked in under Show "all", where a taken-back delivery
is navy), Cancelled (navy) only under Show. One search (the number, the supplier invoice, the order, the supplier's name, a scanned
delivery note), one Show menu (Today and open, All deliveries, Cancelled), "+ New delivery" at the toolbar's right (the section's create
button, now worded "New delivery"; it opens the drawer `#new` with the old form: the order or the supplier, the invoice number, copy). Home's
links (`?state=checked`, `?state=refused`) and `?supplier=` still narrow it (an old state link looks at every day, not only today). A
group's rows are the deliveries of the board's query (300 newest, as before); the arriving orders are `receivableOrders()`'s.

**GV2. One page for everyone who receives goods.** A delivery not booked in yet opens as the one page for every holder of `doc.GRN.post`
(goods in, the purchasing desk and manager): its keyer (the creator) changes everything, as the editor let them; anyone else checks it,
sets its supplier invoice number, delivery note and invoice date (`GoodsReceipts::setInvoice`, I172: only when changed, so only then is
that person kept out of its review) and books it in, as the bench page and the read-only page let them; the lines' quantities, the order,
the supplier and the arrival time are shown, not fields (sent anyway, `saveDraft` refuses them: 403 `not_creator`). Someone who only looks
(a reviewer, the stock controller, the accountant) keeps the read-only page; so does a delivery booked in or cancelled. The old bench
address (`GET /ui/receiving/{id}/bench`) leads to the page; the bench list (Checking) opens it. Its parts, top to bottom: the head (the
title as before, its place on the board as a solid block, the supplier and the order, More: the keyer's "Copy the order's lines still to
come", "Import the supplier's sheet" with the sample, "Cancel this delivery" in red last, each its own form after the page's); the progress
strip (`.doc-progress`: Lines; Checked N of M with a purple bar; Problems, the lines checked with a problem; Items in, the items that go
into stock of the items on the paperwork, from the plan); the details (three columns, two on a tablet, one on a phone: Supplier, From
order, Arrived, Delivery note number, Supplier's invoice number, Paperwork (the bench's question: matches the boxes / does not match);
"More details" folds the invoice date, the paper sheet, the reason it is keyed late (only when it arrived before the day it was started,
or the sheet or a reason is there) and the note, open when one of them is needed); the scan box; the lines; the prices fold; photos and
papers and the note (the bench's note, the delivery's own note being one of the rarely used fields); "Before it can be booked in" (the
plan's problems and warnings, folded, open after a refused booking); the sticky bar (Leave without saving, "N lines still to check", Save,
"Book in N items" the one main button; "Save and show the next N lines" when the lines are paged).

**GV3. The one form, and "Book in".** One form (`POST /ui/receiving/{id}/lines`, multipart) carries everything. In ONE transaction, in this
order: the keyer's save (`saveDraft`: the header and the lines of the page as edited), someone else's supplier invoice (`setInvoice`), the
check (`bench()`: the lines this person touched, at their numbers after the save, and the checklist answers they changed), the file
(`attach()`: the invoice copy, a photo, a delivery note or the duty proof; a photo taken from a line's panel names its line), then what
was scanned or chosen (`addLine` / `addChoice`). Each service locks the delivery and checks the version the step before left; a refusal
saves nothing and the page comes back with what was typed (the panel of the line it names open). "Book in" (`action=post`) is that save,
committed, then `GoodsReceipts::post` with the version the save left, in the posting's own transaction: no transaction is opened around
the posting, so its lock order (number series, the order, the stock) is the one it always had. Refused, the delivery stays a draft with
everything saved and the page says so in plain words: "Saved. Not booked in yet: 1 thing must be settled first…" (the problems under
"Before it can be booked in", open), "…someone changed this delivery a moment ago…" (409), else the refusal's own words; the same form sent
twice lands on the delivery the first one booked in. A form saved on a version it was not drawn with (GV4: someone else saved meanwhile
something this form did not change) is not booked in: the save stays and the page says "…someone changed this delivery a moment ago. Check
it and book it in again." (409), so nothing is booked in that its person did not see (the read-only page's "Book in" sent its version too).
Words left in the scan box refuse "Book in" before anything is saved (as before).
(The editor's "Save and post" used to post inside the save's transaction: a refused posting threw the typed edits away.)

**GV4. A line's check: touched, "All fine", stale.** A line's row carries its identity (`b_<n>_present`) and `b_<n>_was`: the bench
stamp of the line as drawn (`benchStamps`, I175) and a fingerprint of the answers the row shows (checked, short, over, damaged, wrong, and
for a duty line its stamp answer, code, items without a stamp, what to do, the proof). A line whose answers come back as drawn is not
touched and never written: a save of the keyer's prices, or of another line, never writes back a line as an older page showed it, and
never stamps a new check time on lines already checked (the bench page re-counted every ticked line on each save). A touched line is
written as the bench page did (I168): counted when ticked or an answer changed, its count taken back when its tick is taken off. "All fine"
is the bench's counted tick with no problem: the line ticked, short, over, damaged, wrong and without a stamp 0, what to do and the proof
cleared, its stamp answer kept; a duty line needs that answer first (422 `fine_needs_stamp`, nothing saved) and "No stamp" is not all fine
(422 `fine_no_stamp`: press Problem and count the items without one). Without the script it is a submit button (`fine=<n>`, the form
saved); with it the row is ticked in the page (`b_<n>_fine`, which a problem typed in the panel afterwards takes off again). A form drawn
before someone else's save is saved on the current version while what it changes was not changed meanwhile: the keyer's part by the desk
stamp (I175, as the editor), someone else's supplier invoice by the fingerprint of what was drawn, the checklist by its stamp (only when
this person changed an answer of it), each touched line by its own stamp. Otherwise it is drawn again (409) with what was typed, except on
the lines whose product or quantity changed (the old bench's words, `version_conflict_bench` and `bench_except`); the keyer's conflict keeps
the editor's words and drops the line rows when lines were added or removed. A line the same form changes the quantity of is counted
again only when this person touched its check (pressed "All fine" or changed an answer) in that form; otherwise its check is cleared and

### The Codex review of 5c070f8 (`runs/gione_codex_review2.txt`): seven MEDIUM, all real (branch `gi-fixes2`, GV18-GV22)

Each shown failing first: `runs/gione_codex2_red.log` (the five new kernel tests and the script's pin on main `b3c7829`: 1 error, 5 failures
of 6); the node harness's new checks failed 4 of 4 on main's app.js (a refused send left both buttons disabled).

**GV18. A supplier's invoice copy is decided by what it is attached as, not only by how it was first kept.** The file store keeps the same
bytes once, with the kind they were first kept as: a scan attached first as a line's photo and then as a delivery's supplier invoice stayed
`kind = photo`, so goods in still got its link and its download. Now a file is the invoice copy when it is kept as one or attached to any
record with the role `supplier_invoice` (`FilesController::isInvoiceCopy()`); the download (`/ui/files/{id}`, 403 `file_invoices` without
`invoices.view`), the one page's and the read-only page's file lists and the record page (`/ui/documents/{id}`) all use that one rule (the
name without its link). `testAnInvoiceCopyKeptFirstAsAPhotoIsStillTheBuyingDesks`.

**GV19. One save is never half kept: its size and its number of files come from PHP's own settings.**
- The script counted only the files' bytes; the request also carries every field as a part (its boundary and header), and past
  `post_max_size` PHP drops the whole body, so everything typed was lost. The page now carries `data-max-total` = `post_max_size`
  (`UiRequest::postMaxBytes()`, read with `ini_get`, never a number in the code) and the script counts each field's part as the browser sends
  it (about 100 bytes of boundary and header, its name and value; a file its name, its type line and its bytes): too much is said in the bar
  ("Too big together for one save (at most N MB): attach them one or two at a time.") and not sent.
- Without the script (or past the estimate) the body arrives empty: the kernel sends a POST to `/ui/receiving/{id}/lines` with no field, no
  file and a `Content-Length` over `post_max_size` to `ReceivingController::droppedBody()`: the delivery's page again (413) with "Not saved:
  the photos and papers were too big together (at most N MB in one save). Attach them one or two at a time." (after the origin check;
  nothing is written, no form came). Any other page keeps the plain 413 `too_large`.
- Past `max_file_uploads` PHP drops the later files without a word. `UiRequest::maxFileUploads()` (from `ini_get`): a save carrying that
  many files may have lost one, so the server refuses it (422 `too_many_files`, "Not saved: at most N photos and papers go in one save.
  Attach the others after saving.", N = the limit less one) and saves nothing; the page carries `data-max-files` and the script says the
  same before sending (`data-files-words`). Empty file fields do not count (PHP does not count them either).
- A send the page refuses left every submit button disabled: `sendOnce` had already scheduled the disable. It now looks at
  `ev.defaultPrevented` inside its timer, once every listener of that send has run (all forms, not only this page).
`testFilesTooBigTogetherOrTooManyNeverSaveHalf`; the pins in `UiUnitTest::testTheScriptNeverOpensABrowserDialog`; the node harness.

**GV20. Every line of a page removed, then "Save and show the next lines", skips nothing.** The next page started at least one line on
(GV16 5 kept a minimum of one): with none of the page's lines left, the next lines start where this page did.
`testRemovingAWholePageThenNextSkipsNothing`.

**GV21. A refusal's link to a line of another page goes to that page.** "Check line 48" linked `#line-48`, which is not on a page of lines
1-47. `ReceivingController::fixes()` now links a line not drawn to `/ui/receiving/{id}?from=<line>#line-<line>` (the duty stamp and any
plan problem naming a line alike); a line on this page keeps its `#line-N` (or its field). `testARefusalLinksALineOfAnotherPageToItsPage`.

**GV22. A draft is not stuck when its keyer can no longer receive goods.** Creator-only cancel stays the rule (GV17). The one way round it:
once the keyer no longer holds `doc.GRN.post` (another job) or is switched off, someone who holds both `doc.GRN.post` and `doc.PO.post`
(the purchasing manager's permissions; no role name in the code, and never admin, who never drafts or posts) cancels the draft, with the
required reason as always; the audit row `grn.cancel` records `for_keyer` (the keyer's staff id) beside the reason. While the keyer can still
receive, the purchasing manager is refused like anyone else (403 `not_keyer_cancel`, whose words now say who else can). The page shows
Cancel under More to them only then (`GoodsReceipts::mayCancel()`, the same rule; copy and import stay the keyer's: since DA1 anyone's
who receives goods; cancel still the keyer's).
`testAKeyerWhoCanNoLongerReceiveLeavesTheDraftToThePurchasingManager`.

## Approvals › Waiting for you: one inbox, one record at a time (branch `approvals-inbox`, 29 Oct 2026; AV1-AV14)

The owner approved the Approvals screens of the canvas "CW Daily Screens" on 29 Oct 2026 (relayed by the coordinator with the static mockups
`AP_Inbox` and `AP_Phone`): one page listing every record the signed-in person may answer, grouped by kind, one record open with its facts and
ONE decision. Built from main `7cfcc89`, rebased on `d18e699` (goods in on one page), in `/root/cw-apone`. No migration, no new permission, no
service rule changed: every answer is the kind's own route. Code: `src/Ui/Controller/InboxController.php` (new), views `approvals_inbox`,
`approvals_record`, `lq_item_box` (new), the hooks in `StoreQueuesController`, `CountsController`, `StaffRequestsController`,
`ReviewsController`, `SuppliersController`, `CompanyController`; `src/Ui/Sections.php`, `src/Ui/Context.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php` (`INBOX`),
`public/ui/assets/app.css` (the `.ap-*` block).

**AV1. One page.** `GET /ui/approvals`, "Approvals › Waiting for you", the first tab of Approvals, so the menu's Approvals entry opens it.
The route is `Route::ANY`; the page itself refuses (403, `INBOX not_yours`) a person whose jobs answer none of its kinds, and the tab is shown
to exactly those people: a page of `Ui\Sections` may now name a list of permissions (any of them, `Sections::may`), and the inbox names
`InboxController::PERMS` (every kind's permission; `InboxUnitTest` holds the two equal for every job). A buyer, a viewer, the auditor and
admin answer nothing: their Approvals entry opens History, as before.

**AV2. The kinds, in the brief's order.** Who answers each is its own page's permission; the colour is a tone of `Words::TONES`.

| Kind | Rows (as on its own page) | Who | Colour | Its own page (the group's "Open the list") |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERPNext corrections | `Corrections::list('open')` | `queues.corrections` | amber `needs` | /ui/queues/corrections |
| Lines to place | `Suspense::list('open')` | `queues.suspense` | blue `info` | /ui/queues/suspense |
| Count differences | `CountsController::differences()`, only the rows without a refusal | `doc.CNT.post` (`Documents::mayPost`) | purple `review` | /ui/stock/counts/differences |
| Oversold | `Oversells::list('open')` | `queues.oversell` | red `blocked` | /ui/queues/oversold |
| Mode changes | `ModeChanges::list('open')` | `queues.modes` | navy `off` | /ui/queues/modes |
| Website bugs | `LandingOrders::list('open')` | `queues.oversell` | grey `waiting` | /ui/queues/landing |
| Staff requests | `RoleRequests::pending()`, only `can` | `staff.approve` | blue `info` | /ui/staff-requests |
| Documents to review | `ReviewsController::tasks()` (documents, suppliers, the company details), only the rows without a refusal; the OKs first | `documents.review`, `documents.approve`, `suppliers.approve`, `company.confirm` | purple `review` | /ui/documents/reviews |

Seven tones for eight kinds: blue and purple are used twice, never side by side. A kind with nothing waiting is not drawn.

**AV3. The list.** A card; each group a heading (the dot and the name in the kind's colour, its count, "Open the list"), each row a plain link
`?open=<kind>-<id>` (its title, and one muted line: "Set to 22 · 29 Oct 2026", "CS-00041 · counted 160, system 200", …), the open one on
the selected tint with the accent's 4 px edge (`aria-current`). At most a page of a kind is listed (the queues' 50, the count differences'
page), then "The first N are shown"; the heading's count is the kind's whole count, the badge's. Without `open` the first record is open
(as the mockup draws it); an `open` that is not waiting, or not of the right shape, opens the first one (never an error).

**AV4. The same rows as the kinds' pages.** Two readers were moved, unchanged, out of a page method so both pages read them:
`CountsController::differences()` (from `reviews()`) and `ReviewsController::tasks()` (from `queue()`; each row now also says its `subject`
and `kind`). `StoreQueuesController::pickedLabel()` (the item box's chip of a refused answer) likewise; `DocumentsController::plain()` (a
record page's refusal in words) and `CompanyController::plain()` became public.

**AV5. No decision logic of its own.** An answer is a form of the kind's OWN route (`/ui/queues/<queue>/<id>/<answer>`,
`/ui/stock/counts/differences/line|review/…`, `/ui/staff-requests/<id>/approve|reject`, `/ui/documents/reviews/<task>/approve|reject`,
`/ui/purchasing/suppliers/tasks/<task>/approve|reject`, `/ui/reference/company/reviews/<task>/approve|reject`): the same permission on the
route, CSRF, field parsing, service call, note rules, outcome, notice and audit. The form adds `inbox=1`, `inbox_next` (the record drawn after
it) and `inbox_pos` (its place in the list). Each of those actions, when `InboxController::from()` (a POST with `inbox=1`), leads back to the
inbox instead of its page: `answered()` redirects to `/ui/approvals?notice=<its code>&words=<whose notice words>&open=<next>&pos=<place>` (the
inbox shows that page's own notice: `QUEUE_NOTICE`, `COUNT_NOTICE`, `StaffRequestsController::NOTICES`, `RECORD_NOTICE`, `SUPPLIER_NOTICE`,
`COMPANY_NOTICE`); a refusal (`refused()`) draws the inbox with the same status, on that record, the refusal in that page's words, and what
was typed kept. Only the inbox's own address is ever a target; `inbox_next` must be a key (`/^[a-z]{4,12}-[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$/`), `inbox_pos`
digits, else they are dropped. A supplier's Withdraw is not offered in the inbox and never leads there.

**AV6. The open record.** A card with the kind's colour on a 6 px top edge (the tone sits on a wrapper, so `.card.waiting`'s amber panel
never applies): "<kind> · <from> · N of M", the title (a link to the item, the variant or the record's own page where the person may open
it), a muted line (the CW code, the variant, the e-mail), the status block "Waiting" in the kind's colour; the facts as big figures
(`dl.ap-facts`; a difference signed and green or red); the lines that say what it is and what the answers do (the kinds' own words: the
correction's effect, the line's place and why it waits, why a difference waits, the order and what happened, what accepting a mode does,
"No stock moved for it", how the person set up their sign-in, what OK and Not OK do); the notes so far (Oversold); links (the count sheet,
the supplier). Then ONE decision: the form `#ap-answer` with the fields the kind needs and the main answer in magenta (outside the form, it
names it), then More (`details.more`) with the rarer answers: a button of the same form with its own route (`formaction`; it sends the same
note: Close a correction, Keep what CW has, Add the note only, Reject a count) or, where the main answer takes no note or another one, a fold
with its own small form and note (Not OK of a staff request, a document, a supplier's task or the company details; Close a line to place).
The note is the kind's: required with the queues' and the counts' limits, optional on a record's OK, none on a staff request's OK (its page
has none). Then "Next: <its title>", or "This is the last one."

| Kind | Facts | Main answer | Under More |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERPNext corrections | ERPNext set it to, CW held then, Kept for paid orders, Difference | Confirm (note) | Close it (same note) |
| Lines to place | Units (or Set to), Came in as, From | Place / Send to corrections (item box, units each, note) | Close it (its own note) |
| Count differences | Counted, System, Difference, Counted by | Accept the count (`answer=accept`, note) | Reject: put it back (`answer=reject`, same note), when it may be rejected |
| Oversold | Short by, Left for sale, Order, From | Mark handled (how, note) | Add the note (same note) |
| Mode changes | ERPNext set, CW has now, Low-stock level | Accept the change (note) | Keep what CW has (same note) |
| Website bugs | Units ordered, Paid, Option number | Mark handled (how, note, `paid` as seen) | — |
| Staff requests | What is asked, Jobs now, Jobs asked for, Asked by | OK (no note) | Not OK (its own note) |
| Documents to review | Value (no VAT) or Items, Asked by, Check by (red when late) | the record page's OK (optional note) | Not OK (its own note) |

**AV7. Lines to place keeps its item box (LQ).** The box of LQ4-LQ6 became the partial `lq_item_box` (the input with `data-lq-pick`, its
list, chip, note line and "+ Add new item"), drawn by `queue_suspense` in its cell as before and by the inbox (`id` `ap`, form `ap-answer`);
app.js is unchanged (the box's parent holds its parts). Without the script it is the CW code's text box.

**AV8. The next record, keeping the place.** `inbox_next` is the row after the open one in the page's order: the next of the same kind, else
the first of the next kind. After an answer that record opens; if it is not waiting any more, the record now at the answered one's place
(`pos`, the list being one shorter), else the last. An answer that settles nothing (Oversold's "Add the note") keeps the same record open.
A refused answer of a record that is still waiting comes back on it; one that was answered meanwhile (409) is said above the list and the
record now at its place opens.

**AV9. One name for one thing.** The old tab "Waiting for me" (the review queue) is now "Documents to review" (`MENU`, `PAGE_TITLE`), the name
of its group in the inbox; "Waiting for you" is the inbox.

**AV10. The badge counts the inbox.** `Context::badges()['approvals_inbox']` is the sum of what each kind's own badge counts for this person
(`queue_*`, `counts_open`, `reviews_open`) plus the staff requests they may decide (`RoleRequests::decidableCount`), for a person who answers
a kind. A section may name the tab whose count is its own (`Sections::MAP` `count`): Approvals counts its inbox once, where it summed its
tabs (which list the same records again: the tabs keep their own counts). The Stock section still counts its count differences under Counts.

**AV11. Phone and no script.** Under 700 px the open record comes first (`order: -1`, the mockup's "1 of 5" in its head) and the list after it;
the facts fill three a row, 20 px; the main answer takes two thirds of its row and More the rest; the fields are 16 px; every row and link
is 44 px or more; no sideways scroll (the long names wrap). Every answer is a plain POST form; More and its folds are `<details>`.

**AV12. Not built, said here.** The mockup's Show menu (Waiting / Answered today / All) and a search: an answered record stays on its kind's
own page, whose Show filter lists it, and each group links there. A supplier's task is decided in the inbox with the words of its slot (the
card's), its evidence one link away ("Open the supplier"); the inbox does not repeat the card's "not OK" words that depend on the supplier
being abroad.

**AV13. The main-button checks miss no case (the Codex review of DS1-DS6, two findings).** `tests/Support/MainButtons` (every page a kernel
test opens) now also fails a main button in a form that only filters or searches (method GET or none, or `formmethod` GET), and forms of one
route (its path, every number `{n}`) for two or more records (the numbers differ) that each hold a main button: a main button repeated row by
row. Two forms of the very same address are one record's answers (the variant page's quick "Yes" beside its full form: one per form, DS5) and
pass. Allowed, as DS5 documents (`ROW_ANSWERS`): Lines to place's Place, Simple matching's Apply, and the OK of each record's decision
(`/ui/documents/reviews/{n}/approve`, `/ui/staff-requests/{n}/approve`, `/ui/reference/company/reviews/{n}/approve`,
`/ui/purchasing/suppliers/tasks/{n}/approve`, and the second approval of a match, `/ui/review/decision/{n}/approve`).
`UiTemplatesTest::testEveryPageHasAtMostOneMainButtonPerForm` reads the same two cases in the source (a `GET form …`, a form a loop opens
` (each row)`; the exceptions by template and action, `ROW_MAIN`) and names each problem. Caught and fixed: the barcode review's "Save
decision" on every row is plain now. Arrivals' "Receive" was plain already (DS5).

**AV14. Tests.** Red first (`runs/apone_red.log`: 15 failures and errors on `7cfcc89`). `ApprovalsInboxScreensTest` (new): who sees which
kinds (the stock controller, the desk, a reviewer, and the 403 of a buyer, a viewer, admin, the auditor), the menu and the badge; every answer
of the stores' queues sent on its own page and in the inbox on twin records, with the same record, stock and audit rows; Website bugs, Count
differences (accept, and reject under More) and Staff requests and Documents to review (OK; Not OK refused without a note, the fold open
again, then reversed) likewise; the next record and the kept place, a refusal with what was typed, an answer refused because someone answered
it meanwhile; the plain forms, the one main button and the item box; the inbox's fields change nothing but where the answer leads (the
route's permission and CSRF; an outside `inbox_next` dropped). `InboxUnitTest` (new): the tab for exactly the people the page lets in, the
section's count, the kinds' words and colours, the CSS of the approved design, the templates. Changed: `SectionsTest`, `MenusTest`, `PeopleScreenTest`,
`ReviewScreensTest`, `HomeScreenTest`, `StartSettingsWordsTest`, `WordsTest` (the inbox tab, the renamed tab, the menu's link), and the
main-button checks (AV13). Not seen in a real browser.

## Typed values are never lost through a tab or a filter link (branch `counts-tab-fix`, 29 Oct 2026; CV13-CV14)

Codex's review of `7cfcc89` (`runs/ctone_codex_review.txt`, one MEDIUM, the same one the tabs and buttons review had found on the count
sheet): on a sheet showing "Every line", type 7 into a box, then click the "Every line" tab, which is the one shown: its link reloads the
sheet with no save and no question, and the quantity and its count time are lost. The unsaved-changes question only guarded forms. The
coordinator asked for the fix in the shared tab markup, for every tab row beside a form that keeps typed values (the count sheet, a
delivery, a stock record, a hand-over, the order and invoice pages). Built from main `d18e699` in `/root/cw-ctone`, rebased onto `5c070f8`
(the approvals inbox, the goods-in fixes). No route, rule,
permission, form field or service changed.

**CV13. The tab of the page shown has no link.** Every tab (`a.tab`, DS2) draws its href only when it is not the page shown, so the open
one is the tab's look (`aria-current="page"`, the accent bar) and nothing to click, with or without the script, and never reloads the page.
Applied in every template that draws tabs: `page_frame` (the section's tabs and the segments) and the pages' own rows (the count sheet's
Show, barcodes, By Item's states, new items, new variants, the match strengths and Show of To review, the low and slow stock reports, the
stock value's grouping, dispatch, Store Products' states, the store choice). In `page_frame` the current tab or segment of a record's page
leads back to its list (another page): it stays a link, which asks first while a form holds typed values (CV14); `Sections::frame` marks a
tab or segment `here` when it is current and leads to the page's own path (whatever the query: a filter of the page is still the page).
CSS: the open tab without a link keeps its colour on hover and shows no pointer. Tests: `tests/Support/CurrentTabs`, run by `KernelBrowser`
on every HTML page a kernel test opens (a current tab linking to the page's own path fails the test that opened it);
`UiTemplatesTest::testTheTabOfThePageShownHasNoLinkAndTheEditorsAskBeforeALinkLeaves` (every tab of every template: one href, drawn only in
the branch where it is not the page shown); `UnsavedTabsScreensTest` (Codex's case on the sheet, with "Every line", "Not counted yet" and
"Counted", a notice in the address too; the board's own tab and segment; the sheet's tab and segment back to the lists stay links). The
kernel test helpers `sectionTabs()` and `segments()` give a link-less tab's href as null.

**CV14. A link that leaves a page with typed values says so first.** app.js spoke only before another form left the page (OV5, GV11); now a
click on a link that leaves the page while a form marked `data-unsaved` holds typed values (`data-dirty`) goes nowhere the first time, and a
red note at the bottom of the screen (`p.toast.error`, `role="alert"`) says why: "You have changes on this page that are not saved. They are
lost if you leave: save them first, or press the same link again to go on without them." (`Words::UI unsaved_link`, carried by the layout's
`body[data-unsaved-link]`). The same link pressed again goes on, as a leaving form's second press does since GV11 (never a browser dialog:
main's rule since GV11, pinned). A press on the note puts it away. A tab of another page, a filter, the pager, a crumb, the menu, an item's
name. It never stops a link to a part of the page
(`#…`), a download (`download`: the count sheet's paper copy, the order's lines file, the delivery's sample file), a link opened elsewhere
or with a modifier key (a new tab), or "Leave without saving" (`data-leave` on `doc_bar`'s link: it says what it does). It listens on
`window`, so a component's own link handler (the dropdowns' "+ Add new", the drawers) has had its say first. The order's and the
supplier invoice's one-page forms (`purchase_order_edit`, `invoice_edit`) now carry `data-unsaved` (`Words::DOC unsaved`), as a delivery, a
stock record, a hand-over and the count sheet already did, so their typed lines are guarded too (`DOC unsaved`, GV11's words: "press the
same button again"); their other forms are unchanged (they are not `data-leaves`). Without the script nothing stops a link (nothing is marked
unsaved either), and the open tab is still no link. Rebased onto main `5c070f8` (GV11-GV17): the first version asked with a browser dialog,
which GV11 removed from app.js; this one says it in the page. Tests:
`UnsavedTabsScreensTest::testTheOrderAndInvoicePagesAskBeforeALinkLeavesWithTypedValues`, the template lint above (the six editors carry
`data-unsaved`, their `.csv`/`.xlsx` links `download`, the leave link `data-leave`), `UiUnitTest::testTheCountPagesFollowTheApprovedDesign`
(the JS and CSS pins; main's pin that app.js has no alert, confirm or prompt holds). Not seen in a real browser; app.js checked with `node --check`.

## The item page, stock first (branch `item-stock-first`, 29 Oct 2026; IV1-IV12)

The owner approved the item screens of the canvas "CW Daily Screens" on 29 Oct 2026 (relayed by the coordinator with the static mockups
`IT_Item` and `IT_Phone`): the stock first, the editing below, monday.com's board look, one main action, no help paragraphs. Built from main
`5c070f8` (OV, LQ, DS1-DS6, CV, GV, AV) in `/root/cw-itone`, rebased onto `b3c7829` (CV13-CV14). Layout and navigation: no
migration, no new route, no new permission, no service rule changed. Code: `src/Ui/Controller/ItemController.php` (`top()`, `weekly()`,
`mainSupply()`, `countWarehouse()`, `sells()`, `openTab()`, `TABS`, `NOTICE_TABS`), `src/Ui/Queries.php` (`comingIn()`), views `item` and `item_bar` (new), `src/Ui/Controller/StockOpsController.php` and
view `stock_ops` (the item carried into a new record), `src/Ui/Controller/PurchaseOrdersController.php` (`newPage` reads `pick_si`),
`src/Ui/Words.php` (`ITEM`, `COUNTS item_*`, `STOCK_OPS for_item`, the new groups `ITEM_SELLS` and `MOVE_KIND` with their tones; `CARD change`
removed), `public/ui/assets/app.css` (the "item-stock-first" block).

**IV1. The head.** `div.doc-head` around the statement: the name as the heading, the status block (a 32 px solid chip in `.ph-meta`) and one
identity line after it: the CW number, the brand, the kind of nicotine, and for the people who may see suppliers (`suppliers.view`) the main
supply ("box of 10 from Prime Vape Supply": the preferred supplier item in use, from a supplier not switched off). The status: joined into
another product (navy), not sold any more (its product card; navy), not for sale (the stock rule `stopped`; red), blocked (its product card;
red), selling (matched on a store, on sale or its state not known; green), else not on sale yet (grey). The old "(CW-000123)" after the name
went (the name alone is the heading; `MatchingWordsTest` and `BuyingWordsTest` expect it so now); the page's one sentence stays, as on the
other redesigned pages.

**IV2. The actions, in the head at its right (`item_bar`, the shared `.doc-actions` and More).** Only what the person may use, none on an
item joined into another (its stock and orders moved there). **Count it** (`doc.CNT.post`): the count board's own form posted to the count
route as it is (`POST /ui/stock/counts`: csrf, a FormOnce key, the board's first warehouse, `mode=ticked`, `pick_<item>`): a count sheet of
this item, one however often it is pressed; every check of the route stays. **Move stock** (`doc.TRF.post`): `/ui/stock/transfers?item=<id>#new`,
the transfer's new form open and naming the item (a hidden `item`); "Start" makes the draft as before and its page opens with the item's CW
number in the add box (`add=CW-…`; only a CW number is put there; an item not there or joined away is not carried; the FormOnce request
names the item). **Order more** (`doc.PO.post`): the new order's page with the main supplier chosen and its box in the product box
(`/ui/purchasing/orders/new?supplier=&pick_si=&q=`: `newPage` now reads `pick_si` beside `pick_sku`, checked by `picked()`: this supplier's,
in use, its item not joined away), so Add adds that box; nothing is written by opening it (PX1). With no main supply: the item alone
(`pick_sku`), the supplier to choose. **More**: Book stock in, Take stock out, Correct the stock (each kind's new form with the item, as Move
stock), Reorder settings (`reorder.view`). ONE main action (DS5): Order more, else Count it, else Move stock.

**IV3. The stock strip (`section.doc-progress.item-strip`, the shared progress strip).** The sellable warehouses' sums, as the page added them
before. On the shelf (`on_hand`; under it "counted <day>" or "never counted": the latest count of its stock). Held for orders (allocated +
held; under it "N sold, waiting to ship" and "N reserved, not paid", each the link to Stock › Reservations the warehouse table's total row
had, which now shows plain figures). Free to sell (`available` as everywhere: on_hand + incoming − allocated − held, PJ1; "includes N on its
way" when units of a final supplier invoice are on their way). Coming in (the units still to come on the open confirmed orders,
`Queries::comingIn`: PurchaseOrders::onOrder's sum, per order; under it the first one due, its number a link for `purchasing.view`, and
"due <day>" when it has an expected date). Sells a week (only when the reorder engine has a sales rate for it, `reorder_demand.rate`, central
units a day: × 7 rounded half up, "under 1" for less than half; "lasts about N weeks" in whole weeks of the free stock, "under a week",
"about 1 week", "over a year" from 52 weeks, nothing when nothing sells or nothing is free; integer arithmetic as the engine's). The
per-warehouse table (its "?" help and the totals) is kept in a fold under the strip, "Each warehouse".

**IV4. Recent movements.** The same 30 rows (`Queries::ledgerOf`), as a board (`.doc-board`, `table.doc-list`): when; what, a solid cell
(`td.doc-st`) in the colour of its kind (`Words::TONE['MOVE_KIND']`: in green, a sale blue, a count or correction purple, out amber, a write-off
red, a reservation's own steps grey, a join's move navy) with a short word (`MOVE_KIND`; the bucket under it when it is not the shelf);
the document (its record's link and reason, as before, or its reference with the full movement words); the warehouse only when the rows
come from more than one; who; the units with their sign (+20, −4) in green or red; what the bucket held after. "All movements" leads to
Stock › Movements for this item (`q=<CW number>`, `figure=all`: every bucket, as the page's rows).

**IV5. Where it sells.** One solid chip per store, in the owner's order (`SimpleMatchController::stores`), from By Item's own read of the
item's cells (`Queries::productCells`): on sale (matched there and its website state, as `SiteState` reads it and not too old, says
Published), "matched, Draft" (the store's own word when it says it is not on sale), matched (its state not known), on hold (every matched
variant there quarantined), waiting for a second OK, suggested, not linked. No store set up: one line says so.

**IV6. The tabs.** Details (the product card with its rules, suggestions, confirmation and "Edit details", which was "Change the product
card"; then what the matching knows), Barcodes (2), Suppliers and packs (the suppliers block for `suppliers.view`, the family and packs box),
Store matching (the website products matched to it, the selling mode and its switch), History (the product card's changes, a list now, not a
fold in the card). The ONE tabs component (DS2: `nav.tabs` > `a.tab[aria-current]`, a count as `span.count`), written in the view (`nav.tabs.
item-tabs`: the section's tab bar keeps the plain `tabs`). The shared tab partial (`page_frame`, with main's CV13) is used as it is, not
changed here: it draws the section's tabs (Products › All products) under the statement. Rebased onto main `b3c7829` (CV13-CV14): the open
tab of the item's row has no link either (CV13; `tests/Support/CurrentTabs` and the template lint pass), so a click on it never reloads the
page; the item page has no form that keeps typed values over a link (CV14's `data-unsaved` pages are the editors).

**IV7. Which tab opens, without a script.** The tabs are plain links (`?tab=<key>#it-tabs`; the open one none, CV13). The page draws
every part and opens one (`.it-panel.open`; the others `display: none`): the address's `tab`; else the tab of the change a redirect's
notice names (`NOTICE_TABS`: a barcode's, the selling mode's, the family's), so every redirect of before still lands where the change was
made, with no address changed; after a refused form (the page drawn again for its POST) the form's own tab, read from its address. A
`#fragment` inside a closed part opens that part instead (CSS `:target` and `:has`), so the old anchors (`#selling-mode`, `#groups`,
`#barcodes`, `#card`) still work.

**IV8. Look-only staff see no edit control, as before.** Every form keeps its permission test; the panels hold the same forms; the actions bar
shows nothing to someone who may use none of them.

**IV9. Phone (`IT_Phone`).** The strip two figures a row (a fifth across the row); the movements' rows are cards with their solid cell; the
chips wrap. The actions are a bar at the bottom of the screen in the tab bar's place (like `.doc-bar`), their buttons side by side, More
opening upwards; the page keeps room for it. 44 px or more for every target; nothing scrolls sideways (the tab row scrolls inside itself).

**IV10. Kept.** Every edit rule, permission, version check, FormOnce and CSRF of the card, barcodes, family, selling mode and the routes
the actions use; the meaning of available, allocated and held; the merged-into, joined-here and duplicate notes and the error line at the top.
`CountsScreensTest`'s "Stock last counted", `ReservationsScreenTest`'s two reservation links and `UiReviewFlowTest`'s "Stock" table read the
same things where they are now.

**IV11. Words.** New: `ITEM` (the head, the actions, the strip, the movements' board, where it sells, the tabs), `ITEM_SELLS`, `MOVE_KIND`
(+ `TONE`), `COUNTS item_count_it`, `item_counted`, `item_never` (in COUNTS: "count" is only for shelf counts, correction b, and these are
shelf counts), `STOCK_OPS for_item`. `ITEM movements` is "Recent movements". `CARD change` went (Details says "Edit details").

**IV12. Tests.** Red first: `ItemPageScreensTest` (new) failed 7 of 7 on `5c070f8`. It covers the head and who sees which action (a viewer,
a buyer, the stock controller), Count it through the count route (one sheet twice, no token refused), Move stock into the draft's add box (a
missing or joined item not carried, only a CW number in the box), Order more into the new order's page and its Add, the status blocks, the
strip's figures and links (three orders, the first due; a viewer sees no link), every "Sells a week" case, the movements' cells and the way
to all of them, each store's chip, the tabs' links, counts, panels and forms, the tab after a change, a refusal and a notice, and the look-only
page. `ItemPageUnitTest` (new): the weekly arithmetic, every movement's short word and colour, the stores' states, the tabs and notices, the
CSS and markup of the design. `UiTemplatesTest` lints `item_bar` with the matching pages. Not seen in a real browser.

## Waiting for you: the Codex review of c5780dc and the counts builder's two points (branch `inbox-fixes`, 29 Oct 2026; AV15-AV19)

Codex reviewed `c5780dc` (AV1-AV14): no HIGH, two MEDIUM, two LOW (`runs/apone_codex_review.txt`); the counts builder reported two more
(the open row, the unsaved guard). Fixed from main `e15fe51`, each with its failing test first (`runs/apone_fix_red.log`).

**AV15. A page of count differences is a page the person may answer (MEDIUM).** The inbox took the Differences page's rows (a page, newest
first) and then dropped those the person may not clear: with a second person asked for every difference (`review_rule` all), the person's own
50 newest differences hid an older one by someone else, and the badge said 1 while the inbox showed nothing. `CountReviews::open()` now
takes `$mayClear` (a staff id) and keeps, in SQL, only the rows that person may clear (`mayClear()`: `refusal()`'s second-person rule, for a
sheet line and for a review the count engine opened about one; a flag about a count's time is nobody's own), so the limit applies to what
they may answer; the inbox asks for it (`CountsController::differences($ctx, null, true)`), the Differences page does not (it lists every
row with its reason). `openCount()` (the badge) uses the same condition, now for the engine's reviews too: it counted every one of them,
also the ones about the person's own count that someone else must clear.

**AV16. The inbox offers what each kind's route lets the person send (MEDIUM).** A person given the OK of documents (`documents.approve`)
without their check (`documents.review`, on Roles and permissions) saw a blocking OK in the inbox, and sending it was refused (403): both
routes of a document's answer check `documents.review`. The documents kind is now for `documents.review`, `suppliers.approve` and
`company.confirm` (the permissions of its three routes; `InboxController::PERMS`, the tab's), a task is listed only when the route of its
answers lets the person in (`TASK_ROUTE_PERMS` by its subject) as well as when the service would not refuse it, and the badge counts the
documents' checks only for who holds `documents.review` (the suppliers' and the company's were counted by their own permissions already).
The other kinds' permissions were already their routes'.

**AV17. An answer to a record's check says what its page says (LOW).** `ReviewsController::decide` led the inbox to `words=record` for
every type, and an order's or a delivery's check gives `approved_review`, which only their pages' words have: no notice was shown. The
inbox now gets the words of the page the answer would have led to (`po` PO_NOTICE, `receipt` RECEIPT_NOTICE, `stock` STOCK_NOTICE then
RECORD_NOTICE, `handover`, `invoice`, `return` likewise, else `record`), read in that order (`InboxController::notice()`).

**AV18. A flag about a count's time shows no counted figure (LOW).** `ship_near_count` and `unship_near_count` have no counted quantity;
the record showed "Counted 0". The fact is left out when there is none, as on Differences.

**AV19. The open row is no link; what is typed is guarded.** The open record's row is the page shown: it has no href now (a click reloaded
the page and lost a note typed in the answer), as a tab of the page shown (CV13); `tests/Support/CurrentTabs` checks it on every page
(`.ap-row` with `aria-current`). The answer form and the folds' forms carry `data-unsaved` (main's guard, CV14: a link that leaves the
page while something is typed asks first), and a refused answer comes back with its form marked as not saved (`data-dirty`).
`UiTemplatesTest` lists the inbox's record among the pages whose forms keep typed values.

Tests (`ApprovalsInboxScreensTest`): a count difference of someone else behind 51 of the person's own (the list, its title, the badge; and
the other counter's page of 50 with "The first 50 are shown" and the count of 51); the OK of a document given to two jobs without the
check (goods in: 403 from the inbox, no tab; a stock controller: not listed, not counted; a reviewer: listed and counted); a purchase
order's check answered in the inbox shows the order page's notice; a flag about a count's time has no "Counted"; the open row has no link
and the forms carry `data-unsaved`. Not seen in a real browser.

## The item page: the Codex review of e15fe51 (`runs/itone_codex_review.txt`), three MEDIUM and one LOW, each shown failing first (branch `item-fixes`, 29 Oct 2026; IV13-IV16)

The coordinator checked e15fe51 on staging in Chrome (desktop): it matches the design. Fixed from main `e15fe51` in `/root/cw-itone` (rebased
onto `5b8420a`, AV15-AV19); red first:
`runs/itone_fix_red.log`.

**IV13. A tab link no longer throws typed values away (MEDIUM 1).** A barcode typed in Barcodes, items per scan, a removal's reason, the
selling mode's reason and threshold, a family's name were lost by a click on another tab (a plain link: the page reloads). Every form of the
page that keeps typed values now carries main's guard (`data-unsaved="1"`, its words `OP_FINAL unsaved`), so main's link guard (CV14) asks
first, in the page, and the same link pressed again goes on; every form of the page that leaves it (Count it, "Use this", the card's
confirmation) carries `data-leaves="1"`, so it asks first when another form holds typed values. The card's confirmation is guarded only when
it draws its tick box. The tabs stay plain links (never a `#fragment`, which the guard lets through). `UiTemplatesTest` lists `item` and
`item_groups` with the editors.

**IV14. "Order more" keeps its box for a long name (MEDIUM 2).** The link carried the box's words in `q`; `newPage` cuts `q` at 255
characters, so for a 255-character name (with its CW number and pack after it) `picked()` no longer knew the choice and the box lost it (Add
then searched the words). The link now carries the pick alone (`supplier`, `pick_si`; `pick_sku` without a main supply), and `newPage` names
a pick from the address by its own words (`pickChoice()`, split out of `picked()`: this supplier's box, in use, its item not joined away; else
nothing, and the address's words stay as typed). "+ Add new supplier" coming back works as before (its `q` is the pick's own words too).

**IV15. A retried "Start" replays after its item is joined (MEDIUM 3).** FormOnce compared the request with the item only when the item could
still be carried (`itemOf()`), so the same form sent again after the item was joined into another was "another request" (422
`idempotency_key_reused`) instead of the first send's redirect. The request is now the item as sent; whether it is carried (`add=`) is decided
once, inside the effect. The same key with another item is still refused.

**IV16. A #fragment keeps the tabs in step, without the script (LOW).** An old link into a part (`#barcodes`, `#card`) shows that part
(CSS `:target`), but the open tab stayed marked and, being the open tab, had no link (CV13): no way back to it without the script. Each tab now
names its part (`data-tab`); the open tab has a hidden twin right after it (`a.tab.tab-back`, a link to `?tab=<open>`, never current). When a
fragment shows another part, CSS shows that part's tab as open, hides the open tab and shows its twin in its place. `UiTemplatesTest` lets
the twin (item page only, never current) hold its link; `CurrentTabs` passes (the twin is not current).

## Home and a shorter menu (branch `home-menu`, 29 Oct 2026; HV1-HV8)

The owner approved the Home screens of the canvas "CW Daily Screens" on 29 Oct 2026 (relayed by the coordinator with the static mockups
`HM_Home` and `HM_Phone`): Home is the list of jobs waiting for the person, biggest first, plus four figures; the menu keeps the daily pages in
front and the rest under More. Built from main `5b8420a` in `/root/cw-hmone`, rebased on `67ba18e` (IV13-IV16). Layout, words and navigation
only: no route, permission, service rule, form, FormOnce, CSRF or migration changed; every page keeps its address. Red first:
`runs/hmone_red.log` (21 failures and errors on `5b8420a`). Code: `src/Ui/Sections.php` (the map, `DAILY`, `MORE`, `PHONE`, `ICON`, `frame()`),
`src/Ui/Controller/DashboardController.php`, `src/Ui/DashboardTiles.php`, `src/Ui/Context.php`, `src/Ui/View.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php` (`SECTION`,
`SECTION_DESC`, `NAV`, `MENU_HELP`, `HOME`, `TILE`, `UI bell`), views `layout`, `page_frame`, `home`, `cards`, `home_find`, `bell` (new),
`matching_coverage` (new, from the removed `matching_progress`), `mapping_overview`; `public/ui/assets/app.css`, `icons.svg`.

**HV1. Home (HM_Home, HM_Phone).** Top to bottom: today's date as the eyebrow, "Good morning, <first name>" (afternoon from noon, evening from
6 pm, London time; the first word of the person's name) and ONE Find box on its right (the product search, `catalogue.view`; on a phone under
the greeting); "Waiting for you": the existing task list of `Ui\HomeTasks` (the same cards, counts, permissions and order, RANK: what holds
others up first) as rows: a 52 px square with the number in the task's colour (its tone: amber needs a look, red blocked, purple waiting for
someone, blue, grey), the task's name, ONE plain line (the card's `text`) and ONE button; the first job's button is the page's main action
(magenta), the others plain. A spot check shows "answered/of" (0/20); a task with no number shows "!", and a screen reader hears the number
with its unit ("25 to confirm") or the task's state ("Needs you"). The notes (no job) follow under "Good to know", quieter (the tint, not the
fill), their buttons plain; the staff and rule changes to look at keep their lines under the row (the security review's Y45: the reviewer

The mockup's figures (orders sent today, out of stock, coming in this week, oversold today) are not built: the brief asks for existing ones.
