## Stock moves and hand-overs on the approved patterns (wave `w8`, branch `wave-w8`, 29 Oct 2026; W8.1-W8.12)

The owner's word of 29 Oct 2026 ("all design convert our new claude suggested design"), relayed by the coordinator as wave w8: the stock
records (Stock In, Stock Out, Adjustments, Transfers, Releases), Repack, the hand-overs with their customers and balances, Reservations,
Movements, the Overview and the balance owed to another account, each on the pattern the approved canvases show (`Main.dc.html`, `GI_List`,
`CT_Board`, `PO_View`, `PI_View`, `PI_New`, `TP_Report`). Built from main `67ba18e` (OV, DS1-DS6, CV13-CV14, GV11, IV) in `/root/cw-w8`.
Layout and words only: no migration, no route, no permission, no service rule changed; every page keeps its address and every form posts
what and where it did. The receiving pages, `Sections`, the home page and the layout (the menu build's) are not touched.

**W8.1. The lists are boards (pattern 1).** Stock In/Out, Adjustments, Transfers, Releases (`stock_ops`), Hand-overs (`handovers`), the
hand-over customers (`handover_customers`), Repack (`repacks`) and Reservations (`stock_reservations`): one search and one Show row
(`.tb-state`), Clear and Export at the right; each group a coloured heading with its count (`div.grp-block.doc-group.<tone>`) over a white card
with the group's colour on its 6 px left edge (`div.table-wrap.doc-board`), the status cell filled with it (`td.c-status.doc-st`), the
number a `row-link` (the row opens the record); "+ New …" stays the head's create button (Sections, unchanged) and is also the last row of
the Draft group (In use for the customers), both opening the page's new form (`#new`). The Filter pop-over, the "How it works" folds, the
"Next step" column (the status cell says it) and the group total rows went.

**W8.2. The Show menu is the filter the list already read.** No controller reads a new parameter: the stock records', hand-overs',
repack's and reservations' Show menu is their `state` select ("Every record not stopped" first, then every state, "Stopped before it was final"
among them); the stock records keep their warehouse beside it in the same row (their search does not find a warehouse); the customers'
Show row is the kind of customer and the tick "Show switched-off customers too" (as the orders' Show row holds "drafts"). What an old link
carries that the row does not show (`cancelled=1`, a customer's `counterparty=`) is kept by a hidden field, so a search keeps it.

**W8.3. The new forms (pattern 3's fields).** The create form stays the list page's drawer (`details.drawer#new`: no new route), its fields
in two columns (`fieldset.doc-grid`; `form.record fieldset.doc-grid` is two columns too, one on a phone). The hand-over's, customer's and
repack's fields, which drew a label and its control side by side, are each a `div.field` (one grid cell, its error under it); the stock
record's note spans both columns (`.doc-wide`). The drawers' forms guard typed values (`data-unsaved`, CV14).

**W8.4. A draft is the one-page form (pattern 3, PI_New), the one form of OV kept as it is.** Its creator's draft of a stock record or a
hand-over: the head (`div.doc-head`, the status block in the heading, More at the right with "Stop this draft" and a draft's PDF); its
details in two columns, still their own form (`POST …/details`, the same fields, data-unsaved); the add box over the products board
(`table.doc-lines`); then, inside the lines form, what making it final does and the totals on the right (`div.doc-foot`, `doc_totals`), and
the bar at the bottom: "Leave without saving" (`data-leave`, to the list), what it holds (`span.doc-bar-note`: units, amount), Save, the
record's final button. The OV form is unchanged: the same fields, the same two buttons in that order (Save first, so Enter saves), the final
one the main one, in `.actions.sticky` (now `div.actions.sticky.doc-bar`: the document bar's look); the add box and the files stay outside
it (the field budget of OV4 counts the lines form's fields), and a record too big for one form still saves page by page, then the final box.
The add box's "Add" is plain: one main button on the page.

**W8.5. A saved record is the record page (pattern 2, PO_View).** Any stock record or hand-over that is not its creator's draft: the head with
the status block and the action bar at its right (`stock_op_bar`, `handover_bar`): the one main action is the transfer note or release
invoice of a final record, a final hand-over's invoice once it prints (PH8; else it says why beside the company details' link); under More
the PDF of a record not final, "Take it back", "Cancel this record" (its reason opens under the bar), "Copy into a new draft"; then the
figures strip (products, units, value or total, date), the paper card (`article.doc-view`: the party beside the facts, the products, the
files on the left and the totals on the right), the history. The party: where the stock is ("Warehouse", a transfer's "From"), for a release
the account it is owed to (its link: that account on Balance owed, the room under it), for a hand-over the customer (its link, its kind
under it). The facts link what they name: the record it cancels or that cancelled it, what the customer owes. The "Kind" fact went (the
title names it), and so did the explaining paragraphs of "Take it back" and "Make it again" (one line in More each).

**W8.6. A hand-over customer is a record page too.** Its name with its status block; at the right "Change the details" (the main action: its
form opens under the bar, open again with what was typed when refused, data-unsaved) and More with "Switch this customer off" (or on); the
figures strip (owes us, hand-overs, the last one, the prices kept); the paper card (its kind, its name and address as its invoices print
them, beside its company and VAT numbers, VAT code, e-mail, phone, note, what it owes with its link, the last change); then its related
records as boards (`section.doc-related`): the prices it paid last and its latest hand-overs, their status cells filled.

**W8.7. The overview, the movements, the balances and the balance owed are reports (pattern 5, TP_Report).** The figures strip
(`section.doc-progress.rp-figs`, any number of figures in a row, two a row on a phone, a line under one) replaces the figure tiles (`.kpis`):
the overview's four; the movements' changes shown, units added, units taken away (the page's rows); the balances' "Owed to us in all",
handed over this month, customers who owe us; the balance owed's units held, released this month, the balance owed (every account added up).
The overview's toolbar holds the search, the warehouse and Show; the movements' the search, the warehouse, the kind and the figure. Their
boards keep their groups (out of stock / in stock; a day) as `doc-group` cards. The balances and the balance owed have one board of every
customer or account (its name leads to its part below; the customers' total under it), then each part at its own address (`#customer-<id>`,
`#account-<id>`, where a payment lands: unchanged) with its payment fold (its fields in two columns, data-unsaved) and its entries as a
board. The help footnotes went (no help paragraphs); the accountant's line stays under the balances' heading.

**W8.8. Repack.** A board by status like the others; a draft left by its maker is made final or stopped, one waiting taken back, from its
row's own small forms (`td.c-next`, which stays above the row's link: `table.doc-list td.c-next` has `z-index: 2`); the cancelling hint went
(a row opens its record, where it is cancelled).

**W8.9. Shared classes added (docs/dev.md).** `.rp-figs` (the figures strip of a report or a record), `.doc-related` (a record's or report's
related part), `.actions.sticky.doc-bar` (OV's bar in the document bar's look), `form.doc-details`, `.doc-lines-box`, `.doc-files`; the
Show row wraps (`.toolbar .tb-state`). The partials `stock_op_bar`, `handover_bar`, `customer_bar` (a record's action bar, as `po_bar`) and
`stock_op_files` (a stock record's files and their form).

**W8.10. Words.** New: `HANDOVER add_row`, `CUSTOMER group_one / group_many / add_row / prices_kept`, `BALANCE figures / fig_owed / fig_owing
/ customer / last_col / total`, `ACCOUNTS figures / units_word / account_col`, `STOCK_VIEW fig_moves / fig_in / fig_out`, `REPACK actions /
add_row`. Changed: `STOCK_OPS limit` and `HANDOVER limit` ("use Search or Show"), `HANDOVER any_state` ("Every hand-over not stopped": what the
list shows without a choice).

**W8.11. Controllers hand the templates what the patterns show, nothing more.** `StockOpsController::page()` the party and facts (`party()`,
`facts()` with links), the products, the totals' rows; `HandoversController::page()` the same, `customers()` the groups, `customer()` the paper
card and the last hand-over, `balances()` the figures; `OtherAccountsController::index()` the figures; `StockController::movements()` the
figures; `RepackController::index()` the groups. No query, rule or check changed.

**W8.12. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testTheStockPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` pins each page's pattern in its template (the board's
toolbar, groups, cards, status cells and row link; the record's head, bar, strip, card; the document's foot, totals, history and files; the
form's grid, lines board, guard, bar with Leave first and Save before the final button; the report's strip and board; none of the old
pop-over, folds, tiles or facts list; every tag the new pieces open closed). `tests/Integration/UiKernel/StockPatternsScreensTest.php` checks
the served pages (a stock in and a transfer from the board to the draft to the record page, a hand-over and its customer and balances, the
reports). `StockScreensTest` and `ReservationsScreenTest` read the figures from the strip. Red first: `runs/w8_red.log` (5 failures on main).

## Home and a shorter menu: the Codex review of fcddc98 (`runs/hmone_codex_review.txt`), one MEDIUM, fixed test-first (branch `menu-more-fix`, 29 Oct 2026; HV9)

The coordinator checked fcddc98 on staging in Chrome at desktop width (Home and the menu look right); Codex found one MEDIUM. Red first:
`runs/hmone_more_red.log`.

**HV9. The tab row's More menu never leaves the screen (MEDIUM).** A buyer on Products › All Products at 375 px has All Products and More alone
in the row. The strip did not grow (`flex: 0 1 auto`), so More sat near the left edge, and its menu (up to 32rem wide) was put against More's
right edge: it ran off the left of the screen and cut Families and Multipacks, with or without the script (on a wide screen a short row sent
it under the sidebar the same way). Now the strip fills the row (`flex: 1 1 auto`), so More is always at the row's right end (also on a long
row, which scrolls inside the strip while More stays put), and the menu is placed against the whole row: the row is its positioned box
(`.tabs-row { position: relative }`, the More `details` static), its right edge is the row's and it is never wider than the row
(`max-width: min(32rem, 100%)`, `min-width: min(220px, 100%)`), at every width; the narrow-screen rule that put it against More is gone. The
row is the page's width inside its gutters, so the menu keeps the 16 px gutters on a phone. `UiUnitTest::testTheTabRowsMoreMenuStaysOnTheScreen`
pins the rules.

## Suppliers and buying on the approved patterns (wave w9, branch `wave-w9`, 29 Oct 2026; W9.1-W9.14)

The owner's word of 29 Oct ("all design convert our new claude suggested design") for Purchasing's suppliers, returns, credit notes, the
invoice lists, Goods In's Arriving, Incidents and Duty register, and Reorder with its pages. Layout and words only: no route, permission,
migration, setting or service rule changed; every form posts what and where it did (FormOnce, versions, CSRF as before). Built on main's
shared parts (docs/dev.md "The approved design's shared classes", DS1-DS6, CV13-CV14, GV11, GV25, HV1-HV9) and, on main `b06e109`,
W8's (the figures strip `.doc-progress.rp-figs` with `.step-sub`, the related records `.doc-related`, the details forms `form.doc-details`, the
row action `td.c-next` above the row's link); no new CSS class.

**W9.1. One way to group a board.** `Html::groups($rows, [key => [tone, words]])` turns rows that carry their `group` key into the board's
groups in a fixed order, only those with rows (the three boards of main keep their own `boardGroups()`). Each list below builds its rows'
`group` in its controller (or, for the small settings lists, in its template) and draws the board of PV18: a coloured heading with its count
over a card with the 6 px edge, the status cell filled with its colour.

**W9.2. Suppliers is a board.** Groups by status in this order: waiting for a reviewer's OK, draft ("+ New supplier" at its end), can order,
stopped. One search (name, code, VAT number), one Show row: the status menu (every supplier or one status) with the two ticks it had
(background check due soon, approved by one person), Export and "+ New supplier" at the right (`OWN_TOOLBAR`). Home's links (`?status=draft`,
`?due=1`) still narrow it. "Approved alone" is the line under the status; an overdue check is the red date (`td.late`). The bank sentence
moved to the form (it is about what the form keeps).

**W9.3. A supplier is a record page with four tabs.** The head: its name, the status as the solid block, the action bar at the right
(`supplier_bar`): the next step in the accent ("Ask a reviewer to approve" / "Make it usable" for a draft or stopped supplier whose details are
complete; else "Start a new order" for one we order from), the rest under More (change the details, start an order, add a proof document,
stop ordering: each fold opens under the bar). Then the reviewer's or second person's boxes (unchanged), whether we can order (one line, with
what is missing), the figures strip (products, main supplier of, no price yet, the next background check), and the tabs (`nav.tabs.record-tabs`,
`?tab=`, the open one without href): Details (the paper card: the supplier's block beside its terms, the background check and duty stamps, then
the arrivals settings at `#arrivals` as before), Items and packs (the supplier's products as a board, `supplier_items_board`, shared with the
products page; "+ Add a product" at the end of the first group), Orders (its last 10 orders as a board), Invoices (its latest 10 invoices as the
invoices board's rows, `InvoicesController::listRow()`, now public; the whole list one link away; Items, Orders and Invoices are related records, `.doc-related`). A tab's rows are read only when it is open
(the Invoices tab adds one read of the existing `SupplierInvoices::list()` with its supplier filter, the only new read). Orders and Invoices
are drawn only for who reads them (`purchasing.view`, `invoices.view`). The history stays at the bottom.

**W9.4. A new supplier is one page.** The 27 fields in three sections of two columns (`fieldset.doc-grid`, one field a `div.doc-field`:
`supplier_field`): Details (name, code, legal name, company and VAT numbers, the country, the address, the contact, other contacts, notes), Terms
(payment terms and days, delivery and order days, smallest order, VAT code), Background check (checked on, by, next check, what was checked,
bought from abroad, the duty-stamp arrangement). The country is a picker of every ISO 3166-1 country by name (`Words::COUNTRY`, 249; the United
Kingdom first and chosen by default), which sends the same two-letter code the service checks (a saved code outside the list is kept as its own
choice). The bar at the bottom (`doc_bar`): "Leave without saving" and the one Save ("Save as draft" for a new one); typed values are guarded
(`data-unsaved`, and `data-dirty` when a refused form is drawn back). The same page changes a supplier. The help lines under the fields went
(the picker replaces the code hint; the error says "Choose the supplier's country from the list").

**W9.5. Returns is a board.** Groups: draft ("+ New return" at its end), waiting for an OK, final with the credit still to come, credited,
cancelled. One search (it finds the supplier too, so the supplier menu went; a `?supplier=` link still narrows it), one Show row (any status or
one, the tick for cancelled drafts). The new return's drawer holds the quick way from a delivery first, then the four fields in two columns.
The "How it works" fold went.

**W9.6. A return: its draft is one page, a final one a record page.** The head and its bar (`return_bar`: "Book the supplier's credit note" the
next step on a final return; under More: stop a draft, take back a request, cancel a final return) and the figures strip (units going back,
lines, claimed, credit) on both. The creator's draft: its details in two columns (their own form and button, as before), the lines board in its
own form (`#ret-lines`), the add row (an item, a claim), the files on the left and the claim on the right, and the bar at the bottom: "Leave
without saving", what making it final does, "Save the lines" (`form="ret-lines"`) and "Make the return final" (`form="ret-post"`, the form
that always posted it). The forms stay separate (not OV's one form: not in this brief); the leaving forms carry `data-leaves`, so a typed
line is said before a final or an add leaves it (CV14). A final return: the paper card (the supplier's block beside the facts, the lines, the
files and the claim), its credit notes as a board, its history.

**W9.7. Credit notes.** The list was already the board (PV18); its Draft group now ends with "+ New credit note" (the drawer), whose fields are
in two columns. Both kinds of paper keep the same words' keys (`INVOICE_KIND add_row`). A credit note's page is PV19's, unchanged.

**W9.8. To match, Not invoiced yet, Timed and Arriving are boards.** To match: the Show menu (to check, differences accepted) in place of its
two links, "Check these again" plain in the head's bar, the invoices grouped by their match, the claims under the status. Not invoiced yet: one
search and the supplier in the Show row, one group with the value waiting in its count; each row keeps its "Book its invoice" form (in `td.c-next`, above the row's link). Timed: could
not be made final (red, the reason under it), then waiting for its time. Arriving: late, being received (a receipt started), on the way; each
row keeps "Receive" or "Open its receipt". These lists have no search of their own today (To match, Timed, Arriving): none was added.

**W9.9. Incidents is a board.** The Show row (open, dealt with, nothing needed or all; the kind), the incidents grouped by state, each row the
problem with where the items are, its state filled, the delivery line it came from, who found it; an open one closes from its row's fold (the

**W9.10. The duty register is a report.** Export at the head's right, the alarm or note as before, the figures strip (delivery lines with what
the register lists, held unstamped, taken in on a declaration, the day the held place must be empty), one search and the Show row (the dates,
the supplier, the stamp, the delivery's state), then the register's lines as a board with the stamp filled with its colour, the unstamped stock
and where it is, and what was taken in on a declaration (its warning to count them kept).

**W9.11. What to buy: the suggestion list first, ONE "Create draft orders", the sales data's upkeep under More.** The head's bar holds only
More: the download, "Sales data and settings" (what is loaded per website, when the demand was worked out, Work out again, Work out sales

and the Show row (to buy or every product, the two ticks; the brand, the main supplier, the stock to use), the suggestions grouped will run out,

The draft form carries what it did (`row_count` first, FormOnce, the filters) and now `data-unsaved` (a typed pack count is said before a link
leaves).

**W9.12. Reorder's other pages are reports.** Brands, Days left out, Suppliers, Low-stock warnings and Sales history: the figures strip, then
the board(s) with the coloured edge; a brand's or a supplier's change form in two columns at `#change` (Leave, Save); the days to add in two
columns; the periods grouped left out and used again; low-stock grouped below the safety stock and every other, its two buttons in the bar at
the bottom (keep each website's own, then use the safety stock: the main one), "Work out again" under More; each website's sales a group
(amber while products are unmatched). Their help paragraphs went; the figures say the normal days.

**W9.13. Not done here, said here.** No page moved in the menu (Sections unchanged). Proposed for the owner: Reorder's Brands, Days left out,
Sales history, Suppliers and Low-stock warnings are set-up pages and could go under Purchasing's More (they are Reorder's segments today); so
could Invoices › Timed and Goods In › Duty register. A search box on To match, Timed and Arriving (a filter the lists do not have) and a figures
strip on a credit note's page (PV19) are left for a later step. Not seen in a real browser here: check the pages at 375 px and 1,280 px.

**W9.14. Tests.** Red first (`runs/w9_red.log`: main `fcddc98` with the new tests). `UiTemplatesTest::testTheBuyingPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns`
(each template's pattern parts, no old toolbar pieces, the supplier form's 27 fields in three sections and the country picker, ONE "Create draft

## Stock moves and hand-overs: the Codex review of 589351d (`runs/w8_codex_review.txt`), two LOW (branch `w8-fixes`, 30 Oct 2026; W8.13-W8.14)

**W8.13. The stock boards' "+ New" is back in the head (LOW).** The five stock boards (Stock In, Stock Out, Adjustments, Transfers,
Releases) draw their own toolbar (`Context::OWN_TOOLBAR`), so the layout hands their create button to the page as `newActions` and draws
none; w8 took the toolbar's split button away and drew nothing in its place, so a person who may make one saw no "+ New" at the top (only the
last row of the Draft group). The head now draws it through its `side` (the same `split` partial as every other page's head). The drawer
and the Draft group's last row are unchanged. `StockPatternsScreensTest` pins the head's button on Stock In.

**W8.14. A customer's figures say when they reach the list's limit (LOW).** The customer's page counts the hand-overs and kept prices it
lists, and those lists stop at `Handovers::LIST_LIMIT` (200) and `Counterparties::PRICE_LIMIT` (500). At the limit the figure now reads
"200+" / "500+" instead of looking like the whole total. The lists and their limits are unchanged.

## The Sales pages on the approved patterns (wave `w10`, branch `wave-w10`, 30 Oct 2026; W10.1-W10.11)

The owner's word of 29 Oct 2026 ("all design convert our new claude suggested design"), relayed by the coordinator as wave w10: Store orders,
an order, Dispatch, Returns and Reports › Sales by Store, each on the pattern the approved canvases show (`Main.dc.html`, `GI_List`, `CT_Board`,
`PO_View`, `TP_Report`). Built from main `b06e109` (W8's shared classes, DS1-DS6, CV13-CV14, GV11, GV25, HV1-HV9) in `/root/cw-w10`. Layout and
words only: no migration, route, permission, setting, query or service rule changed; every page keeps its address, its parameters and its CSV,
and none posts anything. `Sections` is not touched (no move is needed: Sales keeps its three tabs, Sales by Store stays under Reports, as
`TP_Report`'s menu shows it). Wave w9's pages (suppliers, supplier returns, credit notes, reorder, arriving, incidents, duty) are not touched.

**W10.1. Store orders is a board (pattern 1).** The page's orders are grouped by state, in the reservations board's groups and words
(`ReservationViews::GROUPS`, `RESV_GROUP`: reserved now, sold waiting to ship, sold and dealt with, freed, ran out), newest first inside each
group; each group a coloured heading with its count ("5 on this page", `RESV group_many`: the list is paged) over a card with the 6 px edge; the
status cell, right after the order, filled (`RESV_CHIP`); the order's number a `row-link`. The groups are drawn from the page the list already
reads (the same key paging, the same page size), so an older page may hold rows of an earlier group, as on Reservations (W8.1). The board
heading, its "newest first, N on this page" note and the foot paragraph went.

**W10.2. Its Show row is the filter the list already read.** The Filter pop-over is gone: the Show menu is the `state` select ("Every state"
and the seven states), and the way in and the days typed (`from`, `to`) sit in the same row (`label.tb-day`: the word beside its box), with
one Show button; Clear and Export (a download) at the right; the hidden `period` keeps "Any time" through a choice (as before). The period line
under the store selector stays (it says the days and links to the other choice). **No search box**: the list has no text filter, and adding one
(an order reference, a product) would be a new query and a new parameter, a behaviour change outside this wave; reported to the coordinator as
the one part of pattern 1 these boards lack (Dispatch and Returns too).

**W10.3. An order is a record page (pattern 2, PO_View).** The head: "Order V2003" with the status block (`RESV_CHIP`, the board's word) and
at its right the bar (`sales_order_bar`): "See the reservation" (the stock CW keeps for it), plain: the order is read only, so the page has no
main action. The strip (`rp-figs`): one figure per state its sold units are in, the number of units in it ("Sent to the customer 1 ·
Returned by the customer 1"; `RESV_UNIT` words, from the `by_state` counts the row already carries), PO_View's progress for an order. The
paper card (`article.doc-view`): the store as its party (its name opens the list at that store) beside the facts (reference, state, placed,
paid, how it came in, waiting since payment with "late", store variants, warehouse units: the facts it listed, less the store and the
reservation link, which moved to the party and the bar); then the sold units as the card's lines (`table.doc-lines`, the status cell filled,
their pager inside the card). Then the history (`section.doc-related`): each unit's stock changes a group (`doc-group info`, its unit and item
as the heading, folding) over its ledger board; the explaining lines over the units and the steps went (the headings say it).

**W10.4. Dispatch is a board.** The four lists are its Show menu (a GET form of `show`, the parameter the tab links carried; the store kept by a
hidden field; Show without a script), not a row of tabs. The five figure tiles are the strip (`rp-figs`, their lines under them). Waiting to
ship is grouped Late, then On time (the status cell, `DISPATCH_CHIP`), oldest first in each; a sent list is a group a UK day of sending
(`Html::day`), newest first, its status cell what the order is now (to ship, or dealt with: `RESV_CHIP`); sending undone is one group, its
status cell what the unit is now (`RESV_UNIT`). The undone list's line on units not linked stays (it says why a sending is missing). The board
headings, notes and the foot paragraph went.

**W10.5. Returns is a board; its record is the order.** There is no return record: the owner's answer to Q12 (8 Oct 2026) keeps returns on the
store's own return page, so a unit's order (pattern 2, W10.3) is the record its row opens, and the brief's "1, 2" for Returns is the board plus
that page. The Show menu is the `kind` select (returned, cancelled or both); the units are grouped by what happened (returned, then cancelled;
`RESV_UNIT`'s tones), newest order first in each; the status cell says whether the unit is back on sale (`SALE_RESTOCK`, filled); the "What
happened" column went (the group says it). The item heads the row (a link to the item) and the order is its own link, so the row has no
`row-link` (two places to open). The one figure (units waiting for a recount) is the strip.

**W10.6. Sales by Store is a report (pattern 5, TP_Report).** One Show row: the days (`period`), From / To (`label.tb-day`), the store (all or
one) and Show; the file at the right ("Download as CSV", a download). The days and when the figures were last brought up to date under it,
muted, as TP_Report's "as of" line. The strip: the days' totals (orders, units sold, sent, cancelled, returned). Then two boards
(`section.doc-related`, the blue edge): By store, the total row under it (`tr.grp-foot`, as W8's balances), and Day by day. The note under the
boards (what a unit is, which day a figure belongs to) is the page's "?" (`HELP sales_by_store`): no help paragraph.

**W10.7. One class added, one rule.** `label.tb-day` in a Show row (the word and its date box, as tall as the row's selects; on a phone each
takes a share of the row, 44 px high, never wider than the page), used by Store orders and Sales by Store; `.doc-board > p` (a card holding a
line instead of a table: a unit with no stock change). The partial `sales_order_bar`. Everything else is W8's and the pi-design block's.
One shared rule mended: on a phone (a list 640 px or narrower) the stacked list's generic `table.stack td { background: none }` outranked the
status cell's fill (`td.doc-st`), so the cell's white words sat on the white card and the state did not show, on these boards and on every
board before them (GV23 found it on Goods in and drew its cells there by hand). `table.stack td.doc-st:not(.gi-duty)` now keeps the fill on a
phone, the "pill-like block" docs/dev.md describes; Goods in's duty cell, deliberately a white field there (GV23), is left as it is. CSS
only; it changes every board's look on a phone (from no visible state to the coloured pill), which is why it is named here.

**W10.8. Words.** Changed: `SALE from / to` ("From", "To": they sit beside their boxes in the Show row now). New: `SALE_ORDER figures` (the
strip's name), `REPORTS sales_figures`, `HELP sales_by_store` (the note, worded without "count", which the words test keeps for shelf counts).
Gone with the parts they named: `SALE board / board_note / on_page_one / on_page_many / foot`, `SALE_ORDER f_kept / units_text / steps_text`,
`DISPATCH board_waiting / board_sent / foot`, `SALE_RETURNS board / board_note / foot`, `REPORTS sales_note`. The groups' counts are
`RESV group_one / group_many` ("on this page").

**W10.9. Controllers hand the templates the groups, nothing more.** `SalesController::index()` the groups (the row's `group`), `show()` the
party, the facts as the card's, the strip; `DispatchController` each list's groups (`id`, `name`, `tone`, `rows`), the Show menu's options and
the store; `SalesReturnsController::index()` the groups (the row's `kind`). The CSVs, the queries, the paging keys and every setting are as
they were.

**W10.10. What a reviewer should know.** A board groups the page it was given, so the first group on page two may be one page one also had;
the order of rows inside a group is the list's own. The Show menus are GET forms: a store chosen in the store selector travels as a hidden
`channel`; Dispatch's `show=waiting` (the form's value) reads as no `show` (the default), as before.

**W10.11. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testTheSalesPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` pins each page's pattern in its template (the board's Show
row, groups, toggles, cards, filled status cells and row links; the record's head, bar, strip, card, lines and history groups; the report's
Show row with its days, Download, strip, two boards and total row; none of the Filter pop-over, tiles, facts list, foot, tabs row, chips in a
row or POST form; every tag closed). `SalesScreensTest::testTheSalesPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` checks the pages as served (the groups and
their counts, a cell and a row link a row, each heading folding its own card, the Show row's fields and the choice shown, Dispatch's lists from
its GET form without a script, a group a day, the record's head, bar, strip, card and history). `ReportsScreenTest::testSalesByStoreOverAPeriod`
reads the strip, the two boards, the Show row's fields, the download and the "?". The existing sales tests read the board's order through
`onBoard()` (grouped, newest first in each), the row texts with the status cell after the order, the figures from the strip and the store from
the card's party. `UiUnitTest::testTheShowRowHoldsTheDaysTypedAtEveryWidth` pins the CSS. Red first: `runs/w10_red.log`.

## Sales: the Codex review of a260cba (`runs/w10_codex_review.txt`), one MEDIUM and one LOW (branch `wave-w10`, 30 Oct 2026; W10.12-W10.14)

Codex reviewed a260cba (read only); it found one MEDIUM and one LOW, both on a phone, and nothing in the Show rows, the grouping, the
controllers, the figures or the record page. The w8 review's fix (W8.13-W8.14, `509a74a`) came in first as its own commit. Layout only. Red
first: `runs/w10_fix_red.log`.

**W10.12. An order's unit status never lies over the item on a phone (MEDIUM).** The units became the card's lines (`doc-lines`), whose
phone card has three equal columns: the status cell went to the last third and kept its one line (`td.c-status { white-space: nowrap }`).
At 500 px a returned unit with a long name had "Returned by the customer" drawn over the name; before, the stacked list gave the status its
full width. Now, on a phone (container 640 px or less), `table.stack.doc-lines.sales-units` rows have two columns: the item the rest
(`minmax(0, 1fr)`), the status its own width up to half the card (`fit-content(50%)`), wrapping inside it (`white-space: normal`). Other
lines tables are unchanged. `UiUnitTest::testAnOrdersUnitStatusTakesItsOwnWidthOnAPhone` pins the rules.

**W10.13. A filled status cell's own label is readable on a phone (LOW).** W10's phone rule fills every board's status cell (except Goods
in's duty cell); a status cell that carries a `data-label` (Lines to place's "Status") also draws that word before its value, in the stacked
list's muted grey, so on the blue fill of an open line it was hard to read. Now that word takes the cell's white
(`table.stack td.doc-st:not(.gi-duty)[data-label]::before { color: inherit }`); the duty cell, a white field there, keeps its grey word.
`UiUnitTest::testAFilledStatusCellsLabelIsInTheCellsWhiteOnAPhone` pins it.

**W10.14. Stock In and the other stock boards: the head's "+ New" through a variable.** W8.13 handed the head its button as
`side: $partial('split', ['actions' => ...])`; the head lint (`UiTemplatesTest::testTheStatementsRawPartsAreOnlyHelperOutput`) cannot read
an array's `=>` inside a `$head` call, so it failed. The partial is now made before the head (`$split`) and passed as `side: $split`, the way
the record pages pass their bars. Same output.

## Suppliers and buying: the Codex review of a96ff5b (`runs/w9_codex_review.txt`), two MEDIUM and two LOW, each shown failing first (branch `wave-w9`, second commit, 30 Oct 2026; W9.15-W9.19)

Fixed on `3f95e53` (a96ff5b with W9.14's test lines) in `/root/cw-w9`, then rebased onto main `672fae9` (W10, W8.13-W8.14). Red first:
`runs/w9_fix_red.log` (the tip with the new tests and the two limit constants alone, so each test fails on what it checks). The owner's
word of 30 Oct ("strictly follow our design guidelines") holds: no new line, note, button or chip on any page; a cut figure is its shortest
form ("100+").

**W9.15. A typed value is never lost by another form of the page (MEDIUM 1).** On a return's draft, a line's quantity changed and then
"Save details" pressed sent the details alone, and the page came back with the line as it was, without a word: the details and the lines
forms kept their typed values (`data-unsaved`) but neither said so before it left (no `data-leaves`), and the add row's two forms and the
stop's reason were not guarded at all. Main's rule (CV14, IV13) now holds on every page of this wave: a POST form with a field to type in or
choose carries `data-unsaved="1"` in DOC's words (an upload is its own send, as main's files forms), and on a page with such a form and
another, every form carries `data-leaves="1"`, the toolbar's filter too, so the first press of another form says, in the page, that the
changes are not saved, and the same press again goes on without them. The pages: a return (its details, its lines, add an item, add a
claim, the stop's and the cancel's reasons; Make final, take back, Book the credit note, the files ask first), a supplier (the arrivals
settings, the stop's reason, the reviewer's and the second person's notes; the proof upload, Ask a reviewer, take back ask first), the
incidents (each close's note), the returns' and the credit notes' drawers, What to buy and Low-stock warnings (their filters ask first),
Days left out (each End asks first). Attributes only: no form posts anything else or anywhere else. `UiTemplatesTest` reads every branch
of these templates; `BuyingPatternsScreensTest` checks the pages as served.

**W9.16. The Items and packs tab draws at most `SuppliersController::ITEM_TAB_ROWS` (100) records (MEDIUM 2).** The tab read and drew every
pack record of the supplier (50,000 records, 50,000 rows in one page). It now reads the first 100 in the board's own group order (main
supplier, a backup supplier, no longer bought here; within a group by name and pack, as the board draws them), so every group above the
cut is whole and only the last one drawn is cut: its count reads "98+ products" (the shortest form, W8.14's "+"). The board head's "Open the
products" link is the way to every record. The products page and its CSV read every record in their order, unchanged
(`SupplierItemsController::rowsOf()` without a limit); the figures strip counts every record as before.

**W9.17. Sales history's "Loads" reads "100+" at its list's limit (LOW 1).** The figure counted the loads the page lists, and the list stops at
the newest 100 (`SalesHistoryController::LOADS`, the query's `LIMIT 100` named): with 150 loads it said 100. At the limit it now reads
"100+"; below it, the count. The list is unchanged.

**W9.18. The supplier form's Save sends what it sent before (LOW 2).** On the one-page form the Save came from `doc_bar`, which names every
button `action`, so a save also sent `action=save` (the controller ignored it, but the form no longer posted exactly what it did). `doc_bar`
now names a button and gives it its value only when its caller passes one; the supplier form passes none (its Save is unnamed, as before).
The order, invoice and delivery pages pass theirs, so their buttons are drawn exactly as before.

**W9.19. Tests.** Red first (`runs/w9_fix_red.log`, 6 of 6 fail). `UiTemplatesTest::testTheBuyingPagesGuardTypedValuesAndEveryFormThatLeavesAsksFirst`
(W9.15's rule over every template of the wave, with the count of guarded forms per page), `testTheSupplierFormsSaveIsUnnamedAndTheOtherBarsKeepTheirAction`
(W9.18); `BuyingPatternsScreensTest::testEveryFormThatKeepsTypedValuesIsGuardedAndEveryFormThatLeavesAsksFirst` (a return's draft with a
line, the final return, a supplier, the returns' and the credit notes' lists, as served), `testTheItemsTabDrawsTheFirstRowsAndItsCutGroupReadsWithAPlus`
(103 records: the tab's 100 with "98+", the products page's 103), `testTheLoadsFigureReadsWithAPlusAtTheListsLimit` (3, then 150 loads),
`testTheSupplierFormsSaveSendsItsFieldsAloneAsBefore` (new and change).

## The Products pages on the approved patterns (wave w11, branch `wave-w11`, 30 Oct 2026; W11.1-W11.11)

The owner's word of 29 Oct ("all design convert our new claude suggested design") for Products: All Products, Add Item, Families, Multipacks
(Pack items, Pack links) and Barcodes; and the owner's word of 30 Oct ("strictly follow our design guidelines"): each page has the mockup's
parts in the mockup's order and nothing more. Layout and words only: no route, permission, migration, setting or service rule changed; every
form posts what and where it did (FormOnce, versions, CSRF as before). Built on main's shared parts (PV18-PV20, DS1-DS6, CV13-CV14, AV1-AV19)
and W8's and W9's (`.rp-figs`, `form.doc-details`, `td.c-next` above the row's link, `Html::groups`); no new CSS class. The item page itself
is the itone build's (IV1-IV16), already on the approved pattern: unchanged.

**W11.1. All Products is a board (GI_List).** The page's products (still a page of `ItemCardList::PAGE`, most stock first) grouped by their
card: Blocked (red: a card whose confirmed rule blocks), Not confirmed yet (amber: not confirmed, or changed since), Confirmed (green), No card
yet (grey). The status cell says the card (Blocked, Not confirmed, Changed since it was confirmed, Confirmed, No card yet); a block's rules are
the muted line under the name (not a second "Blocked"), a warning and "Not sold any more" soft tags there, a flavour from a file a soft tag in
its cell. A card's group has the card's columns; the No card group has none, and, for the catalogue team, "Fill in the card" (`a.btn.sm` in
`td.c-next`, naming its product for a screen reader). The filters are plain inputs in the one Show row (the brief: "plain filter inputs and
one Clear link instead of removable filter chips"): the card (first choice "Every product"), the kind of product ("Any kind of product"), the
four ticks with their short words (Holds stock, Warning or blocked, Blocked, Not sold any more), one Show button; ONE Clear (`clear_filters`)
at the right takes every filter and the search off. The Filter pop-over, its count, the chips and the search's own clear mark are gone (their
CSS stays: other pages use it). The empty state of a search still clears the search alone, keeping the filters. The figures line and the
"Products" heading over the list are gone (the approved board has neither; the groups carry the counts); "Page n of m" is in the pager.

**W11.2. Add Item is the one-page form (PI_New).** The link to the items made by hand above the heading (the mockup's "Supplier invoices ›"),
no create button in the head (`side: ''`: the page is that button's form); the refusal and the "same item" warning first; then one form
(`form.doc-details.item-new#new`, `data-unsaved`): what the item is in two columns, name, brand and barcode first (then items per scan,
line, flavour, strength, nicotine type, form, volume, puffs); "Legal details" (the product card's confirmed fields: kind, ml, mg/ml, duty,
single-use, ECID, manufacturer, brand and flavour on the box) and "Buying details" (units in one box, the family, "discontinued / do not
reorder") each a closed fold that opens when something in it was typed or refused (a card's errors, an unknown or switched-off family); then
the bar at the bottom (`doc_bar`: "Leave without saving" back to All Products, "Add the item"). The bar's button is given no value, so
`doc_bar` draws it without a name (W9.18) and the form posts exactly the fields it did. The paragraph hints ("Only the name is needed…", "The legal and buying details…", what Add does, what
single-use means) are gone; the short hints in the labels stay.

**W11.3. The items made by hand are a list of their own (GI_List).** `GET /ui/items/new?show=all` (and `?show=waiting`, which already
existed) draw the board `items_by_hand` instead of the form: the head's "+ Add Item", one Show row (All of them / Only those waiting for a
check; Clear back to all), the items grouped by their check (Waiting for a check, Checked, No check asked), newest first in each (a page of
`HandMade::PER_PAGE`), a row opening the item, another person's check (note + "Checked: it is right", `btn sm`) in `td.c-next`, "+ Add an
item" at the end of the first group. Whether a second person checks is the head's muted line. The check's redirect
(`?notice=checked&show=waiting`) lands on this list; a refused check is answered with it too (it was the form page). The pager's links carry
`show=all` (the form page no longer lists).

**W11.4. Families is a board.** One search, one Show row (`off`: In use / In use and switched off, the same values the tick sent), Clear at
the right; the groups In use (green) and Switched off (navy); a row opens the family; "+ New family" at the end of In use opens the drawer,
its two fields in two columns (`form.doc-details`). The count line over the list is gone (the groups' counts).

**W11.5. A family is the record page (PO_View).** The link back to Families; its name with its status block and its bar at the head's right
(`family_bar`): in use, "Add items" (the pasted list, open at first while the family is empty or after a refused list) is the main action,
Rename and "Switch the family off" (risky) under More; switched off, "Switch the family on again" is the main action and Rename under More.
The figures strip: Items, Added, Last changed. The paper card: the family and its note beside its facts (State, Added by, Last changed by),
its items as the card's lines (tick and take out, each a link to its item), the pager under them. The lines "Added by …", the note paragraph
and "This family is switched off …" are gone (the facts and the status block say them). There is no History part: the family keeps no
history of its own beyond those two facts.

**W11.6. Pack items is a board.** One search, one Show row (`off`), Clear; the groups In use and Switched off; a row opens the pack item;
its single item (a link), what to check (soft tags, the variants that could take singles, the note) and its actions (Repack it, Switch
off / on) sit in `td.c-next` cells above the row's link; "+ Define a pack item" at the end of In use. The "Two ways of selling a pack" fold
and the rule's line are gone (no help fold on the approved board; the rule is on Settings).

**W11.7. Pack links is a board.** The variants matched with more than 1 unit a sale, grouped To check (amber: a pack item of that many
exists, or the item is a pack itself; the reasons soft tags) and Nothing to check (green); a row opens the variant's page (where its match is
changed); its item a link above the row's link. It has no filter of its own, so no toolbar.

**W11.8. Barcodes is an inbox (AP_Inbox).** The barcode search and one Show row (Waiting (n) / Decided); the list on the left grouped by why
the barcode waits (On another product red, Pack or single item? amber, Removed by a person blue), each row the barcode and the product whose
website product carries it, a link `?open=<id>` (keeping the Show and the search); the open one on the right (first on a phone): the reason
and its place ("1 of 3"), the barcode, its status block, the facts (`dl.doc-facts`), and ONE decision: the answers, the items per scan where
they matter, the note, "Save the decision" (`form="ap-answer"`), "Next: <barcode>". The first one opens unless `open` names another; a refused
decision opens its own record with the refusal in it. The decision posts where and what it did, and its redirect is unchanged (the first one
left opens).

**W11.9. Where the pages still differ from the mockups (kept on purpose, or for the later design-conformance build).** Shared, left for the
one design build (the coordinator's note of 30 Oct): the titles' case and full stop, the intro lines under the titles, "+ New" in the toolbar
row, the Show select with its button (the mockups show the choices alone). Kept on purpose: All Products' "?" (the rules about warnings and
blocks, the owner's request of 21 Oct), Import and Export in its toolbar, its pager; Barcodes' search (finding a scanned barcode is the page's
use; the mockup's inbox has none); the drawers of Families and Pack items (the forms of a board, W8's pattern); the family has no History part
(W11.5).

**W11.10. Typed values are guarded (W9.15's rule).** A POST form with a field to type or choose carries `data-unsaved` with DOC's words
(the check of an item made by hand, a new family, a family's rename, its pasted list and its ticked items, a new pack item, a barcode's
decision, Add Item), and on a page with one every form carries `data-leaves` (the toolbars, the switches): it says so first when another
form holds typed values. Nothing is sent differently.

**W11.11. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testTheProductPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` (the templates), `ProductPatternsScreensTest` (the pages as
served, shown failing on main first: `runs/w11_red.log`); `ItemCardScreensTest` (the All Products tests now pin the board, the plain filters
and the one Clear instead of the chips; the barcode review reads the open record), `ItemManagementScreensTest` (the list view, the family's
status block), `ItemManagementUnitTest` (the two new templates).

## Design conformance across every page (branch `ds-conform`, 30 Oct 2026; DC1-DC28)

The owner, 30 Oct 2026: "strictly follow our design guidelines". Codex compared every approved mockup (`cwdaily/*`, `cwdesign/*`) with main
`3f95e53` (`runs/dsaudit_findings.txt`): section A, the differences that come from shared code; section B, page by page. Section A is fixed
in the shared code, one place each, each with a pin that failed on main first; section B for the pages listed below. Where two approved
designs disagree the newer wins (`cwdaily/*` of 29 Oct over the `cwdesign/*` sidebars; HM_Home and HM_Phone for the shell; TP_Parts for
the parts). Layout and words only: no route, permission, posted field, service rule or safety message changed. Rebased on `672fae9` (w10).

**DC1. No sentence under a heading (audit A1).** `View::head` no longer draws the page's intro (`Words::PAGE_INTRO` keeps the words; `intro:`
still names the page). Kept, as the one muted line under the heading, only where it is the step's rule or a safety message said nowhere else
(`View::INTRO_KEPT`): the sign-in (what to type, the code app), the password's length, the sign-in set-up and its code, the bulk change's
"nothing is saved until you press the red button", the two previews' "nothing is saved yet", the two pending cancellations' "changes nothing
until it is final". Who may change a page a person can only look at (`look:`, a look-only `more:`, and `Words::INTRO_LOOK`: the four
read-only pages whose intro said it) is the "?" beside the heading (`Html::lookOnly`, `details.help.look-only`), not a line under it. A
claim-only return's intro was the only place that said no goods go back: its eyebrow's tag says so now (`RETURNS['claim_tag']`).

**DC2. The heading (A2, A3).** No full stop (the drawn `.stmt.stop::after` and its class are gone; a heading is its text). 26 px / 1.25,
no negative tracking; 24 px / 1.3 on the item page and the matching page (IT_Item, TP_Match; `.item-head`, `.match-head`); 22 px on a phone
(HM_Phone). The eyebrow is 12 px semi-bold with .08em tracking, the heading 2 px under it.

**DC3. A record's eyebrow is its list (A17).** `$head(back: [href, label])` draws the mockups' breadcrumb as the eyebrow: the list as an
accent link, then "›" (`p.ph-eyebrow.ph-back`). Used on the purchase order (view and draft), the supplier invoice (view and new), the item,
the count sheet and "Before it is final" (CT_Final: that heading, under the sheet's own name as its eyebrow). The separate `p.crumbs` above
them is gone. Goods in's delivery keeps its crumb: it carries the phone's Leave (GV24).

**DC4. "+ New" in the header, alone (A6, A7).** `Context::OWN_TOOLBAR` is gone: the purchase orders, suppliers, Goods in, stock records and
counts boards no longer take the create button into their toolbar; the header draws it at the title's right like every page (the stock boards'
W8.13 `side: $split` went with it; Counts keeps its "Open sheets (N)" as CT_Board draws). `Sections::frame` gives only the page's own create
action: no second More of the section's other "New …" (each is on its own list). The open groups keep their quiet "+ New …" last row.

**DC5. No buying-flow strip (A5).** The four-card flow strip on Purchasing is gone (`page_frame`, `Ui\FlowCounts`, `Words::FLOW`). The tab
rows are DC28's (a first step here kept the section's tab row and put six tabs' segments under its More; the owner's word of 30 Oct
replaced both).

**DC6. Sentence case (A4).** "Purchase orders", "Goods in", "All products", "Stock in", "Stock out", "Stock by store", "Sales by store",
"Low stock", "Stock value", "Slow stock", "Audit log", "Approval rules", "Store products", "By item", "New variants", "Add item": in the menu,
the tabs, the titles and every sentence that names them (one source, `Words`).

**DC7. The shell of HM_Home and HM_Phone (A8, A9).** The sidebar: the plain name (no CW tile), Home, Every day, More, each entry its words
only (no icons), a magenta 22 px count where something waits; no bell (the Approvals entry carries the inbox's count) and no find link (Home's
Find box finds); the person at the bottom keeps their account and Sign out (a function). The phone's top bar: the name and the person's
initials (`.appbar-me`, which open the menu where Sign out is); the menu button only where no bottom bar is (a page with a document or answer
bar: PI_New_Phone draws it there). The bottom bar is as before. The record pages' phone headers (back, number, status: GI_Phone, CT_Phone,
IT_Phone, AP_Phone) are not built here: each needs its page's own parts (DC25).

**DC8. The page's width (A11).** The work area 28 px / 32 px (`--gutter: 32px`), the column centred at 1,180 px (`--page-w`), Home's at 1,100.

**DC9. Tabs as TP_Parts draws them (A16).** From 700 px up a tab row wraps, 12 px by 14 px, the open tab's 3 px bar over the row's 1 px line;
on a phone it stays one row that scrolls inside itself (DS2's reason: a wrapped row of eight tabs is three lines on a phone).

**DC10. The toolbar (A12).** Search and Show 40 px, 14 px; the search takes the free width (`flex: 1 1 280px`), the muted "Show" beside its
choice (170 px). The Show button stays: without it the choice needs the script, and applying a choice by itself on change reloads the page
under a keyboard user's arrow keys (WCAG 3.2.2). The fields keep their darker edge (`--field`, 5.6:1): the mockups' #d9d0e1 is 1.4:1 on white
and fails WCAG 1.4.11 (`UiUnitTest::testTheDesignTokensMeetTheContrastTheyAreUsedFor`); for the owner to decide (DC25).

**DC11. One field (A13).** `input[type=datetime-local]` joins the shared field and its 16 px phone size; fields are 40 px as drawn, 44 px on a
phone or a touch screen.

**DC12. Boards (A14).** Group headings 16 px bold in their colour, the count 13 px medium; no chevron while open (the heading is still the fold's
button, `aria-expanded`), the chevron shows on a folded group so it is not lost; "+ Add …" rows are quiet text (no dashed edge); 12 px
semi-bold heads, 14 px cell sides, 48 px rows, the 170 px status cell (a phone card keeps its own).

**DC13. A phone's status cell keeps its fill (A10).** Main's W10 rule (`table.stack td.doc-st:not(.gi-duty)`) is the fix; no second copy.

**DC14. TP_Parts' parts (A15).** Chips have no 110 px minimum; All fine's edge `#9fd4bf`, the risky edge `#f1b9c2` (the tokens); More's menu
has no inset, 10 by 14 px rows with a divider, square rows in its 12 px corners, its soft shadow (`--shadow-menu`).

**DC15. The bar at the bottom and the totals (A17).** The dock 24 px above it, 14 px inside (12 on a phone), the softer shadow; a saved
document's totals are rows of its paper, not a card of their own (PO_View, PI_View); a new document's totals stay in their card (PI_New).

**DC16. Purchase orders (B).** Columns Order, Status, Supplier, Expected, Received, By, Total: By is who made it, their initials (`Html::initials`,
`.initials`), Supplier and Total in ink; the order's date and reference after its number on one line; an empty Expected or Received is "—"; the
quiet "+ New purchase order" row ends Waiting for approval, On the way and Draft. The statuses' words are the mockups' (Waiting for approval,
Part received, Received). Download, Show drafts too (goods in and the desk; it now also hides them again) and Clear are under the toolbar's one
More; the drafts strip went (its words are the item's). The same filters, CSV and draft rule as before (F305).

**DC17. Goods in (B).** Units, not Items (the column counts units); arrival times "Today 09:40" / "Yesterday 15:10" (`Html::near`); a checked
delivery's status cell says "Checked" or "Checked, 1 problem" (its group says ready to book in); the order or invoice after the number on
one line; Clear under the toolbar's More.

**DC18. From the stores (B).** The queues' Show is the board toolbar's (the muted word, its choice, its Show button); the row-count line went
(each group counts its rows; a cut list still says so); Lines to place's eyebrow is "Approvals · from the stores" and its Place is the small
button.

**DC19. Home on a phone (B).** A task row is the link (no button drawn; its words stay for a screen reader, the row takes the focus ring); no
figures section (HM_Phone has none).

**DC20. Counts (B).** The toolbar is search and Warehouse; how many the list takes ("List the next 50/100/200"), the plan's days (with the plan
as the item's line) and Clear are under its More; a row's code beside its name; never counted is "—".

**DC21. Supplier invoices (B).** "Due" and, once passed with money owed, "N days late" beside the date; Clear under the toolbar's More.

**DC22. Smaller page fixes (B).** The purchase order's heading is its number with its status block beside it (the review tag under it);
a saved supplier invoice's heading is the supplier's own number, CW's number the quiet line under it (PI_View; a draft or a cancellation
keeps its title); What to buy no longer repeats "Will run out" as a chip beside its status cell; the supplier's latest invoices' first column
is "Invoice" (it read "Col": a nested word group); the item's movements board has no coloured edge and its times say Today / Yesterday
(IT_Item).

**DC23. Kept as they are, on purpose.** The TEST SYSTEM strip and the strip that says which jobs Admin switches off (brief rule 3: safety).
The person's panel at the bottom of the sidebar (Change password, Sign out: functions). The Show buttons and the fields' darker edge (DC10).
The tab row scrolling on a phone (DC9). The chevron of a folded group (DC12). Leave without saving on a phone's bar of the supplier invoice
(PI_New_Phone has no place for it; it is a function). A board's "?" help beside its heading (a "?" is the agreed place for help).

**DC24. Not changed here, and why (the rest of the audit).** Each needs a page's own conversion, a new figure or query (DC25), or is a
behaviour the earlier decisions chose:
- the record pages' phone headers (back, number, status) and their phone layouts (GI_Phone, CT_Phone, IT_Phone, AP_Phone, PI_New_Phone);
- New purchase order (PO_New: its field set, the lines' columns, the add-line row, the staff note and totals, the bar's words), the purchase
  order's view beyond its heading (the exposed actions, Ordered's bar, Deliver to and payment terms, the five columns, the deliveries,
  invoices and history cards), New supplier invoice and its phone page (the asterisks and hints, the match result's place, the line's
  hierarchy, the charge and attach layout, the Charges row, the rare folds), the supplier invoice's view beyond its heading (the exposed
  actions, the differences sentence, the VAT number, the facts, the four columns, the totals' words, History);
- the delivery's one page (Main, GI_Phone: GV2-GV25), the count sheet and counting on a phone (CV5-CV11), Before it is final's rows and its
  Keep my count (CV9), the approvals record's facts (AV6), the item page's strip and details (IV3-IV10);
- Lines to place's "Placed" (the state word is shared by every queue) and its closing line; Counts' "Sold a day" (CV1: a figure) and the
  Count menu's choices (CV2: behaviour); the purchase orders' "Received or closed" (a setting's days, not a month: behaviour);
- the reports on TP_Report, Settings on TP_Settings, the matching page on TP_Match (whole-page conversions; their missing figures DC25);
- Goods in's open-issue tag and paper-sheet note on a row (the only place a booked delivery says so).

**DC25. Needs a build (for the owner).** Home's four figures (Orders sent today, Out of stock, Coming in this week, Oversold today) and its
combined task rows (Approvals, Counts overdue, Delivery being checked, Lines to place, Supplier invoice needs a look); Home's Find for orders
and deliveries; the purchase orders' search by item; the supplier invoices' search by order, its money summary, Overdue and Paid (CW does not
know the payments) and its Show choices; the three sales-invoice pages (SI_List, SI_New, SI_View); Lines to place's search; the count sheet's
name search; Waiting for you's Show (Answered today) and a correction's value at cost; the stock value report's Not sold in 90 days, Share,
total row and Category / Supplier grouping; TP_Settings' inline settings and their search; the mockups' #d9d0e1 field edge, if the owner
accepts it below WCAG's 3:1 (DC10).


**DC27. The Products pages of w11 (rebased on `d0f98d9`).** Their cross-cutting parts are the shared ones above (W11.9 left them here):
no sentence and no full stop, sentence case, the Show buttons kept (DC10). All Products' main create action is in its header: "+ Add an
item" (for items.create, through the head's `side`: Add Item's page is the form, and `Sections` keeps its rule that a create button leads to
its own page's form); its Clear, Import and Export are under the toolbar's one More; its filters (the card, the kind of product, the four
ticks) are inside ONE Show control, a pop-over with its Show button (`details.tb-pop.tb-show`, no script needed; its count says how many are
on), so the toolbar is one search and one Show as the board mockups draw it (the coordinator's Chrome check of w11: the Show row was two
lines on a computer and four rows on a phone). Every filter's parameter and the submit without script are as before. Add Item's link to the items made by hand and the family's link to Families are their eyebrows (DC3). A page's own
`more:` line that is not who may change it (whether a second person checks items made by hand) is under the general "?" ("What does this
mean?"), the look-only "?" keeps its own name.

**DC28. No tab view: the sidebar holds a section's pages (the owner, 30 Oct 2026: "dont need tab view use sidebar and sub section"; it
replaces the brief's "keep the one section tab row" and settles audit A5 and A8).** No page draws a section tab row or a segment row
(`page_frame.php` keeps only the switched-off strip; the tab row's More, its CSS and HV9's placement went with it). The sidebar keeps
HM_Home's grouping (Home, Every day, More); the current section's entry is open (`.nav-item.open`, the mockups' `.nav.on`) and lists the
section's pages under it as sub-items (`ul.nav-sub > li > a.nav-sub-item`: 13 px, 26 px in, 8 px corners, muted; the current one the dark
accent, semi-bold, as CT_Board's and IT_Item's `nav.side .sub`), and the current page's segments one more indent (`ul.nav-sub.nav-seg`, 40 px
in). Every other entry stays one link. A page's count is on its item (and still summed on its section, as before). The page shown has no
link (CV13); the deepest current item is `aria-current="page"`, the entries that hold it `aria-current="true"` (so a daily tab's entry, Counts,
stays marked while Stock lists its pages). A page not built yet (Quality) is a sub-item with no link and its "Soon". The set-up and
specialist pages (HV3's More) are sub-items like the others (`.more`, no look of their own). The phone's menu is the same tree, 44 px to
tap; the bottom bar is HM_Phone's. Tabs inside a record stay where a mockup draws them (the item's parts, the supplier's tabs). Who sees
which page is unchanged: `Sections::frame` builds the tree from the same visible map (`subs`, `segs`), and a test walks every page each role
may open and finds it in that role's tree. `Sections::SHOW_REPLACES` and the MENU_HELP lines it needed are gone; the kernel tests' helpers
(`sectionTabs`, `moreTabs`, `segments`, `currentTab`, `currentSection`) read the sidebar now, so every earlier assertion on who sees which
page still runs.

**DC26. Tests.** Red first (`runs/dsc_red.log`: main `672fae9` with the new tests: 4 of 4 fail on their assertions).
`UiTemplatesTest::testTheSharedPartsFollowTheApprovedMockups` (the statement without full stop or sentence, the look-only "?", the record
eyebrow, the header's lone "+ New", no flow strip, Goods in's segments under More, the HM shell, sentence case for every page name, no
board template asks for `newActions`), `UiUnitTest::testTheSharedCssFollowsTheApprovedMockups` (every measurement of DC2, DC5, DC7-DC15),
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/DesignConformanceScreensTest.php` (the boards as served: "+ New" in the head and none in the toolbar, no sentence,
no full stop, no flow strip, Goods in's and Counts' pages under More, the plain shell; a look-only page's "?"; the password's kept rule). The
pins of the old layout were moved to the new one, never dropped: the layout and statement tests, `SectionsTest`'s frame, `MenusTest`, the
pages' intro checks (now: no sentence, or the step's kept line, or the "?"), the segment checks of the six tabs (now the row's More), the
create buttons (now the header's), the page names' sentence case, the PO view's heading and the PO states' words.

*Tests* (30 Oct 2026, on `8aa4cc8`, the tree rebased on main `d0f98d9`): `tests/Unit` and `tests/Integration/UiKernel`: OK (1052 tests, 128101
assertions); the rest of the suite (`runs/smlabel_partc.cmd`): OK, 1098 tests, 82 skipped (the HTTP tests of slot `ui`); slot `ui`
(`UiAuthTest`, `UiSecurityTest`, `UiReviewFlowTest`): OK (44 tests). Logs: `runs/dsc_end_unit_uikernel.log`, `runs/dsc_end_partc.log`,
`runs/dsc_end_ui.log`. DC28 also added `UiUnitTest::testTheSidebarHoldsTheSectionsPagesAndNoPageHasATabRow` and, in
`testTheSharedPartsFollowTheApprovedMockups`, the walk that finds every page each of nine roles reached through a tab row in that role's
sidebar tree; the kernel helpers read the tree, so the earlier who-sees-what assertions (tabs, More pages, segments, their counts) all run
on it. Not seen in a real browser here: the coordinator's Chrome check should look at the sidebar tree, the All Products Show control and
the boards at 375 px and 1,280 px.

## Products: the Codex review of d0f98d9 (`runs/w11_codex_findings.txt`), two MEDIUM and two LOW, each shown failing first (branch `wave-w11`, second commit, 30 Oct 2026; W11.12-W11.16)

Fixed on `d0f98d9` (W11.1-W11.11, merged to main and on staging). Red first: `runs/w11_fix_red.log` (the four new tests on `d0f98d9`, each
failing on what it checks). The owner's word of 30 Oct ("strictly follow our design guidelines") holds: no new line, note, button or chip on
any page; a fold or More opens where a refused form's values are, as main's bars already do (PV, W8). No route, permission, rule or posted
field changed; the shared parts (`View::head`, `Html::statement`, `layout.php`, `page_frame.php`, `Sections.php`, the shared `app.css`)
untouched.

**W11.12. A refused decision opens its own barcode, also past the list's limit (MEDIUM 1).** The decision posts to
`/ui/items/barcodes/{id}/decide` without the page's search, and its refusal drew the waiting list unfiltered: with 201 waiting, a barcode
found by its search (the 201st) and sent without an answer came back with the first one open, its refusal over the list. The refusal now
reads its record alone (`BarcodeReviews::rows()` takes the row's id) when the list does not hold it and it still waits, and lists it with
the others (the last of its reason's group, open); its refusal is said in it, and its form keeps `data-dirty`. Decided meanwhile
(409), it is not drawn as waiting: the refusal goes over the list, as before. The page itself, its list and its limit are unchanged.

**W11.13. Values a refused form brings back are guarded as typed (MEDIUM 2).** A refused new family (its name taken, a note typed) came back
with the name and the note in the open drawer, but the form had no `data-dirty`: a family row, Show or a pager link left without a word and
the note was lost. The same for a refused new pack item and a family's rename and pasted list. Now a refused form whose values come back
carries `data-dirty="1"` (W9.15's guard then asks first): the new family when its name or note is not empty, the new pack item when any of its
four is not empty, a family's rename when the name brought back differs from the family's, its list when it is not empty. Where such values
sat in a closed part they are shown, as main's bars do: a refused rename opens More and Rename, a refused list opens Add items (it opened
for an empty or a too long list only). A refusal with nothing typed (an empty name) and every page drawn fresh hold nothing unsaved.

**W11.14. "Next" names the barcode the save opens (LOW 1).** The decision's redirect (unchanged) is the waiting list, no search, the first
one open; "Next" named the row after the open one in the list shown, so with A, B and C and B open it said C and the save opened A, and a
barcode found by its search said "The last one in this list." though others waited. "Next" is now the first of the waiting ones left once
this one is decided, in the list's order (its reasons' groups, oldest first; the first `LIST_LIMIT` as the list reads them):
`BarcodesController::nextAfter()` over `BarcodeReviews::waiting()` (id, barcode, reason of the oldest `LIST_LIMIT + 1`, one indexed read).
"The last one in this list." when none is left. One case it cannot know: a "move" also closes the old holder's own review of that barcode
(I116), so when that review is the one named, the save opens the one after it.

**W11.15. Typed text "on" is typed (LOW 2).** Add Item's folds open when something in them was typed, and every value "on" was taken for
nothing typed (a radio without a value sends "on"): a brand typed "on", refused for its barcode, came back in a closed Legal details. Text,
the kind and the tick count when not empty, whatever they say; the two yes / no answers (duty, single-use) only by their yes or their no
(`HandMadeController::ANSWERS`): their "not known" opens nothing.

**W11.16. Tests.** Red first (`runs/w11_fix_red.log`, 4 of 4 fail). `ProductPatternsScreensTest::testARefusedDecisionOpensItsOwnRecordPastTheListsLimit`
(201 waiting: the 201st found, refused, open again with its refusal, its row selected; decided meanwhile, the refusal over the list),
`testWhatARefusedFormBringsBackIsGuardedAsTyped` (a new family, an empty one, a rename, a pasted list, a new pack item; the pages drawn
fresh), `testNextNamesTheBarcodeTheSaveOpens` (A, B, C: B open and C found by its search name A; the save opens A; the last one),
`testTypedTextOnOpensItsFold` (a brand "on"; "not known" alone opens nothing). `UiTemplatesTest::testTheProductPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns`
pins the family bar's More with its open-again condition.

## Reports, settings and system on the approved patterns (wave w13, branch `wave-w13`, 30 Oct 2026; W13.1-W13.20)

The owner, 30 Oct 2026: "strictly follow our design guidelines" and "dont need tab view use sidebar and sub section". The mockups are the
spec: `cwdaily/TP_Report` (the reports and the audit log), `cwdaily/TP_Settings` (Settings' pages), the board and record patterns
(`GI_List`, `PO_View`) and `TP_Parts`. Built on `ds-conform` (DC1-DC28; rebased on main `559a2fe`): no sentence under a heading, sentence case, "+ New" in
the header, no tab row. Layout and words: no route, permission, posted field or service rule changed; every audit write is as before.

**W13.1. The settings shell is the sidebar's.** TP_Settings draws its sections as a list at the left of the page; with DC28 the sidebar holds
the open section's pages, so that list IS the sidebar (an in-page list too would be the section's pages twice, and a vertical tab row is the
tab view the owner said no to). Each Settings page is a column of cards (`.set-list` > `section.set-card`), a card a heading over rows
(`.set-row`): what it is at the left (`.set-k`: `.set-kt` the name, `.set-kd` what it does, `.set-kh` who changed it last), its value or its
own small form at the right (`.set-v`), each saved on its own. A change of several fields is the row's Change (`details.set-fold`), at the
row's right like a Save and the card's width when open. A record's facts are rows too (`.set-row.set-fact`). The History is the last card.

**W13.2. A report's head.** As TP_Report: the eyebrow, the title, the as-of line under it (the head's `meta`: when the figures were brought up
to date; the days shown on Sales by store), and "Download (Excel)" at the right, a plain bordered button (`report_bar`; the file is the same
CSV, which opens in Excel; PE1). Then the figures strip, then the toolbar (one search, the Show row with its Show button, rare things under
the toolbar's More), then the list as one board with the blue edge (`.doc-board.info`) and its total row (`tr.grp-foot`). What a report's
figures leave out is its "?" (`more:`), not a paragraph.

**W13.3. Stock value.** The strip is TP_Report's: Value at cost, Units on the shelf, Items with stock (`ReportViews::valueFigures` counts
them), Not sold in N days (`ReportViews::notSoldValue`: Slow stock's two lists together, N its setting `reports.slow_after_days`, so the
figure and that report agree; no new number). Under a figure, a small line only where something is left out: another account's units, the
units without a cost. The tabs by product / brand / warehouse are the Show row's "Group by" (Item, Brand, Warehouse; `by` as before). The one
search finds a brand or an item: by brand or by warehouse it keeps the rows whose name holds the words (the page and its file alike). Brand
and warehouse have TP_Report's Share (`meter.rp-share`, our value only) and a Total row (pennies, exact; another account's warehouse left
out). The products without a cost and Clear are under the toolbar's More. The brand and warehouse boards no longer show "Units without a
cost" (the CSV keeps the column; the strip says how many).

**W13.4. Stock by store.** The store's four tiles of every store became one strip of the store shown (units it can sell with the warehouse
it sells from, matched, in stock, out of stock); the store is chosen in the Show row with All / In stock / Out of stock (the filter pop-over
went); a product's status is a solid cell; "the website uses its own stock" is on the product's line. Download for the store shown.

**W13.5. Low stock.** The strip: Low, None left, the level a product is low at (the setting, with its rule under it). Low / None left is the
Show choice with its count (the tab row went); "its own" level is a tag.

**W13.6. Slow stock.** The strip: Slow and Dead, each with its days under it; Slow / Dead is the Show choice with its count; when the sales
were last read is the as-of line; what a sale is, the "?".

**W13.7. Sales by store (w10's) follows the same head:** Download and the days shown in the head, the strip before the Show row.

**W13.8. The audit log is a report.** Download in the head; the record number is the one search; from, to, who, what was done and the kind
of record are the Show row; Clear under More; the entries one board; "Older entries" the pager. Read only, append-only as before.

**W13.9. Rules and numbers (`/ui/reference/settings`).** TP_Settings' title. A card per topic, a row per setting: its name (its own page:
the value, the agreed tick and the History), what it does, "Not agreed yet" while the owner has not said yes, who changed it last. For whoever
changes settings (settings.manage) a simple value (a number, a date, a short text, yes or no) is a box in its row with its unit (read from
the key's end: days, minutes, %, units…), a reason (Why; the service has always needed one) and a plain Save. The row posts to the setting's
own route (`SettingsController::save`) with the fields its page sends: `key`, `seen` (the version the row was drawn with: one read for
every setting), `value`, `reason`, and `agreed` as it is now, so a row's Save never agrees or un-agrees a value; that and every refusal are
on the setting's page, where a Save lands. A list (ticked boxes), a long text or a hidden value (a secret) has "Change" to its page.
"Find a setting" (`q`) keeps the rows whose name, what it does or topic holds the words. The company details' card is first (their state,
their own page); the VAT codes the last card (read only); then TP_Settings' one line that each change is kept. Removed from this page, kept
elsewhere: the links to the other Settings pages (the sidebar), Who checks what (the Approval rules page says the same, rule by rule), the
technical keys (in a row's `data-key` only), the footer (the suppliers' and the costs' own pages).

**W13.10. Numbering** is one card, a row per kind of record (in the kinds' order): its name and whether it is in use, who checks it, the OK
first and the days, how its numbers start and the last one; at the right the next number. How numbers are made: the "?".

**W13.11. Reasons and a reason.** The list: "+ New reason" in the head (its form opens here), a card of the reasons in use (the spreadsheet
under its More) and one of those switched off; a row a reason: its name, what it is used for and which way, its rules as tags, its short code
at the right. A reason: the list as its eyebrow, a card of what it is, a card of its changes (its name inline with its reason and Save;
where it is offered, its stock-out rules and the switch each under its row's Change), its History.

**W13.12. Warehouses and a warehouse.** The same: the list's cards in use / switched off, a row a warehouse (whether websites sell from it,
whose stock, its places; what is in the building at the right); a warehouse: its facts, its changes each under a Change (or why not: a
system warehouse, stock inside, a website using it), its places (a row each, changed under its Change), its History.

**W13.13. Approval rules.** A card per part, a row per rule (its state as tags, the rule in sentences); its Change holds the rule's form and
its history (for whoever only looks, the row's History). What loosening needs, what switching off does not let through, what always needs a
second OK and the one-rule-per-kind line are the heading's "?".

**W13.14. Roles and permissions.** The rules that always apply are the "?"; a card of who may do each thing (a row a task: "Change who can",
or its History, or Fixed) and one of what each job may do (a row a job). A task's page is the shell's record (facts, the one form, History).

**W13.15. Company.** Its state card (confirmed or not, what is missing or wrong, the orders it touches, the confirm form) with Change and the
sample PDF at the right; the checks of a change as rows; the details as rows (`data-field`); the History. Its edit page has Company as its
eyebrow; "Until then the PDFs say DO NOT SEND" is its "?".

**W13.16. Users is a board (pattern 1).** One search (a name or an e-mail, `q`) and one Show (everyone, can sign in, switched off: `show`);
the spreadsheet, Roles and permissions and Clear under the toolbar's More; the groups Can sign in / Switched off with the status cell filled,
a row opens the person, "+ Add a staff member" ends the first group. Everyone signed in now is a related board under it. The warnings are
as before (they read everyone, whatever the search).

**W13.17. A user is a record page (pattern 2).** Users as the eyebrow, the name with whether they can sign in; the account's switch, a new
sign-up sheet / sign-in code / password and signing out everywhere under the head's More (`person_bar`, each with its tick as before); the
strip (jobs, last signed in, added, signed in now); the paper card (the e-mail beside jobs, sign-in, set-up); then the jobs form (Save the
jobs, the page's one main button), the devices and the jobs' history as related boards.
