**W13.18. Stores (`/ui/system/sites`).** A board grouped by the mode in CW (live, watching only, off), the mode a solid cell, a row opening the
store's part below (its facts in the paper card, the server's commands folded). Still no form.

**W13.19. System checks.** The last check as a card (when, how long, the result as a tag, what it found folded open), the earlier checks a
card of rows.

**W13.20. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testTheReportsSettingsAndSystemPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` (the templates),
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/ReportsSettingsPatternsScreensTest.php` (the pages as served: the head's Download, the strip, the toolbar, the
board; a settings row saved on its own through the setting's route and kept in its history; the people board's search). The earlier pins were
moved to the new markup, never dropped (`ReportsScreenTest`, `ReferenceScreensTest`, `SetItYourselfScreensTest`, `SupplierScreensTest`'s
settings page, `CompanyScreensTest`, `InvoiceScreensTest`, `StartSettingsWordsTest`). The W9.15 guard covers these pages: a POST form with a
field to type carries `data-unsaved`, and on a page with one every form carries `data-leaves`.

## Design conformance: the Codex review of f4d1126 (branch `ds-conform-fix`, 30 Oct 2026; DC29-DC32)

Three MEDIUM and one note, each fixed with a test that failed first (`runs/dsc_fix_red.log`: main `b12544a` with the new tests).

**DC29. A count sheet's opener is told nothing is booked yet (MEDIUM).** DC1 dropped `count_sheet_open`'s intro, and its "nothing is booked
until you make it final" was said nowhere else: the opener saw quantities "Saved". CT_Sheet draws one muted line under the board (how the
numbers are saved); that is where it is now, one short line under an open sheet's lines (`p.muted.count-booked`, `COUNTS['not_booked']`:
"Each number is saved with the time you typed it; nothing is booked until you make the sheet final."), not a paragraph under the heading.
The other dropped intros were swept for a safety or permission line a person needs before acting; each is said where they act:
- `card_import`: "nothing is saved until you choose…" is the page's own hint (`CARD_IMPORT['how']`) and its report says "nothing was saved";
- `queue_corrections`: each card says what confirming books, and closing books nothing;
- `reviews` and the records waiting for an OK: "Nothing is booked until they say OK" on the record and its notice;
- `order_draft`: the editor's button asks a reviewer's OK over the limit and says so; `suppliers`: the order editor marks a supplier not
  approved yet ("you can prepare an order, but not confirm it yet");
- `timed`: the board's column "Becomes final at"; `supplier_*_final`, `supplier_paper_reversal`: their Final / Cancelled status block;
- `staff_sheet`: its red "shown only once" alert; `audit`, `documents`: read only, nothing to act on;
- `queue_Conflict`: the decide box's "Only a matching lead can decide these. You can look."; `listing_spot`, `reservations`, `sales_orders`,
  `sales_dispatch`: `Words::INTRO_LOOK`, the "?" (DC1); a claim-only return: its eyebrow's tag (DC1);
- `count_before`, `count_differences`, `to_match`, `not_invoiced`, `arriving`, `queue_suspense`: their buttons say what they do.

**DC30. The purchase orders' More keeps every filter (MEDIUM).** At `?state=sent&drafts=1` "Hide the drafts again" led to the whole list
(the old checkbox kept the hidden `state`). The More's links now carry every filter on: the status, the supplier, the search, sent back and
the view.

**DC31. A toolbar's panel stays inside the toolbar (MEDIUM).** The search that takes the free width (DC10) puts Filter or Show at the
toolbar's right edge, and the panel opened from the button's left edge, 300 px wide, ran past the screen (Mapping at 1,280 px; All
Products' Show at tablet widths). Every toolbar panel (`details.tb-pop > .pop`) is now placed against the toolbar (`.tb-pop` is not its
box), right-aligned under it and never wider than it (`max-width: min(400px, 100%)`, the form `min-width: min(300px, 100%)`), at every width;
on a phone it is the toolbar's full width as before.

**DC32. The sidebar helpers check the exact aria-current (note).** `KernelUiTestCase::currentSection()` asserts the entry's value ("true"
when a page of the section in the tree is the page, "page" when it is itself the page) and that one link of the menu is the page;
`sectionTabs()` and `moreTabs()` assert a page's "true" (one of its segments is the page) or "page"; `segments()` asserts "page". A
regression of DC28's marks now fails every kernel test that reads the sidebar.

## The Matching pages on the approved patterns (wave w12, branch `wave-w12`, 30 Oct 2026; W12.1-W12.16)

The owner's word of 29 Oct ("all design convert our new claude suggested design") for Matching and the review pages around it, and of 30 Oct
("strictly follow our design guidelines"): a store product's decision page is the approved TP_Match (its parts, order, buttons and words), the
lists are boards (GI_List), the pages that hand out one decision at a time are inboxes (AP_Inbox). Layout and words only: no route, permission,
migration, setting or service rule changed; every form posts the fields it did to where it did (FormOnce, versions, CSRF as before). The
matching rules stay where they are, in `DecisionService` and `OneAtATime`: a second OK (1 sale that is not 1 item, a protected item, a match
marked wrong before), the units of a pack, protected items, one at a time (held back, a spot check's matches, found on arrival).

**W12.1. A store product's page is TP_Match.** The head asks "Is this the same item?"; its eyebrow is the section, the store and how many are
left to match on the list it was opened from (`MATCH to_match`; a spot check's "n of 20 checked"); at its right a bar: the part answered today
of what is answered today and what is left (`listing_progress`, its words for a screen reader are the progress line's as before, in
`data-progress`), a spot check's 20 blocks instead. Then the store product on the left (`section.card.mt-card.info`, the blue 6 px top edge:
"On the store", the photo block, its name and variant title, "Variant … · £price") and the item on the right (`.mt-card.done`, green: its
heading as before, "N other suggestions" a fold with the candidates the computer looked at, the photo block, its name, "CW-… · N in stock" (the
stock buckets' on hand, one read by the item: `Queries::stockOf`), the small tags "Second OK needed" for a protected item and "Said not the same
before"); their facts side by side in the approved order (brand, line, flavour, strength, pack, then the rest either side states), each value on
the green tint where the two agree (same, or a brand spelt differently) and on the amber one where they differ or one side does not say
(`span.mt-mark`, `data-state`, the word for a screen reader). "Or find another item" is in the item's card, its own GET form (`form="mt-find"`,
the box `?s=`, "/" puts the cursor there) with what it finds under it. Then one card: "One store product is [N] of this item" and "Note (when the
line or pack differs)". Then the bar at the bottom (`.doc-bar.mt-bar`): Skip (the next one, or back), More, Not the same, Same item. ONE form
(`form#decide.mt-form`) holds the cards, the card of units and note and the bar: the answer is the button pressed (`name="action"`: link,
reject; under More new_item and ignore), so the quick yes over the old form is gone (Same item is it) and so are the answer radios and "What
each answer does". Its first button is a disabled hidden default (`button.po-default`, as the order editor's), so Enter in the units or the note
answers nothing. A store product the computer suggests a new item for, with no item and no barcode clash, has New item as its main answer in
Same item's place (what the form chose first before); with no item at all Same item is drawn faded with "Find the item first" beside it (TP_Parts:
a button not allowed yet says why). Same item names the pack ("Same item (10 a sale)") when the units are not 1.

**W12.2. The rest of the page is under the bar's More.** In this order: New item (its fold: the details of the new item, in two columns, and
"Create the new item"), "Ignore: not a real product", "Mark as a landing page" (its own small form, `form="mark-landing"`), then the folds of
`listing_more`: why the computer suggests this, more details (the website, its status, what it sold, its page, its attributes, what it is
matched to, the item's family and stock rule), where its barcode is too, its duplicate groups (links), the spot check it is in (its legend and
the way back), its history, the technical details. The comparison table is gone (the facts' marks say it); the help lines ("?", "C1, C2 … are
the rows …", the units' hint, the second OK's paragraph) are gone; nothing else is. The menu opens upwards and scrolls (the bar's `.more-menu`).
A refused new item opens More and its fold at the field.

**W12.3. A spot check's own match keeps its three answers.** Skip (the next one, nothing saved), "Not the same" (a fold of the bar that opens
upwards with its warning first and the answer form behind it, as before), "Same item" (its own small form: always the suggestion with the
suggestion's units, which the spot check counts as a yes). Two forms, as before: the yes must never carry what the second step's form holds.
Its line "Say yes only if it is right …" is where the units and the note are.

**W12.4. A store product that is not answered here says so where the units and the note are.** A landing page (its box, "This is a real
product" for a lead), one waiting for a second OK (the waiting card with its approve and cancel), a matched one (the note; a lead's "Change
this match" is a fold of the bar's More, open when another item was picked), one only a lead or the spot check's owner decides, look only. Its
bar: Skip, More; a finished spot check's member "Check the next one (n of 20)" as its main action.

**W12.5. To review is a board.** The overview: ONE Show row (the store: the store tabs before), each store a group over a card with the coloured
edge. A list (a match strength): one search and ONE Show row (the store, the list, what it shows, how a match was found, sold at least: the
store tabs, the strength battery and its tabs, the show tabs and the Filter pop-over before), Clear at the right; how much is left and answered
today under the title (`data-progress`); the list as one group (its colour, "n in all · n shown", Select all on this page), each row its status
cell (the strength), its Check & match under its name, Open at its end; the bulk bar as before. "Same barcode" is a soft tag.

**W12.6. Store Products is a board.** One search and ONE Show row (the store, the state, the sort: the store tabs, the state tabs and the Sort
pop-over before), Clear; the page's products grouped by their state, what is still to match first (Suggested, Not matched, Waiting for a second
OK, On hold, Matched, Ignored, Landing pages; best sellers first in each, by the sort chosen), each group its colour and count over a card with
the coloured edge, the state the solid cell; the old heading "…: website products" with its count line and the undo-a-match note are gone
(the groups and the Show row's counts say them; undoing a match is on the product's page). The quiet line of products not sold in a year stays.

**W12.7. By Item is a board.** One search and ONE Show row (what it shows: All, On every store, Missing on …, With a suggestion waiting, each
with its count), the number of rows (its three links as before: another number keeps the place, so it is not a choice of the form), Clear and
Export at the right; the page's items as ONE group in their CW number order (the list's own heading and "n in all · n shown"), "Stores matched"
the solid status cell at the row's end (green on every store, amber on some, grey on none); each store's cell as before (its state chip, its
variant, its quick match). The note under the list is gone (help); the bulk bar's limit line stays.

**W12.8. New Variants and Duplicates are boards; a duplicate group is the matching frame.** New Variants: one search and ONE Show row (the store,
the period, what it shows), Clear and Export; the lines of what the store sends and the check on arrival (its help sentence, "Where new
variants come from", gone); the page's variants newest first as ONE group (the store's, "n in all · n shown"), each row's state its solid
cell. Duplicates: "Start with the first group" the head's main action; the open groups, biggest sellers first (the order "Next" follows), as
ONE group, each row where it stands its solid cell (waiting for a second OK, partly decided, a reason against joining, to decide; the
reasons themselves in its last column); the groups
decided lately a board of their own with its pager. A list whose order is its point (newest first, biggest sellers first, CW number) is one
group with the row's own status cell rather than regrouped by status: the order the person works in and "Next" stay as they were. A group's
page: the question in the head; the reasons against joining under it when the rules found any (the tick that they were read stays required);
the pages side by side (`.mt-card`, the kept one on the green edge); the answer card (who is kept, each page's choice when there are several);
the bar: Skip, More (what the rules say when they found nothing, what the titles say, why the computer thinks they match, undo a wrong join),
then the answers (keep apart, join; with several, Save my choices last), the main one as before (Keep apart when the rules found a reason
against, else Join; Save with several). The answers send the form by `form="dup-decide"`.

**W12.9. Staff requests is an inbox.** The requests on the left grouped by what is asked (changes of jobs, sign-in resets), each row the person
and what is asked, `?open=<id>`; the open one on the right: its group and place, the person and their e-mail, the status block, its facts (what
is asked, e-mail, account made, set up, jobs now and asked for, asked by and on), the note when they have not set up their sign-in, then ONE
decision: OK the main button (its form as before), "Not OK" under More with its note; "Next: …". A refused answer opens its own request.

**W12.10. To check is an inbox; All records is a board.** To check: ONE Show row (the kind of work: the Filter pop-over before); the two lists
as groups (needs your OK, already done), each row what it is and when it is due ("Late"), `?open=<task>`; the open one: its facts and ONE main
action, Open its own page, where it is decided as before (each record's page says what each answer does; the answers are not copied here, so
no form posts from a new place). A task this person may not decide says why. All records: one search and ONE Show row (kind, status, check),
Clear; the page's records grouped by their status, a row opening the record.

**W12.11. Spot checks is an inbox.** ONE Show row (the store); the spot checks grouped by their result (in progress, failed, cannot be used, all
right), `?open=<id>`; the open one: its result block, its 20 blocks, its facts (checked, picked from, confirmed together), who started it, and
its one action: for its owner while in progress "Check the next one (n of 20)", else Open its page. A spot check's own page is unchanged.

**W12.12. Simple matching opens one cell's picker at a time.** Every cell's box and Apply are in a fold ("Match" in an empty cell, "+" in a cell
with a product), and the page's folds are one group (`details name="sm-pick"`): opening one closes the open one, so one picker and one Apply are
open, the selected cell's. A refused or to-be-confirmed answer opens its cell. Without the script the folds open as before.

**W12.13. Typed values are guarded (W9.15's rule).** On these pages a POST form with a field to type or choose carries `data-unsaved` with DOC's
words (a store product's answer, its change of match and its second step, a landing page's "real product", a waiting decision's approve note,
the bulk forms' ticks, a duplicate group's answer and undo, simple matching's box, a staff request's Not OK), and on a page with one every form
carries `data-leaves`; a form a refusal draws again with what was sent carries `data-dirty` (W11.13's rule: the answer form, its second steps, a
landing page's "real product", a duplicate group's answer, a simple-matching box with its text). app.js: a field inside a form that belongs to another form (`form="…"`: "Or find another item", By Item's quick match
box inside the bulk form) no longer marks the form around it as typed in.

**W12.14. Where the pages still differ from the mockups.** The shared differences are the design-conformance build's (DC1-DC28, W12.16):
the Show button beside a choice is kept there (DC10), as here. Kept on purpose: the photo block says "No photo" (CW keeps no photos yet; the block is where they go); the crumb back to the list a
page was opened from (the record pages' pattern); the held-back note over the cards (one at a time is a rule); a spot check's two forms
(W12.3); To check's decision stays on each record's page (W12.10); the Check & match fold of a list row keeps its own compact layout (CM1);
the lists keep their Open buttons and tick boxes (their rows hold the Check & match fold and the quick match, so a row link over the whole row
would cover them); By Item's store cells keep their state chips (a state per store, not the row's) and its number of rows stays three links
(another number keeps the place); the lists whose order is their point are one group (W12.8). No page here draws a tab row or a segment row
of its own (the owner's word of 30 Oct, "use sidebar and sub section"): every filter is a choice of the one Show row.

**W12.15. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testTheMatchingPagesFollowTheApprovedPatterns` (the templates) and its guard list
(`testTheBuyingPagesGuardTypedValuesAndEveryFormThatLeavesAsksFirst`), `MatchingPatternsScreensTest` (the pages as served), both shown failing on
main first (`runs/w12_red.log`); `UiResponse::buttons()` reads the answers a form sends by its buttons. The tests that pinned the old layouts
now pin the new one: the quick yes and the preselected radio became "the main button", a refused form's answer is sent as its button would send
it (`+ ['action' => 'link']`), the comparison table became the cards' marks, the progress line `data-progress`, Skip the bar's first link.

**W12.16. Rebased on the design-conformance build (`f4d1126`, DC1-DC28).** The pages take the shared parts as they are now: no sentence under
a heading (DC1: `intro:` still names the page), no tab or segment row (DC28: the sidebar lists Matching's and Approvals' pages and segments;
these pages draw none of their own), sentence case. A store product's page and a duplicate group draw their way back as the eyebrow (DC3:
`$head(back: […])`, the list they were opened from, then the store and how many are left as its tag) instead of `p.crumbs`, inside
`div.match-head` (DC2's 24 px heading of TP_Match). A list with several filters has them in ONE Show control, DC27's pop-over
(`details.tb-pop.tb-show` with its Show button, its count the filters on): To review's list (the store, the list, what it shows, found by,
sold at least), Store Products (the store, the state, the sort), New Variants (the store, the period, what it shows) and All records (the
kind, the status, the check); a list with one filter keeps the plain Show choice (By Item, the spot checks, To check, the overview). The
kernel tests read a page's way back from either (`p.crumbs` or the eyebrow `p.ph-back`).

## The Matching pages and settings: the last fix round (branch `final-fixes`, 30 Oct 2026; W12.17-W12.22, W13.21)

The Codex review of `da7c620` (`runs/w12_codex_findings.txt`), two MEDIUM and two LOW, the w13 LOW (`runs/w13_codex_findings.txt`) and the
owner's Chrome check of the decision page's eyebrow. Each was shown failing first (`runs/final_fix_red.log`).

**W12.17. A field typed in marks the form it belongs to.** app.js listens on the document (input, change) and marks the field's OWNING form
(`field.form`: the form around it, or the one it names with `form="…"` wherever it stands) when that form guards its values
(`data-unsaved`). w12 stopped a form marking itself for a field of another form, and so lost an invoice's planned date: its fields stand in
the invoice's form but belong to `pi-schedule`, which was not guarded, so a sidebar link left without asking. Every POST form that owns a
field from elsewhere now carries `data-unsaved` with DOC's words: an invoice's planned date (`pi-schedule`), an order's cancel reason
(`po-cancel`), a line to place's item, units and note (`lq-pick-<id>`); the approvals' and barcode reviews' answers already did. GET forms
(a store product's "Or find another item", By Item's quick match box) are not guarded and their fields mark nothing.

**W12.18. The bar's menus stay inside the bar.** `.mt-bar > details.more` is not their box (`position: static`): the sticky bar is. More's
menu starts at the bar's left gutter, Not the same's (a spot check) at its right one, each `min(36rem, 100% - 2 gutters)` wide, never wider
than the bar (at 800 px with the sidebar the menu began after Skip and ran off the screen). On a phone the menus are in the flow, the row's
width, as every menu there.

**W12.19. Store Products' fold goes on to the row the board shows under it.** The rows are put in the board's order (the groups' order,
still to match first, a stable sort keeping best sellers first in each) BEFORE each fold's next row (`nx`) is taken. With A suggested,
B matched and C suggested, A's Yes came back at B, a group further down, and C was skipped.

**W12.20. A refused New item opens More.** When New item is the main answer (no item to compare, the computer suggests a new one) its
details are under More, closed while nothing was refused. A New item the service refused (a strength that is not a number: the field is
marked; no name: the item as a whole) is drawn again with More open and the New item fold open in it.

**W12.21. A store product's eyebrow is the list it was opened from, never Home.** Store Products' Open (the row's name and its button)
carries the list as the person has it (`via=store` and the store, state, sort, search and page: StoreContext, as its Check & match fold
did), so the page's eyebrow, Skip, picks and answers lead back to it (CM3). A list whose rows link the page without naming themselves is
read from the Referer (same origin, its own filters only): New Variants, Simple matching, Store Products, as before Search, an item's page
and Possible duplicates. Opened from nowhere known, the eyebrow is the section's list: Store Products of the store product's store. Its tag
always says the store and how many are left: a list's own count when opened from To review (and its bar), a spot check's progress, else
the store's still to match (Store Products' suggested and not matched), with no bar.

**W12.22. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testAFieldMarksTheFormItBelongsToAndEveryFormOwningAFieldElsewhereIsGuarded` (app.js marks the owner;
every POST form a `form="…"` field names is guarded), `UiUnitTest::testTheMatchingBarsMenusStayInsideTheBar`,
`CheckMatchScreenTest::testStoreProductsFoldGoesOnToTheRowTheBoardShowsUnderIt`,
`MatchingPatternsScreensTest::testARefusedNewItemIsDrawnWithMoreAndItsDetailsOpen` and `::testAStoreProductsEyebrowIsTheListItWasOpenedFrom`.
`CheckMatchScreenTest`'s pin of Store Products' Open now has the list in its address.

**W13.21. A settings row's value and version are read together.** The settings page read every setting's version, then the names of who
changed them, then the values: another person's save in between drew the new value with the old version, and the row's valid save was
refused (409 changed_meanwhile). `Settings::allWithVersions()` reads each value with its version in ONE statement (one read view; the
sessions are READ COMMITTED, so two statements are two snapshots), first of the page's reads, never from rows read earlier.
`ReportsSettingsPatternsScreensTest::testASettingsRowsValueAndVersionAreReadTogether` puts another reviewer's save exactly between the
page's reads: the row shows a value with its own version, and its save is refused only when it did not see the other's.

## Polish after the final Chrome check, 30 Oct (branch `polish`, 30 Oct 2026; DC33-DC39)

The coordinator's final Chrome check of staging `1b9a695` found five small differences from the owner's rules of 30 Oct ("strictly follow
our design guidelines"; "dont need tab view use sidebar and sub section", DC28). Layout and words only: no route, permission, parameter,
query, setting or service rule changed; every address, filter link, CSV and bookmark reads as before. Each was shown failing first
(`runs/polish_red.log`: 14 of 15 tests fail on main `1b9a695` with the new tests).

**DC33. The store is a choice of the page's ONE Show row, not a tab row.** Waiting for a second OK, Store orders, Dispatch, Returns and
Reservations drew the store tab row (`store_seg`: "All stores | Electrofag | Vape and Go | Vape Big" with counts). Each now has the store
as a select in its Show row (`form.toolbar .tb-state`), beside the choices it had: the same `channel` parameter and values (the store's
code; "All stores" sends it empty, which every controller reads as no store, as the tab's link without one), the options from the same
`ReviewController::storeItems`, the count in the option's label ("Vape Big (12)", as the matching pages since W12.5), the one shown
`selected` (never a link: CV13). The hidden `channel` the forms carried beside the tab row went (it would send the store twice). The Show
button sends it without a script, with the row's other fields: the list's state, way in, days, Dispatch's list, Returns' kind, the
search, so a store chosen keeps them as the tab links did (Dispatch's list goes as `show=waiting`, its own default: W10.10). Waiting for a
second OK had no Show row: its store is the plain Show choice of To review's overview (one filter, `action="/ui/review"`, its
`queue=pending` hidden). What a number counts is the select's hover text (`BULK store_count_title`: "The number beside each store: paid
orders waiting to ship"), the words the tabs carried for a screen reader. The partial `store_seg.php` is removed: nothing else used it.
Store orders' row is now state, way in, From, To, store and Show: on a phone it wraps as before (W10.7), each control its share.

**DC34. ONE "?" beside a heading.** Store orders showed two: its own help (`aside: $explain('sales_orders', …)`) and DC1's look-only "?"
(`Words::INTRO_LOOK`). A page with its own help now has the look-only line as that "?"'s last paragraph (`Html::helpWithLook`, from
`View::head`; the whole is `details.help.look-only`, its name the help's own); a page with only one of them is as before. It changes
every page whose head has both: Store orders, Dispatch and Reservations always; Purchase orders, Goods in, the stock records, incidents,
warehouses, the cards and Waiting for a second OK for a person who can only look; Approvals with its own line (`more:`).

**DC35. The count sheet's lines are its Show choice.** An open sheet drew `nav.tabs.show-tabs` (Every line, Not counted yet, Counted) over
its lines; CT_Sheet draws no tab row. It is a Show form over the lines now (GET, `action` the sheet, the same `show` values: all, todo,
done; its Show button; the one shown selected). Typed counts are never lost: the form carries `data-leaves`, so while the quantities
form holds a number typed and not saved, app.js stops the first press and says so in the form (the same guard as the scan box and the
other forms, GV11, CV14); the second press goes on. A choice changed but not sent changes nothing.

**DC36. Counts' "Sold a day" is CT_Board's "Sells a week".** The board showed the plan's sales figure as stored (216.3417 units a day).
CT_Board's column is "Sells a week" in whole units: the same figure (`reorder_demand.rate`) times 7, rounded half up, "under 1" when
something sells but less than half a unit a week: the item page's rule (`ItemController::weekly`, IV3), so the two pages agree. A pure
display change: the query, the plan's order and the setting are as before.

**DC37. A record's eyebrow has one separator after its list.** The matching decision page's eyebrow read "Store products › · Electrofag ·
8,767 to match": `Html::statement` put " · " before the tag after the "›". With `back:` the tag follows the "›" ("Store products ›
Electrofag · 8,767 to match"); without it, the section and its tag keep their " · ". Every page with `back:` was checked (seventeen
templates): only the matching page passes a tag with it, so it was the only page with the double separator; no template draws "›" itself.

**DC38. The sweep: no page-level tab or segment row is left.** Every template was searched for `nav.tabs`, `role="tablist"` and a `.seg`
row. Left: the item page's tabs (`nav.tabs.item-tabs`, IT_Item draws them) and the supplier's (`nav.tabs.record-tabs`, the supplier
record): tabs inside a record a mockup draws (DC28). Gone here: the store row (DC33) and the count sheet's (DC35). Not tab rows, kept:
By Item's rows per page (`nav.rows-choice` at the toolbar's end, a size picker like the pager, U123; its current size is still a link, a
CV13 difference left for its page), Store orders' period line ("Last 7 days · Show all", one link in a sentence), the pagers, the
sidebar's `ul.nav-seg` (DC28's segments, in the menu). No tablist anywhere; app.js's `nav.tabs` code serves the two record rows.

**DC39. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testNoPageDrawsATabOrSegmentRowOutsideARecordAMockupDraws` (the sweep as a pin: a tab row only in
`item.php` and `supplier.php`, no tablist or `.seg`, no `store_seg`; the five pages' store select of the same values in their Show form
with its button and no hidden store; the sheet's guarded Show form), `testEveryPageOpensWithItsStatement` (one "?" with the look-only
line last), `testTheSharedPartsFollowTheApprovedMockups` (the eyebrow's tag after "›"). `KernelUiTestCase::storeChoice()` reads a Show
row's store as the address its button sends (path and the row's fields, empty ones left out); `SalesScreensTest`,
`ReservationsScreenTest` and `BulkScreensTest` read the store through it where they read the tab row (the same stores, counts, current
store and kept filters), and check one "?" with the page's help and who changes it. `UnsavedTabsScreensTest` pins the sheet's Show form
(no tab row, the values, the one shown, guarded, no link); `CountsScreensTest` "Sells a week" (53 for 7.5 a day, 2 for 0.25);
`MatchingPatternsScreensTest` the whole eyebrow; `DesignConformanceScreensTest` and `ItemCardScreensTest` the look-only "?" as the one
"?" (Purchase orders for an auditor; the cards' rules, then who changes them, for a buyer). The tab-link floor of
`testTheTabOfThePageShownHasNoLinkAndTheEditorsAskBeforeALinkLeaves` is 3 (the item's two and the supplier's).

## The redesign, step 1: the shared parts (branch `redesign-shared`, 30 Oct 2026; RD1-RD12)

The owner approved the redesign canvas on 30 Oct 2026 ("Yes, approve all"; `/root/cw_work/design/redesign_20261030/project/`). Step 1 is
what every page shares: the sidebar and the phone bars, the page header, the grouped pages' Show, the simple list's look and the status
pill. The page bodies are step 2 (three module builds); here they changed only where a shared part forced it (the status cell's pill).

**RD1. The sidebar is Sidebar.dc.html.** The CW tile, "Central Warehouse" and the stores' names (`channel`, in the order they joined:
`Queries::storeNames`, one small read per page); the find box; then one row per section: Home, Approvals, a divider, Items, Inventory,
Purchases, Sales, Store listings, a divider, Reports, Settings, each with its colour and icon chip (the artboard's `renderVals`: tokens
`--st-*`/`--sf-*` plus the new `--st-teal`/`--sf-teal` for Inventory; the icons are new views of the sprite, `ico-sec-<section>`), its
count a pill in its colour; the current section tinted, the only one that shows its entries (13 px, 34 px, the current one in the
section's words on its tint); the person at the bottom (a blue circle, the name, the jobs, the account menu). HM_Home's "Every day" and
"More" groups are gone (`Sections::DAILY`, `MORE`, `Words::SECTION_DESC`, `Words::TAB` with them). `Sections::MAP` is
section => entries ("tabs") => pages, in the artboard's order; every page of the old map is in it with its address, `match` and
permission unchanged (SectionsTest), and the section keys are the artboard's (`home`, `approvals`, `items`, `inventory`, `purchases`,
`sales`, `listings`, `reports`, `settings`). Where the old pages went:

| Entry | Pages (its Show choices) | Was |
|---|---|---|
| Items › Items | All items `/ui/items/cards` (+ item pages, search, the one-page form `/ui/items/new`), Made by hand `/ui/items/new?show=all` | Products › All products; Add item (More) |
| Items › Item groups, Multipacks (+ Pack links), Barcodes | as named | Products (Families and Multipacks were under More) |
| Inventory › Stock on hand, Stock history, Reserved stock, Repack | `/ui/stock`, `/movements`, `/reservations`, `/repack` | Stock › Overview, Movements; Reservations, Repack (More) |
| Inventory › Adjustments | Corrections `/ui/stock/adjustments`, Stock in, Stock out, Releases | Stock › Adjustments, Stock in, Stock out; Transfers › Releases |
| Inventory › Transfers | Transfers, Balance owed `/ui/stock/accounts` | Stock › Transfers (More) |
| Inventory › Stock counts | Items to count, Count sheets, Differences | Stock › Counts |
| Purchases › Suppliers, Purchase orders | as before | Purchasing |
| Purchases › Goods received | To receive, Checking, Issues, Duty register, Arriving | Purchasing › Goods in |
| Purchases › Purchase invoices | Invoices, To match, Delivered no invoice yet, Timed | Purchasing › Invoices (without its credit notes) |
| Purchases › Purchase returns | Returns to suppliers, Credit notes | Purchasing › Returns; Invoices › Credit notes |
| Purchases › Reorder | Suggestions, Brands, Anomalies, Suppliers, Low-stock warnings, Sales history | Purchasing › Reorder |
| Sales › Sales orders, Shipments, Sales returns | as before (the store kept across the three) | Sales › Store orders, Dispatch, Returns and cancels |
| Sales › Trade sales, Customers (+ Balances) | `/ui/stock/handovers`, `/customers`, `/balances` | Stock › Hand-overs (More) |
| Store listings › By item, Check a match | `/ui/review/products`; `/ui/review` (+ a store product's decision page) | Matching › By item (More), Mapping › To review |
| Store listings (specialist, RD6) | Simple matching, Store products, Spot check, Second approval, New variants, Duplicates | Matching |
| Approvals (one entry) | Waiting for you, Documents to review, History, Staff requests, the five queues from the stores | Approvals' five tabs |
| Reports | Inventory valuation summary, Stock summary by store, Low stock, Inventory aging, Sales by store | Reports (Stock value, Stock by store, Slow stock renamed) |
| Settings (one entry) | Company, Warehouses, Stores, Users, Roles and permissions, Approval rules, Reasons, Rules and numbers, Numbering, System checks, Audit log | Settings' seven tabs; Reports › Audit log |

A section's link opens its first entry's first page the person may open (Purchases: Suppliers, the artboard's first entry). The
"Quality" placeholder (a tab "not built yet", no route) is not drawn: the artboard has no such entry and nothing opened from it.

**RD2. The pages that belong together are ONE Show.** No tab row and no third level in the sidebar: an entry's two or more pages are its
Show choices. `View`'s `$showMenu(?array $choices = null)` draws them as `details.show-menu` > `summary.show-select` (looks like the
artboards' 44 px select, the current choice's words) + `ul.show-list` of `a.show-item` links, the current one a `span[aria-current=page]`
(no link, CV13). A real `<select>` would need a script or a form; the brief forbids a new route, and a GET form whose select names a page
would need one, so the choices are links in a menu that opens without a script. `$groupPages()` gives the choices as data so a page can
mix its own filters in (rd2: "Open invoices / To match / … / All invoices"). A page that draws no Show of its own gets the group's
under its header (`div.show-row`): `$head` leaves a slot (an HTML comment no template can print: escaping) that `View::page()` fills
after the body, so every grouped page is reachable today and a page that calls `$showMenu()` in its toolbar moves it there. The slot
draws only on a page that is one of the choices (a list), never on a record. Esc and a click elsewhere close it (app.js's small menus).
Sales keeps the store across its three entries, Check a match across the spot check and the second approval (`keep` on an entry).

**RD3. The page header.** A list is its title alone (26 px, 600, the artboards' weight; no section eyebrow, no intro) with ONE main button
and More on its right; a record has `back:` drawn as "‹ Items" (13 px, muted; the "‹" is the stylesheet's so the link's words are the
list's name: the tests read them), its status pill beside the title (`chips:`), one fact line under it (`meta:`, 14 px muted) and its
actions on the right (`side:`). An eyebrow a page names itself (Home's date, an error's code) is still drawn; a record's tag follows its
back link after " · " (DC37's "Store products · Electrofag · 8,767 to match").

**RD4. Inventory's groups.** Adjustments holds the four kinds of stock change, as Inventory.dc.html's Show lists them: corrections (the
`/ui/stock/adjustments` page, "Corrections" in the Show), stock in, stock out and releases; its link opens the adjustments themselves.
`/ui/stock/accounts` (the balance owed to another account) stays with Transfers: it is another account's room and what we owe it (an
account-to-account matter, the words staff know as "Transfers › Balance owed"), and Adjustments' Show in the artboard lists only kinds of
stock change, where a money page would be the odd one out. Its page keeps its "Release stock" for each account.

**RD5. The phone.** The top bar of Phone.dc.html: the CW tile (Home), the current section's name, Find (the item search) and Menu (the
same sidebar as the drawer, `#menu`, no script); the person's initials are no longer there (Sign out is in the drawer). The bottom bar:
Home, Receive (Goods received), Count (Stock counts), Approvals, More (the drawer), each only for the people who may open it
(`Sections::PHONE`), the current one in the accent; 72 px, 44 px targets.

**RD6. Store listings' specialist pages.** Only By item and Check a match are the section's entries (the owner). Simple matching, Store
products, Spot check, Second approval, New variants and Duplicates belong to the section (it is marked on their pages) and are listed,
with their counts and their lines (`MENU_HELP`), under the header's More of the section's list pages (`View::head`, `split.php`), so every
one of them is reachable now; step 2 builds the Product matching page's own More from the same data (`pagebar['more']`).

**RD7. Approvals and Settings are one entry each; the audit log is a Settings page.** Approvals' five tabs and Settings' seven are one Show
each (the artboard draws neither with sub-items). Approvals' count is still its inbox's, counted once (`'count' => 'inbox'` now names the
page). The audit log moves from Reports to Settings (Settings.dc.html's list), with the same permission (`audit.view`): admin, whose only
report it was, now has no Reports section and reaches the log through Settings.

**RD8. The simple list and the status pill, shared.** Every board at once, by CSS: a group's heading is a 10 px dot in its colour, the
name 15 px semi-bold in ink, the count in muted words; the card has 12 px corners and no coloured edge; the head row 12 px muted (500),
rows 14 px with 14 px padding. The status is a pill everywhere: `.chip` (and so `$chip`, `$stateChip`) is now the tone's tint with its
darker words, fully rounded (Items.dc.html's `pill`), a little wider beside a record's title. A board's status cell no longer fills:
`td.doc-st` keeps the tone and holds the pill (`<span class="chip">`, which takes the cell's tone); the 54 status cells of the templates
were changed to hold it (a template's one line each; o-sub lines stay under the pill). Goods in's duty answer is a select in the cell's
tint; app.js writes "All fine" into the check cell's pill, not over it. The phone's "keep the cell's fill" rules (W10.12, W10.13) went
with the fill.

**RD9. The find box searches items.** `/ui/search` finds warehouse items (name, barcode, CW number) and store products; it does not find
orders, so the box says "Find an item", not the artboard's "Find an item or an order" (needs a build: an order search). Its edge, like
every field's, stays CW's `--field` (3:1 for WCAG 1.4.11), not the artboard's lighter #d9d0e1.

**RD10. No figure tiles on a list.** The owner's rule (figures only on Home and the reports): a list page (an entry's own page outside
Home and Reports, `Sections::frame`'s `list`, `main.work.is-list`) does not draw its `.rp-figs` strip (CSS; the markup and its tests stay
for step 2). A record (the item's stock card, a purchase order's progress) and the reports keep theirs.

**RD11. The words.** `Words::SECTION` and `NAV` (the phone bar) are the artboards'; `MENU` (an entry's name, also its page's title and the
way back to it) and `SEGMENT` (the Show's words) are renamed in sentence case: Items (was All products), Item groups (Families), Stock on
hand (Overview), Stock history (Movements), Reserved stock (Reservations), Stock counts (Counts), Goods received (Goods in), Purchase
invoices (Invoices), Purchase returns (Returns), Sales orders (Store orders), Shipments (Dispatch), Sales returns (Returns and cancels),
Trade sales (Hand-overs), Check a match (Mapping), Inventory valuation summary (Stock value), Stock summary by store (Stock by store),
Inventory aging (Slow stock); Show: Items to count (Next to count), Delivered, no invoice yet (Not invoiced yet), Corrections, Made by
hand, Rules and numbers, Audit log. The Items page's create button is "New item" (`NEW add_item`), as the artboard's "+ New item".

**RD12. Tests.** `SectionsTest` (rewritten): every page a live route with its permission and words; every staff page's section, entry and
page; each job's menu; the sidebar tree, its counts, the phone bar and the bell; the Show choices, the header's More, the kept store and
the create buttons; and `testEveryPageAPersonMayOpenIsReachedFromHome`: from Home, following only what the shell draws (the sidebar, a
group's Show, Store listings' More), every page each job may open is reached, for all 14 jobs and three job sets. `UiTemplatesTest`
(the layout's sidebar and bars as drawn, the statement with its Show row and slot, the back link), `UiUnitTest` (the sidebar's, the
pill's, the board's and the header's CSS), and the kernel helpers: `segments()` reads the page's Show, `moreTabs()` the header's More,
`sectionTabs()` the open section's entries. The old pins of HM_Home's sidebar, the tab-row More, the solid cell and the eyebrow were
moved to these.

## The Purchases and Sales pages on the approved redesign (step 2 B, branch `redesign-rd2b`, 30 Oct 2026; RD-B1-RD-B10)

The owner approved the redesign canvas on 30 Oct 2026 ("Yes, approve all"; `cw_work/design/redesign_20261030/project/`). This build brings
its Purchases and Sales artboards (Purchases, PurchaseOrder, GoodsReceived, PurchaseInvoices, Sales) to their pages and the simple list
look to the other Purchases and Sales lists. Layout only: every route, permission, posted field, total, server rule, FormOnce and version
check is as before. It was built at the same time as the shared step (rd1) and committed on main 8acedfb, so where a shared piece was not
on main it uses rd1's announced shape (`td.c-status.doc-st` holding `span.chip`; the group heading's count) and draws the look itself in
the `rd2b` CSS block, scoped by `.rd-list` on a list's group (RD-B9).

**RD-B1. Purchase orders is the simple list of Purchases.dc.html.** Five columns: Order (its number, the row's link), Supplier, Status
(a small pill), Expected, Total; the received meter, the initials (By) and the order's date and reference after its number are gone (the
date, the reference and who made it are on the order; the reference is still searched). A part delivery's pill says how much came ("28
of 30 received", `ORDERS part_of`: the old Received column's figure), a cancellation record's says so; a reviewer's "not OK" stays under
the pill. The groups keep their meaning and names (waiting for approval, on the way, draft, received or closed lately, cancelled): the
artboard's "Received this month" would be untrue, the window is `po.board_recent_days`. No "+ New purchase order" row at a group's end:
the head's button is the one way (the add row of every list in this build goes the same way). The search, the Show menu, More (drafts
too, download, clear) and every URL filter are as before.

**RD-B2. Purchase invoices is the simple list of PurchaseInvoices.dc.html.** Five columns: Invoice (the supplier's number), Supplier,
Status, Due (how late beside it, red once passed with money owed), Total. The status pill says what the invoice's own page says (Needs a
look, Draft, Waiting for an OK, Final, Cancelled: the rule that the list and the page agree stays), the match under it ("2 differences",
"Matches", "Accepted", "Not checked yet": the old Match column), where the artboard puts the match in the pill. The Balance column is gone: CW does not know payments, so it equalled the total except after a credit note; then "£x still owed"
stands under the total (`owed_line`). The invoices' groups are named as the artboard names them, "Needs a look", "To match" (the drafts:
an invoice is matched when it is made final) and "Matched" (final; one with nothing to match says "Final" in its pill);
`InvoicesController::boardGroups($rows, $kind)`; a credit note is never matched, so its groups stay draft and final, its fourth column the
invoice it credits. The page's name is "Purchase invoices" (`INVOICE_KIND invoice tab`, also the record's back link).

**RD-B3. Sales orders is the simple list of Sales.dc.html.** Four columns: Order, Store, Placed, Units; no status column, the groups say
it: "Waiting to ship" (blue), "Shipped" (a unit of it went to the customer, green), "Returned or cancelled" (none did, grey), then the
store's orders not paid as before (reserved now, freed, ran out of time); `SalesController::GROUPS`, `SALE_GROUP`, `TONE SALE_GROUP`. A paid
order whose units ended more than one way says how under its number (the old "What became of it"); the unlinked items and the try number
stay there too. Paid and How it came in are on the order. The head's one button is Download (the artboard's; the page is read only, so
no magenta button). The Show row is one select, the stores with their paid orders waiting to ship, and its Show button; the period links,
From / To, the state and the way in are under More in the same GET form (the row's Show button sends them; More opens when one is set).
The artboard's search ("order number or item") is not built: CW has no search on this page (needs a build). Its "Today" is From and To
under More.

**RD-B4. A purchase order is the record of PurchaseOrder.dc.html.** The list's link above the number, the status pill beside it, one line
under it (the reviewer's check, then "Greenline Wholesale · ordered 19 Oct 2026 by Business owner", `ORDER fact_ordered`; a draft "started"), the
actions at the right as before (More, then the next step). The figures strip is four steps, Approved, Sent to supplier, Received,
Invoiced (`PurchaseOrdersController::steps()`): a step done is green with its day or its units, the first one not done is amber, the rest
white; the figures are `progress()`'s, unchanged, and Received says what is still to come line by line (PV24) while it is part received. The paper: three blocks, the supplier (its address on one line), Deliver to (the
company's delivery address the PDF prints: the order's snapshot once confirmed, else the details in use) and the dates (order date,
expected, payment terms from the supplier, their reference); the lines in five columns, Item (code, their code, pack, VAT code and line
under the name), Ordered (items; the packs under it when a pack holds more than one), Received (green when all came, amber in part; "N to
come" beside it while the order is open), Unit cost (the pack price; "per box of 10" under it), Line total; under them the note to the
supplier and the totals, whose rows are exactly as before (products, before VAT, VAT by code, with VAT). Related lists the order's
deliveries (the goods-received list searched by its number) and invoices (the supplier's invoices) each with a pill of how far it got, the
order it corrects or that correct it, its cancellation record (its PDF) and its files; History lists what happened, newest first (started
with how it was made, OK asked, confirmed, sent with how and to whom, closed with why, cancelled with why), then its checks and OKs as
before. The lines' downloads (Excel, CSV) and the record moved under More. The artboard's Print is not built: CW's order PDF is a download
(it stays under More; needs a build).

**RD-B5. A delivery's one page is GoodsReceived.dc.html.** The list's link above its number (a draft its title), its status pill beside
it, one line under it: the supplier, its order (a link), "N of M lines checked" and the problems when there are any; the figures strip is
gone (that line and "Book in N items" say it). The lines in four columns, Item, Expected, Received, Check (a pill), then the line's
answers: the duty stamp (its select in a small pill of its answer's colour, app.js colours it as before), "All fine", "Problem" / "Open".
The artboard's "Counted" says Received: "count" is only for shelf counts (correction b, `ReceivingWordsTest`); what is typed there is the
packs in, the items they make under them. The details, the scan box, the problem panels, the prices fold, the files, the note, "Before
it can be booked in" and the bar (Leave, what is left, Save, Book in) are as before; every field keeps its name and the one form posts
the same. A phone keeps "Leave without saving" above the head (`p.crumbs.gi-crumbs`, hidden from 700 px), the bar two rows as GV24.

**RD-B6. The other Purchases and Sales lists are simple lists.** Goods received, Suppliers, Purchase returns, Credit notes, Arriving,
Incidents, To match, Delivered no invoice yet, Timed, Shipments, Sales returns, Trade sales, Customers: three to five columns besides a
row's own action (Receive, Book its invoice, close an incident), the status a pill in its cell, no add row. What a dropped column said moved under a cell where it is still needed: a delivery being
checked "3 / 6 lines" and a booked one's incidents under its pill; a return's credit is its pill once final; arriving units "N sold
before they arrive"; to match's lines that differ, claims and who accepted under the pill; delivered-no-invoice's units under the value;
a shipment's wait under Paid, its note under the order, a sent order's units now under the pill, who undid a sending under when; a sales
return's unit under the item, where it is now under the pill; a customer's VAT code under the name. Who booked a delivery in, who made a
return, a trade sale's products and maker, an order's made-by are on their records.

**RD-B7. The reorder pages keep their figures.** What to buy, Low stock, Brand settings, Supplier lead times, Days to leave out and Sales
data get the dot heading, the plain card and the pill; their strip stays: it says when the suggestions were worked out and warns when
the sales data is old (a report's strip, dev.md pattern 5). Their columns hold the form's fields and are unchanged.

**RD-B8. A list shows no figures strip.** Shipments' five figures are each list's count in its Show choice ("Sent today (12)"; the late
ones are the Late group's count, and a late order says after how many hours it is late under its pill: `sales.late_hours`); the strip's
unit totals (units waiting, units sent today or this week) are gone, the rows give each order's. Sales returns' one figure (units to
recount) is each store's count in the store choice already (DC33).

**RD-B9. Until the shared step lands, these lists draw the shared look themselves.** `.rd-list` on a list's group: the 10 px dot, the 15 px
name, the muted count (its words as before, "2 orders": rd1 keeps `span.grp-count` as it is; the artboards' bare number would need a
word list per list, and a number with hidden words reads "22 orders" to anything that reads the text), the card without a coloured edge, the 12 px head row, 14 px rows, the cell no longer filled and its `span.chip` a
tint pill; the order's and the delivery's pills likewise. rd1 draws the same for every list; when both are in, the `.rd-list` rules and
class go (the values are the artboards', so nothing moves). app.js writes "Checked" straight into a delivery line's check cell after "All
fine" (the pill's span goes): until app.js keeps the span, that word is in the tone's ink (`td.gi-check:not(:has(.chip))`).

**RD-B10. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testThePurchasesAndSalesPagesFollowTheRedesign` (every list: scoped, its group's count, no add row,
meter, initials or strip, three to five columns, the pill in the cell; the three artboard lists' columns; the order's steps, paper, five
line columns, Related, History and More's downloads; the delivery's back link, line, no strip, columns and answers). The kernel pins of
the pages were moved to the new design where they pinned the old: `BuyingPatternsScreensTest` (the head's "+ New" instead of an add row),
`GoodsInOnePageScreensTest` and `ReceivingScreensTest` (the title's words, the back link, the line under it, the duty in the answers,
Received with the items under it, the board's pill and its lines checked), `InvoiceOnePageScreensTest` (the three lists' columns, groups,
pills; the order's steps, paper, Related, More; the part delivery's pill), `SalesScreensTest` (the groups, the rows, the Show, Download,
the Show counts instead of the strip, a late order's hours), `StockPatternsScreensTest` (Trade sales). Each fails on 8acedfb
(`runs/rd2b_red.log`: 24 of 93); every behaviour pin is unchanged.

## The redesign, step 2 part C: Product matching, Check a match, the reports, Approvals, Settings, Home (branch `redesign-rd2c`, 30 Oct 2026; RD-C1-RD-C16)

The owner approved the canvas "CW Redesign: All Modules" on 30 Oct 2026 ("Yes, approve all"; `cw_work/design/redesign_20261030/project`).
Part C builds six of its artboards: ByItem, Listings, Reports, Approvals, Settings and Main. Only these pages' templates, their controllers'
view data, a page-scoped "rd2c" block in `app.css`, their words and their tests change. No query, rule, route or permission changes.
The shared pieces (sidebar, page head, list style, phone bar) belong to step 1 (rd1). Until the branches are combined, these pages use
main's shared code, and a small page-scoped version of a shared look lives in the "rd2c" block.

**RD-C1. Check a match is ONE comparison card.** `listing.php` draws `section.card.mt-compare`. Its first row
(`div.mt-row.mt-heads`) has the store product's column (`div.mt-side.mt-store`: its blue dot, "On the store", the name, "Variant N ·
price") and our item's column (`div.mt-side.mt-item`: its green dot, "Our item" for the suggestion, else what the column holds: the item
you picked, the item it is matched to, what a waiting decision does; then the name as a link, "CW-… · N in stock" and the protected or
refused-before tags). After it comes one `div.mt-row.mt-fact` per fact, with four cells: the label, the store's value, our value, and a
mark. The mark is a green tick (`span.mt-mark.same`, role img, "Same") where the two sides agree, or an amber "!" (`.diff`, "Differs")
where they differ or one side does not say. A row that differs is tinted (`.diff`, #fffaf1). The facts keep the old order (brand,
line, flavour, strength, pack, then the rest). A store product with no item to compare lists its own facts with our column empty. The
old photo blocks ("No photo") are gone: the artboard has none.

**RD-C2. The head is the question and one line.** The head shows "Is this the same item?" and under it "<store> · N left to check"
(`MATCH to_match`, now "%s left to check"). The list's progress words stay on that line (`span.mt-line[data-progress]`) for a screen
reader and the tests. The list's progress bar is gone (the line says how many are left). A spot check's 20 blocks stay at the head's
right (`listing_progress`), because they belong to the spot check. The way back to the list stays as the head's `back:` (step 1 draws it
as "‹ list").

**RD-C3. Under the card: "Not this one? Find another item" and "1 sale on the store is N of our item".** These sit side by side in
`div.mt-pick`. The search is still its own GET form (`form="mt-find"`). The units are the decision form's `units_per_item` as before.
The search's results and "N other suggestions" (`details.mt-others#cand`, its "Use" links) follow under them. The why-evidence's
`#cand-…` links still reach it.

**RD-C4. The note is under the bar's More.** The artboard draws no note, and the rule "what an artboard does not show goes under More"
applies. It is the same field of the same form (`name="reason"`, `#f-reason`), so the form posts exactly what it posted before. When a
note is refused, More opens on it (`$noteOpen`) and the error's "go to the field" link reaches it.

**RD-C5. The bar: Skip at the left; More, Not the same and Same item at the right.** More stays. It holds New item, Ignore, "It is a
landing page", Change this match, the note and the evidence (`listing_more`): nothing of the page is removed.

**RD-C6. Nothing about deciding changes.** The one decision form, its hidden fields and its answers (the button pressed) are as before:
`expected_map_version`, the proposal, the item, `seen`, the way back, and the disabled hidden default button. The second OK, pack units,
protected items, one-at-a-time and the spot check's own three answers are untouched (template and words only;
`ReviewController` adds only the way back to the New on the stores tab, RD-C7).

**RD-C7. Product matching has two tabs: By item and New on the stores.** The owner asked for these (the one tab row outside a record,
`nav.tabs.bi-tabs`; the tab shown has no link). The page title is "Product matching" with "Which store sells each item" under it.
New on the stores (`/ui/review/products?tab=new`, the same route and permission) lists the stores' products first seen in New variants'
period (`mapping.new_variants_days`) that are still to match. It reads them with New variants' own reads (`Queries::seenRange`,
`newVariantCounts`, `newVariants`, `newVariantRows`). Its count is the tab's number, so both tabs make those reads, about two small reads
a store.

The tab has a search and the store choice, each store with its count; "All stores" is not offered (the reads are per store; needs a
build). Each row shows the name, "<store> · added <day>", the likely match (the suggested item with its strength on the amber pill,
otherwise what the computer said, on the grey one) and Match, which opens the product's own decision page. That page's way back leads to
this tab (`ReviewController::back`). "Match all new" is the tab's one main button, for whoever may decide. It opens New variants for the
store shown: CW's way to match or create many at once is that page's bar. A store that does not exist answers 404, as New variants does.

**RD-C8. The page's More holds every other matching page.** These are Store products, Simple matching, To review, Spot check, Second
approval, New variants and Duplicates (`ByProductController::morePages`; all `linking.view`, this page's permission). By item's list
file and its rows a page (50 / 100 / 200, the current one not a link) are there too.

**RD-C9. A By item row is the item and a chip per store.** The row's name links to the item's page. Its line is "CW-… · brand · N of
M stores". Each store has one chip:

- green with a tick: matched. Someone who may decide goes to that store's picker, which shows the match and lets them match one more
  variant ("Match another…" was there). Anyone else goes to the variant's page.
- amber: waiting for a second OK. It opens the variant's page.
- dashed "+ Store": a suggestion waits. It opens the suggestion's page with the way back (the old "Review").
- dashed "+ Store" as the quick match's fold (`details.quick-pick.bi-quick`): not on the store, for someone who may decide. Its
  search runs in place with the script, and its GET form opens the picker without it. For anyone else it is a plain dashed name.

The cell's other lines (the variant, its strength, a sale's units, on hold, also waiting or suggested, more variants) are in the chip's
title and its screen-reader words. An item on hold is amber. The bulk ticks stay on the row (a function), and "Select all on this page"
is at the top of the card. The bar, the preview and the apply are unchanged.

**RD-C10. The filters are only what the page supports.** The artboard draws Store, Match status, Brand, Kind and Stock. CW's By item has
ONE filter (`cov`), whose choices already name the store ("Missing on Electrofag"). So it is one select (all, on every store, missing
on each store, a suggestion waiting, each with its count) with its Show button and "Clear filters". A separate store filter, "On no
store", Brand, Kind and Stock are needs-a-build.

**RD-C11. One report layout for the five reports and the duty register.** Each has:

- "‹ All reports" (the head's `back:` to `#all-reports`: no page lists the reports, so the link leads to the list on the same page),
  the title (the artboard's names, `RD_REPORTS`), and Export at the right.
- The options card (`form.card.rp-options`): only the options each report has, each with its label above it, and Run report (the
  magenta button).
- The report (`article.card.rp-paper`). Its centred head (`report_paper_head`) shows the company's name from CW's company details
  ("<name> · Central Warehouse"; with no name, Central Warehouse alone), the report's name, its line (the day or the days, how it is
  run) and the lines its figure strip used to show. Then a plain `table.rp-table`:
  - a group is a heading row (`tr.rp-group`) with its rows indented and its total (`tr.rp-gtotal`);
  - the report's Total row (`tr.rp-total`, under a 2 px rule) is drawn where CW has the total: the value and units of all stock
    unfiltered, a store's units it can sell, each brand or warehouse view, the sales totals, the duty register's lines and its two groups;
  - otherwise the Total row is the number of items.
- "All reports" (`report_all`): Inventory, Sales and Purchases, each report behind its route's permission
  (`ReportsController::shared`), the one shown not a link. Reorder suggestions links to the reorder list.

The figure strips are gone (the artboard: figure tiles only on Home), and their figures are in the report's head.

**RD-C12. Left out of the report layout (needs a build).**

- Print: a button needs a script, and the page must work without one. The browser's own print works: the print style leaves out the menus.
- Excel and PDF: CW makes only the CSV for reports.
- "As of" a past date: the valuation is today's.
- A warehouse filter on the valuation: it groups by warehouse but does not filter by it.
- The artboard's items under brand headings: CW has the brand totals and the item list, not both at once.

**RD-C13. Approvals: Show = kind.** The heading's right has a GET form (`form.ap-show`) offering "Everything waiting (N)" or one kind,
each with its count. `?show=` keeps only that kind's group, and every count is still read. Rows keep it. An answer carries it
(`inbox_show`, read by `InboxController::answered` and `refused`), so the list stays on that kind. The record's figures are tiles. The
first tile is in the kind's tint, and a rise is on the green tint (`.rd-inbox`, scoped: the other inboxes keep their look). The note's
label is above it. "Next: …" sits at the left of More and the main answer. "Answered today" is needs-a-build: the inbox lists only what
waits.

**RD-C14. One settings shell.** Every settings page (17 templates) draws `settings_nav` at the left of `div.set-main`. The ten sections
appear in the artboard's order, each behind the permission its route checks; the one shown is tinted and not a link. Users and roles
opens the people, or who can do what for someone who may not see the people. The cards' headings sit on the quiet fill in a topic colour,
taken in turn. The rows (name, "Not agreed yet", the value, its unit, Why, Save) keep their own form and fields (W13.9).

**RD-C15. Home.** The parts, top to bottom:

- The date and the greeting, with Receive a delivery (`doc.GRN.post`) and "+ New purchase order" (`doc.PO.post`, the main button)
  beside them.
- Four tinted tiles (`DashboardTiles`): the stock value at cost (`values.view`, the valuation report's own figures), the units on the
  shelf, what waits for this person's OK (Approvals' badge and its biggest kind), and the listings to match. For fewer permissions, the
  figures Home showed before fill in.
- "Waiting for you" with "· N jobs" and Open Approvals; each task row is a link with its action at the right (no magenta row: the
  page's main button is the new order).
- The Stores card (`system.view`): each store's mode in CW and when its connector was last heard from (`Queries::storeLink`).
- The Today card: only figures CW has. These are the store orders taken today and their units (`reports.view`, the sales report's
  day), the deliveries being checked (`receiving.view`) and the oversold records (`queues.oversell`'s badge).

"Deliveries expected" is needs-a-build. Home's Find box is gone: the artboard draws none, and step 1's sidebar has "Find an item or an
order". A phone shows the greeting and "Waiting for you", as the Phone artboard does.

**RD-C16. Tests.** `tests/Unit/RedesignCTemplatesTest.php` pins each page's parts in its template. The old pins of these pages in
`UiTemplatesTest` are moved there. `tests/Integration/UiKernel/RedesignCScreensTest.php` pins:

- the comparison card, its marks, the find and units row, the note under More, and the form's fields as before;
- the two tabs, the New tab's rows and its way back, the chips, and More's pages;
- a report's layout, Total row and All reports per permission;
- Approvals' Show kept through an answer;
- the settings list per role;
- Home's tiles, buttons and cards.

The existing screen tests of these pages read the new markup.

## The Items and Inventory pages on the approved redesign (branch `redesign-rd2a`, 30 Oct 2026; RD-A1-RD-A9)

The owner approved the redesign canvas on 30 Oct 2026 ("Yes, approve all"; `cw_work/design/redesign_20261030/project/`). This build is step 2
for the Items and Inventory pages, on the artboards Items, Item, Inventory (Adjustments) and Counts (Stock counts), and the same simple list on
every other page of the two sections. Layout and view data only: every address, permission, posted field, rule and safety message is as before.

**RD-A1. Built on 8acedfb without step 1.** The shared pieces of step 1 (the sidebar, the page header, the pill status, the dot group heading,
the grouped-pages Show helper) are another branch built at the same time (`redesign-shared`). On the coordinator's word (30 Oct: finish on
8acedfb, do not wait), the two pieces these pages need are page-scoped here and go when step 1's own are in: `views/rda_show.php` (the ONE Show
choice) and `views/rda_bar.php` (the head's More and ONE main button), styled in the "rd2a" block at the end of `app.css`. The group heading,
the table card and the status cell keep the shared classes (`.doc-group`, `.grp-title`, `.doc-board`, `td.doc-st`), so step 1's restyle reaches
these pages unchanged.

**RD-A2. One search, ONE Show choice, More, ONE main button.** A list's Show is a menu of links drawn as the artboards' select (the More menu's
engine, `details.more.show-pick`: no script needed, Esc and a click elsewhere close it); the choice shown is not a link (CV13); each choice is
another page of the group or the same page with its filter, the search and the other filters kept. What the artboard does not show goes under
the head's More: the filters of before as a GET form in a fold ("More filters", open in the menu when one the Show choice does not name is on,
the Show button then saying "Chosen filters"), Clear, Import, the download, the other links. The head's right is More, then the page's ONE main
button (its "+ New …", a `#new` link to the create fold of before). GET forms carry no `action` (they send to the page itself), so a test's
`form('<path>')` still finds the page's POST form.

**RD-A3. Items.** Three columns (the item: its name opens it, its CW number under it; the status label; on hand) in the artboard's three
groups: Needs a look (a blocked card, "Blocked" in red, or a card still to confirm, "Check the card" in amber), No card yet ("No card"), Ready
("Ready", a confirmed card); most stock first in each. Show: All items, Holding stock (`stock=1`), Needs a look (`state=unconfirmed`: a card
not confirmed or no card), Made by hand (`/ui/items/new?show=all`, which shows the same Show and the title Items). A block's rules and a
warning stay a small line under the name (safety). Left the list, kept elsewhere: the card's six columns (the item page's LEGAL, the CSV) and
"Fill in the card" (the item page's Change). The search box says "name, brand or CW number": it does not find barcodes (the artboard's
placeholder names them: needs a build).

**RD-A4. The item page is one page in sections.** No tab row: the head (back to Items, the name with its status label, the fact line "CW
number · brand · size · strength and nicotine type", More and the ONE main button: Order more, else Count it, else Move stock; the others under
More), the stock card (on the shelf; held for orders, a link to Reserved stock when some are held; free to sell, with "includes N on its way"
when it does; coming in, with "Sells about N a week" and the first order coming), Details (PRODUCT: what the matching knows, the stock rule,
when it was added and last counted; BUYING, for who sees suppliers: the main supplier, the box it is bought in, the average cost so far
(`CostHints::average`, the figure a release's price falls back to); LEGAL: every field of the product card and the card's state; under them the
card's rules, its confirmation, the file's flavour and the suggestions, as before; Change opens the card's form), the recent stock history
(when, what and its record, the units; All history). Beside them: Store listings (each store, its state, the store product matched there and
Change, or Match… for who may decide; Matching opens By item for the item), Barcodes (+ Add opens the add form; each barcode "single" or "box
of N", its Change holds the items per scan and Remove), Suppliers (each with Main, the box and the last price). What the tabs held that the
artboard does not draw is a closed fold under the history: Stock in each warehouse, Selling on the stores (the website products with their
history, the selling-mode switch), Item group and packs, Card history. `ItemController::PARTS`/`openPart()` open the fold a refused form, a
notice (`NOTICE_PARTS`) or an old `?tab=` link names (`OLD_TABS`); the Barcodes' add form opens after a refused add. Left: "lasts about N
weeks", the held figure's paid/unpaid split (Reserved stock shows it), who made each change in the recent history (All history shows it).

**RD-A5. Adjustments and Transfers.** Stock in, Stock out, Corrections (`/ui/stock/adjustments`) and Releases are one page to staff, titled
Adjustments, the kind its Show choice (each its own address, the filters kept; the artboard's "All kinds" has no page: needs a build). Groups:
Waiting for an OK, Draft, Done this week (made final since Monday 00:00, UK time), then, when the list holds them, Done before this week,
Cancelled, Cancellation records, Stopped. Four columns: the record (its number opens it, its date under it), the kind, the reason (a stock in's
or out's reason, a release's account; a correction's reasons are on its lines: "On each line"), the units (stock in "+N" green, stock out
"−N" red; a correction's lines go both ways and a release moves stock between rooms: no sign). The state and the warehouse are under More,
with Goods received on Stock in. Transfers keep their page: Show = the state; Transfer, From, To, Units.

**RD-A6. Stock counts.** Items to count, Count sheets and Differences are one page to staff, titled Stock counts, the view its Show choice. Items
to count: Overdue (red) and Never counted (grey, the artboard's dot; it was purple), each heading the plan's figure; four columns (the tick,
the item, last counted, sells a week; the status column went: the group says it). The bar: "N ticked", More (the next N due or everything
found, an empty sheet, the shelf, a note) and ONE main button "Count the ticked items" (`mode=ticked`); Enter in a field counts the ticked items
(the hidden first button). The warehouse and how many to list are under the head's More with the plan's days; "Open sheets (N)" beside it.
Count sheets: four columns (the sheet with what waits on it, where, counted of lines with the units changed, who opened it), the Filter of
before under More. Differences: five columns (the item with its sheet, the difference with what CW held and what was counted, who counted,
why it waits, the answer); the approval rules under More; the second-check line stays (safety).

**RD-A7. Every other Items and Inventory page.** Item groups (Show: in use / with the switched-off ones), Multipacks (Show: pack items in use,
with the switched-off ones, Pack links for who may look at matching), Barcodes (Show: waiting / decided), Repack (Show: the state; four
columns), Reserved stock (Show: the state; the store under More; five columns: the order with when it started, the store, the status, the
units with how many products, until when it is kept and what became of it), Stock history (Show: the kind of change; the warehouse and the
figure under More; five columns, the record and who under what changed), Stock on hand (Show: with stock / every item / below zero; the
warehouse under More; five columns: one On hand figure, every warehouse together or the one chosen; each warehouse's own is on the item page).
No figures strip on a list (the owner: tiles only on Home), no "+ Add" row (the head's main button), a group's count is a figure.

**RD-A8. Words.** `Words::INV_LIST` (the lists) and `Words::ITEM_PAGE` (the item page) hold the artboards' names; nothing else changed name.

**RD-A9. Tests.** `tests/Integration/UiKernel/InventoryRedesignScreensTest.php` (shown failing first on 8acedfb: the lists' simple shape, their
groups, columns, Show choices and More; the counts bar; the item page's sections and folds) and the pins of before brought to the new shape
(`ItemPageScreensTest`, `ItemPageUnitTest`, `ItemCardScreensTest`, `ProductPatternsScreensTest`, `StockPatternsScreensTest`, `CountsScreensTest`,
`UiTemplatesTest` and the others the full suite named).

## The redesign integrated (branch `redesign-all`, 30 Oct 2026; RD-I1-RD-I8)

The four builds of the approved redesign (rd1 `redesign-shared`, rd2b `redesign-rd2b`, rd2c `redesign-rd2c`, rd2a `redesign-rd2a`), each one
commit on 8acedfb, merged in that order with `--no-ff` (each builder's commit kept as it is), then the integration's own changes. rd1 owns the
shared code; the module pages keep their templates and are switched onto rd1's shared pieces.

**RD-I1. The stand-ins went.** rd2b's `.rd-list` (the class on 21 lists and its rules: the dot heading, the plain card, the unfilled status
cell, the pill) is rd1's look for every list (RD8). rd2c's `.bi-hint` pill is the shared `.chip` (`needs` for the likely match, `waiting`
otherwise; the class stays for its place). rd2a's `rda_show` and `rda_bar` are rd1's Show and header More (RD-I8). The delivery's check cell on a
phone was still the old solid block (GV23): it holds its pill now, no fill. Home's Find box went with rd2c (the sidebar's find box, RD9;
the phone's top bar keeps Find): its CSS went too.

**RD-I2. ONE Show per page.** rd1's head draws the group's Show under the title only when the page draws none (RD2). A grouped page with a
toolbar now draws it there:
- A page whose own filter is a GET form (rd2b's and rd2c's pages: Goods received, Issues, Purchase invoices and credit notes, To match,
  Delivered no invoice yet, Purchase returns, Customers, What to buy, Low stock, Documents to review, History, the stores' queues, Approvals'
  kind) puts `$showStart()` and `$showEnd()` around its `div.tb-state`: ONE `details.show-menu` whose panel (`div.show-panel`) lists the
  group's pages, then the page's own fields and Show button (its `div.tb-state`), in the same GET form as the search. Every field keeps its
  name and value; with fewer than two pages in the group the two draw nothing (the `div.tb-state` as before). History's pop-over Show
  (DC27) is its fields in that panel.
- A page whose own choices are links (rd2a's pages) draws `$showMine($choices, $other)` (RD-I8).
- Settings' section list (RD-C14) is the Settings group's way between its pages (`$showNav()`): no Show row on a settings page.
- A grouped page without a toolbar (Arriving, Timed, the duty register, Brand settings and the other reorder pages, Balances, Staff
  requests) keeps the head's Show row.
`MenusTest`'s crawl now also checks that no page it reaches draws two Shows or two Mores in its header.

**RD-I3. ONE More.** Product matching draws its own actions beside its title (`side:`), so rd1's head draws no More there; its More lists the
section's specialist pages as the header's More does elsewhere (`$sectionMore()`: Simple matching, Store products, Spot check, Second
approval, New variants, Duplicates, with their counts and lines), then the list's file and its rows a page. `ByProductController::morePages()`
went (it also listed "To review", which is the sidebar's Check a match).

**RD-I4. /ui/review is titled as the sidebar names it**: "Check a match" (`MENU review`), also its page title and the way back from a batch
or an unknown store product (rd1's open point).

**RD-I5. What to buy and Low stock keep their figures strip.** rd1 hides a list's strip (RD10, the owner's rule); rd2b kept the reorder
pages' strips (RD-B7) because they say when the suggestions were worked out and warn when the sales data is old or the last run failed. A
safety message is never removed: those two strips are `.rp-keep` and stay; the other reorder pages' strips (no warning in them) are hidden
as RD10 says.

**RD-I6. The status cells.** rd1 put `span.chip` in 54 cells; where rd2b and rd2c rewrote the same rows their templates were kept (they
hold the pill already, or draw it with `$chip`); the delivery's duty stamp is in the line's answers (RD-B5), so rd1's pill in the old duty
cell and its CSS went.

**RD-I7. Tests.** `UiTemplatesTest::testOneShowHoldsThePagesOwnFieldsAndTheHeadDrawsNoSecond` (the helpers on a page of their own),
