## The redesign's fix round (branch `redesign-fixes`, 30 Oct 2026; RD-F1-RD-F11)

The Codex review of the integrated redesign (8cba061, on staging) and the coordinator's Chrome check. Each fix has a test that failed first
(`runs/rdfix_red.log`).

**RD-F1. Enter sends the main answer on every Approvals record.** Since the redesign the record's answers are "Next", More, then the main
answer, so More's buttons of the same form (Reject a count difference, Dismiss a correction or a mode change, a note on an oversold order)
came first in the page's order and Enter in a field sent the rarer one. The answer form now starts with a hidden twin of the main answer
(`button.po-default`, the same name and value, no other route; out of the tab order and hidden from a screen reader), the pattern of the
other one-form pages. `ApprovalsInboxScreensTest::testEnterSendsTheMainAnswerOnEveryKind` opens every record of every kind and checks the
form's first submit button.

**RD-F2. A purchase order's Related links only to what the person may open.** Goods received needs `receiving.view` (a buyer has not),
the invoices `invoices.view` (goods in has not), a file `documents.view`: without it the row keeps its words and its pill, with no link.

**RD-F3. Items' Show says what each choice holds.** The group "Needs a look" holds the cards still to confirm and the blocked ones, and a
confirmed card can be blocked; its one Show choice sent `state=unconfirmed`, which leaves those out. The Show now has two truthful choices,
"Not confirmed" (`state=unconfirmed`: a card not confirmed, or none) and "Blocked" (the existing `blocked=1`); the group keeps its name.
Made by hand's Show says the same.

**RD-F4. A cancellation record moves the units the other way on the list.** A stock in's cancellation record takes them off (−, red), a stock
out's puts them back (+, green): `StockOpsController::unitsWay($kind, $cancellation)` (`reverses_id`).

**RD-F5. A filter on is said on its closed control.** ONE Show holds a grouped page's own fields in its panel (RD-I2) and a list's More its
filter fold (RD-I8): both were closed with nothing to say a filter was on. The closed Show now shows how many of its fields are on (a select
not on its first choice, a ticked box, a filter kept from the address: `View::filtersOn`, worked out from the fields as drawn), and the
closed More how many of the list's filters are (`split.php`, when its fold is open), each a count with "filters on" (DC27's words).

**RD-F6. A kind with nothing left keeps its Show.** Answering the last record of the kind shown kept `inbox_show`, but the kind left the
choices, so the Show fell back to "Everything waiting" while the page said nothing was waiting. The kind shown stays a choice (0) and the page
says nothing under that kind waits, how many wait under the others, and links to everything waiting.

**RD-F7. An empty report still says how fresh its figures are.** Sales by store, Inventory aging and the valuation drew their "brought up to
date … / not yet / switched off" line only in the report's head, which an empty report does not draw: it is now said above the empty state too.

**RD-F8. Home reads no whole valuation.** The stock value tile summed every balance with its average cost on every Home load. CW keeps no
stored total of it, so the tile is not drawn: Home's four are the units, what waits for the person's OK, the listings to match and, filling
in, the open orders. Needs a build: a valuation total kept by the reports' refresh (then the tile can come back as the artboard draws it).

**RD-F9. By item counts no new store products.** The New on the stores tab's number was worked out on every By item load (two reads a store,
more after an import); it is now counted only on the open New tab (its store choice needs those reads anyway), and By item's tab has no number.

**RD-F10. By item's search and filter are one row.** The search, the match status and its Show button share the toolbar's row and wrap on a
phone (the Chrome check: they were stacked full width under the search).

**RD-F11. New on the stores stays per store.** "All stores" would need New variants' reads across every store merged and paged together (one
read per store is what CW has): not built (needs a build, as RD-C7 says); the store choice lists each store with its count.

**RD-S1. Simple matching is Product matching's second tab** (the owner, 31 Oct 2026, on the design canvas: "this page add in product
matching another tab"). Product matching's tabs are By item | Simple matching | New on the stores (`by_product_tabs`, plain links, the

## "Confirm all ready" for ERPNext corrections (branch `confirm-all`, 31 Oct 2026; CA1-CA12)

The owner, 31 Oct 2026: "Design a Confirm-all", then on the design (the approved boards `ConfirmAll.dc.html`, `ConfirmAllCheck.dc.html`,
`ConfirmAllDone.dc.html`; the canvas note "Confirm all ERPNext corrections (owner, 31 Oct): on Approvals with Show = ERPNext corrections,
the list splits into Ready to confirm and Needs a look (each with why); "Confirm all ready (N)" opens a check page that saves nothing, then
confirms only the ready ones, each as if one by one and checked again; the rest are left and listed"): "Yes, build it". Why: 253 ERPNext
corrections wait in Approvals and are answered one by one, so the Vape and Go stock match falls about 25 items a day (the 99.5 % plan of 31
Oct, decision 1 A). It BOOKS STOCK, so every rule is pinned by a test, and the owner's rule holds: skip anything doubtful, finish the rest,
list what was skipped.

**CA1. Where.** Approvals (`InboxController`) with Show = ERPNext corrections: the list is two groups, "Ready to confirm · N" (the green
dot, tone `done`) then "Needs a look · K" (the amber dot, `needs`), each oldest first, a page (50) of each. A ready row's line is "ERPNext set
X · adds Y" / "· takes off Y" (no difference: "· no difference"); a Needs a look row's line is its reason, in the amber ink (`span.ap-m.ap-why`).
The header gets the green "Confirm all ready (N)" after the Show (`a.btn.ok.ap-confirm-all`, a plain link to the check page; not a main
button: the record's Confirm stays the page's one magenta button), only for a person with `queues.corrections` and only when N > 0. Until a
row is opened, the right of the list is the board's "The list is split in two" (`approvals_split`: Ready to confirm, Needs a look and the
rules in their order, "Open any row to answer it one by one, as today."); a row opens its record exactly as before (its own route, note,
More, next record), and an answer from it comes back to the list kept on the kind. Everything waiting (no Show) is unchanged: one ERPNext
corrections group, no button, the first record open. The inbox decides nothing (AV5): the groups and N are `Corrections::readiness()`'s,
the words `StoreQueuesController::confirmAllLine()`'s.

**CA2. Readiness** (`Corrections::why()`, one rule set used by the list, the check page and again at booking time). An open correction is
READY unless one of these applies, checked in this order; the first that applies is its reason (`Corrections::NOT_READY`; the words
`Words::CONFIRM_ALL` `why_<code>` on a row, `rule_<code>` in the board's list):
- a `counted`: counted on the shelf after ERPNext set it (`stock_balance.counted_at` later than the correction's time; what `confirm()`
  refuses, `newer_count`) - "Counted on the shelf after ERPNext set it";
- b `newer`: a newer ERPNext correction of the item was confirmed already (`effect()['newer']`; what `confirm()` refuses) - "A newer ERPNext
  correction of the item was confirmed already";
- c `big`: it adds or takes off more than the setting (CA3; 100 = "over 100", so exactly 100 is ready) - "Big change: +150 (over 100 units)";
- d `below_zero`: on hand now plus what confirming books is below zero (also an item already below zero that stays below zero) - "The
  item would go below zero";
- e `variants`: the correction's store links 2 or more of its website products to the item (`channel_listing` rows with the item, mapped
  or quarantined; a correction that names no store counts every store's: the safe side) - "Sold as 2 variants: ERPNext set only one";
- f `fixed`: a one-time stock fix was booked for the item at the correction's place after the correction's time (an on-hand `adjustment`
  whose doc_ref starts `listening-fix:`, the fix of 31 Oct and any later pass or undo; check B of `cw_listening_fix.php`): confirming would
  book the fix's units again - "Made before the one-time stock fix of 31 Oct 2026 for an item the fix set" (the UK day of that fix row).
Nothing else is held back: a correction with no difference is ready and closes as "no difference", as one by one. The facts (on hand,
counted_at, links, the newest fix) are read for all rows at once (`Corrections::facts()`); `effect()` is the one-by-one figure.

**CA3. The setting** `relay.correction_bulk_max_units` (0054; 100; 0-100000; Settings > Rules and numbers > Messages from ERPNext, beside the
other relay settings, with a reason, its history in config_change): the big-change limit of c. 0: only corrections with no difference are
confirmed together. The code reads it with the default 100 (`Corrections::bigLimit()`), so it may run before 0054. One by one, a person still
confirms any correction, whatever its size.

**CA4. The check page** (`GET /ui/queues/corrections/confirm-all`, `queues.corrections`; `confirm_all.php`). It saves nothing (tested: the
ledger, the queue, the stored answers and the audit log are the same after it). "Approvals · ERPNext corrections", "Confirm N ERPNext
corrections?" (one: "Confirm 1 ERPNext correction?"), "From <stores> · <warehouses> · nothing is saved until you press Confirm"; the three
lines in a card: "Confirmed, the stock set to ERPNext's figure · N items", "Units added / taken off in <warehouses> · +A / −B", "Left for you
under Needs a look · K items"; the three plain sentences; "Note (saved on each one)" (QueueRules::note: 3 to 500 characters, required, as one
by one); Back and the magenta "Confirm N". The form carries the ids drawn (`ids`, comma-separated, oldest first) and the CSRF token, so a
correction that arrives after the page was drawn is never confirmed by its press. Nothing ready: no form, "Nothing is ready to confirm now."
and Back. A refused press (the note) draws the page again from now, with the refusal in the queue's words and the note as typed.

**CA5. The press** (`POST` the same path, `queues.corrections`, the CSRF token and the same-origin check of every POST;
`Corrections::confirmAll()`). For each id of the form, in its order: `confirm($caller, $id, $note, whenReady: true)`: the one-by-one
confirmation itself (the same caller, the same key `queue:correction:<id>` with the same stored request `{id, note}`, the same ledger line,
the same audit rows; a test confirms a twin one by one and compares), which, under the row's and the balance's locks and after its own
checks a and b, reads the facts again and applies c-f (`why()`): not ready -> 409 `not_ready`, nothing booked or stored, the key free for a
person's answer. Any refusal (counted or confirmed or closed meanwhile, a rule applies now, an unknown id, the key holding another answer)
or a database failure of one leaves that id with "Changed while Confirm all ran: answer it on its own" (it was ready on the page; the
refusal's code and today's reason are kept in the run row), and the rest go on. A form that is not a check page's (no ids, a bad one, more
than 5,000) is refused whole (400 bad_form). Then 303 to the done page.

**CA6. The cap.** At most 500 ids (`Corrections::BULK_MAX`, also how many open corrections the list reads) per press, and no id started
after 25 seconds (CA15); the rest are left as "Not reached: run it again", untouched. Technical bounds of one request, not business rules:
constants, not settings.

**CA7. The press in the audit log** (since CA15: its run row first, its end row last; as first built: one row at the end) (`count_review.confirm_all`, "Confirm all ERPNext corrections"; entity `count_review`, no id): who (actor,
staff id, IP), when, the note, how many ids were sent, the ids confirmed (and of them the ones that were already confirmed: `replayed`), how
many booked a difference, the units added and taken off, and every one left with why (the press's own, then the open ones that need a look
now). Each confirmation keeps its own audit rows, as one by one.

**CA8. The done page** (`GET /ui/queues/corrections/confirm-all/{id}`, the run row's id; `confirm_all_done.php`): "Confirm all: done", the
green status line "N confirmed. K left for you.", the "Left for you · K" card (each the item, why in amber, "Open ›" to the record in
Approvals with Show = ERPNext corrections), "Saved as one run in the audit log: Confirm all ERPNext corrections, <UK date, time>, by
<person>." and "Back to Approvals". Read from the run row, so it needs no session state and no script. Only the person who pressed sees
it: anyone else, an unknown id or another audit row's id is 404 (the same answer, so an id tells a stranger nothing).

**CA9. Twice.** A second press of the same page (a double click, back and press again) books nothing twice: each id's key replays its first
answer (`confirmed`, listed under `replayed`, units 0); with another note the key refuses (422 idempotency_key_reused) and it is left. Tested
on the service and through the screens.

**CA10. Phone** (600 px and less; CSS only, the "ca" block at the end of `app.css`): 16 px in, Back, Confirm, the button and Open › 44 px,
the note 44 px, a long name wraps; nothing wider than the screen.

**CA11. Judgement calls where the boards say nothing** (for the reviewer): the board's list says "of 31 Oct" for the fix; a second pass is
planned (1 Nov), so a row names the day of the fix it hit and the list says "a one-time stock fix"; one correction is "Confirm 1 ERPNext
correction?" / "1 item"; a ready row with no difference says "no difference"; "The shop and the website do not change." is the board's
sentence: true while the store listens (a confirmation books in CW only; the store's connector writes nothing in shadow); once a store is
live, CW's figure reaches its website as after any confirmation one by one. The undo of a fix also counts as a fix for f (its doc_ref starts
`listening-fix:`): the safe side.

**CA12. Tests.** `tests/Unit/ConfirmAllUnitTest` (why(): each rule alone, its edges, the order a-f; the words; the setting's rule),
`tests/Integration/Queues/ConfirmAllTest` (real relayed corrections: each reason a-f and the ready ones, the first rule on one correction,
the setting moves c also at booking time, the twin booked one by one, changed / settled / unknown ids left and the rest booked, a later one
untouched, the second press, the cap and the run row, who may press; the stock invariants after each), `tests/Integration/Queues/Migration0054Test`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/ConfirmAllScreensTest` (the groups and lines, the button only for the job and when N > 0, the board's panel and a
row opening as before, the check page saves nothing, the press, the done page, CSRF, origin, a hand-made form, a short note, a changed one,
a later one, twice, the stranger's 404, the phone CSS).

## "Confirm all ready": the Codex review of a6af366, 3 HIGH and 6 MEDIUM, each shown failing first (branch `confirm-all`, second commit, 31 Oct 2026; CA12-CA21)

The review: `runs/ca_codex_review.txt`, the last block. The coordinator's decision per finding is followed; where the code says otherwise it
says why. Each fix is pinned by a test that failed on a6af366 (`runs/ca_fix_failfirst_a6af366.log`).

**CA12. The press books only what its check page drew** (HIGH 1). The check page signs the ids it drew, exactly as drawn and in their order,
for the person it drew them for, with the moment it was drawn: `StoreQueuesController::confirmAllSignature()`, an HMAC-SHA256 under the
server's existing secret (`ui_secret_key`, through `Csrf::forForm()`, its own domain `f:`, so it is never a CSRF token nor the reverse);
hidden fields `ids`, `at`, `sig`. The press checks it before anything: an id added, taken away or moved, a touched time or signature,
another person's page, or a page more than 30 minutes old (`CONFIRM_ALL_PAGE_SECONDS`; a time more than a minute ahead also) refuses the whole
press with 409 `check_page_changed` and the check page drawn again from now ("This check page was changed, or it is more than 30 minutes
old. It is shown again below: look at it, then press Confirm. Nothing was booked."); nothing is booked. A form that is not a check page's at
all (no ids, a bad one, too many) stays 400. Test: `ConfirmAllScreensTest::testThePressIsBoundToTheIdsItsCheckPageDrew`.

**CA13. Rule e and the link writers** (HIGH 2). The coordinator's question first: does the link writer lock the item? Yes:
`DecisionService` (the only code that changes `channel_listing.sku_id`) reads every item a decision touches `FOR SHARE`
(`lockSkus()`, before it changes the listing). A shared lock taken by the gate too would not wait for it (two shared locks do not
conflict), so the gate takes the item's row `FOR UPDATE`: `SELECT id FROM sku WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE`, after the item's balance, which is
the stock core's own lock order (`Stock::setPolicy()` and `Reservations` lock the balances, then the item). While the gate holds it no link
of the item can change; a link being made is waited for, then counted (READ COMMITTED reads it). The writers are not touched. The one
path that takes the two the other way round is a link that adopts units sold while unlinked (the item `FOR SHARE`, then its balance):
InnoDB then reports a deadlock, which `Db::transaction()` retries (each side) as it does for every booking; nothing is half done. The
test pins the writer's `FOR SHARE` (if it ever goes, the test fails) and both orders: the link waits for the booking, and the booking waits
for the link and leaves the correction. Test: `ConfirmAllTest::testALinkMadeMeanwhileAndTheBookingWaitForEachOther`.

**CA14. The limit is read under a lock** (HIGH 3). Inside the gate, after the item's row, `relay.correction_bulk_max_units` is read with
`SELECT ... FROM app_setting WHERE setting_key = ? FOR SHARE` and held to the commit (`Corrections::lockedLimit()`): a change of the limit
(`Settings::change()`, the setting's row `FOR UPDATE`; it locks no balance or item, so the order holds) waits until the booking that read it
is committed. The list and the check page read it without a lock (they book nothing). Test (two connections):
`ConfirmAllTest::testTheBigLimitIsHeldWhileACorrectionIsBooked`.

**CA15. The press's time, and a press that stops** (MEDIUM 4). The press is saved FIRST: its run row (`count_review.confirm_all`: who, when,
the note, the ids it was given, `state: running`; its id is the done page's), then each id, then its end row (`count_review.confirm_all_end`,
"Confirm all ERPNext corrections: what it did"; entity `count_review`, id `confirm_all:<run>`: the ids confirmed and replayed, the counts,
every one left with why). The audit log is append-only for the app login (`Grants::APPEND_ONLY`), so the run row cannot be updated at the
end as the coordinator suggested: the end is a second row, found by its entity (`ix_audit_entity`). `Corrections::run()` reads both; a press
that stopped before its end (the worker killed, the page timed out) shows what the queue says of its ids: the ones its person confirmed with
its note, the rest "Not reached: run it again", and the done page says "This press stopped before its end. What it confirmed is counted; the
rest is left for you." While a press runs, its session waits at most 5 seconds for a lock (`innodb_lock_wait_timeout`, given back after) and
a confirmation waits at most 5 seconds for its key (`Idempotency`'s wait, a new constructor parameter, default unchanged): one busy id is left
("changed") and the press goes on. No id is started after 40 − 2 × 5 − 5 = 25 seconds (`BULK_SECONDS` 40, `BULK_LOCK_WAIT` 5,
`BULK_FINAL_SECONDS` 5), so the id under way and the end fit in 40 s, inside the UI pool's 50 s. Tests: a clock that passes the deadline, a
clock that stops the press after one id (`run()` then shows it), an id whose balance another connection holds (left after the short wait,
the next one booked, the session's wait given back).

**CA16. A database failure inside one id** (MEDIUM 9). Test only (the code was right): a statement that fails after the id's stock line was
written, and a deadlock on every try (retried by `Db::transaction()` 3 times, then given up): the id is rolled back whole (no ledger line,
the row open, no stored answer for its key, no confirmation audit row, no transaction left open), the next id books, the end row names the
failed one (`error: failed`), and the failed one is then confirmed one by one. Connection loss is not tested (a lost connection fails every
later id and the end row too; the run row stays, and `run()` shows the press as stopped).

**CA17. The list's reads** (MEDIUM 5). `Corrections::list()` reads the figures of all its open rows at once (`effects()`): effect()'s own
statements gathered into three per 200 rows (the last ledger row booked by each moment, both buckets of each balance at that row, each a
`UNION ALL` branch with effect()'s exact SQL and plan; the confirmed corrections of the items in one query), and effect() and effects() share
the arithmetic (`fold()`). A booking still reads effect() itself, fresh, under its locks. For 254 open corrections Approvals' readiness now
reads at most 30 statements (it read 1,026). Test: the count, and effects() equal to effect() row by row, a carried correction included.

**CA18. Open beyond the first 50** (MEDIUM 8). A correction asked for by its link (`?open=corrections-<id>`: the done page's Open ›, a
bookmark) that is waiting is shown after its group's 50 rows, marked open, and its record opens: on ERPNext corrections shown and on
everything waiting ("The first 50 are shown" still counts the page). Test with 55.

**CA19. Migration 0054 runs again safely** (MEDIUM 7). Both inserts are `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS`: a run stopped between them
completes the baseline once; a second run changes nothing and keeps a value set since. Test on a scratch schema: applied, then the baseline
removed and both statements run again, then the value changed and both run again.

**CA20. The fix lookup** (MEDIUM 6): NOT built, as the coordinator decided. `stock_ledger` has no index on `doc_ref` (its indexes:
`ix_stock_ledger_balance` (warehouse, item, id), `_order`, `_created`, `_effective` (warehouse, item, bucket, effective_at), `_unit`,
`_document`, `_store_type`), so rule f still reads each item's on-hand rows at its place (one statement per 200 corrections on the list; one
item under its lock at booking). Proposals for the owner, none built: (a) `ALTER TABLE stock_ledger ADD INDEX ix_stock_ledger_doc_ref
(doc_ref, warehouse_id, sku_id, created_at), ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`: the lookup becomes one range read of the fix's rows (about 1,600
per doc_ref) per request; (b) the audit log's existing `ix_audit_entity`: every fix booking writes an audit row with entity `movement` and
id = its doc_ref, and its key `<doc_ref>:<item>` names the item: one indexed query, but a second source for a stock fact and no warehouse;
(c) a small table the fix tool writes per item. (a) is the plain one.

**CA21. Not changed.** The other findings' parts the review confirmed (the same key and request as one by one, the lock order, the done
page's access) stay as built. Tests: the four files of CA12 plus `ConfirmAllUnitTest` (the signature's binding, the time bounds),
`Migration0054Test`, `ConfirmAllTest` and `ConfirmAllScreensTest` (new and updated cases above).

## "Confirm all ready": the Codex re-review of 557cf03, 2 MEDIUM and 2 LOW, each shown failing first (branch `confirm-all`, third commit, 1 Nov 2026; CA22-CA26)

The owner, 1 Nov 2026: "Fix CW-110 first". The re-review (`runs/ca2_codex_review.txt`, its last block) found the three HIGH of the first
review FIXED; the four below remained. Each fix is pinned by a test that failed on 557cf03 (`runs/ca3_failfirst_557cf03.log`).

**CA22. A stopped press claims only what it booked** (MEDIUM 1). Each confirmation a press books carries the press's run id on its row,
written in its booking's own transaction: `count_review.detail.booked.run` (beside `delta` and `at`, which confirm() already writes there;
the audit log stays append-only). The run id is not part of the key's stored request (`{id, note}`), so a one-by-one click on the record
afterwards still replays. `Corrections::run()` builds a stopped press (no end row) from these marks only: the ids carrying its run id are
"confirmed", with what they booked; every other id of the press is "Not reached, or answered elsewhere: open it to see" (`not_reached_or_elsewhere`),
whoever answered it and with whatever note. A finished press keeps reading its end row. Test, Codex's case: 41 confirmed one by one, the
press (same person, same note) stops before its first id, 42 confirmed one by one after: the stopped press shows nothing confirmed, nothing
booked. A press's booking carries its mark, a one-by-one booking none, and a click on the record after the press replays.

**CA23. One deadline for the whole press** (MEDIUM 2). The press has one deadline, `BULK_SECONDS` (40 s) from its start (by its clock, which
tests move). The ids and all their waits end `BULK_FINAL_SECONDS` (5 s) before it, and the end runs in that reserve. Before each id, and again
at the start of every try of it inside confirm()'s transaction (the first try, and a retry after a deadlock, which `Db::transaction()`
makes), the press works out what is left until then and gives each of the `BULK_WAITS` (8) waits one confirmation may meet (its key, its
queue row, its balance, the item's row, the limit's setting, the value clock, the feed clock, one to spare) an equal share, at most
`BULK_LOCK_WAIT` (5 s): the session's `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` and the key's wait are set to it. When that is less than a second each, the
id is not started (or the try is stopped with `out_of_time`, before it books anything: "Not reached: run it again"). So no try runs past
the ids' time, and no retry is made after it; one-by-one confirmations are unchanged (no deadline outside a press). The end: the list of
what needs a look now is read with `max_execution_time` set to what is left until the deadline; if it does not fit it is left out of the
end row (`unlisted`), and the end row is always written. Tests: a deadlock whose retry would come after the deadline (the retry starts,
sees it and stops: the id rolled back whole and left "not reached", the next not started, the end row written), and each wait's share as
the time goes down (4 s at the start, 1 s at 25 s, nothing started at 28 s).

**CA24. The session comes back exactly** (LOW 3). The session's `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` and `max_execution_time` are read before the press
changes them and set back to exactly those values in a `finally` (a press that ends, one refused, one stopped by an error), not
`max(1, ...)`. Tests: a session whose wait reads 0 (scripted: the server keeps at least 1) gets 0 back, after a press that ends and one that
stops; on the server, a session at 50 is at 50 again after both.

**CA25. Rule f reads the ledger only when it can apply** (LOW 4). No schema change, no `stock_ledger` index. `facts()` first reads when the
last one-time stock fix was booked, once per call (once per list or check page; once per booking, inside its transaction, so it is never
older than the booking), from the audit log's existing entity index: `SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM audit_log FORCE INDEX (ix_audit_entity)
WHERE entity_type = 'movement' AND entity_id LIKE 'listening-fix:%'` (`LATEST_FIX_SQL`): every fix booking (the fix tool books through
`Movements::record()`) writes that audit row in its own transaction, after its ledger row, so the audit time is never earlier than the
ledger's. A correction made at or after that moment cannot have been made before a fix: its ledger is not read for rule f. The ledger is
still read, as before, for the corrections made before it. The guard relies on every listening-fix booking going through
`Movements::record()` (the fix tool does; nothing else writes that doc_ref). Tests: with every open correction newer than the last fix,
the list and the press read no ledger row for rule f; a correction made before it is read and left as "fixed"; the plan of the audit read
is a range on `ix_audit_entity`.

**CA26. Tests.** `ConfirmAllTest`: `testAStoppedPressClaimsOnlyWhatItBooked`, `testADeadlockRetryPastTheDeadlineIsNotTriedAndThePressEndsWhole`,
`testEachWaitGetsItsShareOfTheTimeLeft`, `testTheSessionsLockWaitIsGivenBackExactly`, `testRuleFReadsTheLedgerOnlyForCorrectionsMadeBeforeTheLastFix`,
and the deadline test on a clock the test moves (the number of clock calls per id changed); `QueueListPlansTest` (the last fix's plan);
`ConfirmAllUnitTest` (the bounds, the new reason's words); `tests/Support/ScriptedStatement.php` (a scripted answer, for the 0 case).

## The nightly Confirm all (branch `nightly-confirm`, 1 Nov 2026; NC1-NC12)

The owner, 1 Nov 2026, after the first press of Confirm all ready in production (02:59 UK: 331 confirmed, the match at 99.55 %): "Make it
automatic", then on the design (`NightlyConfirm.dc.html`; the canvas note "Every night (owner, 1 Nov)"): "Yes, build it". It books stock in
production, so every rule below is pinned by a test that failed on 69cba94 (`runs/nc_failfirst_69cba94.log`).

**NC1. What it is.** Once a night, while the switch is on, CW does what a person's "Confirm all ready" does (CA1-CA26): the ready ERPNext
corrections (the same rules a-f, `Corrections::readiness()`), each through the same gate under its locks (`confirm(..., whenReady)`), within
a deadline, the doubtful ones left in Approvals for a person. It is `CW\Queues\NightlyConfirm`; its press is `Corrections::confirmNightly()`.

**NC2. Its settings** (0055; Settings > Rules and numbers > Messages from ERPNext, each changed with a reason, its history in config_change,
"Not agreed yet" until the owner ticks it agreed, as every new setting): `relay.nightly_confirm` "Confirm ready ERPNext corrections every
night" (On / Off, OFF), `relay.nightly_confirm_at` "Time it runs" (UK time HH:MM, 00:00-23:59, 04:30), the existing
`relay.correction_bulk_max_units` now named as the board names it, "Big change: leave for a person above" (100; at night and when pressed),
and `relay.nightly_confirm_max` "At most per night" (500; 1-5000). Each line is the board's. 0055 is safe to run again (as 0054). The code
reads each with its default while 0055 is not there (off: nothing happens).

**NC3. When it runs** (`NightlyConfirm::tick()`, from `bin/confirm_corrections_nightly.php`, cron every five minutes): only while the switch
is on (read from the database on every tick, and again on every confirmation, so switching it off stops the rest of the night: "not
reached"); only inside the night's window, [the time it runs, one hour later), worked out in UK time (`night()`: Europe/London, so across
the clock change of 25 Oct 04:30 UK is 03:30 UTC the day before and 04:30 UTC that day; in the hour that happens twice the window opens
once; a window that crosses midnight belongs to the night it started); and only when no nightly run has started for that night: the run row
of a night carries the night (`entity_id` `nightly:<UK date>`, by audit_log's entity index), looked for and written under the night's named
lock (`GET_LOCK`, server-wide, freed on disconnect; `lockName()` names the schema), so two starts at once make one run (the other says
"busy"), a second tick that night says "done already", and a run that stopped half way is not started again that night (the next night
or a person's press takes the rest). The job's own lock (Ops\Cli, one run of the job per schema) is a second guard.

**NC4. Its caller, and only it.** `confirm()` authorised staff only (QueueRules: 403 staff_required for any system job or store). The
nightly job has its own system caller, `system:confirm_nightly` (`Corrections::NIGHTLY_JOB`), let through by `Corrections::authorise()` only
while `confirmNightly()` runs (a flag set there and cleared in its `finally`) and only while the switch is on. The same caller one by one,
in a person's Confirm all, closing a correction (`dismiss()` asks QueueRules alone), or in another queue, is refused as before; so is
every other system job and every store. `confirmNightly()` itself refuses while the switch is off (409 nightly_off) before it writes
anything. Tested: the nightly caller, `system:housekeeping` and a store, each refused one by one, in Confirm all and closing; a line to
place refused; the press refused while off; one by one refused again after a nightly press.

**NC5. What it books.** Exactly a person's press: one adjustment per difference through the movement route (actor
`system:confirm_nightly`), the row closed by CW (no person: "done by CW"), the note on each, the press's mark (`detail.booked.run`), the
same audit rows, the same key per correction (scoped to the job's caller; the row's own lock and status keep it from being answered
twice by anyone). The note says whose switch it is: "Nightly Confirm all (setting on since <UK date, time>, by <person>)" (the switch's
last change). At most "At most per night"; the rest "not reached". Its deadline is `NIGHTLY_SECONDS` (240 s: no web page waits for it, and
it ends well inside the five-minute cron), with CA23's shares of the time for every wait and retry.

**NC6. The job and its cron line.** `php bin/confirm_corrections_nightly.php --db=<schema>`: no options of its own (the time and the switch
are settings; the command line is read whole or not at all). One log line per tick, as the other bin jobs: "off: relay.nightly_confirm is
off", "outside the night's window (04:30 UK, for 60 minutes): nothing to do", "busy: ...", "done already tonight (<date>): run <id>",
"ran <date>: run <id>, N confirmed (B booked), K left; done page /ui/queues/corrections/confirm-all/<id>". Exit 0 for each of these, 3 when
it cannot run. ONE cron line on each server, the same words (ProductionDeployTest): `*/5 * * * *  root  cd /opt/cw-prod && php
bin/confirm_corrections_nightly.php --db=cw_prod >> /var/log/cw/confirm_corrections_nightly.log 2>&1` (staging: /opt/cw-staging,
cw_staging); rotated with the other /var/log/cw logs. The installers never run it as a smoke check (it books).

**NC7. A second OK for switching it on: none exists, none invented.** The settings framework has no second-person path: "Not agreed yet"
is the `provisional` mark (the owner's agreed tick on the setting's page, any person with settings.manage may set it), and the one rule
that needs a particular person is `ApprovalRules::loosens` (loosening an approval rule needs a Reviewer), which covers only the approval
rules of their own page. So switching the nightly run on is one change by an admin or a reviewer, with its reason, in the setting's history
and the audit log; the board draws the switch "On" with "Not agreed yet" and a run, so the run does not wait for the agreed tick. If the
owner wants the agreed tick (or a second person) to be required before it runs, that is a small rule to add: say so.

**NC8. The Settings page** (`settings.php`, ReferenceController): the card "Messages from ERPNext" opens with the four rows in the board's
order (the switch reads On / Off: `Words::SETTING_BOOL`, also on the setting's own page; the other switches keep Yes / No). Above the search,
the "Last night" line (`section.card.nc-last`): switched off, "Every night: off. ERPNext corrections wait for a person, or for Confirm all
ready."; on with no run yet, "No night run yet." and the next run; on with a run, "**Last night, HH:MM:** N ERPNext corrections confirmed, K
left for you in Approvals." (the run's UK time; "Last run, <day, time>:" when it is older than last night; a run that stopped says so), "Open
last night's run ›" to its done page for whoever may open it (queues.corrections), and "Next run: tonight at HH:MM. It confirms only the ready
ones, exactly like pressing Confirm all ready; the doubtful ones wait for a person." Approvals and Home need no change (their counts are
the open corrections).

**NC9. A nightly run's done page** is everyone's who answers ERPNext corrections (the route's permission, queues.corrections): a run with no
person whose actor is the nightly job's; its saved line says "by CW, every night". A person's press stays its presser's (404 to anyone else,
as CA8).

**NC10. Phone.** CSS only (the "nc" block at the end of app.css): the line wraps, the link is 44 px on a phone, 16 px in.

**NC11. Not built.** Nothing tells a person by message that the night ran (the alerts are the owner's; the Settings line and the done page
say it). The run does not retry a night it missed (a server down for the whole hour): the next night runs, or a person presses.

**NC12. Tests.** `tests/Unit/NightlyConfirmUnitTest` (the window in UK time: BST, GMT, 25 Oct, the hour twice, 29 Mar, midnight, not a time;
the rules and the board's words and order; the cron line on each server and never in the installers), `tests/Integration/Queues/NightlyConfirmTest`
(off; outside; inside: the ready ones booked by the job, the rest left, the run with its night, its note, the bookings' actor and mark;
a second tick; the next night; another start holding the lock; the job twice at once as cron runs it: one run; the cap; the job's caller
refused everywhere else), `tests/Integration/Queues/Migration0055Test` (the settings, their rules and words, run twice),
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/NightlyConfirmScreensTest` (the Last night line off, none yet and with a run, its link only for who may open
it, the card's rows and On / Off; a nightly run's done page for every stock controller, refused to a buyer; a person's press still its
presser's). The stock invariants after each.

**CA27-CA29. Confirm all ready: the tracker's follow-ups CW-913, CW-111, CW-109 (1 Nov 2026, branch `ca-followups`; each shown failing first).**
- **CA27 (CW-913, CA20 (a)). The fix lookup reads an index.** Migration 0056 adds `ix_stock_ledger_doc_ref (doc_ref, warehouse_id, sku_id,
  created_at)` to stock_ledger (ALGORITHM = INPLACE, LOCK = NONE; the ALTER runs only while the index is not there, so the file runs again
  safely). `Corrections::FIX_SQL` reads it by FORCE INDEX: one range read of the fixes' own rows, not each item's whole ledger at its place
  (QueueListPlansTest, Migration0056Test). The code needs 0056 first: the installers migrate before they switch.
- **CA28 (CW-111, the Codex re-check ca3 MEDIUM, and its review of 0317222). The end's reads end by the deadline.** `Db::readsUntil($until,
  $clock, $fn)`: before each statement $fn makes, the time left until $until becomes the session's max_execution_time, and with none left
  none is started (out_of_time); the session's own value comes back after. The press's end reads its list through it, so the reads end by the
  deadline however long the ones before took (round trips and PHP included: the time is read again before each). Either way the end row is
  written (`unlisted` when the list did not fit: Approvals lists them). NightlyConfirm's search reads each page through it too (NC14).
  `readStatements()` (READ_FIXED 8, READ_PER_CHUNK 6 per CHUNK of 200) is the few fixed statements the list makes; the tests hold it to them.
- **CA30. Staging's installer publishes before it migrates (the review of 0317222, MEDIUM): accepted for staging.** deploy/staging copies
  the code into the served directory and then migrates, so for the seconds between, the new FIX_SQL can name an index 0056 has not made
  yet (error 1176 on a correction page). Production's installer migrates first and switches after (install_cron.sh), so production never
  runs the code before its migration; merge_deploy always passes --migrate. Not changed.
- **CA29 (CW-109). A press that booked nothing new says so.** Its done page reads "Already confirmed before: N. Nothing was booked again. K
  left for you." when every one it confirmed was confirmed already (each key replayed: the same page pressed again), instead of "N confirmed".

**NC13-NC16. The Codex review of 774f39e (3 MEDIUM, 1 LOW), each shown failing first on 774f39e.**
- **NC13. The whole queue is searched.** The ready ones were read from the oldest 500 open corrections only, so 500 doubtful ones in front hid
  a ready one every night. `NightlyConfirm::ready()` reads the open queue page by page (`Corrections::readiness(..., $after)`, by the open
  index, oldest first) until the page that reaches "At most per night" (all its ready ones: the press confirms the most and shows the rest
  "not reached") or the queue's end.
- **NC14. One deadline for the whole run.** The 240 seconds (`NIGHTLY_SECONDS`) start before the search: the search may take at most
  `FIND_SECONDS` (60) of them, and the press gets what is left (its own reserve for the end row inside it), on the same clock. A page is
  `PAGE` (200) rows, one chunk of readiness()'s reads, so it runs a few fixed statements (the test counts them); each page is read through
  `Db::readsUntil` (CA28): before each statement the time left is its time, so the search ends by its 60 s however slow the reads (the
  Codex re-check of 3de1a33: one limit per page let five slow statements run past the whole budget). A page that does not fit ends the
  search with what was found.
- **NC15. The installer waits longer than the longest job.** `install_cron.sh --migrate` waited 2 minutes for running jobs; a night's run may
  take 4. It now waits 6 minutes (the run and a margin) before it stops with the writers paused.
- **NC16. A run still going is "running".** A night's run with no end row while its job holds the night's lock, started less than
  `NIGHTLY_SECONDS` + 60 seconds ago, is `running` (Corrections::run()): Settings' Last night line says "It is running now: what it
  confirmed so far is counted." and its done page "This night run is still going ...", instead of "stopped". Without the lock, or older, it
  stopped, as before.

## The small screens: five gaps the redesign left as "needs a build" (branch `small-screens`, 1 Nov 2026; SS1-SS6)

The owner's tracker CW-901, CW-906, CW-908, CW-910 and CW-911: what the approved artboards draw and the redesign could not build (RD-A3,
RD-B3, RD-C13, RD-C7/RD-F11, RD9). Layout and reads only: no migration, no setting, no stock or money write.

**SS1. Items: the search finds a barcode** (CW-901; the Items artboard's "Search name, brand, barcode or CW number"). `ItemCardList::where()`:
a bare number of 6 to 64 digits is also looked up in `sku_barcode` (its GTIN key: leading zeros left out, as `Queries::searchSkus` reads
it; any barcode row, usable or not, as /ui/search finds it). A number of up to 10 digits is still a CW number too: both match (an
8-digit EAN and a CW number never meet in practice; when they do, both items are listed). The box's words, the label and the empty
state say a barcode can be typed. The CSV is the same list.

**SS2. Sales orders: one search** (CW-906; Sales.dc.html's "Search order number or item"). The box is the Show row's first field, in the
same GET form (the store choice, the days and More's filters keep it; the pager and the file carry `q`). `SalesViews::searched()`:
(1) the store's order reference as typed (a leading # left out; the collation's case) on the stores shown, by `uq_reservation_order`, on
the first page only and whatever the days, state or way in (an order number names one order: hiding it behind "the last 7 days" would
say "no order" for an order that is there); (2) the items the text names (`Queries::searchSkus`, at most 20: words, CW number, barcode)
give the orders with a unit of one of them, in the days, state (a unit state on the unit, an order state on the order) and way in
chosen, newest first, a page of `sales.page_size` by order id below `before` (order ids follow the time an order was placed, as
`byUnit` relies on). The read starts from the items' units (`ix_reservation_unit_sku_state`), so a word naming many popular items reads
all their units (every day's); the 20 items are the bound. The order the reference names is left out of the item list (`r.order_ref <>`
the reference), so it is listed once over all the pages (the Codex review of 517a331, MEDIUM 1).

**SS3. Approvals: Answered today** (CW-908; the Approvals artboard's last Show choice). `Ui\AnsweredToday`: since midnight UK time, by anyone,
in the kinds this person answers (`InboxController::kinds`), what was answered: each kind's closed rows from its own table by its
answer time (`count_review` by source for ERPNext corrections and count differences, `goods_in_suspense`, `oversell_event`,
`policy_review` of the website modes, `landing_order`, `staff_role_request`, `review_task`), newest first, 50 a kind. A row: what it
was, how it ended (Done, Dismissed, OK, Not OK), who (a name; "the system" when no person), the time; it links the kind's own page (the
record waits no more: the inbox cannot open it), and no record is drawn on the right. A count difference's answer is its resolution
(accepted: OK, rejected: Not OK; both are `resolved` rows), and Count differences lists only `CountReviews::LISTED_SOURCES` (a VERIFY
recount the system closes is not one; the Codex review, MEDIUM 2 and LOW 3). The choice has no count: the answer times are
in no index (the tables are indexed for what waits), so they are read only when the choice is shown, never on the inbox's every view.
Not in it: a count sheet line made final (it is a document's posting, not an answer row); left out on purpose.

**SS4. New on the stores: All stores** (CW-910; the ByItem artboard's first store choice, "All stores (N)"; RD-F11 said why it was not
built). It is the first choice and the default (no `channel`); its number is the tab's. `ByProductController::newOnEveryStore()`: each
store's newest page × 50 ids by New variants' own read (`Queries::newVariants`, page null: its total too, the counts' or a search's),
merged by when they were first seen (then id), cut to the page; a store with nothing new and no search is not read; at most 20 pages
(`NEW_ALL_PAGES`: 1,000 products) are offered, enough for a week's new products on every store. Each row says its own store. "Match
all new" stays New variants' (one store's page): with All stores it opens the first store with new products (the default of before).
Match's way back keeps All stores (no `channel`).

**SS5. The find box finds an order** (CW-911; Sidebar.dc.html's "Find an item or an order"; RD9 said why it was not built). /ui/search
lists, before the items, the stores' orders whose order reference is the text as typed (a leading # left out), on every store
(`uq_reservation_order`, one read a store), any day, at most 10, each linking the order's page — only for who may look at sales
(`sales.view`, the order page's permission): their box (sidebar, phone top bar) says "Find an item or an order"; anyone else's still

the item search still needs two; the Codex review, LOW 4).

**SS6. Tests.** `ItemCardScreensTest::testTheSearchFindsAnItemByItsBarcode`, `SalesScreensTest::testStoreOrdersSearchByOrderNumberOrItem`,

## The design gaps: what the approved boards draw and the redesign left as "needs a build" (branch `design-gaps`, 1 Nov 2026; DG1-)

The owner's tracker CW-902, 903, 904, 909, 912, 905, 907 (BATCH 2 of the second account): strictly as the approved boards in
`redesign_20261030/project/` draw them; one commit each, each test failing first.

**DG1. Adjustments: "All kinds"** (CW-902; Inventory.dc.html's first Show choice, the one it shows; RD-A5 said "no page: needs a build").
`/ui/stock/adjustments/all` (documents.view, as every kind's list): the four kinds' lists (`StockOps::list`, the same search, state,
warehouse and "stopped too") together, newest first, at most `LIST_LIMIT`, in the artboard's groups; each row is its own kind's (its kind
word, reason, units and way; a correction's reason "On each line"). It is a page of the Adjustments entry (`Sections`, key
`adjustments_all`, first): the sidebar's Adjustments opens it, as the board shows All kinds chosen; every kind's Show lists it first and
keeps the filters. No create fold and no download of its own: the head's main button is the entry's "+ New adjustment" (the Corrections
page's fold, `doc.ADJ.post`), each kind's page keeps its own CSV.

**DG2. Corrections: the net units and the reason on the row** (CW-903; Inventory.dc.html's correction rows: "Count difference", "−12").
`StockOps::list` also reads each record's net units (the signed sum of its lines, `net_units`) and the reason its lines share
(`line_reason`: the label when every line carries the same reason code, else NULL). A correction's row says that reason, or "On each line"
when its lines give more than one (or one has none); its units are the net change, "+N" green or "−N" red, plain "0" when it nets out
(a cancellation record's lines are already the other way, so its sign is right). The other kinds are as before.

**DG3. The item page: "+ Add" on Suppliers** (CW-904; Item.dc.html's Suppliers card head). For who manages suppliers (`suppliers.manage`):
the card's "+ Add" is a fold (as Barcodes' "+ Add") with one choice, the supplier (every supplier not stopped, by name), and Next: a GET
form to `/ui/items/{id}/add-supplier?supplier=N`, which opens that supplier's own "add an item" form with this item chosen
(`SupplierItemsController::newForm` reads `sku_id`), where the box, price and the rest are typed and saved as before. Nothing is saved by
the fold or the redirect. An item that is not there (or joined away), a supplier that is not there or is stopped: 404. Who only looks
at suppliers sees the card without "+ Add"; the route refuses them (403).

**DG4. By item: the board's five filters** (CW-909; ByItem.dc.html: Store, Match status, Brand, Kind, Stock; RD-C10 had kept one). The
reading of the board, agreed with the first session and the owner's brief (1 Nov): Store and Match status make the list's one coverage
filter (`cov`, as before, so every link, the pager, the CSV, the bulk bar and the way back from a variant's page keep working):
a store and "Missing on a store" = missing on that store (`missing-<code>`, as before); All stores and it = missing on at least one store
(`missing`, new); a store and "Any match status" = matched on that store (`on-<code>`, new); "On every store" (`every`) and "On no
store" (`none`, new) leave the store aside; "With a suggestion" (`suggested`) stays as the last choice (nothing removed). The form sends
`store` and `match`; the controller turns them into `cov` (`ByProductContext::coverageOf`), and an address with only `cov` (an old link)
reads as before. Brand (the item's brand, every brand an item has, by name), Kind (the item card's product type, `ItemRules::TYPES`:
CW's own kinds, not the board's sample words) and Stock ("Holding stock" = on hand above zero over every warehouse, "No stock" = zero or
below) narrow any of them (`Queries::productExtra`). The board's words are the options; the counts beside each choice of before are gone

**DG5. Home: the stock value tile and "Deliveries expected"** (CW-912; Main.dc.html's first tile "Stock value at cost · N items with
stock" and its Today card). The tile is back as RD-F8 asked: migration **0057** adds `report_refresh.stock_value`, `items_with_stock` and

## The Inventory valuation "As of" a past day, and its PDF (branch `as-of`, 1 Nov 2026; AO1-AO6; tracker CW-914)

The plan (runs/cw914_plan.md) was put to the owner through the first session; his answer, 1 Nov 2026: **"Yes, A B C"**.

**AO1. The day.** The valuation's options start with the board's "As of" (a date box; empty = today, as before). A real UK day before
today is a past day; today, a later day or anything that is not a real day is today's report. "As of 15 Oct" is the end of 15 Oct, UK
time (the next midnight in London, as a UTC time: `ReportsController::endOfDay`). The line under the title says the day; the head's
second line says (rule C) "A past day can change when a record dated on or before it is entered later." The files carry the day too.

**AO2. Rule A (the owner's yes): when a ledger row happened** = its effective time (a count's counted time, a dispatch's time), else
when it was entered: `COALESCE(effective_at, created_at)`, the rule the reports already use for first-in and last-sale days.

**AO3. Rule B (the owner's yes): units and cost then.** `ReportViews::valueAt($end)`: each balance's units = the sum of its on-hand ledger
rows that happened before the end (invariant 2: the ledger adds up to the balance; read whole, not as "today minus later", so a row
entered before the day with a later date, or after it with an earlier one, is placed by its own date); an item's average cost then = CW's
own rule (report_item's): every on-hand rise with a unit cost, in any warehouse, that happened before the end: their value / their
units, rounded half up to 6 places; a balance's value = units x that cost to the penny, as today's VALUE; units above zero only, ours
in our value, another account's shown by warehouse and in "units of another account", as today. Items, brands, warehouses and the
strip's figures come from that one read, in today's shapes and orders; the item search, "only without a cost" and the Warehouse choice
work as for today. Worked by hand in `ReportsScreenTest::testStockValueAsOfAPastDayIsWorkedOutFromTheLedger` (47/13, 77/23, the
shares, the other account's room, the CSV's six places).

**AO4. Rule C (the owner's yes): a past day can change** when a record dated on or before it is entered later (a count, a late delivery
with its real date); the page says so (AO1). A frozen month-end figure would need a saved snapshot: not built.

**AO5. PDF.** The valuation's Export menu has PDF (`/ui/reports/stock-value.pdf`, values.view): A4, the company and the line under the
title (the day, the warehouse, at average cost), the rule C note for a past day, then the table with the CSV's columns and rows.
The other reports have no PDF (CW-914 is the valuation's).

**AO6. Safety and limits.** Reads only. The one statement of a past day (and the first-record day) runs at most
`ReportViews::AS_OF_MAX_MS` (20 s, `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`): when it runs out (MySQL 3024) the page says "Too much to read for that day.
Choose a later day." and shows no table. A day before CW's first stock record says "CW has no stock records before <day>". A past day
has no "not sold in N days" figure (the sales data is today's). The help sentence "The value on a past date is not available yet" went.

**AO7. The Codex review of 18ca94b** (runs/asof_codex_review.txt: 1 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 2 LOW; failing first on 18ca94b, runs/asof_fix_red.log).
A past day is now **today's SQL with its two sources as they stood then** (`ReportViews::at($end)` + `sources()`: the balances and
report_item's two sums from the ledger, rules A-B; `valueAt()` and its PHP grouping went). So the brands group, the ties order and the
pages cut exactly as today's (MEDIUM 2, LOW 5: collation, NULL and '' brands, `name, sku_id`), only one page is read (MEDIUM 3: no
loading every balance into PHP; a file reads every row, as today's files do), and with nothing since the day every figure equals
today's (tested by item, brand and warehouse). Every statement of a past day runs inside `ReportViews::bounded()` (the session's
`max_execution_time` = AS_OF_MAX_MS, put back after), the first-record lookup too (MEDIUM 4); a statement out of time (3024) shows "Too
much to read for that day" and **makes no file**: the CSV, Excel and PDF answer 503 with those words (HIGH 1). `pastDay()` takes only a
real calendar day from 2000 on (LOW 6: year 0000). Test: `testStockValueAsOfIsTodaysReadsAndAStatementOutOfTimeMakesNoFile` (a 3024
scripted on the kernel's own connection, `StatementHook`).

**AO8. The Codex re-check of 4e37d82** (runs/asof_codex_recheck.txt: the six of AO7 confirmed fixed; 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW new; failing first,
runs/asof_fix2_red.log). MEDIUM: a past day's rows and totals were separate statements under READ COMMITTED: a back-dated record
committed between them could make the table and its Total disagree. `bounded()` now runs every read of a past day in one read-only
REPEATABLE READ transaction (`SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY`, then the connection's own transaction,
committed after): one snapshot for the page. LOW: a page number beyond any list (`page=999999999999999999`) made an offset the SQL refused;
the page is capped at 1,000,000 before the offset (the last page after that, as before). Today's report is unchanged.

## Returns of orders CW never held (branch `auto-returns`, 2 Nov 2026; AR1-AR8; tracker CW-211; connector 0.4.7)

The plan: /root/cw_work/runs/cw211_auto_returns_plan.md (the owner's "Yes, build", 2 Nov). The match fell from 99.55% to 99.40% on 1 Nov: 7 returns of orders from before T0
(72 units) were restocked on the shop that evening and CW never heard. Those batches touch 24 to 97 items and land after staff hours, with room for about 10 items.

**AR1. A store sends a return; CW books it as a Customer return.** POST /v1/movements takes `type: return` from a site: on_hand + |qty| x u at the store's warehouse, ledger
`movement_type` `return`, channel set, `order_ref` and `unit_id` NULL (there is no reservation to tie it to), `doc_ref` `return:<RMA>:<unit>`. The existing type was
chosen, not a new one: its label, the sales report's units returned and `RollbackExport::WEBSITE_TYPES` are already right. An adjustment is CARRIED on a way-back, so a
booking by hand would count twice for every unit ERPNext already has.

**AR2. Least privilege (R17).** `return` is in `Movements::SITE_RETURN_TYPES`, not CHANNEL_TYPES: `RELAY_GRANTS` and so `--relay=on` stay the five relay kinds, and the grant is
given by name (`--relay=<list>`). Staff get 403 for it: a person's correction stays an adjustment. `RollbackExport`'s classification of channel rows is unchanged.

**AR3. What it must carry.** doc_ref is required, a site sends no cost (valued at the average cost, as any return), the type sets the sign. It is NOT a SUSPENSE type: a line CW
cannot place refuses the call (422 `unresolved_line`, nothing booked) and nothing lands in goods-in suspense, whose queue is for ERPNext documents.

**AR4. Once only.** One unit per call, one key per unit. /v1/movements keys are never pruned (Housekeeping), so a resend answers from the stored result, whatever the outbox
has pruned. It does not use `relay_line`: that is per document line for the ERP relay, and a unit is its own document here.

**AR5. The connector (0.4.7, old_returns.php).** No hook and no SQL: a worker step reads `order_return_items` once a minute and queues `relay_movement` rows, a kind that
already has the ENUM value, the long timeout, the answer handler and the park on a missing grant. It reads no site table in a hot path, so no page gets slower. Off until the
config's `old_returns_from` is a London-local moment; nothing before that moment is sent. Selected: restocked, order at or below T0's last order, no `cw_unit_state` row, a CW link.
Reviewed plan: the unit test goes by "CW holds this unit", not the date: 2 of the 340 units since T0 were opening units, sent by the sweep.
The key and doc_ref name the order unit (`ordi_id`), not the return row: a unit comes back once, whatever rows name it. The step reads the saved record and nothing else, not the
staff's request (the owner, 2 Nov: "any successful restock shouldn't be missed, any failed restock shouldn't add the stock"): a rolled-back restock is not there, a saved one is, however the
worker was. Sending from the request was rejected: the save can still fail after it, and a lost send is lost for good.

**AR6. Waiting for the opening.** A missing `cw_unit_state` row proves nothing until the opening batch is answered (its handler seeds the units), so the step waits while an
`opening_orders` row is pending or dead (Codex's plan review, HIGH 2). On Vape and Go all 5 batches are sent.

**AR7. The window.** The read goes back at most 10 days, inside the outbox's 14-day prune, so the outbox still blocks a repeat; a unit older than that with the step off is the
report's `missing` line, and `bin/cw_old_returns.php --catch-up --apply` sends it (CW's stored keys book nothing twice). Starting from a past moment works within 10 days of it without the catch-up.

**AR8. A refused line.** CW stores the 422 under the key, so a retry cannot work. `bin/cw_old_returns.php --resend=<orti_id> --apply` voids the dead row and sends the unit under a
new key, in one transaction, only for a dead row answered 422. Left as gaps, the owner told: these returns are not in Sales > Returns (it reads order units); an As-of value
for a day before they were sent stays short by them.

**AR9. If it ever goes wrong, it is found (the owner's rule, 2 Nov).** The 05:10 report compares both sides from the start moment, not a day's: the units saved on the shop against CW's own
`return:` ledger rows (`store_returns`, by the doc_ref index). Three lines: every saved return is on CW (15 minutes' grace), CW has none the shop did not save, none booked twice; the units in
old_returns_audit.csv. If CW sends no list the first line FAILs: the compare is never silently left out. Restocks that do not pass through Returns are not sent: a cancel before dispatch is of a
unit CW holds, and a refund's Restock has no saved restock date, so a unit restocked long ago and refunded today would look like a new return (since T0 none on an order CW does not hold). A
fourth line FAILs when such a restock leaves an item above CW and its gap moved since the last report.

**AR10. The Codex review of the build** (runs/ar_codex_review.txt: 3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, each checked by hand and shown failing first). HIGH 1: an order below T0's id can still complete
after it, so its commit may be waiting while a unit comes back: the sweep would then send the unit as well. The step leaves out an order with a `cw_order_state` row and reads ownership again
just before queueing (unit state, order state, a commit pending or dead). HIGH 2: a restock before T0 is in CW's opening figure, so the read starts at the later of old_returns_from and T0;
a T0 with no readable time stops the step. HIGH 3: any dead 422 used to allow a new key, but `idempotency_key_reused` can mean the key booked: only `unresolved_line`, where CW books nothing.
MEDIUM 1: only a real calendar moment switches the step on (`cw_config_moment_ok`, one check for the config and the writer). MEDIUM 2: the mock gives a return CW's real answers (a stored
422, no line dedupe) and the recovery test drains the new key. LOW: the Stores page shows a return-only grant. The report's compare uses the same selection.
Cost measured on live, read only: the step's read 5-7 ms for 72 rows of 3,800, the outbox check 4 ms for 500 keys, `idem_key` ascii_bin takes the IN as it is.

**AR11. The Codex re-check** (runs/ar_codex_recheck.txt: 1 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, each checked by hand). HIGH: an order the opening `skipped` has a `cw_order_state` row but never reached CW: its return is sent;
any other order state stays back and the report says "held back". The report's compare now reads the same ownership, also finds a wrong item or quantity (`store_returns` gives the item, the shop's
link gives `units_per_item`), looks an "extra" up at any date so moving the start cannot make a booked unit extra, and keeps the proto prefix when the start is given by hand. The mock's return moves
its stock and the recovery test asserts one unit. Accepted, not changed: a --catch-up over 14 days after a re-send gets a dead row with nothing booked (the base key holds a refusal, or the unit a
second document): loud, no stock effect, and it needs a refusal, a re-send and a stop of over 14 days together.

**AR12. The last Codex check** (runs/ar_codex_recheck2.txt: 3 MEDIUM). Fixed in the report: a CW return whose doc_ref names no unit counts as extra, never passed over; a return from before the start moment gets the same item and
quantity check. Accepted: the mock's `returned` is a count, not its stock figure: what proves one unit on the real stock is CW's own AR1 test (assertBal) and the staging run.

## The quick adjustment screen (branch `adjust-grid`, 2 Nov 2026; AG1-AG8; tracker CW-212)

The owner watched an adjustment being typed product by product and asked for ERPNext's way: "you can just keep going on by pressing tab and add new line". He drew the
screen with Claude on the canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/7tqoX6sbiPJH4LKqTvPq6M and said "Yes, build it". Adjustments only: Stock in, Stock out, Transfers and Releases
keep the add box, because their lines carry prices, a place to and a "given to".

**AG1. One page, nothing saved until a button.** "New adjustment" opens `/ui/stock/adjustments/new`; the list has no start form. The item page's `?item=` lands there with
the item as the first line. The creator's draft shows the same screen; every other record keeps the record page. The add and lines routes stay: older pages open in a
tab keep working.

**AG2. One reason for every line.** "Why, for every line" opens on Data correction while it is offered. A line's Why says "Same as above" unless it has its own, and Tab
skips it. On a saved draft the box takes the first line's reason.

**AG3. Every line in one field.** The form sends `lines`, JSON of `[{sku, u, r, l}]`, so PHP's max_input_vars cannot cut lines off (OV4). The server trusts nothing in it: not
a list, or a product that is no positive whole number, is 400 bad_form; units are read as before. `l` names the saved line a row came from, so a line the screen does not
show keeps its unit cost and description (gridKept) when the product and the direction are the same, even with the same product on two lines. New: the draft and its lines
are one transaction under FormOnce, so a refusal leaves no record and a second send makes no second one. A draft: details and lines are one transaction. Make it final then
posts in its own transaction (OV3): a refused posting keeps the saved draft and says so.

**AG4. The product box is the site's one dropdown** (SM11, combo) filled from a read-only fragment, `/ui/stock/adjustments/products`, marker `data-aj-fragment`, using
StockOps::resolve, so a barcode, a CW number and words of a name all work. It gives each choice's stock in the warehouse on the page. Changing the warehouse asks again by
`skus`. A choice is never taken on an exact answer alone: a CW number being typed passes through other numbers on the way (id 1380 on the way to 13801). Only Tab or Enter takes one.

**AG5. Keys.** Tab or Enter in Product takes the marked choice, else the first; before the answer comes (a scanner) it waits for it. Tab or Enter in Units goes to the next
line, or to After when Units is empty. After sets Units, and Units sets After. Up and Down move in a column, Left and Right between cells, in a text box from its ends. In
Why, Space opens the list. Enter never sends the form. One empty line is always ready at the end.

**AG6. Stock now is on hand**, as the old line showed first, and After is on hand plus the units. The units are what is booked: stock that moves after the page was drawn
does not change them.

**AG7. A reason that needs a note says so before the send.** Data correction needs one (reason_code.needs_note), which the old page only said after the press. The Note box's
hint changes and Make it final stops in the page. The server's own check stays.

**AG8. The rules are unchanged.** Who may post, the OK first, the reviewer's check, below-zero and reason direction all stay in Documents and StockOpHandler. The hint under
the lines shows while a rule can ask for an OK.

Codex read the build twice (2 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, all fixed): the answer of an older warehouse overwriting a newer one, a stored cost lost on save, a merged product, 501 lines
losing what was typed, After taking part of a number, the phone's foot under the tab bar, the cost of a product on two lines, After typed while the stock figures refresh.

## A store's choice at Add product (branch `store-choice`, 3 Nov 2026; SC1-SC12; tracker CW-217)

The owner, 2 Nov 2026: a new product on Vape and Go should connect to the warehouse by itself, without matching by hand. His drawing of 3 Nov ("Add product to CW",
five screens) was approved with "ശരി, പണി തുടങ്ങൂ" (start the work). Step 1 is Vape and Go only; the other stores follow once Vape and Go is fully right.

**SC1. The store says what a new variant is, once.** At Add product (simple and variable) and Add variant, staff choose per new variant: New item (already chosen), A pack
of an item (its CW number and how many one pack holds), or Not stock. A variable product's landing page is Not stock by itself. The store keeps the choice and its
connector sends it, after the variant's own listing, with PUT /v1/store-choices. `store_choice` (0058) keeps it; never removed.

**SC2. The first choice of a variant is the one.** A second send of a variant is answered `already_received` and changes nothing: a store that retries after a timeout is
harmless, and a later choice never undoes what was followed. A malformed call is refused whole (400), so a product is never half-sent. Allowed while the store is off: a
choice moves no stock (like a listing push).

**SC3. Followed only once the variant is there.** bin/apply_store_choices.php, every minute, looks at the waiting choices whose listing and profile have arrived, oldest
first, one transaction each: the choice's row locked first, then DecisionService's own locks in its order, then the row's state (no new lock after the feed clock).

**SC4. No warehouse person, so the store's person is named.** The job decides as `system:store_choice`. The CHECK of 0058 lets that actor make a new item or a link with no
`decided_by`; every other decision still names its person. The decision's reason says whose choice it followed ("Chosen at Add product on vapeandgo by Aswin: a new item.")
and its detail holds `store_choice` {id, store, staff_ref, staff_name, chosen_at}. DecisionService takes `store_choice` only from that job, and always from it (400 else).
The job never makes a bulk batch, only decides a variant nobody has decided (unmapped or suggested; not held back, not in a spot check: 409 not_open, one_at_a_time), and
names the suggestion it saw (I7: a suggestion written in between makes it try again on the next run).

**SC5. Not stock is the landing mark.** The system's landing mark (LP2) with the reason `store_choice`; a person's "it is a real product" still stops it (said_real).

**SC6. A new item is made only when the warehouse has nothing like it.** Before `new_item` the job looks for: a suggestion of the check on arrival that names an item; a
barcode of the variant (any form one scan may take, Gtin::forms) on an item or on another store's variant; an item, not joined into another, with the same name (the
item table's own comparison) or a name that differs only in letter case, spaces and punctuation, "&" read as "and" (StoreChoices::key(): "Mr Blue Nic-Salt 10ml - 10mg"
and "mr blue nic salt 10ml 10mg" are one name; 10mg and 20mg stay apart). Any of them: nothing is made, the row waits for a person (to_check) with what was found. Two
variants of one name in one run: the second waits. Unlike the bulk "create as new" (seedCheck), a Draft variant is made: connecting at the Draft stage is the point.
Before it makes the item the job takes the name's guard row (item_name_guard, as an item made by hand does) and looks again with fresh reads, so a making of the same
name at the same moment is seen. The close-name check reads the items' names fresh each time (one pass in the database, the same key), never a list kept from earlier.
A Conflict suggestion (two or more items look like it) is a matching lead's: the row waits (to_check conflict), and DecisionService refuses the job on it under the lock.

**SC7. A pack is a link with its units, and keeps the two-person rule.** The CW number is followed to the item it was joined into. While approvals.match_multiple is on, the
link waits for a matching lead (pending_second): the store's staff member chose it, a warehouse person says yes, which one person may do since the decision has no
`decided_by`. An unknown CW number is refused (no_such_item) and waits for a person.

**SC8. What each row says.** done: made, linked, waiting_second, not_stock, already_decided (someone decided the variant first: a link, an ignore, a landing page, a
decision waiting for a second person), and the answers below. to_check: suggested_match, conflict, barcode_on_item, barcode_on_listing, same_name, close_name, said_real, held,
has_history (a person decided the variant before, whatever it is now; asked again under the listing's lock, since a "not this item" moves no version). refused: no_such_item, no_name, or DecisionService's code.

**SC9. A person answers on Approvals > New products** (and in Waiting for you): Yes, the same (a link to the item found, one sale one item), No, a new item, or Not stock;
a pack is decided on the variant's own page. Each answer is a DecisionService decision as that person (their role, the version, the suggestion and what the page
showed of a variant decided one at a time, `seen`), in one transaction with the row. A variant set aside or in a spot check is answered only on its own page (409). A row whose variant was decided on its own page leaves the list at once and the job settles it (decided_elsewhere).

**SC10. The store shows the result.** The feed already carries each variant's link and CW number to the store (cw_listing_state): the product page's Variations table
shows the CW number, Not stock, or Waiting for CW. Nothing new is sent back.

**SC11. The barcodes follow nightly.** A barcode often comes days after the Draft. bin/sync_barcodes.php (I106-I108) is now on the timer at 02:41: a new barcode on a
linked variant is added to its item; one already on another item opens a barcode review, as before. Held at go-live (3 Nov 2026) and switched on the same afternoon on the
owner's word, for Vape and Go only: the first production night adds 271, opens 20 reviews and makes 18 barcodes unusable until each
review is decided (all channels would be 556, 64 and 62; Electrofag and Vape Big wait for Vape and Go).

**SC12. What it does not do.** It never replaces a choice, never touches a decided variant, never makes a second item of a name or a barcode the warehouse has, never
deletes. Price, descriptions and the other stores (the plan's step 2) are not part of this.

Codex read the core (0a65014) at xhigh: 2 HIGH (a Conflict followed without a lead; a name made twice at once), 5 MEDIUM (a person's "not this item" between the look
and the decision, the close-name list kept for a whole run, two first sends at once, a day like 31 February, an answer on a variant set aside), all fixed in b0de157
with tests; the eighth (the screen) is SC9's.

## Two small screen fixes (branch `small-fixes`, 3 Nov 2026; MA1-MA3)
**MA1. A mistyped address while signed in keeps the person's frame.** Seen in Chrome on 2 Nov: a wrong address showed the bare page with
"Back to sign in" to someone signed in. A 404 or 405 from the router with no session cookie is unchanged (no database work,
`testAnUnknownPathOrMethodNeverTouchesTheDatabase`). With a cookie, `Kernel::missed()` checks it: a live session gets the page in its own
frame (the menu, Back to Home; a 405 keeps its Allow); a cookie that resolves to nobody gets the plain page and is cleared (SL7, SL8 now
cover a 404 with a cookie); any failure on the way (the database, the key, the frame) gives the plain 404 or 405, never a 503 or 500, and
leaves the cookie alone. `MistypedAddressTest`, `UiUnitTest::testAMistypedAddressWithACookieKeepsItsStatusWhenTheDatabaseFails`,
`SessionLimitsTest::testAFailurePageClearsAnEndedCookieButNeverALiveOne`.

**MA2. The bottom bar of a short page stands at the foot of the screen.** Seen on 2 Nov: a new purchase order with one line had its bar
half way up the screen (sticky only sticks on a page that scrolls). app.js moves the free space under the page above the last `.doc-bar`
(and the work area's bottom padding with it, so nothing scrolls), again on resize and when the page changes size. A page that scrolls,
and a bar with something drawn under it (a stock operation's files), are left as they are. No change without the script.

**MA3. Review.** Codex (runs/sf_codex1.txt): 1 MEDIUM (a database failure while checking the cookie turned the 404 into a 503 without
Allow) and 2 LOW (the bar stopped the padding's height above the foot; a bar with files under it was moved), all fixed; the re-check
(runs/sf_codex2.txt) found none.

## ERPNext mode changes no longer wait in Approvals (branch `mode-review-off`, 4 Nov 2026; MO1-MO4; tracker CW-209)

**MO1. A switch, off.** The owner, 4 Nov 2026, seeing 1,924 "Mode changes" in Approvals: "you close it all and it should not come to
approvals any more". While CW only listens ERPNext owns the selling modes, so answering them changed nothing useful (CW-209), and at the
switch CW starts from the shop's modes. 0059 adds `relay.mode_review` (bool, off, agreed: Settings › Rules and numbers › Messages from
ERPNext, "Ask about ERPNext mode changes"; On / Off). On is the behaviour before 0059, for the day someone wants them asked again.

**MO2. Off: noted, never asked.** `RelayIntake::modeLine()` checks the switch after the "changes nothing" filter (D14), so every line is
still claimed and settled in relay_line (`no_change`, reason `review_off`), relay_mode_seen keeps the newest change time (an older message
arriving late is still `older_than_known` after the switch goes back on), and an older request of the same variant still open is closed
as `superseded`, exactly as a change that changes nothing closes it. Unknown or unmatched variants stay `skipped`. Nothing is applied: no
stock rule, selling mode or low-stock level changes.

**MO3. The ones open are closed in one go, by 0059.** Every open policy_review row of source `erp_update_product` becomes `dismissed`,
resolution `review_off`, with a note; one audit row (`queues.modes.close_all`, actor system:migrate) says how many and the oldest and
newest, written before the close and only while some are open, so a second run adds nothing. Other policy_review sources (count_gate and
the rest) are untouched. `Migration0059Test`.

**MO4. Tests and review.** Codex (runs/mo_codex_review.txt): 1 MEDIUM, fixed: a migration run stopped between the audit row and the close wrote a second audit row when run again; the audit row now waits for none from 0059 before it. Tests: The tests that relay mode changes to see them queued turn the switch on (`IntegrationTestCase::askModeChanges()`); every
integration test starts with it back at its seeded off. `RelayIntakeTest::testWithTheSwitchOffAModeChangeIsNotedAndAsksNoOne`.

## Copies of ERPNext purchase invoices (branch `erp-invoice-copy`, 4 Nov 2026; EC1-EC16; tracker CW-917)

The owner, 4 Nov 2026, on the research of the day (`/root/cw_work/runs/erp_invoice_copy_design_20261104.md`): "yes", then "917 do it".
Every Purchase Invoice staff submit in ERPNext is also kept in CW as a posted supplier invoice, so CW holds the suppliers and their prices
