on the switch-over day, WITHOUT ever adding the stock a second time (it reached CW already through the shop's relay as goods_in lines). It
is the "nightly read-only import of ERPNext purchase invoices" of plan §15.4 (Parallel run), started now and every half hour. The owner's
six choices were made for him on the brief (each is a setting he can change, but EC5): a CW job reads ERPNext's REST API; back-fill from 1
Sep; unknown suppliers made; copied prices become last prices; copies never feed the cost; the copies written by a system caller.

**EC1. CW reads ERPNext, GET only, with its own read-only user: a change to PI8.** PI8 ("CW never connects to ERPNext") stays true for the
opening stock and for every write; this job is the one exception, approved by the owner on 4 Nov. `Invoices\ErpApiReader` makes three reads
and nothing else: the list of Purchase Invoices (`company` = erp_copy.company, `docstatus` in (1, 2), `posting_date` >= the from date, and
after the cursor; fields name and modified; `modified asc, name asc`; pages of 100 by KEYSET: each page asks for what comes after the last
(modified, name) read, through `or_filters` (modified > m, name > n), so an invoice changed while the pages are read moves to the end and
none is skipped, and an ERPNext that ignores the keyset is refused, never looped), one invoice by name (its items and taxes inside),
and the Items of its rows (`is_stock_item`, `custom_variant_id`). Never ERPNext's stock feed (PI8: it marks invoices Synced), never a method
call, never a write. The user is CW's OWN (never the shop's write token, `App/api/bulk_with_item.php`): app.env `erp_read_url`,
`erp_read_key`, `erp_read_secret` (or `CW_ERP_READ_*`), parsed by `CW\Config`, sent only in the Authorization header, never printed (a
missing key is named, never a value; `__debugInfo` hides it; errors give the HTTP status and ERPNext's exception type). The transport is
injected (`ErpTransport`; the real one is curl over https only, no redirect, timeouts, a 16 MB cap): the tests use fixtures, no network. An
item ERPNext does not return stops the run (fail closed: without it the relay's line numbers are not known).

**EC2. Six settings, the switch off.** 0060: `erp_copy.on` (OFF; On / Off), `erp_copy.company` (VAPE AND GO; typed as ERPNext writes it,
a formula refused), `erp_copy.from_date` (2026-09-01), `erp_copy.create_suppliers` (on), `erp_copy.update_prices` (on), `erp_copy.per_run`
(200, 2-5000: the most invoices one run reads, EC17, EC19); Settings › Rules and
numbers › "Invoices from ERPNext"; each with its baseline, provisional as every new one. While the switch is off the job reads and writes
nothing and says so. There is no setting for the cost (EC5).

**EC3. What a copy is.** A posted SINV (a debit note: a posted SCN, EC8) with `supplier_invoice.origin` 'erpnext' (0060, INSTANT, in the
posting anchor only for a copy so every older record keeps its V2 content), the supplier (EC11), the supplier's number (ERPNext's bill_no,
else the ERPNext name), the date on the paper (bill_date, else posting_date), the due date when ERPNext has one on or after it, the totals
(GBP: ERPNext's base_* amounts; net = its rows plus its charges that are not VAT; VAT = its tax rows whose account or description says VAT),
and its lines: every stock row a goods line, every other row a service, freight (by its words) or other amount, every charge that is not
VAT and adds to the total a line, and a rounding "other" line so the lines add up to ERPNext's net total to the penny. A goods line is
packs of the ERPNext purchase unit at ERPNext's base_net_rate when they are whole packs of CW units (units per pack = conversion factor x
u), else CW units at the row's unit price. The item and units of a stock row, in this order: (1) the relay line already booked for it
(Vape and Go, goods_in or supplier_return, doc_ref = the ERPNext name, line_index = its place among the invoice's stock rows, as
`relay.php` numbers them): its item, with u from the item's link (sku_erp_item, else the listing) when that link names the same item, else
from what the relay booked; (2) the ERPNext item's sku_erp_item x units_per_item; (3) the Vape and Go listing of Item.custom_variant_id (else
the item code, as the add-on sends it) x units_per_item, linked or quarantined. Units = |stock_qty| x u.

**EC4. Written by a system caller, through a narrow door in the document base.** `Documents::SYSTEM_JOBS` (`erp_copy` => SINV, SCN):
`postBySystem()` makes and posts in one transaction (created_by and posted_by NULL, the actors system:erp_copy, the handler's checks as for
a person), `reverseBySystem()` cancels (CW's own reasons allowed). Never an approval, never a review: the job copies a record ERPNext
already accepted, and the owner wants Approvals to stay clear (MO1). Every other system caller, a store's job and every other document type
are refused (403 system_job_only); a person still posts as a person. This is the least invasive way: the document base kept its staff rule
everywhere else and its columns were already nullable.

**EC5. A copy never moves stock and never feeds the cost; no setting for it.** receive_mode NULL (never createDraft's path, never "count on
arrival" nor "book as received"), no delivery and no order on a line (`createCopy` refuses one, 422 copy_links), so the posting books no
stock, no goods on their way, no value event. `SupplierInvoiceHandler::post()` refuses a copy, under its locks, posted by anyone but the job,
or with a receive mode, a delivery or order link, an arrival row or a ledger row (409 copy_moves_stock), and never writes value events for
one. Average cost reads only ledger rows with a unit cost and the relay's goods_in has none, so the cost is untouched; the opening estimate
already has ERPNext's valuation, and the switch-over re-bases it. This is a rule, not a choice: a copy feeding the cost would count ERPNext's
purchases twice.

**EC6. A row CW cannot place: the whole invoice waits.** No item (`no_item`), a quantity that is not whole CW units (`fractional_qty`), units
other than the relay booked (`units_differ`: the add-on sends the PURCHASE unit, so a box bought as 2 is 2 x u in CW; the copy would say 24),
a price below zero, unclear taxes (a deducting row, or rows + VAT + charges not ERPNext's total to the penny), an unknown supplier with
making suppliers off, the supplier's number already on a live CW invoice (`duplicate_number`, UNIQUE supplier + number), a debit note whose
invoice is not copied or does not match row by row, or the posting refused (`refused`, its code kept): the invoice is not copied at all,
`erp_pi.state` waiting with the problem, the row, the detail. It is tried again on every run from what CW kept (a link made, a supplier
made, its invoice copied since). Never half copied: the copy is made inside a savepoint and a refusal rolls back to it.

**EC7. Cancelled, amended or changed in ERPNext: CW follows; nobody else changes a copy.** docstatus 2: the copy is cancelled (reason
erp_cancelled), the credit notes that credit it first; never copied: skipped. An amendment ("-1", amended_from): the copy of the invoice it
amends is cancelled first (erp_cancelled; that invoice is cancelled in ERPNext), then the amendment is copied as any invoice (its number is
free again) and keeps amended_from. The same name read again with another content hash after it was copied (header, rows, charges; not the
status, the time or the names shown): the copy and its credit notes are cancelled (erp_changed), it is copied again, and its credit notes'
invoices wait to be copied against the new copy: never two live copies. Read again unchanged: nothing. A person cannot edit, receive, time,
make final, stop, cancel or credit a copy (409 erp_copy; the page offers none of them): ERPNext is where they are changed.

**EC8. A debit note is a credit note, never a CW debit note.** An ERPNext return (is_return, return_against) becomes a posted SCN crediting
the copy of the invoice it returns against, each goods line crediting that copy's line for the same ERPNext row (purchase_invoice_item), else
the first line of the same item with enough left; amounts as positives. A CW debit note (DN) would book stock out a second time: the relay's
supplier_return did it. A copy is credited only by such a copy, and a copy credits only a copy (`credits_copy`); the credit note of a CW
return whose invoice is a copy credits no invoice.

**EC9. The match of a copy: matched, or "not booked in CW".** `InvoiceMatch::compute` matches a copy's goods lines against what the relay
booked for their rows (`erp_pi_line.relay_units`), never against a delivery: booked, the units are "there" (a difference is a real one and
goes to To match like any other); not booked, the line is within with the reason `not_booked`, never off. So copies do not flood To match.
The price is not checked (no order). The job keeps relay_units, and works the match out again, in the same transaction (at the copy, and
when a later run finds the relay booked a row since: `relayRecheck`), so the nightly V4 always agrees.

**EC10. V8.** `InvoiceInvariants` checks every night that a copy and its cancellation have no ledger row, no value event, no arrival row and
no receipt made from them, no receive mode, no delivery or order on a line, were made and posted by the job alone; and that erp_pi agrees
(copied: a posted copy; reversed: a reversed copy; every posted copy named by one copied row).

**EC11. An unknown supplier is made as a draft, named from ERPNext.** `Suppliers::createFromErp` (the job only): status draft (never active:
a person completes it and asks for its activation), name = ERPNext's supplier name, erp_name = the ERPNext name, created_by NULL and
created_actor system:erp_copy, a note saying it came from an ERPNext invoice. Existing columns only. With erp_copy.create_suppliers off its
invoices wait (`unknown_supplier`).

**EC12. What is kept.** erp_pi (one row per ERPNext invoice, never deleted: what was read, the hash, the state, the problem, the CW
supplier, the copy, the last cancellation), erp_pi_line (its rows as read and, copied, the item, units, how it was found, the relay line and
units, the copy's line; replaced when a re-read brings other content to an invoice not copied), erp_copy_run (one row per real run: the
company, the from date, the cursor it read from and the one it reached, the summary; written once, finished once). The cursor is the
(modified, name) of the last ERPNext invoice a finished run of the same company and from date read (the list's order): the next run reads
what comes after it, so a limited run goes on even through invoices of the same time; a failed or stopped run keeps the old one. Waiting
invoices are tried again the longest-untried first (each try moves `read_at`), so none is left out behind others that stay blocked.

**EC13. Prices: only where the item and the units are certain.** With erp_copy.update_prices on, a goods line whose item came from the relay
(in the same units) or from the item's sku_erp_item link, in whole ERPNext purchase units, gives an `invoice` price (supplier_item_price,
source_ref = the ERPNext name, document_id = the copy) of the supplier item (supplier, item, pack: made when there is none, an alternative
supply, never preferred: reorder is not changed by a copy) on the paper's date; the last price moves when it is the newest (SupplierItems'
rule, S4). A line found through the listing only, or in CW units, gives none. A price stays in the history when its copy is cancelled
(supplier_item_price is append-only, S4 reads it).
A tax row that only feeds the value (category Valuation), VAT or not, is not in the supplier's total and is left out; the rows, the VAT
and the charges must add up to ERPNext's grand total to the penny, else the invoice waits (`taxes_unclear`).

**EC14. On the screens.** Purchases › Supplier invoices › From ERPNext (a Show choice, no count): the waiting ones with why in words, the
copied, the cancelled and the not copied under Show, each copied one linking its copy; the switch and the last run in one line. A copy
carries the soft tag "From ERPNext: stock already booked" in the list and on its page, with its ERPNext number. Never in Approvals.

**EC15. The job.** `bin/copy_erp_invoices.php`: does nothing while the switch is off (says so, exit 0); a dry run by default (each
invoice's transaction rolled back: nothing written, not even the run; a debit note whose invoice the dry run would copy is counted as
copied); `--apply`, `--from=YYYY-MM-DD` (copies from that date, ignoring the cursor: the back-fill), `--limit`; one log line and each invoice
that waits. The cron line, every 30 minutes with --apply, on both servers (`deploy/*/cw-*.cron`); never run by the installers. A failed
read ends the run (`failed`, the cursor kept); a refusal of one invoice is noted on it and the run goes on.

**EC16. Tests and what is left for the owner.** Tests: `ErpInvoiceCopyTest` (switch off, dry run, copy with no stock, waiting, units,
suppliers, prices, debit note and cancellation, amendment, change, relay later, approval rules, duplicate number, V8, the refusals, a failed
read), `ErpCopyJobTest`, `ErpCopyScreensTest`, `Migration0060Test`, `ErpApiReaderTest`, `ErpCopyUnitTest`. Codex reviewed 0ccc04c
(runs/ec_codex_review1.txt): 8 MEDIUM and 2 LOW, all fixed with tests where they can fail: offset paging could skip an invoice changed
between pages (keyset now), a numeric item code stopped the run, an inclusive time cursor never got past a limit or a tie ((modified, name)
now), a refused attempt could keep an older content for a later retry (kept first now), the relay fallback derived units from the
purchase unit (only when it is the stock unit now), the oldest 2,000 waiting and the newest 500 unbooked copies could starve the others
(longest-untried first; only copies the relay booked since), a VAT row for the value only made an invoice wait (left out now), a total a
few pence off was copied with another total (to the penny now), and a dry run's debit note against an invoice it fetched itself counted as
missing (counted after its invoice now; a dry run stays an estimate for debit notes). The re-check (runs/ec_codex_review2.txt) confirmed
eight and found one more, fixed: a copy whose cancellation was refused was never tried again once the cursor was past it (now every copy
with a problem is read from ERPNext again on the next run). Two of its points are kept as decided: the relay fallback still waits when
the purchase unit is not the stock unit (the relay counted purchase units, so CW's stock for that row is what is in doubt: a person looks;
deriving the units from the stock quantity would hide that), and a dry run's debit notes stay an estimate. Its other point, that 0060 was
changed after the first commit, does not apply: 0060 was never applied outside the test schemas (a migration is never edited once it is).
Before the switch is turned on, the owner makes the
ERPNext user (EC1) and the integrator puts its three keys in app.env; then a dry run with `--from=2026-09-01`.

**EC17. The final Codex review of d8af941: three MEDIUM, fixed.** (1) 0060 resumes after a stop: its three tables are `CREATE TABLE IF
NOT EXISTS`, its inserts were already guarded, and the `ALTER TABLE supplier_invoice ADD COLUMN origin` is now its LAST statement, so a
stop anywhere before it runs again cleanly and the file is recorded once the ALTER succeeds (`Migration0060Test`). (2) A run reads at most
`erp_copy.per_run` invoices from ERPNext (200; `--limit` overrides it), frees each raw invoice once it is in CW's terms, and keeps its
cursor, so a big back-fill goes on run after run instead of running out of memory with its cursor never moving. `cursor()` takes the newest
finished run of the company whose from date is the same OR EARLIER (everything it read, from its date, is everything a later date asks for
up to its cursor): a `--from` back-fill that reached the cap is gone on with by the cron. (3) The job's reasons `erp_cancelled` and
`erp_changed` must exist, be active and apply to reversals (what `Documents::reverseBySystem()` needs): a reason code made by hand before
0060 with the same code is kept as it is (never rewritten by a migration), and every run, a dry run too, stops before it reads ERPNext
while one of them could not cancel a copy (409 erp_copy_reasons, exit 3, naming the reason and Settings › Reasons).

**EC18. The re-check of fac1ea9 (runs/ec_codex_review4.txt), fixed.** (1) The column is added only while it is not there (a prepared
statement, as 0056), so even a stop after the ALTER and before the migration's own record runs again cleanly; a column of that name
with another definition stops the migration, naming it. (2) The cap is ONE budget of invoices read a run, the invoices a debit note or an
amendment needs and the copies read again included: an invoice whose needs no longer fit is left for the next run (the cursor stays on
the one before it; the first invoice of a run is always taken with what it needs, so every run goes on), and the invoices debit notes
wait for (`original_missing`) are read within what is left. (3) A back-fill from a date BEFORE the setting's that reached the cap is
drained by the next runs with its own date (for reading and for copying) until a run of it is not capped; then the setting's date again.

**EC19. The re-checks of ce9e1a0, 438dfb1 and bcb68d1 (runs/ec_codex_review5.txt to 8).** Fixed: a numeric name of an invoice a debit note needs stays a name (no
type error); a run switched off before its end counts as one with more to read, so a back-fill from an earlier date is still gone on
with from its date; and a share of each run's budget (a quarter, at least one, never all: so `erp_copy.per_run` is at least 2) is kept
first for the copies whose cancellation was refused and the invoices waiting debit notes need, so a steady flow of fresh changes can
never starve them; the two kinds are taken in turn, and the kind that goes first changes from one run to the next (a copy whose
cancellation stays refused never keeps out an invoice a debit note waits for), and what the fresh changes leave of the budget reads more
of them (a fresh invoice read and then left for the next run is counted as read; the turn is taken from the runs before, so a dry run
reads what the real run then reads); a debit note whose invoice ERPNext cannot give now waits
for it (`original_missing`) instead of stopping the run; `erp_copy.per_run` is taken as at least 2 whatever is stored (`--limit=1`, a run
by hand, keeps no share); a copy whose attempt was refused is counted with the waiting ones in a run's summary. Kept as decided: the first
invoice of a run is always taken with what it needs (at most two more reads than the budget), and an invoice read and then left for the
next run costs that read: both keep every run moving, and the overshoot is bounded.

## Reorder › Suggestions: "Buy for N days" (branch `reorder-buy-for`, 4 Nov 2026; BF1-BF13)

The owner, 4 Nov 2026: "based on previous data sales how many will we need to buy for custom days, weeks etc. low stock threshold and
all". Before this branch a buyer could not say "buy enough for 2 weeks": the order cycle R came only from the main supplier
(`supplier.review_days`) or the setting `reorder.default_review_days` (I64), and nothing on Suggestions, its download or "Create draft
orders" took a number of days (searched: no `buy_for`, cover or horizon option in `src/`, no word for it in `Words`). Low-stock warnings
already exist (PG7, "Use the safety stock as the warning") and are not rebuilt. Code: `migrations/0061_reorder_buy_for.sql`; changed
`src/Reorder/{ReorderList,ReorderLines,ReorderRefresh,DraftPos,ReorderSettings,Explain}.php`, `src/Ui/{Controller/ReorderController,ReorderWhy,
Words}.php`, `src/Settings.php`, view `reorder`, `public/ui/assets/app.css`; tests BF10.

**BF1. What N is.** On Suggestions a buyer chooses "Buy for": "Usual (each supplier's order cycle)" (the default: exactly the list of
before), 1 week, 2 weeks, 4 weeks (the presets), or types a number of days. With N chosen every line uses N in place of R: target T =
⌈d·(L+N+S)⌉, then the smallest and largest stock, need = T − (available + on order), packs rounded up (or to the nearest), the smallest
order, the steps and "never suggested" exactly as `ReorderMath::line()` does. The reorder point ⌈d·(L+S)⌉, "Will run out" and the safety
stock ⌈d·S⌉ do not depend on R, so they do not change: N says how much to buy, not when. "Products to buy", the count and the cost at the
top, the groups, the order, the pre-ticked packs, the download, the "Why" and "Create draft orders" all follow N; the other filters
(brand, main supplier, words, will run out, below the safety stock, CW or website stock) are as before.

**BF2. One maths, never a second copy of the formula for what is shown.** `ReorderList::forDays($line, N)` works a line out again with
`ReorderMath::line()` from the line's own inputs with N as R, and adds `buy_for` (N) and `usual_review` (the line's own R; `review` is N,
so cover = lead + review + safety still reads true). A stored line (its JSON) and a line worked out now (the website-stock view, the
drafts) go through the same function, so the list, its download and the drafts agree (`ReorderBuyForTest`: the stored list bought for N
equals the list worked out now for N, line by line and in order). The usual line gets no new key: the stored lines, their sha1 and the
usual list are as they were.

**BF3. Where N is worked out (the performance choice).** About 17,000-20,000 lines are listed on production; the page reads 200. Three
ways were weighed: (a) decode every stored JSON line and work N out in PHP: 20,000 JSON lines a page view (the whole download does it:
1.6 s); (b) read the compact rows into PHP and work N out there (measured: 132-186 ms and 20,000 rows sent to PHP on every page view);
(c) **chosen:** keep the few inputs of a line's need in `reorder_line` (0061: `d_e6` (sales a day × the factor, e6), `lead_days`,
`safety_days`, `stock_position` (available + on order), `min_stock`, `max_stock`, `units_per_pack`, `moq_packs`, `multiple_packs`,
`round_nearest`, `pack_price_e4`; `never_suggested` was there) and let SQL choose, count and order the lines for N
(`ReorderLines::buyForSql()`): no row is sent but the page's 200 ids, never a JSON line beyond those 200, never the ledger or an order
line. The 200 lines are then read as always and worked out by `forDays()` (BF2), so the figures shown are ReorderMath's own; the SQL only
decides which lines and in what order. It is the same integer arithmetic (every quantity is whole and never below 0, so `DIV` is PHP's
`intdiv` and `(a + b − 1) DIV b` its `ceilDiv`); `ReorderBuyForTest::testTheSqlWorksNOutExactlyAsReorderMath` holds it to ReorderMath on
400 random lines (rates, factors, days, stock below 0, the smallest and largest stock, packs of 1-100, the smallest order, steps, nearest
rounding, never suggested, no price) for N = 1, 7, 14, 28, 45, 180 and 365: the same lines to buy, in the same order, and the same count.

**BF4. The inputs are written with the line, and a row without them is mended.** `ReorderRefresh` writes the eleven inputs with every line
it writes (`ReorderLines::inputs()`), and a line counts as unchanged only when its sha1 AND its stored inputs are the line's: a row of
before 0061, or one written by older code during a deploy (it names its columns and leaves the inputs as they were), is written again at
the next run whatever its sha1. 0061 fills the rows already there from their own stored line (`reorder_line_detail`), only rows without
inputs and only lines that have them. A listed row without inputs (`d_e6` NULL) is never "to buy" for N and sorts with no value; its own
line is still shown bought for N under "Every product"; while any line of the filters has none, the page says "Some products are still
being worked out for a chosen number of days … within N minutes" (`ReorderLines::page()`'s `waiting`, counted in the same read).

**BF5. Settings (0061, each with its version 1; provisional, owner to confirm; Settings › Rules and numbers › Reorder).**

| Setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `reorder.buy_for_presets` | 7,14,28 | the choices offered, in days, in that order (up to 12, each 1-999); 7 shows as "1 week", 14 as "2 weeks" |
| `reorder.buy_for_min_days` | 1 | 1-365, at most the largest |
| `reorder.buy_for_max_days` | 180 | 1-365, at least the smallest |

A preset outside the smallest and largest is not offered (never refused: the page stays usable); `ReorderSettings::buyFor()` checks the
range like `engine()` (500 bad_setting outside it). A choice or a typed number outside the range is refused in words: a typed one keeps
the choice ("Buy for: type a whole number of days from 1 to 180."), a choice out of range gives the usual list and says so.

**BF6. "Create draft orders" with N.** The draft form carries N (`buy_for`, a hidden field, as the filters are carried); the page's packs
are the packs for N, so the drafts hold what the buyer saw, and each draft line keeps N's suggestion in `suggested_units`
(`DraftPos::create(..., $buyFor)`; the audit row `reorder.draft_pos` says `buy_for`). The check of what was shown (PO11: the main supplier
item and its pack) is unchanged. N outside the range (changed in the form, or the setting changed since): 422 `bad_buy_for`, nothing
ordered, the usual list drawn with the refusal. FormOnce's payload carries N only when chosen (the usual form's payload is as before, so
a form sent twice is still one effect). The redirect after the drafts keeps N, so the list shown is still the one bought for N.

**BF7. The words.** The "Why": "Delivery takes 3 days, bought for 14 days (you chose), plus 5 spare days = 22 days." in place of "…and you
order every 7 days…"; the maths (Explain, the download's `why`): "Cover 3 lead + 14 bought for (you chose, in place of 7 review) + 5 safety
= 22 days". The download keeps its columns: `review_days` is N, `cover_days`, `target`, `need`, `packs`, `units`, `value` are N's.

**BF8. The screen.** "Buy for" sits beside the search, outside Show (a choice of what to buy, not a filter of which lines): its choice
(Usual, the presets, and the number chosen when it is not a preset, so the list drawn for a typed number says so), a box for a typed
number (drawn empty, so a number in it was just typed and wins), and "Work out". No script (the page's own app.js only); the box and the
choice share the row on a phone, 44 px high (`.tb-buyfor`, `input.tb-days`). The figure strip says "Bought for 2 weeks (you chose)" under
"Products to buy"; the pager and the download link carry N; "Show the whole list" goes back to the usual list. Every word is in `Words`
(`REORDER_BUY_FOR`, `WHY cover_buy_for`, `REORDER_ENGINE_ERROR bad_buy_for`, the settings' names and help).

**BF9. EXPLAIN and times on 20,000 lines (`/root/cw_work/runs/bf_explain_scratch.php`, outputs `bf_explain{,2,3,4}.txt`; MySQL 8.4.8 on
the test machine, each the median of 7 warm runs; a "page" is the ids and the 200 lines).** The first build took 370 ms a page for N (23
ms the usual one), and two things changed: (1) the read for N names no index of the list's order (`IGNORE INDEX (ix_reorder_line_need,
_all, _below)`): they start with `listed`, true of nearly every row, so every row read through one was a second look-up by primary key
(100 ms of a 146 ms count); a brand or a supplier still takes its own index (10 ms, 29 ms); (2) each row's packs before the smallest order
and steps is worked out once, into a table of its own (`/*+ NO_MERGE(k) NO_DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN(k) */`): merged, MySQL wrote the
formula out again for "to buy", the count and the order. Now: a page for N **150-185 ms** (one pass of 70 ms for the counts, one of 90-100
ms for the page's ids, then the 200 lines), below the safety stock 113 ms, words 128-137 ms, page 40 178-197 ms, the download's ids
100 ms (the whole download 1.6 s, as the usual one: it decodes every line); the usual list as before (20-23 ms). PHP over the compact rows
(BF3 b) measured 132 ms with inline sums and 186 ms with ReorderMath, before the 200 lines: no faster, and it moves every row.

**BF10. Tests.** `tests/Unit/ReorderBuyForUnitTest.php` (N in place of R on worked examples; the smallest and largest stock, packs, the
smallest order, steps, nearest and never with N; the reorder point, urgent and the safety stock never moved; `forDays()` = ReorderMath with
N; the inputs; the days in words and the choices; the "Why" and the maths; the settings' ranges and words; 0061 runs again cleanly);
`tests/Integration/Reorder/ReorderBuyForTest.php` (the stored list bought for N: lines, "to buy", count, order, filters, = the list worked
out now; the order follows N with a largest stock; SQL = ReorderMath on 400 random lines × 7 N; drafts keep N's suggestion, 422 out of
range; the refresh writes the inputs and mends missing and old ones; the website-stock view); `tests/Integration/UiKernel/
ReorderBuyForScreensTest.php` (the choice, the box and their refusals, the list, its cost, its "Why" and download for N, the presets from the
setting, the website-stock view, "Create draft orders" with N: the packs shown and N's suggestions, the redirect, one effect, N changed in
the form refused); `tests/Integration/Migration0061Test.php` (the columns, the back-fill of the rows there, the settings, a second run, a run
stopped after the columns, some of the columns only). Changed: `ReorderListTest` (the filters' defaults), `Migration0011Test` (pack G's and
these settings are tested by their own migration tests).

**BF11. Left out, and why.** (1) The item's reorder page (`/ui/purchasing/reorder/items/{id}`) still shows the usual line: it is one item's
settings page, and the list's "Why" shows N. (2) Low-stock warnings: the safety stock does not depend on R. (3) "Work out the list again
now" goes back to the usual list (its redirect names no filter, as before). (4) One N for the whole list, not one per supplier: a buyer who
wants different days for two suppliers filters by supplier and chooses again. (5) N never moves the reorder point or "Will run out" (BF1).
(6) No "What's new" entry: nothing is live; the entry is written at the go-live.

**BF12. The review.** Codex (read-only), `runs/bf_codex_review1.txt` on 86f7366: no HIGH, one MEDIUM, fixed test-first
(`runs/bf_fix1_red.log`: four tests red on the INT column): `stock_position` was an INT, but stock + on order may add up past
2,147,483,647 (open orders have no limit in total), and the back-fill or a refresh chunk would then stop (strict mode), the usual list's
refresh with it. It is a BIGINT now (0061 was never applied outside the test schemas). `Migration0061Test` back-fills a position of
3,000,000,000; `ReorderBuyForTest` mends one and its random lines hold positions past an INT both ways. Its remarks on the tests, taken: the
random test's rows now carry their stored lines, so its second page is checked line by line (the ids, and ReorderMath's packs and cost for
N), not only its count.

**BF13. The Codex re-check of 9df1a0e (`runs/bf_codex_review2.txt`): the BIGINT fix confirmed; one MEDIUM, fixed test-first
(`runs/bf_fix2_red.log`: three tests red, `bf_fix2_green.log`).** A line's cost (packs × pack price, e4) can pass what a whole number holds
at the largest accepted demand and price bought for many days (1,000,000 a day, £9,999,999.9999 a pack, 180 days: 179,000,001 packs), and
the list for N stopped with an SQL error ("BIGINT value is out of range" in its order), its page with a 500 (a float cost cannot print).
Now a line's cost is `ReorderMath::value()`: exact up to `ReorderMath::VALUE_MAX_E4` (£100,000,000,000,000.00) and held there above it,
never a float (the usual list's cost is unchanged below it; above it the usual list's refresh failed the same way before). The SQL works the
cost out in DECIMAL and holds it at the same figure, so the order is the same as ReorderMath's; the page's total adds with the same hold
(`ReorderController::addCost()`). Such a line can never be ordered as it stands (an order line takes at most 1,000,000 packs). Tests: the
example in `ReorderBuyForUnitTest`, three lines at the largest demand and price in the random SQL = ReorderMath test, and the page, its
total and its download in `ReorderBuyForScreensTest`. The other products were checked against the columns' limits and stay within a
whole number: d·days at most 5·10^14 × 740 days, a position × 10^7 for the days left.

## A supplier's details are not needed unless switched on (branch `supplier-details-optional`, 5 Nov 2026; SD1-SD3)

The owner, 5 Nov 2026, after the 48 suppliers copied from ERPNext (4 Nov) could not be made usable: "then why we are keeping all those
mandatory same as erp dont make it mandatory. change it and finish the job". ERPNext's 48 suppliers hold a name only (read 5 Nov:
no address, contact, e-mail, phone, VAT number or payment terms on any of them; no Address or Contact linked; the shop's vendor tables
empty), so §5.2's completeness could never be met from what the business has kept.

- **SD1. Four switches, OFF (0062).** `suppliers.need_address` (address line 1, postcode, country), `suppliers.need_contact` (e-mail or
  phone), `suppliers.need_payment_terms`, `suppliers.need_due_diligence` (checked on, by, next review); Settings › Rules and numbers ›
  Suppliers, agreed (provisional 0: the owner asked). `Suppliers::missing($s, Suppliers::needs($db))` leaves out the groups switched off;
  the name is always needed, and an overseas supplier's import route as before (no switch: it is about the duty stamps, not a detail
  ERPNext lacked). The three callers read the switches: the activation request, the supplier page, the ERPNext seed import.
- **SD2. A missing switch row counts as ON** (`Settings::flag(..., true)`): code running on a schema before 0062 behaves as before, and
  `missing($s)` without `$needs` is the full list (unit callers and the earlier tests unchanged).
- **SD3. The approval rules are untouched.** "New suppliers" (`approvals.supplier_activation`) still decides whether a request waits for a
  reviewer; a recorded due-diligence check is still shown, and an overdue one still warns on an order (PurchaseOrders, Home). The tests
  start with the four back at their seeded off (`IntegrationTestCase::setUp`, as MO4 does for mode changes: the nightly history check
  sees a value that matches its baseline); the supplier tests written before 0062 switch them on in `SupplierTestCase::setUp`; `testWithTheDetailSwitchesOffANameIsEnough`
  covers them off.

## A family's "Add items" is a picker with a search and ticks (branch `family-picker`, 5 Nov 2026; FP1-FP11)

The owner, 5 Nov 2026, on a family's page (Items › Item groups › a family): "why does it look like this and no search bar. finding and
adding product like this is going to take ages. i need a drop down with search and multicheck option". Until now "Add items" was only a
box for pasted CW numbers or barcodes (PB5). Built from main `ddbbb0f` in `/root/cw-famsearch`. No migration, no new permission, no new
setting, no service rule changed: the ticked items are put in by `Families::bulkAssign`, exactly as a pasted list is. Code:
`src/Ui/Controller/FamiliesController.php` (`find`, `pick`, the picker's data in `page()`), `src/Ui/Queries.php` (`familyPicks`), views
`family_bar` (the picker and the folded pasted list), `family_find` (new, the fragment), `family` (passes `pick`), `src/Ui/{Kernel,Words}.php`,
`public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`.

**FP1. One picker, in "Add items".** For whoever may add (`families.manage`, the bar's people) while the family is in use, "Add items"
(the bar's main action, PB5/W11.5, unchanged) opens: "Find items" (one search box), the line that says what was found, "Tick all shown",
"Untick all" and "N ticked", the items found as a list in its own scrolling box, each with a tick, then "Ticked items" (each with Untick)
and ONE button, "Put N in this family". Under it, folded, "Paste CW numbers or barcodes": the pasted list of PB5, unchanged (same route,
form key, words and result). A "drop down" read as a panel that stays open while ticking: a list that shut on every tick would make ticking
many items slow, the thing the owner asked to end.

**FP2. What the search finds.** `GET /ui/items/families/{id}/find?q=` (`FamiliesController::find`): fewer than 2 characters, nothing.
Otherwise `Queries::familyPicks` = `Queries::searchSkus` (the item search of the order's product box and the matching pages, SearchText's
rules: every word, in any order, in the name, brand, line and flavour, case and accents ignored, "20 mg" = "20mg"; a CW number however
it is written, "CW-000123", "cw 123", "000123", "123"; a barcode by `sku_barcode`'s key; joined items left out, also by their CW number),
the CW number and the barcode first, then by name, at most `FamiliesController::FIND_LIMIT` = 100 (a display number, as the lists' page
sizes, PB16; one more is read to know there are more: "Showing the first 100. Type more words to narrow it."). Each item: its name; its
CW number, brand and stock on hand in our own warehouses (`Families::onHand`); the family it is in now (`Families::ofItems`); "Not sold
any more" when its card says so (shown, tickable: a family may hold an old item). Cost: the word search is the established one (a scan of
`sku` in name order on `ix_sku_name` that stops at 101 matches), then three reads by primary key or index for at most 101 items
(`skus()`, `ofItems`, `onHand`); typing asks at most once per 300 ms. No item list is loaded whole.

**FP3. Not tickable: an item already in a family.** An item in this family says "In this family"; one in another family says "In another
family: <name>" (with "(switched off)" when that family is off), and its tick is off: `bulkAssign` would skip it (`already_here`,
`in_other_family`), and moving an item out of another family stays a person's choice on the item's page (PB5). The fragment is
`family_find` (root `data-fp-fragment`, no layout); a tick there has no `name` (it sends nothing); app.js's one `fetch` (`fragment()`)
asks it, a path of `/ui/items/families/` with the family's own `/find?` (checked before asking), parsed inert and taken only with its
marker (`FRAGMENTS`, as By Item's quick match). Who searches: everyone who reads the family (`catalogue.view`, the page's own permission);
the picker is drawn only for `families.manage`.

**FP4. Putting the ticked items in.** `POST /ui/items/families/{id}/pick` (`families.manage`, CSRF, the picker's own form key: sent twice,
one change; `FamiliesController::pick`): the ticked items are the form's ONE field `items` (their ids, separated by commas, in the order
ticked; each once; anything else in it left out: FP11); their CW
numbers (`CW-%06d`) are the list given to `Families::bulkAssign`: ONE transaction, audited (`family.bulk_assign`), the person checked
again, at most `items.family_bulk_max_rows` (PB5, 200), a doubtful item skipped and listed with its reason (an item joined or put in a
family since the search). The page comes back as after a pasted list: "Put in the family (N)", "Left out (N), with the reason". Nothing
ticked: 422 `nothing_ticked` ("Nothing was saved: tick at least one item first.") before anything is read; more than the setting: 422
`too_many_rows` in the picker's own words ("… Untick some and put those in, then tick the rest."), nothing saved; a family switched off
meanwhile: 422 `family_off`. A refusal opens "Add items" with the ticked items drawn again (`tickedRows()`: their CW numbers and names, at
most 1,000, the setting's top) and the form guarded as typed (W11.13). Nothing about the paste route changed.

**FP5. Ticks are kept while the words change.** A tick copies the item into the form's ticked list (and its id into `items`); the list shown is
replaced by each answer, the ticked list is not, and an item already ticked shows ticked when it is found again. So "ske 10mg", tick,
"ske 20mg", tick more, then one button. "Untick all" unticks every item (shown or not); "Tick all shown" ticks every item shown that may
be ticked. An answer asked for before newer words is never drawn; a failed one says so ("The search did not answer. Try again, or paste
the CW numbers below.") and keeps the ticks. Enter in the search looks the words up at once and never sends the form (a scanner's Enter).

**FP6. The limit in the page.** The form carries `data-max` (`Families::bulkMax`, the setting read when the page is drawn). A tick past it
is undone and "At most N items at a time. Put the ticked ones in first, then tick more." is said under the tools; "Tick all shown" that
would pass it ticks nothing and says the same; the button is off at none. The server checks again (FP4).

**FP7. Without the script.** The picker is drawn `hidden` and only app.js shows it (it needs the search); the pasted list is drawn open,
so without the script (or without `fetch`) "Add items" is the pasted list, as before. With the script the pasted list is folded, unless
it holds a refused list (`$pasted`: a list brought back, or `empty_list`), and opening "Add items" puts the cursor in the search. The
unsaved-edits guard (W9.15, W11.10): the picker's form carries `data-unsaved` and `data-leaves` (its search is a field to type); it holds
something to keep while, and only while, something is ticked (app.js sets and clears `data-dirty` from the ticked list; words typed in
the search alone are no edit).

**FP8. On a phone (390 px, as every page since 4 Nov).** Shared pieces only (the panel, `.btn`, `.tag`, the label and search field, 44 px
targets on a phone or touch screen): a row of the list is its whole tap target (at least 44 px, the tick 22 px), names and facts wrap
anywhere, the list scrolls in its own box (at most 26rem or 55% of the screen), the ticked list in its own (16rem); under 700 px the panel's
padding is 12 px, the count takes its own line and the button the row's width. Checked by reading the rules, not yet in a real browser at
390 px (the coordinator's check on staging).

**FP9. Words** (`Words::FAMILY_PICK`, new; `ITEMS_ERROR nothing_ticked`), plain and provisional as PB16's: "Find items", "Tick all shown",
"Untick all", "N ticked", "Ticked items", "Put N in this family", "In this family", "In another family: …", "Paste CW numbers or barcodes".
app.js fills the `%s` of the count, the button and Untick's label from the page's own words (`data-ticked-text`, `data-go-text`,
`data-untick-label`).

**FP10. Tests.** `tests/Integration/UiKernel/FamilyPickerScreensTest.php` (new): the search (every word, a CW number with and without
"CW", a barcode, the brand, the joined item left out also by its CW number, one letter, nothing found, an unknown family 404, the
100-item limit said, items in this and in a switched-off other family shown untickable with the name, a viewer may search and has no
picker, signed out the sign-in page) and the putting in (the hidden form and its words, added and skipped with the reason in the order
ticked, sent twice done once, nothing ticked, over the setting with the ticks drawn again and nothing saved, viewer, mapper, admin and
goods in refused, no CSRF token, a switched-off family; 998 ticks in one field, FP11). `UiUnitTest` (the routes' levels, `FRAGMENTS`),
`UiTemplatesTest` (the family's guarded forms: 4), `UiSecurityTest` (the two routes need a session, slot ui). The script was run in node on
a minimal DOM (`runs/fp_js_harness/`, outside the repo, on cw-test: 37 checks, `runs/fp_js.log`, `runs/fp_js_fix1.log`).

**FP11. The Codex review of 3047cb7 (`runs/fp_codex.txt`): one MEDIUM, fixed test-first; one more found in the harness.**
- **MEDIUM: the ticks could pass PHP's field limit.** Each tick was a field of its own (`pick_<id>`); with the bulk setting at its top
  (1,000), 998 ticks + the token + the key made 1,000 fields, and Kernel refuses such a form whole (400 `form_truncated`, I73: PHP drops
  the fields past `max_input_vars` without a word) before the ticks could be drawn again. The ticks are now ONE hidden field, `items`
  (app.js writes it from the ticked list on every change; a refused picker draws it again), so the form has three fields however many are
  ticked. `testAThousandTicksArriveAsOneField` (the old way's 1,000 fields refused, 998 ticks in one field read whole); the harness's
  checks of what the form sends (red on 3047cb7: `runs/fp_js_fix1.log`).
- **The search's `change` left the form "unsaved".** The page's marker (W12.17) counts a field's `change` as an edit; the search box's
  change on leaving it marked the picker as holding something with nothing ticked, so a link or another form asked first for nothing. The
  picker redraws on that change too (FP7: something to keep only while something is ticked). Shown red in the harness first
  (`runs/fp_js_red_change.log`).

## Settings › APIs: the ERPNext key entered on a page (branch `settings-apis`, 5 Nov 2026; AK1-AK12; 0063)

The owner, 5 Nov 2026, on CW-917's read-only ERPNext user (EC1), whose address, key and secret could only be put in `/etc/cw/app.env` by
the integrator: "on cw give me a section called apis and add a section there to add the key i will add there and hit submit". Built from
main `80de927` in `/root/cw-apis`. Code: `migrations/0063_api_credentials.sql`, `src/Admin/ApiCredentials.php` (new),
`src/Invoices/{ErpApiReader,ErpHttpTransport,ErpAddressRefused}.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/ApisController.php` (new), view `apis` (new),
`src/Ui/{Kernel,Sections,Words}.php`, `ReferenceController::SETTINGS_SECTIONS`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`, `bin/copy_erp_invoices.php`,
`public/ui/assets/app.css`.

**AK1. Where, and who.** Settings › APIs (`/ui/system/apis`), in Settings' section list after Stores, one card per API CW calls: today
"ERPNext (read only)". Who LOOKS: `system.view` (Admin, Reviewer, Auditor, Manager), as Stores: narrower than the other settings pages'
`reference.view` (every job), because the page is about another system's access, even though it shows no secret. Who SAVES, CHECKS and
REMOVES: `settings.manage` (Admin and Reviewer: the owner and Fazil, Y1), the level the settings pages use for "a setting that matters"
(no narrower owner-only level exists; `settings.manage` is LOCKED, so the roles screen cannot widen it). The routes check it, and
`Admin\ApiCredentials` checks it again inside its transaction (`ConfigHistory::authorise`). No new permission.

**AK2. The key and the secret are never shown, logged, audited or echoed.** The page shows the address, "Key ends …ABCD" (the key's
last 4 characters), "Secret: saved (hidden)", and who saved it and when; its fields for the key and the secret are always empty. A refused
form comes back with the address as typed and never the key or the secret ("Type the API key and the API secret again"). The secret's
field is `type=password` with `autocomplete="new-password"` (the request said `autocomplete=off`: browsers ignore `off` on a password
field, and Chrome would fill the person's own CW sign-in password into it, a later Save then sealing that password as the API secret;
`new-password` tells the browser not to fill one in); the key's field and the form are `autocomplete="off"`. What FormOnce keeps of a save
(its request hash) holds a keyed fingerprint of the key and the secret (`Csrf::forForm`, HMAC under the server's key), never them; its
stored answer is the redirect. Errors name a code and a sentence only. `ErpApiReader`'s key and secret are `#[\SensitiveParameter]`
(the key newly so), and `__debugInfo` hides them as before.

**AK3. Where they are kept: `api_credential` (0063).** One row per API, made by the migration (`erp_read`, empty, version 0); the app login
may only UPDATE a row's save columns (`Grants::UPDATE_ONLY_COLUMNS`: the address, the sealed key, its last 4, the sealed secret, the
version, who/when; no INSERT, no DELETE, never the name or who made it). The key and the secret are sealed apart with `Staff\SecretBox`
(app.env `ui_secret_key`, the key of the 2-step codes: XSalsa20-Poly1305, a random nonce each: the stored bytes are nonce || box); CHECKs
keep a row whole or empty, the address `https://<name>` in lower case, the last 4 letters and digits, a sealed value longer than a nonce
and a tag, the actors not empty. Every save, removal and check writes one audit row (`api.save`, `api.remove`, `api.check`; words
"API key saved", "API key removed", "API connection checked") naming the API, the address (and the one before), "key ends" and whether
the key and the secret were new or kept: never the key or the secret. The test clean-up empties the row instead of deleting it.

**AK4. The address is a name.** `ApiCredentials::url()`: `https://` and a host name of letters, digits, hyphens and dots with a last
part of letters, in lower case; a trailing "/" and the line end of a paste are dropped; an IP address, a port, a path, a user, a query, a
fragment, a backslash or a control character is refused (422 `api_bad_url`). While nothing is saved the field starts with
`https://vpg-erp.floverfy.com` (the shop's ERPNext; it resolved to a public DigitalOcean address on 5 Nov 2026). The name must also be one
CW trusts (AK12).

**AK5. No request forgery through the address.** A saved address is only ever called through `ErpHttpTransport`'s public-only mode: its
name is looked up once per transport (the system's resolver, IPv4) and every address it gives must be a global internet address (not
private, loopback, link-local such as the cloud's metadata service, shared, documentation, reserved, broadcast or multicast), else
`ErpAddressRefused` and nothing is sent; the connection then goes to that looked-up address only (`CURLOPT_RESOLVE`: a name that changes
its answer between the look-up and the call cannot lead elsewhere), on port 443, without a proxy, following no redirect (as before), the
certificate still checked for the name. "Check the connection" answers in one fixed word and never shows what came back, so the page
cannot read anything from another server. app.env's address (the integrator's) is called as before.

**AK6. A save.** The first save needs the address, the key and the secret (422 `api_need_key` / `api_need_secret`); a key or a secret is
6 to 64 letters and digits (ERPNext's, as `ErpApiReader` checks; spaces round it dropped; 422 `api_bad_key` / `api_bad_secret`). Later an
empty key or secret keeps the saved one (for the same address only: AK12) and a typed one replaces it; the same address with nothing typed changes nothing (no version, no
audit row: "Nothing changed"). A kept key or secret must still open with this server's key (the key of the 2-step codes changed since:
422 `api_cannot_open`, "type the key and the secret again"), so a save never leaves a row the job cannot use. The form carries the version
it was drawn with: a save or removal by someone else since is 409 `api_changed` naming who and when, nothing written; and a FormOnce key:
the same form sent twice is one save, sent again with another key or address (the back button) is 409 with a fresh form.

**AK7. Which key the job uses.** `ErpApiReader::fromConfig($config, $transport, $db, $box)`: the key saved on Settings › APIs when there is
one (called through the public-only transport unless one is given), else app.env's `erp_read_*` exactly as before (the integrator's way
keeps working); before 0063 (no table) app.env's. A saved key this server cannot open (no usable `ui_secret_key`, or another one) stops
with 503 `api_cannot_open`: never a silent fall back to app.env's, since the person typed a key and must know it is not the one used. The
missing-key message names both places. `bin/copy_erp_invoices.php` gives it its database (the cron line is unchanged). The page never
changes `erp_copy.on`: it says whether copying is on ("Saving a key here does not switch it on") and links Admins and Reviewers to the
setting.

**AK8. "Check the connection".** For Admins and Reviewers, while a key is in use (saved, or app.env's): ONE read with that key,
`GET /api/resource/Purchase Invoice?fields=["name"]&limit_page_length=1` (`ErpApiReader::check()`), at most 10 seconds, outside any
transaction. Its answer is one of: connected (ERPNext gave a list), wrong key or secret (401, or ERPNext's AuthenticationError), the user
may not read purchase invoices (403), cannot reach the address, the address does not lead to the internet (AK5), or another answer (its
HTTP code); before anything is sent: no key at all, a saved key this server cannot open, app.env's key not written as the reader takes it.
The page goes back to itself with the word (`?checked=`; only the listed words are drawn, a code only as three digits) and draws the
sentence in the ERPNext card, green for connected. Each check is audited (`api.check`: which key, the word, the code, the address, "key
ends"). It is a POST with the CSRF token but not FormOnce: it creates nothing, a read twice is harmless, and a network call is kept out of
the idempotency transaction.

**AK9. The page.** The settings shell (`apis.php`): the card's facts a row each (in use, address, key, secret, last change, whether
copying is on), the check's sentence, then for Admins and Reviewers the form (address, key, secret; Save, the one main button), the
check's row and Remove (a fold whose form needs its tick, "Yes, remove the saved key": the confirm step is in the page, no script; the
server refuses it without the tick, 422 `api_confirm`). Words in `Words::APIS`, `APIS_NOTICE`, `APIS_CHECK`, `APIS_ERROR` (plain, every
refusal says nothing was saved), `SEGMENT`/`RD_SETTINGS`/`PAGE_TITLE`/`PAGE_INTRO` `apis`, the audit words. No inline script or style; on a
phone the buttons take the row and the address and the key's end wrap (`app.css`, "Settings › APIs").

**AK10. Remove.** Empties the row (the address, the sealed key, its last 4 and the sealed secret; the version goes up and who removed it
and when are kept: "Removed by … on …"), audited. The job then uses app.env's key if there is one, else stops (`erp_read_unconfigured`)
until a key is saved again. Nothing is changed in ERPNext.

**AK11. Tests.** `tests/Unit/ApiCredentialsUnitTest.php` (the address, the public-only transport with a given look-up: no network, the
check's answers with fake transports: ONE GET, its address and header, no secret in what it returns, the words), `tests/Integration/Admin/
ApiCredentialsTest.php` (sealed bytes, last 4, kept and replaced values, version, permissions, every refusal writes nothing, removal, the
reader's order and its fail-closed, the audit rows without the key), `tests/Integration/UiKernel/ApisScreensTest.php` (as the app login:
the page and its fields, a save, a double click, the back button, CSRF, an auditor and a buyer, a form drawn before another save, the four
answers of a check through a fake ERPNext and the env key's check, Remove's tick; never a key or a secret in a page or the audit log),
`tests/Integration/Migration0063Test.php` (the table, its row, its CHECKs, a second run, the grants), `ErpCopyJobTest` (the job with a
saved key it cannot open, and with one it can: its address called through the public-only transport). Pinned lists updated:
`SectionsTest`, `RedesignCTemplatesTest`, `MenusTest`, `UiTemplatesTest`, `SetItYourselfScreensTest`.

**AK12. The Codex review of 9ddf7a0 (`runs/ap_codex.txt`): one HIGH and one MEDIUM, both fixed with tests.**
- **HIGH: a changed address could send the saved key elsewhere.** A person with `settings.manage` could change only the address to a
  public server of their own, leave the key and the secret empty (kept), and "Check the connection" or the next cron run would send the
  saved key and secret there. Now (a) a saved key and secret go only to the address they were saved for: another address needs both typed
  again (422 `api_new_address`, nothing saved), so nobody can send anything but what they typed; and (b) the address must be a name CW
  trusts (`ApiCredentials::allowedHosts()`): the shop's ERPNext, `vpg-erp.floverfy.com` (in the code), plus any name the SERVER's app.env
  lists (`erp_read_hosts=`, comma- or space-separated) and the name of app.env's own `erp_read_url`; never one the page adds (422
  `api_host_not_allowed`). The reader checks a saved address again before calling it (503 `api_host_not_allowed`: a row written around the
  page is never called either; the check says "CW did not call the saved address"). This also keeps a person from pointing the copy job at
  a server of their own that would feed it invoices. Tests: `testOnlyTheNamesTheServerTrustsMayBeSaved`, the "another address" part of
  `testALaterSaveKeepsWhatIsLeftEmptyAndReplacesWhatIsTyped`, the row written around the page in
  `testARemovalEmptiesTheRowAndTheReaderGoesBackToAppEnv`, the screens' and the job's (a name not trusted: never called).
- **MEDIUM: an answer's own text could reach the logs.** `ErpApiReader::get()` copied ERPNext's `exc_type` (any text, up to 60
  characters) into its error, which the job logs and keeps in `erp_copy_run.summary`: a server that echoed the token there put it in both.
  Now an error names the HTTP status and ERPNext's exception type only when it is one of Frappe's known names (`ErpApiReader::EXC_TYPES`);
  nothing else of the answer. Test: `testAnErrorNeverCarriesTheAnswersOwnText`.

## The lines of a document as a standard grid, with the keys of a standard screen (branch `doc-key-grid`, 6 Nov 2026; KG1-KG37)

The owner, 6 Nov 2026: "purchase invoice and sales invoice, purchase order view style need to standard feel, need also key shortcut: item
new and delete, field switching, all need". The purchase order's and the supplier invoice's new/draft page work like a standard accounting
screen (ERPNext, Zoho, Tally): a numbered lines table filled from the keyboard, with no page reload per line. Sales invoices do not exist in
CW yet (they come with accounting): not built; the grid is a shared piece they reuse (`docs/dev.md`, the grid's contract). Later the same
day, on the invoice screens: "this all shape more oval shape dont need this" (KG12); then the keys of a standard screen on every page
(KG13-KG20), no reload per line and Save without leaving the page (KG21-KG25), ERPNext's layout (KG26), the posting time (KG27), the head's
alignment (KG28), fields' corners (KG29), the supplier changed on a draft (KG30), and the demo the owner approved as the picture (KG31). Built from main `9190115` in `/root/cw-keygrid`. No
migration, no new permission. One service rule changed, on the owner's word: a draft's supplier changes with its lines (KG30).

**KG1. The standard look.** Both pages' lines are one table (`table.kg-grid`): a No. column (1, 2, 3...; the empty line has the next
number), Item (the name, its CW number small beside it), the page's own columns (the order: their code, pack, packs, £ per pack, £ total;
the invoice: qty, price, amount; the pack and their code on the invoice's sub line), the x. On a computer a row is one line high (32 px
boxes, the sub line beside the name); on a phone the cards as before, without the No. column. The last line is ALWAYS the empty line whose
Item box is the product box (the site's one dropdown, `combo()`: the supplier's products first, "+ Add new item" last).

**KG2. A line filled in place.** With the script, a choice in the empty line's list (or a scan with Enter that the products route answers
with exactly one item; asked at once, so a scanner's Enter does not wait for the 300 ms) is a new line: the item's name and CW number, its
pack, 1 pack, the supplier's last price for that pack (`resolve()`'s choices now carry `last_pack_price`; the fragment's `data-name`,
`data-code`, `data-pack`, `data-upp`, `data-their`, `data-price`), its amount; the empty line stays last and the cursor is in the new line's
Packs (Qty) box. Words naming several items open the list; none: said under the box; the route failing brings Add back (Enter is Add, as
without the script). The amounts and the totals (the order: products and items, net, delivery, VAT by code, total; the invoice: sub total,
total from the paper's figures when typed) follow the boxes as they are typed, worked out as PoMath does (half-up to the penny, VAT a line
at a time, a new line's VAT the supplier's code, else the setting); on a save the server works everything out again and the page shows
its figures.

**KG3. The keys** (inside the lines, Ctrl+S anywhere; a Mac: Cmd). Tab / Shift+Tab: box to box (Item, Qty, Price, the next line's; the x
and an item's link are out of the Tab order); Tab in the Item box with a choice marked takes it. Enter in a box: the next box (Enter never
sends the form from the grid); in the last box of the last line: the empty line's Item. Up / Down in a box: the same box of the line above
/ below (a line without that box is passed; in the Item box they stay the dropdown's; a number box's own step is not taken). Ctrl+Enter or
Insert: the empty line's Item box. Ctrl+Delete (Cmd+Backspace), or the x: the line goes at once, the numbers close up, the totals follow, the
cursor goes to the same box of the next line (or the empty line); "Line 3 removed." with Undo under the table, until the next removal or a
save. The empty line cannot be removed. Ctrl+S: the page's Save / Save as draft, never Confirm or make final. Esc shuts the dropdown. Never
taken: Alt+D, Ctrl+N/T/W, Ctrl+Shift+Delete, Delete or Backspace alone (Ctrl+Backspace stays the text's). One line of hints under the table
on a computer (hidden under 700 px and without the script), each key a kbd chip, "Cmd" on a Mac (`navigator.userAgentData`, else
`navigator.platform`); the boxes carry `aria-keyshortcuts`.

**KG4. Every line in one post, in the save's transaction (against the brief's field names, a decision).** Every POST of the page (Save,
Confirm, Save and make final, Fill the lines, "+ Add new item", "+ Add new supplier", a charge, Add) sends the saved lines as before
(`line_N_*`, `p_N`/`pp_N`), the saved lines removed (the order: `line_N_remove=1`, now read on any line, before its boxes; the invoice: its
`x_N=1`) and the NEW lines in ONE field, `new_lines`: JSON, `[{si: one of the supplier's packs | sku: an item (+ u, the items a case's
barcode stood for), q: the packs or qty as typed, p: the price as typed}]`, not one field per box (`new_N_si`...): one field however many
lines, so PHP's max_input_vars cannot cut lines off (the quick adjustment's `lines`, AG3; OV4). The server trusts none of it (`DocGrid::read`:
anything but that shape is 400 `bad_form`, nothing read). Each new line becomes its service's line after the saved ones (the order: before
its delivery charge) and is saved in the SAME transaction, version check and FormOnce, BEFORE the action: the order's
`supplier_item_id` (PurchaseOrders refuses another supplier's or a switched-off pack, as Add) or `sku_id` (an item in CW, not joined into
another); the invoice's goods line by `SupplierInvoices::goodsLine()`, Add's own rule taken out of `addItem()` and shared (this supplier's
pack, switched on; an item not joined; the price typed, else the pack's last). Packs: a whole number; on the order 0 leaves a new line out (as
it removes a saved line), on the invoice 1 or more (as a saved line). Prices are read as each page reads them (4 decimals at most, exact).
A new document is made by its first Save / Confirm with all its lines, under its one FormOnce key; choosing an item makes nothing. Add with
nothing in the box but lines in the grid saves them (Enter in a field of the page) instead of "Scan or choose a product first".

**KG5. FormOnce on a draft's save that adds lines.** A draft's Save, Confirm or Add that carries new lines runs through FormOnce (the
form_key every draft page already draws: `ui.po.grid`, `ui.invoice.grid`) as well as the version: sent again (a double click, the back
button, a browser retry) it is answered by its first answer and adds nothing twice; without new lines a draft's save is as before (the
version only). With new lines, an Add that finds several items or none leaves nothing saved (the page shows the choices with every line
kept), as on the new page; without them it saves the table first, as before.

**KG6. A refused save keeps every typed line.** Any refusal (a pack of another supplier, a switched-off one, a price that is not one, the
limit, a duplicate number...) shows the page again with every line as typed, the new ones drawn again (`DocGrid::rows()`, their field
too) and the lines removed still removed; the refusal is said at the top and on the line it concerns (`tr.kg-bad`, its words under the
name): the row the page's own check names (`detail.row`), else the service's line number mapped back to its row (`DocGrid::rowOf`). A
version conflict (the draft changed in another tab) keeps the NEW lines (they name their product), not the edits of the saved lines: those
lines may have changed under them, so the page shows them as they are now, as before.

**KG7. The limit.** A document's limit is its service's (`PurchaseOrders::MAX_LINES`, `SupplierInvoices::MAX_LINES`: constants every way in
already keeps; there is no setting for it, and none is added). The page gives it to the script (`data-kg-max`), which adds no line past it
and says so (`DOC_GRID too_many`); the server refuses more (422, the service's words) with every typed line kept; a field with more than
twice the limit is a bad form. The order's editor limit is unchanged: an order past what its one form can carry shows its saved lines
read-only (I73), and new lines are still added from the grid.

**KG8. Without the script, as before.** The new fields are only ever made by the script (the new lines' boxes have no name; the field stays
empty); the empty line keeps its Packs (Qty, Price) and Add, the x is a submit (a save without that row), Enter is Add. With the script
those boxes and Add go (`html.js … .kg-nojs`), and come back when the products route fails (`.kg-offline`). The hint line is hidden.

**KG9. One engine, on the one dropdown.** `docGrid(table, box)` in `app.js`, started by the product box of a grid's empty line (the box's
own `combo()`; no second dropdown engine: six `combo(` calls, the sixth a line's item box, KG22); what each page has is in its `data-kg-*` attributes (the contract in
`docs/dev.md`), so the sales invoice reuses it with its own columns. The quick adjustment grid's keys (AG5: `move`, `nextLine`, `goTo`) are
NOT shared: they are closures over its own row model with its own rules (After sets Units, Why skipped by Tab, Left/Right between cells);
sharing them would change that page's behaviour. The shared parts are `combo()` and `twoLines()`.

**KG10. The saved documents' lines** (`purchase_order`, `supplier_invoice`; `table.kg-view`): a No. column (the line's number), the CW
code small beside the name, the sub line beside it on a computer, numbers right-aligned, the totals block bottom-right as before. The
order's "Line N" in the sub line went (the No. column says it). On the invoice the Match column shows the pill alone when the line is
Matched; the detail line (billed · there · reference, why, the difference) stays only for a line that is not Matched. Two short notes stay
on a Matched line when they are there: the price that differs while the price check is off (PC19's information, the owner's rule) and
what was credited. Layout only: every action and link kept. Tests changed for it: `UiTemplatesTest` (the order's lines: the No. column and five,
was five), `InvoiceOnePageScreensTest` (the No. column first on the new invoice and the saved order; the add row's five cells, was four).

**KG11. Kept.** Every server rule: the creator's drafts, `doc.PO.post` / `doc.SINV.post`, `suppliers.manage` / `items.create`, versions,
FormOnce, CSRF, the supplier-item rules, VAT as stated, the unique supplier and invoice number, the 3-way match, timed invoices (PJ*),
"make final" after the save (PV16). Known limits: a new order's supplier changed after lines of the other supplier's packs were typed: the
save moves them to the new supplier (KG30, which replaced this limit); "+ Add new supplier" on a NEW page comes back with the new
supplier chosen and the grid empty (its lines were not saved; the address carries only what CARRIED lists; on a draft its lines stay, KG30);
Undo is one removal deep; after a refusal the lines
removed stay removed (no Undo for them; Leave without saving starts again); a new line's item name is not a link until it is saved.

**KG12. Square-ish corners on every page** (the owner: "this all shape more oval shape dont need this"). The radius tokens are small:
`--r-8` and `--r-10` 4 px, `--r-12` and `--r-14` 6 px, `--r-16` 8 px, `--r-pill` 4 px; the corners written by hand (999 px, 96 px, 40 px,
10 px, 9 px, 6 px) are tokens now, so buttons, boxes, dropdowns, status pills and tags, count bubbles, cards, the bar at the bottom and the
sign-in page's shapes are small-radius rectangles; a true circle (50%: a dot, an avatar, the tick) stays. One set of tokens for light and
dark. No test pinned a radius value (they pin the tokens); `UiUnitTest::testEveryCornerIsSmallAndNoneIsOval` pins it now.

**KG13. One layer of keys for the whole site** (the owner: "i need add item multiple short key option in keyboard, i need standard short
key option like Tally, ERPNext"). `app.js` has ONE table of keys (`KEYS`: each an id, a test and what it does) and ONE `keydown` listener
on the document for them; the first key whose test holds runs and its default is stopped (unless it answers that it was not for it). A
letter is read by its place on the keyboard (`ev.code`: `KeyN`, not `ev.key === 'n'`), so Alt / Option's special characters on a Mac and
other layouts work. Ctrl is Cmd on a Mac (`navigator.userAgentData.platform`, else `navigator.platform`); a Windows key is never Ctrl. Never
taken: Ctrl+N / T / W / Tab, Ctrl+Shift+N / T / Delete, Alt+D / E / F, the F keys, Delete or Backspace alone. Two listeners stay their
widget's own, as before: the drawer's Tab trap and the menus' Escape. The "/" of Search and match (SX5) is now the layer's `search` (its
own listener went; the page's `data-page-search` box first, opened when folded, as before).

**KG14. The lines' keys** (the order's and the invoice's grid). Tab / Shift+Tab box to box; Enter the next box; Up / Down the same box of
the line above / below; a new line: Ctrl+Enter, Alt+N or Insert (Insert has no Mac key: hidden there); remove the line: Ctrl+Delete,
Cmd+Backspace on a Mac, or Alt+R; Undo: Alt+U, or Ctrl+Z when the cursor is not in a box (in a box Ctrl+Z is the box's own); Ctrl+D fills
the box down from the line above (in the grid only: elsewhere it is the browser's bookmark); Alt+C in the item or supplier box: "+ Add new
item" / "+ Add new supplier" with what was typed, for who may (Tally's "create on the fly"); Esc shuts the dropdown, then leaves the box.

**KG15. Ctrl+S saves; it never makes final.** Ctrl+S is the page's Save / Save as draft (sent without leaving the page, KG24), never
Confirm or "Save and make final". Confirming an order sends it towards the supplier and fixes it; making an invoice final books its
goods and stock on the websites (now or at its posting time): a key pressed by habit every few seconds must never do that. ERPNext does the
same (Ctrl+S saves; Submit is a click). Confirm and make final stay one deliberate press of their button.

**KG16. The page's keys, on every page.** Ctrl+B: a new order or invoice from their lists and pages (Ctrl+N is the browser's): the
panel's link to it is pressed, so the unsaved-changes guard asks first; only for a person who may make one (`Context::newDoc`, the
document type's posting roles). Ctrl+G, or "/" when not typing: the page's search box, else the sidebar's find. Ctrl+P on a saved order: its
PDF (elsewhere the browser prints). "?" (not typing) or Ctrl+/: the panel of keys.

**KG17. Lists by the keyboard.** On the orders' and invoices' lists (`data-kb-rows`) Up / Down mark a row (scrolled into sight, `tr.kb-on`)
and Enter opens it (its link pressed: the guard asks first).

**KG18. The panel "Keyboard shortcuts".** In the layout of every signed-in page (not a partial: the template tests copy the layout alone),
two groups, Lines and Page; the script shows only the keys the page has (`data-kb-when`: grid, list, new, pdf) and a Mac's keys; Esc, Close
or a press on the backdrop shuts it and the cursor goes back where it was. Each key's words in `Words::KEYS`, its keys as printed on a
keyboard in `Words::KEYS_KBD` (a computer's, then a Mac's: Cmd, Option; '' none).

**KG19. The hint line is short.** Under the grid on a computer: Tab, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Del, Ctrl+S (Cmd on a Mac) with their words, then
"All keys (?)", which opens the panel. The full table is in `docs/dev.md`. The keys are named to screen readers (`aria-keyshortcuts` on
the Save button, the search box, the PDF link, the new-document link, the item and supplier boxes).

**KG20. Nothing of the keys without the script**: the panel and the hints are hidden; every page works as before.

**KG21. "+ Add new item" without a reload** (the owner: "add new item add option add"). The product box's last line "+ Add new item", the
button under the grid and Alt+C open the item's panel (filled with what was typed: digits a barcode, else the name). Its button sends the
panel by the one fetch to a route of its own, `POST /ui/purchasing/orders/new-item` and `/ui/purchasing/invoices/new-item`
(`PoAddNew::newItemLine`): who may add items first (403 for anyone else, before anything is read), the supplier chosen, CSRF, its own
FormOnce key (the same form sent twice makes one item), then Pack B's item (barcode on another item, the same name: refused in words with
the item(s) to use instead, "Use this one") and this supplier's pack of it when a code, pack or price is typed (`PurchaseOrders::makeItem`,
taken out of `addNewItem`, which still uses it). It never touches the document: the answer is a fragment (`data-ni-fragment`) with the new
item as one choice of the product box, which the grid takes as a line (qty 1, the price typed), the cursor in its Qty; every other line
stays. A separate route, not the editor's own post, so making an item can never save half a document. Without the script the panel posts
the editor's form as before.

**KG22. Every box of every line edited in place, the item too** (the owner: "each row within same place edit option"). A saved line's item
name is a box (one more use of `combo()`, with its own list); its page is the CW code's link. Choosing another item for a saved line sends
that line as removed and a new line with `line: N`, which the server puts in N's place (`DocGrid::order`): a line's item is part of what the
line is (its supplier's pack, its VAT, its links to deliveries and orders), so changing it is honestly "line N removed, a new line N".
The order's items per pack stays editable on a line without the supplier's pack. Only an editable draft's lines.

**KG23. Many lines quickly.** "+ Add row" goes to the empty line; "Add several" is a search with ticks ("Add 3 lines": each a line, 1 pack,
the supplier's price); scanning keeps adding (the cursor stays in the box; the same item scanned again is one pack more on its line, as Add
does on the server). Ticking lines shows "Delete N lines" (one Undo for the lot).

**KG24. Save without leaving the page** (the owner: "save all in ajax"). With the script, Save / Save as draft / Ctrl+S send the form by
the one fetch, a POST to its own address with its CSRF token, FormOnce key and version (`fragment()`'s second kind: `SENT` names the only
two things ever sent, this and KG21, each by a whole-address pattern). The answer counts only when it is THIS page's editor
(`form[data-kg-editor]`: the same kind and document; a new document's first save may name its draft); then its parts are put in place (the
messages around the form, the hidden fields, the lines, the totals, the notes; the head's fields only when the page has no supplier box, so
an open dropdown is never redrawn), the grid starts again on them with the cursor on the same line and box, "Saved" is said, and a new
document's address becomes its draft's (`history.replaceState`). A refusal (409, 422) is put in place the same way, every line kept with
its words on its row. Anything else (no network, the sign-in page, another page, a 500) changes nothing, says so, and the next Save is a
plain post. Confirm and make final stay plain posts (KG15).

them and says so on the rows (`DocGrid::rowOf`).
