**KG32. The fix round: the Codex review of `04421ad` (11 findings) and the coordinator's look at it on staging (S1-S6).**
- *The posting time is part of the editor's form; the server decides* (Codex 1 and 2, HIGH: stock could reach the websites before the
  chosen time; S3; Codex 9). The posting box (`submit_at`, and the clock choice) is a field of the invoice editor's own form, on a new
  invoice and on a draft. "Save and make final" with a time typed saves the draft and sets the time in ONE request, under one FormOnce key
  (`ui.invoice.timed`, or the new page's `ui.invoice.create`), by the timed route's own rules (`InvoicesController::postingMoment`, then
  `SupplierInvoices::schedule` in the same transaction): a time gone, or one that does not happen, is refused under the field with the time
  kept and NOTHING saved or made final; the hour the clocks go back is asked. Only an empty box makes it final now, and "Make final now"
  in a timed draft's "..." (`post_now`) leaves the time aside on purpose. The script no longer catches the main button (nothing to lose when a
  save without reload draws the head again): it only says "Schedule" while a time is typed and the line when the stock goes to the
  websites, the button found afresh after each in-place save. The timed route `/schedule` and "Take the time off" are kept (pack J); its
  separate "Set the time" button went (the main button does it, with the save). Tests changed: `ArrivalScreensTest` (the time typed is kept
  in the editor's form now), `DocKeyGridScreensTest::testThePostingTimeIsTheTimedRoute`.
- *A changed saved line refused comes back in its place* (Codex 3, 4): drawn as its new item right after the hidden saved line
  (`data-kg-replace`, sent again as `line: N`); every new line drawn again carries its name, code, pack and supplier code, so the checks
  before a save pass.
- *A save on its way holds the page* (Codex 5): the boxes are read-only and no line is added, removed, changed or put back until the answer
  is in place; nothing typed meanwhile is lost under it.
- *Changed in another tab* (Codex 6): the editor drawn for a version conflict says so (`data-kg-conflict`); the script then posts the same
  form plainly, so the whole page (the head and its supplier too) is drawn as the server has it, the new lines kept, nothing saved.
- *The page's hidden fields are the server's* (Codex 7): those the answer no longer draws are removed.
- *Prices as people type them* (Codex 8): moving lines to another supplier reads a price as the save reads it (`£`, spaces, commas).
- *A removed saved line sends its remove field alone* (Codex 10): its boxes are switched off (on again with Undo; also the lines drawn removed
  after a refusal), so removing many lines of a long document stays inside PHP's max_input_vars; the order's check that the form was not
  cut short counts a line sent with its remove field alone.
- *A line's item box and the keys* (Codex 11): Enter with no choice marked goes on to Qty, Tab takes its marked choice, Alt+C is "+ Add new
  item" with its words, for who may add one.
- *Staging*: S1 a label in the supplier's and "From"'s own column keeps its height (the boxes sat ~190 px under their words); S2 the keys'
  panel lists a key a row (not the site's two-column `dl`); S3 the posting fields on a new invoice (above); S4 the same-item warning said
  again after Undo; S5 a line one row high on a computer (the CW code small beside the item box); S6 while the supplier question is open,
  the box names the supplier asked about (Keep puts the chosen one back).
Tests: `DocKeyGridScreensTest` (the posting time in one request, past and future, a new invoice; a refused replacement in its place; a
removal without its boxes; the conflict mark; prices with £), the node harness (the Schedule label after an in-place save, the form's own
post, the hold, the conflict's plain post, the hidden fields, a removal's boxes off and on, Enter / Alt+C in a line's item box, the warning
after Undo, the supplier's name while asked).

**KG33. The posting time's edge cases (the Codex re-check of `48dc75b`: 10 of 11 fixed, 5 new, all about the posting time).**
- *Its date and its time are two fields* (finding 1, HIGH: a date cleared with the time left, or a date the browser does not take, was
  sent as no time = "make final now"). `submit_date` and `submit_time` (UK) are fields of the editor's form, drawn by the server (no
  script needed); `InvoicesController::postingTyped` reads them: BOTH empty is the only "make final now"; one without the other is refused
  (422 `partial_submit_at`, "Type both the posting date and the time, or clear both to make it final now."), a date or time that is not one
  too (`bad_submit_at`), under the fields, nothing saved or made final. An older form's one `submit_at` is still read when neither is sent;
  the timed route `/schedule` is unchanged (pack J).
- *Kept through a version conflict* (finding 2, HIGH): the conflict's page keeps the date, the time and the clock chosen with the new
  lines, so a retry (and the plain post after a conflict met by a save without reload) is never "make final now" for want of the time; the
  clock choice drawn again, ticked, while the time still comes twice.
- *Kept through "+ Add new supplier"* (finding 3): `submit_date`, `submit_time`, `submit_clock` are CARRIED back to the new invoice.
- *The whole page waits for a save on its way* (finding 4): boxes read-only, and lists, files and ticks switched off (after the form's data
  was taken); fill down, a choice in any dropdown (the supplier's too: `kb.busy`), "+ New item", "Add multiple", removals and Undo do
  nothing until the answer is in place.
- *A time gone is refused before anything is applied* (finding 5: a file sent with it was stored, then the refusal rolled the rows back and
  left its bytes): the editor checks the time is still to come before the save, its file or its lines; the service checks it again when
  it sets it.
Tests: `DocKeyGridScreensTest::testThePostingTimeIsTheTimedRoute` (half a time, a date that is not one, the time before a line's refusal,
a conflict keeping the time, "+ Add new supplier" carrying it), `ArrivalScreensTest` (the time kept is the two fields), the node harness
(the label for half a time, Ctrl+D, the supplier and the lists during a save).

## Goods received as a standard grid (branch `gi-key-grid`, 7 Nov 2026; GW1-GW10; tracker CW-920 part 1)

The owner, 6 Nov 2026: "check all purchase order, purchase invoice, sales order like this all form"; on 7 Nov, one form at a time, Goods
received first (the form staff use most). A delivery's draft page (Purchasing › Goods in › a delivery, `/ui/receiving/{id}`) works like the
purchase order's and the supplier invoice's since CW-919 (KG1-KG37): a numbered lines table worked from the keyboard, no page reload per
line, the same keys, Save without leaving the page, so staff learn it once. Built from main `9b85a22` in `/root/cw-gw`. No migration, no
permission, no setting. One route added (the scan box's choices, read only, GW3). Three of `GoodsReceipts`' Add rules are shared now
(`resolveScan()`, `newLine()`, `merge()`; `addLine()`, `addChoice()`, `addResolved()` use them, unchanged). Only Goods received: the
stock records, hand-overs, purchase returns, adjustments and sales are later parts of CW-920.

**GW1. The standard look (KG1, KG10).** The draft's lines are KG's grid (`table.gi-lines.kg-grid[data-kg-grid]`, on the delivery's board): a
No. column (the line's number on the delivery; a line added in the page after the delivery's last line, where the save puts it; closed up
over a line removed), the item's name (out of the Tab order) with its CW code small beside it (`kg-code`) and the pack and their code on the
sub line (the sub line's "line N" went: the No. column says it, as KG10 did for the order), numbers right-aligned, the Got box a 32 px grid
box (`data-kg-cell`), 4 px corners (KG12's tokens). The prices fold's table has the same No. column and look. The read-only page
(`receipt.php`) has KG10's view look (`table.kg-view`, the No. column, the CW code beside the name). On a phone the GI_Phone cards as before
(GV23-GV25): no No. column (KG's rule for `table.stack.doc-lines`), nothing sideways, 48 px buttons. Layout only, CSS block "gw" (to "end
gw"): the table waits hidden until its first line on a keyer's empty delivery (`data-gi-none`), the problem panel's boxes stay white,
a line's problems and a refusal's words under the name.

**GW2. The keys, KG3's** (Mac: Cmd), through the site's one table of keys (`KEYS`, `kb.grid`): Tab / Shift+Tab the browser's own, box to box
along a line and on to the next (the item's link and a new line's x out of the Tab order); Enter in a box: the next box of its table (the
Got box, items a pack, the duty stamp, an open panel's boxes; the prices fold's boxes their own) and never the form sent; Enter in the last
box of the last line: the scan box. Up / Down in a box: the same box of the line above / below (a number box's own step not taken; a
select keeps its arrows: `KEYS`' updown now returns the grid's answer, false for a select; past the last line: the scan box). Ctrl+Enter,
Alt+N, Insert: the scan box (the delivery's "new line"). Ctrl+Delete, Cmd+Backspace, Alt+R: the line the cursor is on, its keyer's only and
any line of the page, as the server's rule (the keyer's Got 0 takes any line out; nobody else changes lines): "Line 3 removed." with Undo
(Alt+U, Ctrl+Z when not typing), one removal deep. Ctrl+D in a Got box: the figure of the line above (elsewhere the browser's). Ctrl+S: the
page's Save (the bar's button), never "Book in" or anything that moves stock (KG15). Esc shuts the scan box's list (combo) and an open problem
panel (its own listener; the cursor back on its link). Never taken: Alt+D, Ctrl+N/T/W, Ctrl+Shift+Delete, Delete or Backspace alone.
**The problem panel from the keyboard** (the brief's choice): its "Problem" / "Open" link stays in the Tab order; Enter on it opens the panel
with the cursor in its first box (no new key). The hint line under the table (`doc_grid_keys` with the page's keys, `kgKeys`): the keyer's
Tab next, ↑↓ line, Ctrl+Enter new line, Alt+R delete, Alt+U undo, Ctrl+S save; someone else's Tab, Ctrl+Enter scan box (`DOC_GRID k_scan`),
Ctrl+S save; then "All keys (?)". Hidden under 700 px and without the script (KG's rules). The keys' panel shows only the delivery's keys
(`kb.grid.keys`; the layout's rows carry `data-kb-key`; the order's and the invoice's grids name none: as before). `aria-keyshortcuts` on the
Got boxes, the scan box and Save (`doc_bar`'s optional `keys`).

**GW3. The scan box.** The keyer's is the site's one dropdown (`combo()`, its seventh use; no second engine). Its choices come from the
delivery's own route, `GET /ui/receiving/{id}/products?q=` (`ReceivingController::choices`, `doc.GRN.post`, read only, a draft only; the
fragment `gi_products`, marker `data-gi-fragment`): what the delivery's Add would add, by Add's own resolution (`GoodsReceipts::resolveScan`,
taken out of `addLine()`: a barcode's units, a case, the one-unit question, this supplier's code, a CW code, a search). Each choice carries
the packs one scan is (`data-packs`), the delivery's line it adds to when it is one already (`data-line`, Add's same-line rule) and a
case's words; no price (goods in never sees one, GV6; the save sets it, as Add does). A code of a line of THIS page still finds that line
(highlighted, its "All fine" focused, nothing added: today's behaviour). Enter in an empty scan box does nothing (the form is never sent from
the lines). Someone who did not key it: their scan box as before (finds a line, or says it is not on this delivery).

**GW4. A line added in place, the keyer's, by Add's rules.** A scan with Enter (asked at once, so a scanner's Enter does not wait for the
300 ms) or a choice naming one item: not on the delivery: a new line (its name, CW code, pack and their code; packs = the packs a scan is
times the Packs box; the Price box's price when typed), the cursor in its Got box; the same item on a new line of this page: more packs
there; a line of the delivery on this page (`data-line`): more packs in its Got box, as Add adds units to that line, never a second line; a

strict: anything else is 400 `bad_form`, nothing read), appended after the page's edits and removals and saved by the same `saveDraft` (the
same transaction, version check, stamps (GV4, GV16) and FormOnce: GW5), before the check, the files, the Add and "Book in". Each by today's Add
rules (`ReceivingController::withNewLines`): `GoodsReceipts::newLine` (this supplier's pack, switched on, else 422 `unknown_supplier_item`; an
item not joined into another, else 422 `unknown_sku`; an item with `u` a case of u), `GoodsReceipts::merge` (the same purchase already a line
gets the packs, and the typed price, as Add does; else at the end, at the save's own price: Add's: the order line's, else the supplier's last,
else 0); packs a whole number (0 leaves it out, else 422 `grid_packs`), the price as the save reads prices (exact, 4 decimals); `entry`
`scan`. Sent by anyone but the keyer: the service refuses the save (403 `not_creator`, nothing saved).

**GW5. FormOnce on a save that adds lines (KG5).** A delivery's form now draws a `form_key` for its keyer. A save that carries new lines runs
through FormOnce (`ui.grn.grid`): the look for someone else's save meanwhile (`stale()`), the save, the check, the files and an Add all inside
it; the same form sent again (a double click, the back button, a retry after a lost answer) is answered by its first answer and adds nothing
twice. "Book in" comes after it, outside it, with the version the save left (stored with the answer), as GV3; the same "Book in" sent twice
lands on the delivery the first one booked in. An Add with new lines that finds several items or none leaves nothing saved (the choices, or
"Nothing matches … Nothing was saved: your lines and changes are still here.", with every line kept). A refused save stored nothing, so its
page draws the same key again; the page after a save has a new one. Without new lines a save is as before (no key needed).

**GW6. A refused save keeps every typed line (KG6).** The new lines are drawn again (`gi_grid_line`, from `DocGrid::rows`) with their field;
the line a refusal is about is red with its words under the name (`tr.kg-bad`): `DocGrid::rowOf` (a new line's own row, else the save's line
number mapped back through the rows; the panel a refusal opens is now the right line's after a removal on the page); the edits as typed (as
before). A version conflict keeps the new lines (they name their item); the edits of the saved lines as before (kept while the delivery has
the same number of lines, I175).

**GW7. Save without leaving the page (KG24).** `fragment()`'s SENT list gets the delivery's one form by a whole-address pattern
(`/ui/receiving/<id>/lines`). With the script, Save, Ctrl+S and the form's first button with an empty scan box (Enter in a field of the page)
send the form by the one fetch, multipart as the browser sends it (a chosen photo or paper goes with it: the brief's choice; GV19's size and

this delivery's form (`form[data-kg-editor="grn:<id>"]`); then it is put in place (`giSwap`): what comes before the form as the server drew
it (the messages, a refusal's list) but the head, of which only the title, its status and the line under it are taken (its More keeps its

is a plain post. "Book in", "All fine" (GV15: in the page), Add with words in the scan box, "Save and show the next lines", the choices'
Add, copy, import, cancel and reverse stay plain posts, as before.

**GW8. A scanner's code typed into a Got box is the next scan.** The cursor goes to a new line's Got box (the brief), so a scanner's next
code may land there; Enter in a Got box holding 8 or more digits, more than a line can have, gives the box back what it held when the cursor
came in and takes the code as the next scan. Many items in a row by scanning work without the mouse (scan, Enter to the next box or type the

**GW9. Big deliveries.** The paging (`from`, `page_count`, `editorFits`, `editorMaxLines`), the field budget (GV7) and the size guard

**GW10. Without the script, as before; every rule kept.** The new lines' rows only come from the script (or a refusal's page); the field is
empty; Add submits, Save posts, the panels open by their links, Enter in the scan box adds (the form's first button). Kept: who may key,

## The adjustment grid on the site's keys (branch `adjust-key-grid`, 9 Nov 2026; AJ1-AJ8; tracker CW-920 part 2, step 1)

The owner, 6 Nov 2026: "check all purchase order, purchase invoice, sales order like this all form": every form worked from the keyboard with the
same keys and a save that does not leave the page, one form at a time. Goods received went first (GW, live 9 Nov). A read-only look at ERPNext
(last 90 days) showed what staff use of Stock records: 430 stock counts (Stock Reconciliation, 7,213 lines, the biggest 162) against one stock
out and no stock in or transfer. So the quick adjustment screen (AG1-AG8: type the counted number in After, as in ERPNext) comes first. The owner
said "Yes start step 1" (plan: `/root/cw_work/stock_records_plan_20261109/`).

**AJ1. The keys, through the site's one table** (`KEYS`, `kb.grid`; KG3, a Mac's Cmd). This grid is `kb.grid`, naming its keys (GW2), so "All
keys (?)" shows only those. Its cells keep their own Tab / Enter / arrows (AG5): they are not `data-kg-cell`, so the table's `next` and `updown`
pass them by. Ctrl+Enter, Insert, Alt+N: the empty line's Product box (the product box's Enter, and Units' and After's Tab / Enter, now leave a
Ctrl / Cmd / Alt + Enter to the keys; the form's guard that stops Enter sending the page lets Ctrl+Enter in the lines through to them). Ctrl+S:
the page's Save, never "Make it final" (KG15; no key makes it final). Esc shuts the product list (combo, as before). Never taken: Alt+D,
Ctrl+N/T/W, Ctrl+Shift+Delete, Delete or Backspace alone.

**AJ2. A line out, and Undo.** The x, Ctrl+Delete, Cmd+Backspace and Alt+R take the line the cursor is on out at once; the numbers close up, the
sums follow, the cursor goes to the same box of the line that takes its place; "Line 3 removed." with Undo (the button, Alt+U, Ctrl+Z when not
typing) puts it back where it was with everything it held. One removal deep: the next removal or any send ends it, and the line given up takes
its product list with it (combo puts a list under body). The empty line at the end cannot be removed (the key stays the box's own). Nothing is
removed or put back while a save is on its way.

**AJ3. Ctrl+D and the look.** Ctrl+D copies the box above into this one: Units, Why, or After (After then sets Units from this line's own stock
on show, as typing it does). In Product it is the browser's own (no line is made from the line above: a count names each product); on the first
line it does nothing. The look of the other grids (KG1): 32 px boxes, rows one line high (cells 4 px 8 px), the No. column right-aligned; a
phone keeps AG's cards and 44 px boxes. Under the lines: the Undo line and the hint line (`doc_grid_keys`, the order's keys: Tab, ↑↓, Ctrl+Enter,
Alt+R, Alt+U, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+S, "All keys (?)"), hidden under 700 px and without the script. `aria-keyshortcuts`: Control+S on Save, Control+D on
Units and After.

**AJ4. Save without leaving the page** (KG24, GW7). `fragment()`'s `SENT` gets this form by whole-address patterns: a new adjustment's
`/ui/stock/adjustments/new` and a draft's `/ui/stock/adjustments/<id>/grid`, under the editor's marker (`form[data-kg-editor]`: `adj:new`, or
`adj:<id>` for the creator's draft, which also carries its address `data-kg-address` and the page's notice `data-aj-notice`: the layout's
notice is a toast outside the part put in place). With the script, Save and Ctrl+S send the form by the one fetch, with its token, its FormOnce
key (new) or version (draft) and every line in `lines`; meanwhile the boxes are held (`kgHold`), a second Save or "Make it final" sends nothing,
and no line changes (a product answer arriving then is not taken). The answer counts only when it is this grid's editor (a new adjustment's: itself
again, a refusal, or its draft; a draft's: the same draft). "Make it final" stays a plain post, always. Anything else (no network, the sign-in
page, another page, a 500, a record no longer a draft) changes nothing, says so (DOC_GRID's words), and the next Save is a plain post. The server
is unchanged: the same routes, FormOnce, version check, `checkDrawn`, CSRF and refusals.

**AJ5. What the answer puts in place.** In the form: its address, marker and notice; its hidden fields as drawn (a draft's version, no FormOnce
key; a refused new form's new key); its lines from the answer's `data-rows` (a refusal: as typed), so each row names its saved line (`l`) for
the next save; whether it holds something to save; the cursor back on the same line and box. The details at the top stay as on the page (they are
what was sent). Around the form: a FIRST save (a new adjustment's answer is its draft) takes everything as the server drew it (the draft's head
with its More, its files after the form), each form wired as at the start (`sendOnce`, and `leaving()`: the guard that asks before another form
leaves the page, now a function for this), and the address bar says the draft's address (`history.replaceState`); a draft keeps its head (its
More's forms and their state, GW7) and takes the rest before the form (the crumbs, a refusal's words). Every other form of the record on the page
(its `/ui/stock/adjustments/<id>/…` forms: Stop this draft) takes the new version.

**AJ6. Changed meanwhile (another tab).** The server's refusal of a version conflict marks the form (`data-kg-conflict`). The page then keeps
everything as typed (so the person sees what they had), says the server's words, and the next Save is a plain post, which draws the record as
it is now (the brief's choice; the order's grid posts at once instead, KG24 finding 6). Any other refusal (a reason the other way, units that
are not a number, the limit) is put in place with every typed line, its words said, still something to save.

**AJ7. Big counts.** `StockOps::MAX_LINES` (500) is unchanged: 200 and 500 lines save in one send (one field, AG3), 501 is refused with every line
kept (as before). Drawing many lines at once (the page, a save's answer) numbers them, sums them and checks the note once at the end, and the
sums find their places once; a change of warehouse sums once. In the node harness (dom.js, slower than a browser) 500 lines drew in 8.2 s before
and 0.38 s after; a save of 500 lines put back in 0.55 s.

**AJ8. Not in this step.** The reason the page opens on stays Data correction (`GRID_REASON`, a constant; it needs a note). Making it a setting
needs a new `app_setting` row, a migration, so the brief left it out: plan step 2 is the owner's choice ("Count difference" offered on
Adjustments, and opening on it). Rules unchanged (AG8): who may post, below zero, reasons and their direction, notes, drafts, approvals; no
migration, no new permission, no route. Stock in, Stock out, Transfers and Releases keep the old page (plan step 3).
Tests: `AdjustGridScreensTest` (4 new: the editor, words and hints on the new page and the draft; each save answered with the draft's editor and
its new version; the conflict mark; 200 and 500 lines), `UiUnitTest` (SENT), the node harness `/root/cw_work/runs/ajk_js_harness/run_aj.js`
(11 sections; `run_kg.js` and `run_gw.js` stay green).

## The reason a new adjustment opens on is a setting (branch `adjust-open-reason`, 10 Nov 2026; AJ9-AJ13; migration 0065; tracker CW-920 part 2, step 2)

The owner, 10 Nov 2026: "Yes, step 2" (plan: `/root/cw_work/stock_records_plan_20261109/PLAN.md`: the reason "Count difference" offered on
Adjustments and the page opening on it, so an everyday count needs no note). Offering a reason on Adjustments is a setting already (Settings >
Reasons). What the page opens on was a constant (`GRID_REASON`, AJ8), and the owner's rule of 7 Oct is that everything is settable in CW. This
step makes it a setting and changes nothing by itself: as set up, the page opens on Data correction, as before. Which reason it opens on, on
live, is the owner's own choice, on his word, through CW's own screens: Settings > Reasons ("Count difference": offered on stock corrections
too), then Settings > Rules and numbers > Stock records (choose it). No reason and no setting is changed by this release.

**AJ9. The setting.** `stock.adjust_opens_on` (a string; migration `0065_adjust_opens_on.sql` adds its row, "data_correction", not agreed yet,
with its version-1 baseline: two rows, no table changed, no row changed, no reason touched). `StockOpsController::gridTop` reads it. This takes
the place of AJ8's "stays a constant": `GRID_REASON` stays as the fall-back (AJ11), and is what the page uses where the row is not there yet
(the code a moment before the migration).

**AJ10. Only a reason that can be chosen there, and a choice on the screens.** A new rule in `Settings::RULES`: `reason_use` => a use
(`reason_code.applies_to`). The value is the code of a reason that is in use, is offered on that use and is not one CW sets itself
(`Settings::reasonChoices`: the same question and order as the adjustment page's own list), or empty. `checkRule` refuses anything else
(`bad_value`), for the screens, the CLI and the API alike. On the screens it is a choice, never a box to type a code in: on the setting's page
and in its row of the Settings list (a new topic, "Stock records", after Stock counts) a select of "None: choose each time" and the reasons
offered, by name, in the Reasons order (`SettingsController::choices`); the hint says "One of the reasons offered on stock corrections."

**AJ11. What the page opens on.** In order: what was typed (a refused form keeps it), a draft's first line's own reason (AG2, unchanged), then
the reason the setting names, while the page offers it. "None" (empty): no reason is chosen and the person chooses each time. A reason the
setting names that is not offered now (switched off on the Reasons page, or no longer offered on stock corrections) is not used: the page opens
on Data correction again while that is offered, on nothing when it is not. Switching such a reason off is not refused and does not change the
setting (one place for one thing: the Reasons page says what is offered, the setting says which one comes first; the setting's help says what
happens). Switched on or offered again, the setting works again with nothing to set twice.

**AJ12. Shown by name.** The setting's value now, its row in the list and its History show the reason's name as it is now ("Value now: Data
correction → Count difference"), not its code (`ConfigWords::history` passes the names on, an optional last parameter, so every other caller
is as before). A value held that is not offered now is shown, and stays a choice of the select, as "Count difference (not offered now)", so
the page never drops what is stored silently; the same for what a refused form sent (a code that is no reason: the code itself). Saving the
page with such a value left chosen is refused like any other value that is not offered (`bad_value`: the rule is checked before "nothing
changed"); choose a reason that is offered, or None. The CLI (`bin/settings.php`) prints codes, as it takes them.

**AJ13. The red line under the lines (two small things, with this step).** (1) Codex re-check 11, LOW: a look-up of another warehouse's
figures that fails while a save is on its way wrote "The products could not be loaded." after the send's own clearing, and the words stayed
on show after the good save. Now the save's answer put in place (`swapIn`) clears the red line: the page is the server's again, and its words
(a refusal, the notice) are the answer's. An answer that is not put in place (changed meanwhile, no network) leaves the look-up's words with
the box they are about. (2) The staging look of 10 Nov: "Choose a product on line 3." stayed on show after line 3 was removed, until the next
save. Now the words belong to their line (`chooseFor`): removed with it; Undo of the line brings it back without them (the next save says them
again); a line above removed or put back, they say the line's number as it is now (`renumber`). Any other words said meanwhile ("Looking…",
"Write a note.") end that and are left alone.

Rules unchanged: who may post, below zero, reasons and their direction, notes (Data correction needs one; Count difference does not), drafts,
approvals; no new permission, no route, no change to the Reasons page.
Tests, written first: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/AdjustOpensOnTest.php` (7: as set up; offered and chosen, an everyday count posts with no
note; switched off / no longer offered; None; typed and a draft's own reason win; the setting's page; the Settings list) and
`tests/Integration/StockOps/Migration0065Test.php` (2: the row, its baseline, words and rule; the rule's refusals), red on 241739c
(`runs/aor_red.php.log`: 9 tests, 6 errors, 3 failures); the node harness `/root/cw_work/runs/aor_js_harness/run_aj.js` sections 29 and 30
(red on 241739c: `runs/aor_red.js.log`, 7 checks; `run_kg.js` and `run_gw.js` stay green).

### The Codex review of ca9de9e (`runs/aor_codex_review.txt`): no HIGH; 1 MEDIUM and 1 LOW old, 1 LOW new, fixed; 1 MEDIUM old left

- **A key in other letters (MEDIUM, old).** `Settings::change` looked the row up with `WHERE setting_key = ?`, and MySQL finds it whatever
  the case of the letters (its collation; an accent or a space at the end the same), while the rules (`RULES`), the secrets and the "changed
  on its own page" guards (`company.`, the approval switches) go by the exact key. So `STOCK.adjust_opens_on` = `no_such_reason`, from the
  CLI or a form changed by hand, was saved with no rule checked, and an approval switch could be changed the same way past its own page.
  Now only the key as it is stored, letter for letter, is a setting: anything else is `unknown_setting` (400), as a key that is not there;
  the setting's page already answered 404 to such a key (it goes by the exact key) and still does, now with nothing saved before it.
- **A refused form that sent "Choose…" (LOW, old).** `gridTop` took an empty `why` as "nothing typed" and chose again: before this branch
  Data correction, with it the setting's reason. A form that is refused is drawn again as it was sent: "Choose…" stays "Choose…" (a new
  record and a draft's own page). Only a page with nothing typed and no line yet (null) takes the setting.
- **Two reasons of one name in the History (LOW, new).** Reasons lets two reasons share a name (and a reason is renamed), and AJ12 shows a
  setting's change by the names as they are now: a change from one to the other read "Data correction → Data correction", which
  `ConfigWords::changes` took for no change and left "What changed" empty. Now, when the two sides of a reason-naming setting's value read
  the same, each has its short code added: "Value now: Data correction (data_correction) → Data correction (count_difference)"
  (`Words::SETTING_EDIT['reason_coded']`). The short code is what the Reasons page shows at the right of each reason, so it can be looked
  up there. Two names that differ stay without codes; the same value twice (only "agreed" changed) is still not listed.
- **Not fixed here (MEDIUM, old; on the tracker, P3).** A draft whose line was saved with a reason that is switched off (or no longer offered
  on stock corrections) afterwards: its page has no such choice, the line's own reason becomes empty in the browser, and the next Save
  writes the top reason over it with nothing said. Old (the same on 241739c and before), needs a reason switched off while a draft holds it;
  the fix (the saved reason kept as a marked choice, "(not offered now)", until the person chooses another) changes the page's lines and
  the script, so it is its own piece of work.

Tests, written first: `AdjustOpensOnTest` +3 (`testARefusedFormKeepsNoReasonChosenWhenThatIsWhatItSent`,
`testAKeyWrittenInOtherLettersIsNoSetting`, `testTwoReasonsOfOneNameAreToldApartInTheHistoryByTheirCodes`), red on ca9de9e
(`runs/aor_fix1_red.php.log`: 10 tests, 3 failures), green with the fixes (`runs/aor_fix1_green.php.log`: 12 tests with `Migration0065Test`,
225 assertions).

## Doubtful stock: the items to check on the shelf, one at a time (branch `stock-doubt`, 12 Nov 2026; DS1-DS9; migration 0066)

The owner, 12 Nov 2026 ~05:45 UK (CW chat): "create a module in central warehouse for doubt and clear ... only there need doubted product only".
Today CW listens to the Vape and Go shop; from 13 Nov ~06:00 UK it writes the shop's stock. Some items have a doubtful figure (CW and the shop
differ, or CW holds them below zero: 239 on 12 Nov, `/root/cw_work/switch_20261113/doubt_list_12nov.csv`). Staff check each on the shelf and
clear it on a page that shows ONLY those items. Not in this build: finding doubtful items by itself, any shop or ERPNext change, the two draft
count sheets opened on production for the same items (2630, 2631: left as they are).

**DS1. One table, one open row per store and item.** `stock_doubt` (0066): the store, the item, why (`differs`, `below_zero`, `other`), the
shop's and CW's figures and the units sold in 30 days as the list gave them, the list's name (`batch`) and note (and every list that put or refreshed it: `batches`, since the Codex review); `status` open, then cleared
(by a count: `counted_qty`, `booked_delta`, `count_document_id`) or dismissed ("Not needed": `resolved_note`), with who and when. At most ONE
open row per store and item: the database says so (UNIQUE (`channel_id`, `open_sku_id`), `open_sku_id` the item while the row is open: the
pattern of 0004's open proposal per listing), and the only writer of open rows (the loader) reads each open row FOR UPDATE inside one
transaction, under its job's lock (`Cli::tryLock`, one run per schema). CHECKs: answered rows name who and when, open ones neither; a cleared
row has its count and record, any other row none of them. Rows are never removed (`Grants::NO_DELETE`, like the stores' queues). The answer's
note is a column of its own (`resolved_note`), so "Not needed" never overwrites the list's note (the brief names one `note`: two are kept).

**DS2. The load (`bin/doubt_load.php`, `StockDoubt::readFile`, `plan`, `load`).** A CSV with the columns `cw_code, shop_qty, cw_qty, reason,
sold_30d, note` (others ignored; CW's `CsvReader`: comma, semicolon or tab, a BOM, Excel's Windows-1252; at most 2,000 rows). Every row is
checked before anything is written: a CW number, whole numbers (shop_qty and sold_30d may be empty; sold_30d not below 0), a reason of the
three, a note of at most 500 characters; an item twice, an item CW does not have, or one merged into another refuses the WHOLE list (exit 1,
the row named, nothing written). Dry run by default (one line per row: add, refresh, same or skip, then the counts); `--apply` writes all of it
in ONE transaction with one audit row `stock_doubt.load` (the list's name, the file's name and sha256, the counts). An item already open is
refreshed in place (figures, why, list name, note), never doubled. An item answered in the SAME list is not opened again (`skip`), so a list run
twice is safe; a list of another name opens it again. The command line is read whole (`Cli::main` strict: a misspelt option, a value on
`--apply`: exit 2 before anything is read). It runs as the app login (no `--admin`): its rights on the table come from the grants.

**DS3. "Save count" books ONE count of that ONE item through the counts engine.** `StockDoubt::count`: under the key `doubt:<id>`
(`Idempotency::run`, one transaction): the person may count (`CountSheets::mayCount`: doc.CNT.post, never admin; before and again inside), the
row locked and open, the store's selling warehouse (`channel_warehouse.is_sellable`; none: 409 `no_selling_warehouse`), then CountSheets as a
person would: `open` a one-line sheet at that warehouse with the note "Doubtful stock #<id>", `setQuantities` line 1, `post` it (the count
record CNT, its ledger row, the tolerance check and the record's review as the rules say, like any shelf count), then the row is cleared with
what was counted, what the count line booked (`count_sheet_line.booked_delta`) and the record. A count posts at once (`approvalUnits` is 0); a
record that came back not posted would be a bug, and refuses the whole answer. A second press of the same number (a double click, a resend,
another person typing the same) replays the first answer: nothing more is booked. Any other answer for a row no longer open is refused: a
different number finds the key kept with another request (`idempotency_key_reused`), which is said as 409 `doubt_settled` (the key is only
ever kept by a count that cleared the row); "Not needed" on a cleared row and a count on a dismissed one find the row not open (409). Any
refusal keeps nothing: the row stays open and the same key may try again. "Not needed" pressed twice (the same person, the same note: a
double click, a resend) is its first answer and changes nothing more, so the person never reads "someone already checked it" about their own
answer; another person or another note on a dismissed row is refused (409).

**DS4. The moment it was counted is the moment it is saved.** The page has no script (the brief: plain forms), so it cannot send the moment the
box was filled in as a count sheet's page does (CountsController `at_<line>`, review M-7). A sale dispatched between the look at the shelf and
the press is therefore not taken off the count: the same as a count sheet's Enter without the script. Staff type the number and save it at
the shelf (the page works on a phone).

**DS5. What may be typed in "On the shelf".** A whole number of units from 0 to `CountSheets::MAX_QTY`, else 422 `bad_quantity`, said under
the box with what was typed kept in it (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`), nothing booked. Nine digits or more, or 4 to 8 digits that are a
barcode CW knows, is refused as a barcode (422 `barcode_in_quantity`: the count sheet's own guard, review M-5, `CountsController::barcodeIn`,
now public), checked before the range so a scanned EAN-8 is named as a barcode. A count that happens to equal a known 4-8 digit barcode is
refused the same way as on a count sheet (enter it on a count sheet or an adjustment then).

**DS6. "CW now" is on hand at the store's selling warehouse.** The figure a shelf count sets (stock_balance.on_hand of the warehouse the store
sells from), 0 where it has no balance yet. The list's own figures stay as "Shop figure" (when the list was made). The line after a count
says "Counted 42 of CW-000123. CW had 40: booked +2." from the count line's own figures (what CW held just before, what it booked); no
difference: "CW had the same: nothing changed."

**DS7. The page: Inventory › Doubtful stock.** A sidebar entry after Stock counts with two Show choices, To check and Checked (`keep`: the
store). Everyone who reads records looks (documents.view, as Stock counts); the people who count answer (doc.CNT.post, the POST routes); a
person who may not count sees the list and no forms. To check: the store asked for, else the one that has open rows, else one with any; a
choice of store only when two or more have rows. The order (`StockDoubt::order`, pure): CW and the shop differ first, biggest difference first
(a shop figure not known after every known one); then CW below zero, most sold in 30 days first; then the rest; oldest first within. 50 a page
with plain Previous / Next links; the store's open rows are read whole and ordered in PHP (a list holds at most 2,000 rows). A search (CW
number or name, its own % and _ as letters) and the filter by why, in the toolbar and its Show. Per row ONE plain form: "On the shelf" and
"Save count" (a plain button: a main button on every row is not the pattern), and under More "Not needed" with its note (QueueRules::note: 3 to
500 characters). Each form carries the list's store, why, search and page back, so the answer comes back to the list as it was. A phone
gets one card per item (CW's `.stack`); the answer cell spans the card. Checked: newest answer first, who, when, what was on the shelf, what
it changed and its count record, or why it was not needed.

**DS8. Who sees how many.** The badge `stock_doubt` (every store's open rows) for the people who count (Documents::mayPost CNT, as
`counts_open`), on the entry and the Inventory section; Home's "Waiting for you" has the line "Doubtful stock" with "N to check" for the same
people (`HomeTasks` fact `doubt`, rank 69: a wrong figure goes to the shop and its customers; the badge's count, so the two agree), none when
nothing is open. The owner (Matching lead, Reviewer) does not count, so he has no line; his sidebar shows the entry without a count.

**DS9. Undo.** The release before this one; the table can stay (the code before it never names it). Rows already cleared stay cleared: each
count is an ordinary count record (Stock > Counts > Count sheets), cancelled there as a whole if it must be put back.

## An item's own name, changed on its page (branch `item-rename`, 12 Nov 2026; IR1-IR6; no migration)

The owner, 12 Nov 2026 ~16:35 UK (CW chat): "i meant product name. i will change the product name in cw for cw i will keep the names clean with
one structure for each category so easy to understand. just letting you know you dont have to do anything other than giving me an option to
change the name". So: a way to change `sku.name` on the item page; the owner renames. Not in this build: renaming many at once (CSV), any
website product name (CW never writes names to the shops), naming rules per category.

**IR1. The Name part of Details.** For the people who may change product cards (`catalogue.edit`: mapping_lead, stock_controller,
purchasing_manager; never admin) and on an item not joined into another: the first group of Details, "NAME", the name now and "Change the
name", a fold (no script) holding a plain form: one text box (no browser limit: a browser counts an emoji as two characters, CW as
one; the hint says "at most 255 characters" and the server keeps it), a hint that only CW's name changes, "Save the name". `POST /ui/items/{id}/name` (`ItemNameController::save`, route permission `catalogue.edit`) under the
form's key (FormOnce: the same form twice renames once; one key for two different names: 422 in words, a new key). A refusal draws the page
again: the words on top, the fold open, what was typed kept, the same key. Everyone else reads the name in the page's head as before.

**IR2. What a name may be (`ItemNames::clean`).** Trimmed, every run of spaces made one (a no-break space and a Unicode line separator are
spaces); at least one character, at most 255 (`NAME_MAX` = the column's `VARCHAR(255)`, characters not bytes; a test reads the column);
plain text on one line: not UTF-8, a control character (a tab or line break inside it, C0, DEL, C1) or a hidden formatting character
(Unicode Cf: a zero-width space, a right-to-left override, a soft hyphen, a byte-order mark) refuses it (422 `name_empty`,
`name_too_long` with the length, `name_not_plain`). Nothing else is ruled: names are not unique (the owner's own structure decides).

**IR3. One transaction (`ItemNames::rename`).** The person checked again inside it (`ItemCards::editor`: staff, active, not admin,
catalogue.edit; 403 otherwise), and again after the waits below (a job taken away while the rename waited counts); the same name (read
without a lock) writes nothing; else the NEW name's guard row first (see below), then the item row `FOR UPDATE` (404 unknown); an item
joined into another refused (409 `merged_item`, naming
the item to rename instead); the same name (after IR2) writes nothing (`unchanged`, notice "Nothing changed"), also when someone else gave
it that very name meanwhile; otherwise the name the page showed (`name_was`) must be the name it has now (409 `name_changed` with the name
it has now, which the page shows; only the spaces of a stored name are forgiven, and a NUL the page's hidden field carries as U+FFFD; a
case change by someone else is a change): `sku` has no version column, and the item page has no version of the item, so the name itself
is the expected value. Then `UPDATE sku SET name` and ONE audit row `sku.rename` {code, before, after} (CW's writer, `Audit::write`).
The guard: `item_name_guard`, keyed by the new name as the collation compares it, as "Add item" and a store's choice take it before they
make an item of a name, so such a making at this moment waits for the rename and then sees it. Lock order: the guard, then the item, as
those makers (HandMade may lock an existing item after its guard: `ItemBarcodes::add`'s join), so no cycle; a card change holds the item
FOR SHARE and waits, or is waited for. A name that is not UTF-8 is refused (422 `name_not_plain`) before the form's key is stored. No stock feed row: nothing a website reads changes (the feed
views carry code and policy, not the name).

**IR4. The history is read from the audit rows.** `item_card_change` cannot hold a rename cleanly: its versions are the card's
(`item_card.version`, 1..n per card) and the nightly IC1-IC3 compare its snapshot with `item_card`, which has no name. So the page's
"History of the card" fold merges the card's lines with the renames (`ItemNames::history`: `audit_log` by `ix_audit_entity`, entity
`sku`/id, action `sku.rename`), newest first, 20 lines: "<when> · <who>: name changed from "X" to "Y"". No new table, no migration.

**IR5. Find by a name it had.** Find (`/ui/search`) also finds an item by every word of a name it had before a rename
(`Queries::searchSkus(..., formerNames: true)` -> `ItemNames::formerMatches`: the renames' audit rows by `ix_audit_action`, the `before`
name compared as `sku.name` is, accents and case aside), after the items its name now finds and only while they leave room on the page;
one row an item (the newest matching name), items joined into another and ones already found left out before the limit, the room
counted on the items Find can show; two reads each capped at 2 s (`MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`, `ItemNames::FORMER_MS`): the items with their
newest matching rename, then those rows by id; past a cap, Find shows what the names now found. Such a row says "Was called:
<old name>". Its cost is a read of the rename rows (the action's index), the order of the name search's own read of `sku`.
Only Find: the pickers (orders, invoices, stock records, families, matching) and the lists' filters (stock, movements, reservations,
item cards, reorder, counts, duty register) find by the name now, as before.

**IR6. What reads the name, and what a rename changes there (the brief's point 4; checked in the code, 12 Nov 2026).**
- *Posted records keep no copy of the line names.* `document_line` has a free `description` only; `po_line`, `grn_line`, the invoice and
  return lines, `count_sheet_line`, the hand-over have no name column; the posting fingerprints (`document_posting.content`, `po_posting`,
  `grn_posting`, `purchase_doc_posting`) hold the item's id, never its name, so no fingerprint or invariant breaks. Every page, PDF and CSV
  of a record reads `sku.name` when drawn: a purchase order (page, PDF, lines file), a delivery, a supplier invoice and return, a count
  sheet (page, CSV), a stock record (page, PDF), a repack, the generic record page and PDF, and a hand-over's invoice PDF (its company and
  buyer are kept as they were; the lines are not). So printing an OLD posted record again after a rename shows the NEW name. Kept as they
  were: the one stored PDF (a purchase order's PDF "as sent", archived when marked sent), the "Missing on arrival" lines of a claim (their
  description holds "code name" as written then), a store's choice's record, `item.create`'s audit row. Not changed here: the owner
  decides later.
- *Matching.* The matching engine and the product-card suggestions never compare names with `sku.name` (they use the website products'
  features and the identity fields). The name IS read by: By Item's first search for an item with no flavour (its name's first words),
  the guards that stop "Create as new items" and a store's choice making a second item of a name CW already has (`StoreChoices::sameName`,
  exact and close; `BulkDecisions::namesTaken`, exact), "Add item"'s "the same item exists" (`HandMade::sameItems`, name + identity), and
  the fingerprint of a Key proposal (`ProposalBasis` covers `sku.name`). So after a rename: a website product named like the OLD name is no
  longer stopped as "an item of this name exists" (a second item could be made from it by a store's choice or the bulk "new items"), an
  open Key proposal for the item is no longer taken in bulk ("the item changed": a person decides it), and By Item's first search uses the
  new words. No change made.

## "Let the website decide", and each store's own selling mode on the item page (branch `t556-website-decides`, 16 Nov 2026; WD1-WD7; migrations 0067, 0068)

The owner, 16 Nov 2026 ~16:53 UK (CW chat), T-556 step 2: "Yes A". Option A: staff set a product's selling mode in each store again; CW stops
holding the modes it was given (the CW setting `site_writer.receipt_mode_sites` was emptied on live the same minute: a delivery no longer sets
Vape and Go's modes); CW SHOWS each store's own mode (view only). The shop admin keeps a mode only while CW holds one (connector 0.4.12, step 1),
so this build gives (a) the selling-mode switch a way to give a site's mode back to the website, and (b) CW a copy of what each store has.

**WD1. "Let the website decide" is a choice of the selling-mode switch (`SiteModes::WEBSITE` = `website`).** The same form, service, permission
(`modes.set`), reason (3-500 characters), per ticked site (or all), stamp (409 `selling_mode_changed`), legacy items only (409 `protected_item`
for a counted one), audit `selling_mode.set` (mode `website`), one log row per site (`item_channel_mode_log`, version + 1), and LAST one feed
row for the item (`Stock::skuChanged('mode')`), so every linked listing is re-sent at once. Its own notice: "Saved: the ticked websites now
decide this product's selling mode themselves. Staff can change it on each website."

**WD2. How it is kept (0067).** The site's `item_channel_mode` row STAYS (the app login never deletes it, NO_DELETE; W1 compares it with its
newest log row; a deleted row would start its versions again at 1 against the log's unique version key): its `mode` becomes NULL = the website
decides, no "mode before Out-Of-Stock", source `switch`; the log row's `mode_after` is NULL. Two new CHECKs say so in SQL (a NULL mode has no
previous mode and was written by the switch); 0018's CHECKs stay. The threshold is not part of the choice: kept, or the one typed (as for any
mode), so CW still writes a low-stock warning it holds. A site with no row and no threshold typed decides already: nothing is written for it
(`unchanged`). A mode chosen later makes CW hold it again (no "mode before" is known then: the website decided meanwhile).

**WD3. Who reads a NULL mode.** `SiteView::rule`: as no row (why `site_own`, mode null = "leave the site's own"; the threshold from the row as
before); a forced listing (blocked, quarantined, stopped) is still Out-Of-Stock, those are asked first. `SellingModes::current` (a receipt's
"last mode") skips such a row: it holds no mode of CW's. `RelayIntake` (the ERPNext mode relay's "same in CW") reads it as no row.
`RollbackExport`'s selling-mode file leaves out a row with neither a mode nor a threshold, and prints an empty mode otherwise. The connector
(0.4.12) then stops keeping the mode in the shop admin by itself (its held rule reads `site_mode` NULL; a force's restore is unchanged).

**WD4. The website's own mode (0068, `listing_selling`; `CW\Mapping\SiteSelling`).** One row per website product: the mode as the website says
it (VARCHAR 32: the shop's own labels), back-orders (0/1), low-stock warning (INT, the shop's column is signed), `as_of` (the push's time) and
`changed_at` (since when the three are what they are, as far as CW heard). No FK to `channel_listing` (the intake writes up to a thousand a call:
no shared lock on each listing row in that hot path; the ids are the intake's own; listings are never deleted). NO_DELETE for the app login.

**WD5. Who writes it.** Only the listing intake, in its transaction, after the profiles (listing order), from the optional object `selling`
(stock_mode, allow_backorders, low_stock_threshold) the shops' connector sends from 0.4.13. Read leniently (`SiteSelling::parse`): an object
that names `stock_mode` (null included: none set there) is stored whole; a value of the wrong type is ignored, counted and stored as none;
anything else is no state (the stored row stays). Attached after both hashes like `website` (M66): a selling change alone leaves the profile
"unchanged", marks nothing to check, moves no map_version. An older `as_of` never overwrites a newer row. A push without it (an older
connector, an import) leaves the row. The site's answer is unchanged; the audit row `listing.profiles` counts `selling`, `selling_ignored`.
Old CW with the new connector: `selling` is an unknown key, ignored (ListingIngestService::profile reads named keys only; both hashes too).

**WD6. Where it shows.** The item page, "Selling mode on the websites", a column "Mode on the website now" beside "Selling mode it gets": per
website product (with its option number when the store has more than one), its mode in the website's words, "+ back-orders", "low-stock
warning at N", "the website said so on <UK time>"; "not known yet" with no row; "no selling mode set" when the website has none. View only:
nothing in CW decides by it. "Set by" says "given back to the website" for a row the switch gave back.

**WD7. Release order.** CW first (0067 + 0068 + this code; the old connector sends no `selling`: the column says "not known yet"), then the
connector 0.4.13 (old CW ignores `selling`).

### The Codex review of 4f36499 (2 runs): 2 MEDIUM, both fixed test-first

- **0067 could not resume after a stop between its two ALTERs (MEDIUM, CW).** The migrator records a file only after its last statement; a
  run stopped after the log's ALTER failed the second time on the CHECK already there ("Duplicate check constraint name"), and the production
  installer would keep the web, the API and the jobs paused. Now each ALTER (the column made NULL-able and its CHECK: one atomic statement)
  is a prepared statement that runs only while its CHECK is not there (as 0056 and 0060); a CHECK of that name on a column still NOT NULL
  stops the migration, naming it. 0068 (one CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) was already safe; its test now shows it. Tests:
  `Migration0067Test::testARunStoppedAnywhereRunsAgainCleanly` (red on 4f36499: the review's error, 3822), `Migration0068Test`.
- **The connector's one-off re-send after 0.4.13 (MEDIUM, shop connector).** `selling` changes every shop-side hash, so the first full or
  delta pass would have sent the whole catalogue in one worker call. Fixed in the connector (0.4.13, lib/listings.php): re-sends (a variant
  last sent as its profile of before 0.4.13) share one budget kept in the shop's cw_meta, at most 3,000 a minute and 1,000 a call (one
  request), in every pass; the rest waits, and the watch keeps a 0.4.12 memory as website states CW holds, so a status change still goes at
  once. No CW change.

## Items is one list of every item, with an icon per store (branch `items-list-links`, 17 Nov 2026; IL1-IL6; no migration)

The owner, 17 Nov 2026 (CW chat), on https://warehouse.floverfy.com/ui/items/cards: "now this page. i want you to remve and needs a look section.
items pages is to see all products in cw properly so we usee it for that. remove the sstatus coloums add 3 small extra coloum with alt, vpg,
vbig should show icons just iicons to know if it is connected or not." So Items stops being a board by product card (RD-A3) and becomes the
place to see every item; the card itself (its legal fields, its rules, Confirm) stays on the item page, unchanged.

**IL1. ONE list.** Every item that is not merged away, in one card and one table, most stock first (as before: `ItemCardList::rows`, held
DESC then id), 100 a page with the pager. No groups ("Needs a look", "No card yet", "Ready"), no Status column (the "Check the card" /
"Blocked" / "No card" / "Ready" pill), and no card rules line or "Warning: ..." tag under the name either: they were the status column's words
in another place, and the card's state is the item page's LEGAL part. A website whose stock link is on already shows a blocked product as
Out-Of-Stock by itself (WD3, SiteView), which was the reason the block's rules stayed on the list (RD-A3, "safety"). "Not sold any more" stays
a quiet tag under the name: a fact about the product, not a state of its card. The "?" beside the heading keeps the card rules: they still
say what More's "Warning or blocked" and "Blocked" filters keep.

**IL2. Linked = `channel_listing.sku_id` is the item (`ItemCardList::links`).** The link of DecisionService, its only writer. 0001's CHECK ties a
set sku_id to `mapped` or `quarantined` (D32: both are "linked"; quarantined is on hold, held off sale), so a suggestion, a website product not
matched yet, an ignored one and a landing page (all with no sku_id) are never connected. A merged item has no link: a merge moves every link
of the item folded away to the kept item (M10), which then shows them, and the list leaves merged items out (as before). Read-only looks on
17 Nov 2026: production has 0 quarantined listings, 44 merged items holding 0 links, 15,279 items; per store, items linked: Electrofag 6,633,
Vape and Go 15,131, Vape Big 7,550; at most 3 linked website products for one item on one store. Staging the same shape (0 quarantined, 0
links on merged items) with a fourth store, `vpgproto`.
ONE read for a page's icons, whatever its rows (`WHERE cl.sku_id IN (<the page's ids>)` grouped by item and store, on the (sku_id,
channel_id) index of 0024; LINKS_CHUNK 1,000 ids a read, so the CSV of the whole catalogue is sixteen reads); `rows()` attaches it to every
row as `links` (store code => linked, on_hold). Nothing is stored: a link made or undone shows at the next page load.

**IL3. Three small columns, icons only.** Between the item and On hand, in the owner's order and words: Alt (Electrofag), VPG (Vape and Go),
VBig (Vape Big) (`ItemCardList::STORES`; heads `Words::ITEM_LINKS`, the store's full name `Words::SITE` the head's title). A store not there
(a new test system) shows every item not connected; another store (the proto's `vpgproto`) has no column. A cell holds one icon and no text:
connected, a tick in a green disc (`.link-ico.on`, the sprite's `check`); not connected, an empty grey ring (`.link-ico.off`, a CSS circle).
Its words are the icon's `aria-label` (`role="img"`) and its hover `title`: "Vape and Go: connected (2 website products)", "Electrofag: not
connected", "Electrofag: connected, on hold (1 website product)" when every linked one there is on hold (as the item page's "on hold", IV5).
The cell sits above the link that covers the row (`td.c-link`, z-index 2, as `td.c-next`), so pointing at the icon shows its words; the rest
of the row still opens the item. On a phone (the page column 640 px or narrower) the row is a card: the name, then the three on one line,
each after its short name (the cell's data-label), then On hand.

**IL4. Filters.** The Show choice is All items, Holding stock, Made by hand (also on Made by hand's own page). "Not confirmed" and "Blocked"
named the two kinds of the "Needs a look" group (RD-F3) and went with it. Nothing else was dropped or renamed: More keeps every filter of
before (the product card, the kind of product, Holds stock, Warning or blocked, Blocked, Not sold any more), Clear, Import, the download; any
of them on says "Chosen filters" on the Show and opens More's filters. The search (name, brand, barcode, CW number) and the stock order are
unchanged.

**IL5. The CSV ("Download these for Excel").** Three columns after `stock_held`: `alt`, `vpg`, `vbig`, "yes" where the item is linked to one
of that store's website products or more (on hold included), else "no" (`ItemCardCsv::STORE_COLUMNS`, in STORES' order). They are read-only
like `stock_held` (`IGNORED`): an export still goes back through the import unchanged; an import of an older export (without them) is as before.
An export made by this code and imported by an older CW would be refused for unknown columns (only during a rollback).

**IL6. What points here.** Home's "Items" tile (the count of items not merged) and the sidebar's Items (Sections `cards`) still lead here and
still say the right thing. The page's intro words (Words::PAGE_INTRO `cards`, not drawn: DC1) no longer say "Fix the ones marked with a
warning first". The old words of the groups and pills (INV_LIST g_*, p_*, col_status, show_unconfirmed, show_blocked, needs_look) are gone.

## Who is here on a draft order, the server half (branch `live-presence`, 18 Nov 2026; LV1-LV12; migration 0070)

The owner, 18 Nov 2026: "we need to show each other if each others are in the same window as like in google sheets where we know which line
they are pressed in". The plan (`/root/cw_work/live_drafts_20261118/PLAN_fable.md`, step 3) splits it: this branch is the server (step 3a);
the page's script (the poll loop, the chips, the marks on the lines) is step 3b, after the page's look (step 2); saving each box is step 4.

**LV1. Scope.** One table (`draft_presence`), one route (`POST /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/live`), the passive session rule, a line's own id
(`document_line.uid`, `document.next_line_uid`), four settings, the sign-out and the nightly clean-up. No view, no script: with live.mode off
(the default) nothing on the site changes.

**LV2. A small table, not APCu.** `draft_presence` (0070): one row per open page (tab) of a draft, keyed (kind, record_id, tab): who, their
session (`session_id` = staff_session.id, the sha256 of the cookie token, never the token: the plan's 16-character handle became the whole id
so a row can be joined to its session by primary key, LV6), the line (uid) and box they are in (`7:qty`, `h:note`), active or away, typing,
whether they may change the draft (`edits`, written by their own poll from their roles of that request: no roles read for others), and
`seen_at` (the database clock). Indexes: (kind, record_id, seen_at) for the poll, session_id for the sign-out, seen_at for the clean-up. No
foreign keys (a heartbeat never fails on one), the app login's full rights, CHECKs on the tab (16 hex) and the session id (64 hex). APCu would
need a package on three machines and is per pool.

**LV3. The poll.** `POST /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/live` (Ui\Controller\LiveController, CW\Live\Presence::beat): purchasing.view (whoever may
open the order), same origin and the session's token as every POST, no form-once key (a poll changes nothing but its own row). The request:
`csrf`, `tab` (16 hex, 400 bad_tab otherwise), `focus` (`<uid>:<box>`, `h:<box>` or empty; anything else is no place, never a refusal),
`state` (away, or active), `typing`, `active`, `bye`. The answer is JSON (Context::json, the only JSON of /ui; names and numbers, no words):
`{"v", "status": "draft", "mode", "poll_ms", "here": [{"id", "name", "c", "state", "edits", "uid", "field", "typing"}]}`; for a document
that is no longer a draft `{"v", "status", "mode", "number", "by", "to"}` ("by": who made it final, sent it for its OK or stopped it; "to":
the order's page, without a notice yet: step 3b chooses one); for `bye=1` the tab's row goes and `{"v", "status", "mode", "bye": true}`;
with live.mode off `{"mode": "off"}` and nothing read or written. Not a purchase order, or no document: 404 unknown_document.

**LV4. Passive: a poll keeps no session alive.** `Router::add(..., passive: true)` sets `Route::$passive`; the kernel resolves the session with
`touch: !passive || active=1` (Auth\Sessions::resolve). The page sends active=1 at most once a minute and only after a key or the mouse was
used (step 3b). So a page left open is signed out after the idle limit although it polls (its next poll goes to the sign-in page), and the
session row is written once a minute, not per poll. Everything else of the route (sign-in, access, origin, token) is as for any other.

**LV5. Written only on a change.** Per poll: the settings (one read by primary key), the document (by primary key, the name of who posted or
cancelled it by primary key), the draft's rows that can still be shown (the index (kind, record_id, seen_at); the cut-offs of an active
and an away row applied in SQL before the limit; newest first, at most `MAX_ROWS` = 100; each joined to staff_user and staff_session by
primary key; `Presence::rowsSql`); each read carries `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(500)`. Then at most one
write, the poll's own row, only when its place, state, typing or right to change differ from the row read, or the row is 10 seconds old
(`Presence::needsWrite`, REFRESH_SECONDS), or it is not among the rows read. One upsert; a row of the same tab held by another session is
never taken over (each assignment is guarded by the session id). The bound (the Codex review of 50fa425, MEDIUM 3): a page that sends many
tab ids cannot make every poll of the draft heavy; past a hundred fresh rows the oldest are not seen.

**LV6. Here, away, gone.** Only rows of a session that has not ended (`Auth\Sessions::liveSql`: not revoked, the second step done, within
the idle and absolute limits of this request) and of a person not switched off: a session ended any way (a sign-out, a manager's sign-out, a
password change, past a limit although nothing revoked it yet) leaves at once, and a poll still on its way when
its session ended writes a row nobody is shown (the Codex review of 50fa425, MEDIUM 2). Shown: an active row seen within `goneAfter()` seconds (live.gone_seconds, 25; never before the person's next poll
could have written the row: max(poll, alone) + 10 + 5), an away row within 10 minutes (AWAY_SECONDS; away rows have no place and no
typing). The poller's own tabs are nobody; a person on two tabs is shown once (an active tab first, then the newest). `poll_ms`:
live.poll_seconds while anyone else is here (active or away: my row stays fresh for them), live.alone_seconds when alone.

**LV7. Colours.** 1-8, decided on the server over everyone here and the poller, so every screen agrees: in id order, id % 8 + 1 or the next
free one; past eight people a colour is shared. The page draws them as classes (CSP: no inline style), step 3b.

**LV8. A line's own id.** `document_line.uid` (UNIQUE (document_id, uid), NULL allowed) and `document.next_line_uid` (0070; added to
Grants::UPDATE_COLUMNS['document']). `Documents::setLines()` carries the `uid` a line names (a line of the draft now; another, or one twice: 400
bad_lines, nothing saved) and gives a line without one the next free id (never given before in that document). The services of every type
(PO, delivery, supplier invoice, return, stock records, hand-over, count sheet, repack) send no ids yet: each whole save gives new ones, so a
mark goes stale until the page is drawn again. Carrying them through a page's whole save (the form sends each line's id, PurchaseOrders
passes it on) is step 3b's. `Documents::lineUids()` gives the page line number => id. Neither column is in `Documents::lineRow()`: posted_hash and
document_posting are unchanged (tests pin it for every type). A reversal's and a system job's copied lines get no id (never a draft).
0070 backfills uid = line_no for drafts and documents waiting for their OK (only where no line has an id), next_line_uid past the highest.

**LV9. The settings** (Settings > Working together, provisional): `live.mode` off / presence / on, **off on deploy** (the undo of the whole step
without a deploy; on = presence until step 4), `live.poll_seconds` 3 (2-10), `live.alone_seconds` 10 (5-60), `live.gone_seconds` 25 (25-300:
never below the default, so an active person is never called gone between two polls). Read with the same defaults when a row is missing.

**LV10. Leaving.** A page left sends `bye=1` (sendBeacon, step 3b): its row goes. Signing out (AuthController::logout) ends the session
first, then removes every row of the session (`Presence::forget`); a failure there (a deadlock, no table before 0070) is logged and never
stops the sign-out (the Codex review of 50fa425, HIGH 1): the rows left are not shown (LV6). A session ended otherwise leaves its rows
unseen (LV6). The nightly clean-up (Ops\Housekeeping, part `draft_presence`) removes rows older than a day.

**LV11. Cost** (plan 3.5): 10 people on one draft at the quick poll is about 200 polls a minute, each about 5 reads by primary key and at most
one small write (steady about 60 writes a minute); a hidden or closed page costs nothing. No long poll (10 php-fpm workers on production).

**LV12. Left for step 3b.** The view (`data-live`, `data-live-tab` from `Presence::newTab()`, each line's `data-uid` from `lineUids()`, the
words of the chips from Words), the script (the timers of the plan's 3.4, active=1 once a minute after input, bye by sendBeacon, back-off, a
303 stops polling), the colour classes, the whole-save carrying of line ids (LV8), a notice for "confirmed by someone else", and making
the page's own fragment fetches passive too (a hidden page must not keep a session alive by fetching).

### The Codex review of 50fa425 (`presence_20261118/codex_answer_r1.txt`): 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, each shown failing first and fixed (LV13-LV15)

**LV13 (HIGH 1).** The sign-out removed the presence rows before it ended the session and rethrew any failure but a missing table: a deadlock
there gave a 500 and left the session live. Now the session ends first; the removal comes after and a failure is logged (`Context::log`),
never stopping the sign-out (LV10). Test: `LivePresenceScreensTest::testASignOutGoesOnWhenThePresenceRowsCannotBeRemoved` (a deadlock thrown
on the DELETE).

**LV14 (MEDIUM 2).** A poll that passed the sign-in check could write its row after the sign-out removed the rows, and others saw the person
again (up to ten minutes when away). The row now names its session by its whole id and the poll reads only rows of sessions not ended
(LV2, LV6); a session ended without a sign-out leaves at once too. Test: `PresenceTest::testARowIsShownOnlyWhileItsSessionHasNotEnded`.

**LV15 (MEDIUM 3).** The poll read every row of the draft. It now reads only the rows that can still be shown, newest first, at most 100,
by the new index (kind, record_id, seen_at) (LV5). Test: `PresenceTest::testAPollReadsOnlyTheNewestRowsThatCanStillBeShown`.

### The Codex re-check of c1d567d (`presence_20261118/codex_answer_r2.txt`): round 1's three fixed; 2 MEDIUM new, each shown failing first and fixed (LV16-LV17)

**LV16 (MEDIUM 1).** Only a revoked session was left out, but a session past its idle or absolute limit is revoked only at its next request:
a hidden page's away row stayed shown up to ten minutes after its session ended. The read now joins the session under the full rule of a live
session (`Sessions::liveSql('s')`, the limits this request already read: no extra query). Test: `PresenceTest::testARowOfASessionPastItsLimitsIsNotShown`.

**LV17 (MEDIUM 2).** The read took the newest hundred rows of the last ten minutes and only then dropped active rows past the gone time, so
a hundred gone rows could hide an away person still shown. The cut-offs of both states are now in the SQL, before the limit. Test: the end of
`PresenceTest::testAPollReadsOnlyTheNewestRowsThatCanStillBeShown`.


### The Codex re-check of 4afbd44, rebased onto 4b9705e (`presence_20261118/codex_answer_r3.txt`): no finding

Round 2's two fixes checked, and the change on top of "drafts anyone may change" (DA1-DA5: setLines without the creator check; the poll's
`edits` = may post the type, not admin): 0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 0 LOW. The full suite on the rebased branch: Unit 626 OK, UiKernel 678 OK, the
rest 1,286 OK (83 skipped: the HTTP tests of slot ui, one more than before: `UiSecurityTest::testThePollOfADraftOrderOverHttp`).

## One look for a purchase order: a draft is the saved order's paper with its boxes in place (branch `look-paper`, 18 Nov 2026; LP1-LP11; live drafts step 2; migration 0071, two setting rows)

The owner, 18 Nov 2026, of the read-only order page another buyer saw ("Shareef's window") beside the creator's grey form ("Fazil's"): "I liked
how it looks on Shareef's window, the design". After DA1 everyone who writes orders gets the editor, so everyone would get the grey form;
this step makes the editor the paper. The plan: `/root/cw_work/live_drafts_20261118/PLAN_fable.md` sections 2 and 7, step 2. Saving does not
change (whole form, its version, 409 as DA3); presence (step 3) and saving per box (step 4) come later.

(the supplier, where it delivers, the dates), `po_paper_lines` (the table, the "+ Add product" line, the new line's `<template>`, the grid's
tools and key hints), `po_paper_line` (one row: read only, a saved line with boxes, or a new line), `po_paper_foot` (the note, the totals) and
`po_cards` (Related, History). A person who may only look gets the parts as words (`$edit` false), as before; a draft or a new order for
someone who may post (`doc.PO.post`, DA1) gets them as boxes inside the one editor form
`form#po-form.po-editor.kg-doc.kg-paper[data-kg-editor]`, which posts the whole page with its version, as `purchase_order_edit.php` did.
The confirmed page's HTML was the same as before (checked by drawing both from the same data) until LP10 put the draft's changes in

do not change.

**LP2. The way back: the setting `po.draft_look`** (`paper`, the default, or `form`; migration 0071; `PurchaseOrdersController::draftLook`,
"paper" while the row is not there). `form` draws drafts and new orders on the old one-page form again, with no deploy; it is kept for one
release and deleted with the setting at the end of the live-drafts work (plan step 5).

**LP3. The head is the read-only page's.** The title, the Draft chip and the line under it ("UNIVERSAL · started 18 Nov 2026 by Fazil"),

the CW code, then their code, the pack and the VAT on the line under it; a product changed by typing in the name, KG22; items per pack as a

### The Codex reviews of look-paper (`lookpaper_20261118/codex_round1.txt` to `codex_round3.txt`; three rounds, the cap)

- Round 3 (no HIGH, 1 MEDIUM): the hidden old box was still one of the grid's boxes (the keys aimed at it): it leaves them. Fixed after the
