## Who is here on a draft order, on the screen (branch `live-presence-screen`, 19 Nov 2026; LV18-LV25; live drafts step 3b; no migration)

The owner, 19 Nov 2026: "the on-screen 'Fazil is here too' with coloured names on lines. Do this." The server half is LV1-LV17 (live since
18 Nov, switched off: `live.mode` = off); the look is LP1-LP11. Turning it on stays the setting `live.mode` (Settings > Working together):
`presence` (or `on`) shows it, `off` draws nothing and sends nothing (the undo, no deploy).

**LV18. Where it is drawn.** Purchase orders only, a draft with an id (a confirmed order, one waiting for its OK or cancelled, and a new
order without an id show nobody). `LiveController::pageData()` gives the page what its script needs, or null (live.mode off, not a draft):
the poll's address, a new tab id each time the page is drawn (`Presence::newTab()`), the version the page shows (the editor's form version:
a page drawn again after a refusal shows the version it was typed on), the page and the sign-in page with the way back, the rhythm (LV21)
and every word (Words::LIVE). `live_attrs` prints them as `data-live*` on the element the script starts on: the editor form `#po-form` (the
paper, and the old form of `po.draft_look = form`), or, for a person who may only look, the read-only paper (`article.po-paper`, with the
session's token beside it as a hidden input): they poll too, so the others see them "looking" (open question 6 of the plan, the owner's
"yes"). `live_here` is the place under the title for the chips, a note and one polite live region. Each saved line names its own id
(`tr[data-uid]`, `Documents::lineUids` order; a new line not saved yet has none), each box its place (`data-live-cell`: item, qty, price,
upp), the head's and the foot's boxes theirs (`data-live-box`: h:supplier, h:expected_date, h:external_ref, h:note, h:delivery; the plan's
3.2). With live.mode off the read-only paper is drawn as before (its marks only when shown).

**LV19. A line keeps its id through every whole save (LV8's "step 3b's").** `PurchaseOrders::lines()` names each line's `uid`;
`normaliseLines()` takes it (a whole number or null, 400 otherwise) and passes it to `Documents::setLines()`, which keeps it (400
bad_lines for an id that is not a line of the draft, or one twice). So every path that saves the lines it read keeps them: the page's
whole save (the controller maps the form's rows onto `lines()` read inside the save, after the version check: the rows the page showed),
Add and its increment, the grid's new lines (a new id each), a line removed (the others keep theirs), the file appended (Add multiple and
the file), a supplier changed (`repoint()` keeps the line's other keys), a new supplier made on the draft, a new item made on a line. A line
whose item is changed in place (KG22: the saved line removed and a new line in its place in the same post) keeps the replaced line's id
(`gridLines`). New ids: a file that replaces the lines, and another order's lines (`copyLines()` drops them: copy and amend). The form
sends no ids: the version check already guarantees the server's lines are the page's, so nothing of the page is trusted and no field is
added per line (max_input_vars, I73). The ids are not in the posting fingerprint (LV8; the tests of 0070 pin it).

**LV20. What people see.** Under the title, the page's sentence with each person a chip (a coloured dot and the name): "Fazil is here too",
"Fazil and Asha are here too", "4 others are here" (then a chip each), "Asha is looking" (a person who may only look, alone; with others
their chip says "Asha (looking)"), "Fazil (away)" faded. On a phone (640 px), three or more people: their initials, the 4th on folded into
"+N". On a line: a 3 px edge in the person's colour on the row (a phone's card: its left edge), an outline on the box they are in and a
small name tag at its top right (two people in one box: one tag, both names); the head's boxes the same; a removed (hidden) line and an
away person get no mark. The colours are the classes `who-c1`..`who-c8` (the number is the server's, LV7; the CSP allows no inline style),
each passing WCAG AA behind white words; the name tag is always there, so the colour is never the only sign. One `aria-live="polite"`
region says who came and who left in whole sentences, at most one in `data-live-say-ms` (5 s). Names go in as text only.

**LV21. The script's rhythm** (app.js block "live", from `// live drafts` to `// (live ends here)`; the plan's 3.4). ONE timer (setTimeout,
never setInterval; cleared before it is set again) and at most one poll on its way: the next poll is set only from its answer. The pace is
the answer's `poll_ms` (live.poll_seconds while someone else is here, live.alone_seconds alone), spread by ±`JITTER_MS`; the first poll
within the jitter of the page being drawn. No key or mouse for `IDLE_AWAY_SECONDS` (2 min): state away, no place, the slow pace; for
`AWAY_SECONDS` (10 min): no more polls, a goodbye (its row goes), "Paused. Click to carry on." until a key, the mouse or the button. The page
hidden: one away poll, then none; shown again: the person is back (for away and the pause only, never active=1), one poll at once. The page
left (`pagehide`): a goodbye by `navigator.sendBeacon` (bye=1, its token, its tab); back from the browser's cache (`pageshow` persisted):
polling again. No answer, a 5xx, a 409/429 or an answer slower than `SLOW_MS` (2 s): the wait doubles up to `BACKOFF_SECONDS` (30 s); a poll
out that long is given up (AbortController, on the same one timer); the first good answer: the server's pace again. Every number is the
page's (`data-live-*-ms`: the settings and Presence's constants); the script holds none.

**LV22. The session (LV4) from the page.** A poll says `active=1` only after a real key or mouse (`ev.isTrusted`; keydown, pointerdown,
mousedown, touchstart, wheel), at most once in `ACTIVE_SECONDS` (a minute); a key inside that minute is said at the first poll after it. So a
page left open is signed out after the idle limit although it polls. A 303 (the session ended) is never followed (`redirect: 'manual'`):
polling stops and the note says "You were signed out…" with "Sign in again" (the sign-in page, back to the order). A 400, 403 or 404 (another
sign-in in this browser, the right to look taken away): polling stops quietly. The answer `{"mode": "off"}`: nothing more is drawn or sent.
The page's own fragment fetches (Save without leaving the page) are not polls; they move the session as any request (the person pressed Save).

**LV23. "Fazil saved a change at 14:02. [Show it]"** (the plan's step 3). The poll sends the version the page shows (`v`); when the draft
is newer, `LiveController` adds who saved it last and when (`changed`: `by`, `at` (Html::clock, UK time), `you`), one read of the audit
(DraftChanges::last), only then. The page says "Fazil saved a change at 14:02." ("You saved a change at 14:02 in another tab or window."
for the person's own) with "Show it": nothing typed, the page again (GET); something typed (the form dirty, or a new line on it), the
editor form sent with `action=show`: `PurchaseOrdersController::lines()` draws the draft as it is now with the new lines typed kept (as the
409 page keeps them, KG6), nothing saved or checked, with the notice "Here is the order as it is now. The new lines you typed are kept; type
any other change again." The page's own save on its way (`aria-busy`) or a poll sent before the page's version moved never says it; the note
goes when the page shows the newest version.

**LV24. A draft that is no longer one.** The poll's answer for a confirmed, sent-for-OK or cancelled draft (LV3) stops polling and says who:
"Fazil confirmed this order. It is PO-000123 now.", "… sent this order for its OK.", "… cancelled this draft." ("Someone" when CW knows no
name), with "Open the order" (the page's own address). The boxes are not locked in this step (a save is refused as `not_draft`, as before).

**LV25. Tests.** `PoPresenceScreensTest` (new: nothing with live.mode off; the editor form, the old form and a looker's paper carry the poll,
the tab, the version, the rhythm and every word; the chips' place under the title; `data-uid` = `lineUids`; the boxes' places; no inline
style; a confirmed and a new order show nobody; a line keeps its id through the page's save, a new line, a removal, an item changed in
place and Add; the poll's `changed`; Show it); `PoLineUidTest` (two new: the service's every path, copy fresh); `UiUnitTest::
testWhoIsHereIsOneBlockWithItsWordsFromThePage` (one block, one timer, no words or times in it, the poll's own address, the colour classes
and their contrast, the phone rules) and the assets test (two fetches, one beacon, both in the block); `WordsTest::
testWhoIsHereSaysItInWholeSentences`. The script in node: `run_live.js` (outside the repo, `/root/cw_work/presence2_20261119/js_harness/`,
run by `runs/presence2_js.sh` on cw-test: the first poll, the answer drawn and moved, joins and leaves said at the rate, focus, typing,
active only after a real key and once a minute, away, pause and carry on, hidden, left, back from the cache, back-off, a hung poll, 303,
403, off, confirmed, cancelled, Show it both ways, many people, two in one box, a save drawing the page again, nothing started on a wrong
address; never more than one timer); `run_kg.js` stays green on the paper.

### The Codex reviews of c62e742 (`presence2_20261119/codex_r1_{a,b,c}.txt`; three focused runs at once: sessions and security, the script, the line ids): 5 MEDIUM, 2 LOW, each shown failing first and fixed (LV26-LV28)

**LV26 (a2, MEDIUM). A passive route never redirects.** A page's goodbye (`navigator.sendBeacon`) follows redirects: a goodbye of a page
whose session ended, or sent while another person in the same browser must change their password, landed on the sign-in or the password
page, a GET that marks a session seen. The kernel now answers a passive route (the poll) without a live session, or of a person who must
change their password first, with 401 `{"signed_out": true}` (JSON, never a redirect; a dead cookie is still cleared); the script reads a
401 as signed out (as a 303 before). Tests: `LivePresenceScreensTest` (no session, a forced password change: 401 and the session not seen;
past the idle limit: 401), `run_live.js` 11e.

**LV27 (b2, MEDIUM). Who is here starts after a new order's first save.** A new order has no id, so its page carries no poll; its first
save without leaving the page made it a draft, but the form kept no `data-live*`. `swapIn` now takes the draft's `data-live*` onto the form
when it has none (a page that shows who is here keeps its own tab), and the block starts once, on the page drawn or on `kg-swapped`. Tests:
`run_live.js` 11f, `UiUnitTest` (the copy and the start).

**LV28. The rest of the round.** a1 (MEDIUM): a key from before the page was hidden made the poll at its showing say active=1 twenty
minutes later; active=1 now also needs the key to be recent (within twice `ACTIVE_SECONDS`): 11a. b1 (MEDIUM): a poll still out when the
page was left (and kept in the browser's cache) kept `busy` for ever; leaving gives it up (AbortController): 11b. b3 (MEDIUM): a failure
while away (or at a slow alone pace above the back-off's most) made the next poll sooner; the back-off now starts from the pace in force and
never shortens it: 11c. b4 (LOW): a page shown again while its away poll was out waited a whole interval; the next poll goes right after
that answer: 11d. c1 (LOW): a line whose item was changed in place, drawn again after a refusal, carried no id (the hidden saved line kept
it); the new line in its place now carries it and the hidden line none, on the paper and the old form: `PoPresenceScreensTest`.

### The Codex re-check of round 1's fixes (`presence2_20261119/codex_r2_{a,b,c}.txt`; three focused runs at once): no HIGH, no MEDIUM, 1 LOW

All seven fixes checked (a: the session rule, the 401, the copy of `data-live*` from this order's own answer only; b: one timer, one poll,
no dead chain, the redraws; c: one `data-uid` per line, the replacement's, nothing broken on a new order or the read-only paper). The LOW
(b and c): a new order's first save puts the cursor back before who is here starts, so the first polls said no place until the cursor

### The full suite (sequential, one part at a time)

Unit 639 OK; UiKernel 697 OK; the rest 1,288 OK (83 skipped: the HTTP tests of slot ui, as before). On the way, UiKernel failed
`PurchaseOrderItemsPdfScreensTest` (it passes alone and on main): its PDF parser took a stream as the bytes up to `\r?\nendstream`, so a
compressed stream that ended in a carriage return lost that byte and its words; the bytes follow the ids the PDF prints, which
`PoPresenceScreensTest` (run before it) moves on. The test now reads each stream by its `/Length` (test only). `CompanyScreensTest` and
`HandoverPdfCompanyTest` parse PDFs the same old way and can fail the same way some day.

## Existing item at Add product, and the same details before a new item (branch `store-existing`, 19 Nov 2026; SX1-SX8; tracker CW-1138)

The owner, 19 Nov 2026: "we should have an option under new item something like existing. so i can just add the cw code there and if it
can show recommendation then great". That day Vape Big's 5mg (variant 13869, "Elux Legend Lemon & Lime Nic Salt E-liquid 10ml - 5mg", no
barcode) was added as "New item"; CW had it as CW-011468 ("Elux Legend Nic Salt - Lemon & Lime - 10ml - 5mg", two barcodes, Vape and Go's
and Electrofag's variants linked), found no barcode and no near-same name, and made an empty CW-015324 (relinked by hand, decision 46109).

**SX1. A fourth choice: existing.** At Add product and Add variant staff may say a new variant IS an item the warehouse has: `choice`
`existing`, `pack_of` its CW number (CW-000123 as CW writes it; the store turns "cw-11468" or "11468" into that), `units` null. 0073 adds the
value at the end of the column's list; the CHECK keeps every other choice exactly as before. The first choice is kept (SC2).

**SX2. The store asks before it sends.** GET /v1/item-suggestions (the store's key, like every /v1 route; read only; any mode): at most 5
items, not joined into another (one found through a joined item counts as the item it is now), each with its CW number, name, free to sell
for that store (on hand + on its way - allocated - held over its sellable warehouses) and why: `barcode` (a barcode of the variant, any form
one scan takes, on an item or on a store variant linked to one), then `same_details` (SX5), then `similar_name` (most of the name's words in
the item's name: a Dice score of at least 0.5 over the telling words, a little more when strength, size and kind agree). `strong`: the
first is a barcode or the same details (the store shows "CW already has this ... Use it" under New item). With `code` the answer also says
what that number is now (`item`; null = no such item; `named` = the number asked, joined into the one shown). No other store's name is in
the answer.

**SX3. Bounded.** Every field is checked (400 bad_query naming it): title and option at most 512 characters, brand 128, at most 20 option
names/values (128/255), at most 20 barcodes of 1-64 printable characters, code a CW number, limit 1-5; at least one of title, option,
barcodes, code. The reads: the barcode indexes (never a scan), one pass over the items' cards for the same details (narrowed by kind,
strength, brand family and a flavour word; at most 500 read), one pass over the items' names for the words (at most 6 words, the best 80
scored). Measured on staging's copy (14,859 items, the staging droplet to its database): 150-270 ms a question, end to end.

**SX4. Existing is a link, one for one.** The job follows it as `system:store_choice` (SC4): the item its number names, followed to the item
it was joined into, linked with units 1 through DecisionService; nothing else is looked for (staff named the item). The two-person rules of
a link apply as for anyone (a protected item, a variant once said not to be that item: pending_second, outcome `waiting_second`). An
unknown number is refused (`no_such_item`) and waits on Approvals > New products, where a person makes a new item or marks it not stock.
Outcome `linked_existing`; the decision's reason says "the existing item CW-...".

**SX5. The same details (ItemSuggestions::sameDetails).** Strict, because it stops the job: the same flavour words (both known; a brand or
range word read as flavour on one side, "Elux Legend Lemon & Lime" under the brand "Elux", is left out of both), the same kind (form class,
both known), the same strength (both unknown counts as the same), a brand family word in common (the brand's family words or the range's
words), the same nicotine type, size and puffs when both say one, the same pack size (unknown = 1), the same range numbers ("Legend 3500"
is not "Legend 8000") and modifiers ("Pro" is not plain). The variant is read as the matching reads a listing (Normalizer, then
DecisionService::cardFrom), afresh from its profile (stored features are cleared on every identity change); the item side is its card.

**SX6. A new item waits when an item has the same details.** After the older checks, in their order (the check on arrival's suggestion, a
barcode, the same or a close name), the job also looks for an item with the same details; one found: nothing is made, the row waits for a
person (to_check `same_features`, with the item, its name): "Yes, the same" links it one for one, as for the other doubts (SC9). Looked at
again after the name's guard row, like the others (SC6). Items without a card (no flavour or kind) never stop a new item.

**SX7. The connector (0.4.16).** The store's admin shows Existing item second (New item / Existing item / A pack of an item / Not stock) on
Add product (simple and every row of a variable product) and Add variant: a CW number box, what CW says it is (name and free to sell),
up to 5 suggestions to click, and under New item the strong match with "Use it". A number CW says it has not got stops the save; when CW
cannot be asked the save goes ahead and this job checks it (SX4). The store's key stays on the store's server (the admin asks its own
endpoint, which asks CW). The `existing` choices go in a PUT of their own after the others: a CW before 0073 refuses that call whole, and
the other choices never wait for it. Going back: the release before reads an unknown choice as New item, so a CW rollback first waits
until no `existing` choice is waiting (docs/ops.md); a connector rollback first waits until the store has no unsent `existing` choice
(a 0.4.15 worker parks it as a bad choice; the kit's undo gate refuses otherwise).

**SX8. Approvals > New products.** A same_features row shows "Same brand, flavour, strength and size" with the item found and its stock, and
"Yes, the same: use CW-..." as the main answer; an existing choice reads "the existing item CW-..."; `no_such_item` now reads "The CW number
the store gave is not an item" (a pack's or an existing item's). Done rows: "Linked to the existing item the store named"; `waiting_second`
reads "The link waits for a matching lead's second OK" (a pack's or an existing item's).

Reviews (Codex, read only; reports in /root/cw_work/existing_20261119/codex/): round 1, three focused runs at once (a correctness, b security,
c UX and the three shops): 1 HIGH (a CW rollback would read a waiting `existing` choice as New item: the undo steps now wait until none is
waiting, or take the job off the timer), 8 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, all fixed: a pack's barcode (an outer case, a barcode found on two items, a variant
linked as a pack) is never suggested as the item itself; the database narrows the brand as brandTokens() reads it ("R&M" = randm); the
connector's undo has a gate (no unsent `existing` choice, the 0.4.16 admin gone for two minutes); a failed second call never counts the
first group again; the admin's per-session limit is kept in the session for real; the save's check of the numbers is bounded (20 numbers,
6 s); a suggestion answer for details no longer shown is never used. The re-check (three runs) found the barcode filter incomplete on the
listing path and in its leading-zero forms, the undo's running saves, a pack in the shop's offline list, a busy note hidden under New item
and the EF/VB patch route: all fixed (the EF/VB admin goes through the shared master only).

## Each box of a draft order saved by itself (branch `live-save`, 19 Nov 2026; LS1-LS14; live drafts step 4; migration 0072)

The owner, 19 Nov 2026: "Step 4 of working together: each box saves by itself when you leave it. The other person sees the change in about 3
seconds, with no Save button. If you both change the same line, the second person picks which to keep." The plan: sections 4, 5 and step 4 of
`/root/cw_work/live_drafts_20261118/PLAN_fable.md`. Purchase orders only. On with `live.mode = on` (Settings > Working together); `presence`
gives the whole-form Save back at once (the undo, no deploy): the new columns are carried, a draft changed box by box is an ordinary draft.

**LS1. Scope.** The paper's editor (`po.draft_look = paper`, an order the form can carry: `editorFits`) of someone who may post orders. The old
form (`po.draft_look = form`), a person who may only look (they keep step 3's "saved a change [Show it]") and an order too long for the form keep
the whole-form save. Without the script the paper is today's form: Save and Confirm post it whole, with its version (409 as DA3).

**LS2. A line's own version.** `document_line.rev` (1 for a new line), `changed_by`, `changed_at` (0072). `Documents::setLines()` keeps a line's
version, author and time when the line keeps its id and its content is the same (its place may move: a line removed above is no change of it),
else version + 1, the caller's, now; the module's own part of a line is compared too (`$keys`, `$oldKeys`: PurchaseOrders' po_line, so a VAT
code changed alone moves it). Every type that calls setLines gets the rule; none of the three is in the posting fingerprint (`lineRow`).

**LS3. The in-place paths.** `Documents::changeLine` (one line by its id at the version the page saw: 409 line_conflict / line_gone),
`appendLine` (after the last, the next free id, version 1), `replaceLinesLive` (every line again, ids and versions carried: a removal and an
undo renumber, po_line follows by its cascade), `changeHeaderLive`. Each locks the document row first (409 `not_draft`, naming what it became,
its number and who: `Documents::notDraft`), checks the caller may post the type, moves the document's version by one, and writes NO audit row
(the module records the change: LS6). `PurchaseOrders`: `setLine` (packs, the pack's price, items per pack, or the product: the same
`normaliseLines()` as a whole save, one line, its own number in the words), `addLineLive` (a pack, an item and its items per pack, or the
delivery as a charge line), `removeLine`, `restoreLine`, `setHeaderField` (expected date, their reference, note; the supplier and the order
date stay whole saves). Lock order as saveDraft: document row, supplier FOR SHARE, purchase_order FOR UPDATE; the totals over every line
(`PoMath::totals`) on every change. A test holds the in-place paths and the whole save together over random sequences (identical
document_line, po_line and purchase_order rows) and two real workers on one draft (`LiveLinesRaceTest`).

**LS4. No overwrite (the plan's section 5).** A save of the values stored already: 200 `unchanged` (a retry; two people typing the same figure).
The same line changed since the page saw it: 409 `line_conflict` with its version now, who and when and their values (the other lines of both
people are saved). A line gone: 409 `line_gone` (who removed it, its product). Removing a line someone just changed: `line_conflict`; both
removing: done once. The same head box: 409 `field_conflict` with the value now. The same purchase added by someone else within
`SAME_PRODUCT_SECONDS` (120): 409 `line_exists` unless the page asks for more; otherwise today's rule (the packs added to that line). An add
and an undo carry the page's key (`draft_change.op_key`, UNIQUE per draft): sent twice, done once (`done`). Undo puts back the caller's OWN
removed line (their newest `remove` row), after the line before it when it is still there, with a new id (409 `nothing_to_restore`). A
confirmed or cancelled draft refuses every one.

**LS5. draft_change** (0072): one row per change (set, add, remove, restore, header; supplier and replace from the whole saves while live.mode is
on) and per refused clash (`conflict`: the measure of the plan's 7.4), with before and after (a removed line: enough to put it back), the tab,
the document's version after it; no foreign keys; read by (kind, record_id, id).

**LS6. Audit volume.** One `po.live_edit` audit row per person per draft per clock hour (the first change of the hour, decided from the person's
draft_change rows of the hour, inside the document lock); the detail is in draft_change. Confirm, cancel and the whole saves audit as before.
`DraftChanges::last()` (the 409's "who changed it", the poll's `changed`) reads draft_change too: its newest row is the last change while the
draft is still at the version it made (by version, not by clock).

**LS7. History.** The order's History card (`po_history`, also in the fragment) lists the line-by-line changes, one line per person per minute
("18 Nov 2026, 14:02 · Fazil changed 3 lines"), each change in its fold ("Packs 5 → 8 on Elf Bar 600 Blue Razz"); the hourly audit row is not
listed. Kept 90 days after the order is final (LS11), as the owner's answer to the plan's question 9.

**LS8. Routes.** `GET /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/live/doc?since=&tab=` (purchasing.view, passive: the page sends it by itself, it marks no
session seen; signed out: 401), `POST …/live/line` (op set, add, remove, restore) and `…/live/header` (doc.PO.post; the session's token and the
same origin; a person's own act, so the session is seen). Each answers the fragment `po_live` (the draft as it is now; a refusal in words in
its part `conflict`, status 400, 409 or 422); live.mode not on: 409 `live_off`; a request of another shape: 400.

**LS9. Confirm.** The page's Confirm waits for its saves, is refused on the page while a choice is open, says first when someone is typing
("Fazil is typing on line 4. [Confirm anyway] [Not now]"), then posts `/approve` with the version the page shows; changed since, the order's
page says who changed which line ("Fazil changed line 3 a moment ago. Look, then confirm again.", `LiveSaveWords::confirmChanged`). Someone
else confirming or cancelling: the next poll or save locks every box and says who and the number, and which box of mine was not saved.

**LS10. The fragment `po_live`.** Root `data-live-fragment="po:<id>"` with `data-v`, `data-e` (the newest change), `data-status`, `data-at`
(UK time), and what the page's own save did (`data-op`, `data-op-status`, `data-op-uid`, `data-op-key`); parts header (values, supplier,
address, terms), lines (the editor's own rows: `data-uid`, `data-rev`, `data-by`, `data-by-name`, the boxes named by their line number),
foot (the totals), notes, history, events (the changes since the page's newest, not its own tab's, in words), conflict (`live_conflict`).

rows of a document that is no longer a draft once they are older; a draft's rows stay however old (its History, its Undo).

its place; Cmd/Ctrl+S (and Enter in a box) saves the box the cursor is in. The supplier changed: a whole save after my saves (its lines move,

## Store Products' All leaves out the ignored products (branch `hide-ignored`, 20 Nov 2026; HI1-HI4; no migration)

The owner, 20 Nov 2026, of the three Vape and Go "Nic Nic" multipack pages, ignored in CW on purpose (since 4 Nov the shop sells them as
single shots): "why are we keeping it still in CW to confuse staff". He chose: hide the ignored products from CW's normal product list, and
show them only when someone picks "Ignored". CW does not delete the rows: the stores send every product every night, so a deleted row would
come back as "not matched". Built from main `286055a` in `/root/cw-hideignored`. No migration, no setting, no new permission; nothing in the
data is deleted or changed (the list reads one more condition). Code: `src/Ui/Queries.php` (`ALL_WHERE`, `storeAllCount()`, and
`storeProducts()`' new `ignored`), `src/Ui/Controller/StoreProductsController.php` (`ignoredLine()`, All's count, the class docblock), the view
`store_products`, `src/Ui/Words.php` (its marked HI2 block), `src/Ui/Controller/BulkController.php` (the batch page's way back, HI3). Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/HideIgnoredScreenTest.php` (red first:
`runs/hideign_red.log`); `BulkScreensTest` and `HideUnsoldScreenTest` changed where they listed an ignored product on All (it is now on
the Ignored choice).

**HI1. What All leaves out.** A website product whose state (`Queries::STORE_STATES`) is Ignored: status `ignored` and no decision waiting
for a second OK (a waiting one is "Waiting for a second OK" and stays on All). The same on every store; with or without a search, whatever
the search names (its exact store ID or barcode too: unlike HU4, the line of HI2 leads to it). All's count (`storeAllCount()`: the states'
counts minus Ignored), its pages and the search note count what it lists. The Ignored choice keeps its count, lists them, and keeps its tick
boxes and bulk actions (take off the ignored list). Left as they were: the store choice's figures (`productsByStore()`: every product of the
store), the "By store" overview, New Variants, To review, Find and the product's own page.

**HI2. One quiet line.** At the end of All, before the pager (after HU3's line when there is one): one plain paragraph
(`p.muted.ignored-line`, `data-ignored`): "3 ignored products are not shown here. Show them" (one: "1 ignored product is not shown here.
Show it"); nothing when none was left out, and never on another choice (no ignored product is in one). It counts what this search left out:
without a search the Ignored count; with one, the search's own one pass says of each id it finds whether it is Ignored (one more column, no
second pass, as HU3). "Show them" is the Ignored choice of the list as it is: the store, the sort, the search, and HU3's `unsold=1` when it
is on; page 1. When both apply there are two lines, each saying one thing with its one link (HU3's line is unchanged). All listing nothing
because everything was left out says "No website product to show here. The line below says which are not shown, and shows them." in place
of "This store has no website products." No filter chip, no help paragraph.

**HI3. With HU1-HU4, the bulk actions and StoreContext.** HU's hiding is unchanged: an ignored product was never hidden as "not sold in a
year" (HU2) and is never counted there; on All the two conditions are both applied; with HU3's "Show them" the ignored ones are still left
out and the line's link keeps `unsold=1`; the setting off changes nothing for them. StoreContext carries the state, so a row's Open from the
Ignored choice leads back to it (its search, at its row), and from All back to All. A bulk action's way back carries the list too: a refused
or confirmed request's (`BulkController::back`) as before, and now the batch page's as well (`BulkController::storeList`: the choice, the
sort, the search and the page travel in the batch page's address, as a match-strength list's `show` does, U140, and are read there as the
list reads them; a batch page opened with none of them, from Second approval, still leads to the store's All). Before, a batch done on the
Ignored choice led back to All, which now leaves them out. HU3's `unsold=1` is not carried (HU3: the way back is the quiet default). A
product ignored from All leaves All on the way back, and the line counts it; one taken off the ignored list from the Ignored choice is on
All again.

**HI4. Speed (EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the test machine: one store of 30,000 website products, 300 ignored, half first seen 400 days
ago; `runs/hideign_explain_before.txt` on `286055a`, `runs/hideign_explain_after.txt`).** All's condition (`ALL_WHERE`) reads the status
from the index the list already reads, and the OR stops at the status of every row that is not ignored: the waiting decision is looked up

`cl ref ix_channel_listing_unsold` "Using index" (30,000 index entries, the rows never read), `lp ref ix_listing_profile_units` "Using

condition MySQL chose the unique (store, option number) index instead, which is not covering (every listing row read: caught by

ix_channel_listing_unsold` "Using index"), with one more column. The Ignored choice: unchanged (`cl ref ix_channel_listing_status`,
status = 'ignored': 300 entries, 2 ms). All's total is still the three narrow counts (no COUNT of its own); the line's count is the Ignored

## Profit on every order, step 1: the money and the buying cost (branch `profit`, 19-20 Nov 2026; PR1-PR30; migration 0074)

The owner, 19 Nov 2026: "on each order, I just want to know how much is the percentage of profit actually that we are getting ... you know
how much we bought each for, and the rest have an average valuation ... We can copy ERP, that's okay. I don't want everything to be
copied", and "Yes" to build steps 1 and 2 on test CW. Built from /root/cw_work/profit_20261119/build/BRIEF_A_cw_step1.md and the agreed
contract build/CONTRACT.md (with its Changes 1-7, agreed by the lead on 20 Nov). Nothing goes to production without his separate go.

**PR1.** ONE snapshot per order (CONTRACT.md): the shop sends, per order, its money and its parcels as a whole picture; the latest replaces
the earlier one. `PUT /v1/orders/{ref}/snapshot`, the store's key, accepted in every store mode (it moves no stock, like `PUT /v1/listings`).
Answers: `stored`, `same` (the same content, whatever its version: the version is not content, so a newer version is only remembered),
`older_ignored` (an older version with other content); an equal version with other content is stored (last one wins: the shop's version is
the time of its read, two reads in the same millisecond are the only way). 400 `bad_snapshot` with `field`; 413 above 256 KB; 415 not JSON.

**PR2.** Only the contract's fields are kept (CW\Profit\SnapshotBody::parse returns the normalised body; `order_snapshot.body` is that, never
the raw request). An unknown field is ignored AND never stored, so no personal data can ride in on a field CW does not know. Ids are kept as
strings, times as UTC, money as integer pence inc VAT. `sub_of` (an office sub order, CONTRACT change 2) is kept and shown as a link; it is
its own sale. A line id that belongs to another order of the store is refused whole (400, its field).

**PR3.** One service (CW\Profit\OrderSnapshots) for the API, the bulk files (bin/import_order_snapshots.php: the connector's day files,
`.sum` checked, a wrong store's file refused, a refused line reported and the rest go on), the ERPNext import and the re-cost. One
transaction per order. A backfill and the live feed can never disagree (ProfitImportsTest compares them row for row).

**PR4.** ex VAT = inc / (1 + rate), rounded half away from zero; the rate is the setting `profit.vat_rate_pct` (20) and is kept on each order
when it is first stored (`sale_order.vat_bp`), so a later change of the setting does not move old orders. Delivery the same.

**PR5.** A line's sale = price - discount - refund. Coupons and points are a price cut (in the discount). A discount may be below 0 (CONTRACT
change 1: a coupon's rounding pennies), never below minus the line's price nor below -GBP 100 (refused otherwise).

**PR6.** A cancelled line counts nothing (no units, no sale, no cost). A free line counts its units and its cost, sale 0.

**PR7.** A refund kept on the order and not on a line (`order_refund_inc`) comes off the order's goods sold; the lists by product, brand and
supplier do not take it off (it is on no product), the day and the order do.

**PR8.** A re-send (`parent_ref`, CONTRACT change 2: the shop's ord_is_cloned) keeps its own row; its cost belongs to the first order: the
parent shows its re-sends and their cost, and its margin is worked out with them (`sale_order.resend_cost`, `margin_bp`), whichever of the two
CW stores first. In the day summaries the re-send's cost is on the day it was paid (the day the goods went: a closed month never moves), and
it is not counted as an order (`resends` instead).

**PR9.** A unit that came back to stock in CW (its reservation unit is `returned`) has no cost, and no sale when it was refunded. The return
may reach CW after the snapshot, and the shop need not send again: CW\Profit\ReturnsSweep (with the cost job) finds the returns booked since
its mark and works those orders out again from the stored snapshot.

**PR10.** An order counts when it has a paid time, on the UK day of it (`sale_order.day`); an unpaid one counts nothing (its lines are kept,
no cost fixed). The shop sends it once it is paid and then on every change (CONTRACT change 6). An "order" in the figures is a paid order
with at least one unit that counts and no parent.

**PR11.** Margin = profit / goods sold ex VAT (none when nothing was sold). Delivery charged ex VAT is income shown on its own line; what
delivery costs comes in step 2. Parcels (`sale_parcel`) are kept for step 2: a parcel missing from a newer snapshot gets `removed_at`, never
deleted; "orl:" parcels are the shop's Royal Mail return labels of that order (CONTRACT change 4).

**PR12.** The buying price of each CW item is its own table (`item_cost`, every move in `item_cost_event`), a moving average that follows
the invoices ("invoice price wins", the owner, 15 Oct). Nothing of report_item, the stock ledger, CostHints or any stock screen changes. It
starts at `profit.cost_start` (16 Nov 2026, midnight UK: the day purchases moved to CW and ERPNext's valuation froze) from ERPNext's own
valuation (Bin.valuation_rate; item_code "P" + the Vape and Go variant, the CW item through that store's match, a pack's rate divided by its
units; several warehouses weighted by their quantity, by their plain average when none holds stock); the rates erp_opening.placeholder_costs
names (0 and 1) are placeholders, as for the opening (PI5). Else CW's average so far (report_item), else the supplier's last price (the
newest ERPNext purchase invoice copy line, else the supplier item's price, else its last order price), else none.

**PR13.** Then, in time order: a goods receipt's goods_in rows move the average with their own unit price ex VAT (pack price / units);
units on hand = every warehouse of ours as the ledger stood just before (below zero: the receipt's price). A receipt of a final invoice's goods
that were on their way ("count on arrival", pack J) comes in at that invoice's landed price. A receipt taken back takes its units out at the
price they came in at (the average unchanged when nothing, or less than nothing, would be left).

**PR14.** A supplier invoice made final: each goods line's landed price = its amount plus its share of the invoice's carriage, duty, service
and other lines spread over its goods lines BY VALUE (the brief; `invoices.duty_spread` stays the value engine's setting), per unit. For the
units it bills that are still on hand it replaces the price they came in at (the receipt's, or an earlier invoice's for that delivery line).
A credit note that answers our return (it has a debit note) moves nothing (those units left at the average); any other credit note lowers the
units still on hand by what it credits. A reversal of either undoes its moves on the units still on hand. A copy of an ERPNext purchase
invoice never moves it (its stock came through the relay; the start holds ERPNext's valuation). Every other movement (sales, counts,
adjustments, the 130,206 units ERPNext relayed without a cost, returns) comes in or goes out at the price of the moment, which leaves the
average where it is.

**PR15.** bin/refresh_item_cost.php every 10 minutes (setting `profit.cost_refresh_on`): reads deliveries (the ledger) and invoices (posted
documents) from its mark less 10 minutes, up to 2 minutes ago, in time order; each event its own small transaction, written once
(`source_key` UNIQUE): restartable, and a booking committed late is still found. Never inside a booking's transaction. An event's time is
never before the item's previous event (moved up to it), so the price at a moment reads one history.

**PR16.** The cost of a sale line is fixed ONCE: the first time the line is stored on a paid order, the item's price at the paid time
(ItemCosts::at), with `cost_source` (erp_at_sale, cw_cost, estimate, none), `costed_by` (sale) and `cost_at`. Later snapshots keep it, and
the line's CW item is fixed with it (the unit's own item at the sale from reservation_unit, else the listing's link then). Only two
deliberate commands change a fixed cost: the ERPNext history import (costed_by erp_import) and bin/recost_sales.php (costed_by recost; a
line with no item takes its listing's link now). `cost_source` keeps the brief's four values; who changed it is `costed_by`.

**PR17.** Grants: item_cost_event APPEND_ONLY; order_snapshot, sale_order, sale_line, sale_parcel, item_cost and profit_job NO_DELETE;
profit_day and profit_item_day FULL (a batch rebuilds a day).

**PR18.** ERPNext's history (bin/import_erp_sales_cost.php, files si_<day>.tsv or .tsv.gz of the read-only export, read line by line, one
day in memory): for an invoice of an order CW holds (custom_order_id = the order ref), paid before `profit.cost_start`, each line of a
variant gets ERPNext's incoming_rate (several rows of one variant weighted by quantity; per CW unit: / the line's units per item), source
erp_at_sale. A rate of 0 is not taken. Run again: the same costs. Orders paid on or after the cost start keep CW's price (ERPNext's cost is
frozen since 16 Nov).

**PR19.** One reconciliation line per day: ERPNext's orders, goods net and cost at sale, CW's orders and goods sold ex VAT for the same orders,
the lines costed, ERPNext lines with no CW line, orders not in CW, orders paid after the cost start, unpaid in CW, returns (count and net:
reported, not applied), invoices with no order id, variants whose rate is 0.

**PR20.** `profit.erp_history_from` (15 Dec 2025): the first day ERPNext holds a cost at each sale. A sale between it and the cost start that
the import has not reached yet carries the item's starting price as an `estimate`.

**PR21.** Before ERPNext's history: `profit.before_history` = estimate (today's price, marked estimate; the default) or none (the owner's one
switch). Read when the line's cost is fixed.

**PR22.** The day summaries (`profit_day` per store and UK day, `profit_item_day` per store, day and item; sku 0 = no CW item) are kept by the
same transaction that stores a snapshot, by the difference between what the order counted before and now (row increments in key order: no
lost update, no deadlock cycle), and rebuilt from sale_order and sale_line by bin/rebuild_profit_days.php with the SAME definition
(ProfitDays::orderShare); the tests check they agree after every kind of change.

**PR23.** The new job `finance` (0074: at the end of the staff_role ENUM, number 16) holds the new permission `profit.view`, and the two
every job has (catalogue.view, reference.view: LOCKED, so the code gives them whatever 0034's rows say). Nobody holds it by default and it is
not in the "all" list of the staff log-in tool: the owner says who (bin/grant_role.php or Settings > Users). The Profit section (Reports'
chart icon, green) is shown only to it.

**PR24.** Profit summary: today, yesterday, the last 7 and 30 days, this month and last month (UK days), all shops or one: orders, goods
sold, buying cost, profit, margin, delivery charged, and the units with no buying price (a link to that list for the period).

**PR25.** Profit by day: the reports' periods (or From / To, at most `reports.sales_max_days`), day by day, week by week (from Monday) or month
by month, newest first, with the total.

**PR26.** Profit by product: by shop, product, brand or main supplier (the item's preferred supplier item), the biggest first by profit,
goods sold, cost, units, or margin (highest or lowest first); at most 300 rows. From profit_item_day.

**PR27.** Profit by order: the paid orders of the period and shop, newest first or the lowest margin first (`sale_order.margin_bp`, index
(day, margin_bp)); or the orders with the number typed, any day (the shop's order id per store on the key, or the reference the customer
sees). Each order's page: its money, every line (sale ex VAT, the cost of one unit and where it came from, cost, profit, margin; cancelled,
free, back in stock, no longer on the order), its parcels, its re-sends, the order it is a re-send or a sub order of.

**PR28.** No buying price: the products sold in the period whose units have no price (cost_source none, counting, not back in stock), their
units and what those units sold for, from sale_line by (day, cost_source); a link to the product's page; a website product with no CW item by
its number.

**PR29.** Not built here: delivery cost and carrier invoices (step 2, on top of this branch: the parcels are stored), card fees and other
expenses, the connector (builder B), anything sent to a shop, any change to stock, reservations, documents or an existing screen's numbers.

**PR30.** Go-live order on live (README of build/A): migrate 0074; bin/seed_item_cost.php --bin (dry run, then --apply: the start and the
replay since 16 Nov); the connector's bulk days through bin/import_order_snapshots.php; bin/import_erp_sales_cost.php (dry run, then
--apply); bin/recost_sales.php for what is left without a price; bin/rebuild_profit_days.php as a check; then the cron lines. Undo: the

### The Codex review of 92efa82 (three focused runs at once, `build/A/codex_r1_{a,b,c}.txt`): 4 HIGH and 30 MEDIUM, each checked in the code, shown failing first (`runs/profit_r1fix_red1.log`, `red2.log`) and fixed (PR31-PR45)

**PR31.** (a1/b1, HIGH) A sale's cost is fixed only once the cost job has read up to its paid time (`ItemCosts::reached`, the job's mark):
before that the line stays open (`cost_source` NULL with a day: "waiting for its cost"), and `CW\Profit\PendingCosts` (run by
bin/refresh_item_cost.php after each cost run, and by the start) fixes it at the price of the paid time. A delivery booked a minute before a
sale is in that sale's cost. Before the start was ever written every paid line waits. The screens say when units wait (at most ~10 minutes).

**PR32.** (a2, HIGH) An invoice line on a delivery line moves its own units from the price THEY came in at (the receipt's), never from an
earlier invoice's price of other units of the same delivery line: two invoices of 50 units each of one 100-unit line each move their own 50.

**PR33.** (a3, HIGH) An invoice or credit event records the units it really reached (on hand then, 0 when none); its reversal undoes what it
really moved a unit (its value change over those units), on the units still on hand: an invoice that moved nothing is undone by nothing.

**PR34.** (a4) A relative move (a credit, a reversal) on an item whose price nobody knows leaves it unknown (`ProfitMath::shift`); only an
invoice's landed price (an absolute price) gives an unknown item a price.

**PR35.** (a5) A price credit of an invoice whose goods are still on their way (no delivery named, none received from it yet) moves nothing
then (`deferred`); the receipt of those goods comes in at the invoice's landed price less that credit (unless the credit was cancelled
before); a cancellation after the receipt undoes it on the units still on hand.

**PR36.** (a6) Every event keeps its source's own time (`source_at`); an event older than the item's last one (a booking committed late)
triggers a replay: the item's history folded again in source order with the same rule (`ProfitMath::step`, `fold`), and a `replay` event when
that gives another price. (b2) The job reads back an hour (OVERLAP_SECONDS 3600) and leaves the last 5 minutes (LAG_SECONDS 300).

**PR37.** (b3) The job never reads before the start (`profit_job.floor_at`): a delivery before the start is inside ERPNext's valuation.
(b4) A start stopped half way is run again the same way and goes on with the items not written yet; it is refused only once the job has
its mark. (b5) An item made after the start gets its starting price on the next run (CW's average, else the supplier's price, else none),
from when it was made.

**PR38.** (a13) A receipt made from a final invoice finds that invoice from what never changes (goods_receipt_invoice, both documents'
lines of the item in line order), not from the arrival row a later reversal of the receipt opens again; only an invoice final before the
receipt counts. The start resolves ERPNext's item codes exactly as the opening import (ErpItemResolver: CW's ERPNext link first, else the
variant through the store's match; RB10).

**PR39.** (a7/b10/c1, HIGH in c) Every write of an order's figures first locks its day's summary row (ProfitDays::guard: the day it counted
on and the day it counts on, before any row of the order), and a rebuild locks it before it reads the day: a rebuild never drops a snapshot
committed meanwhile. (a8/b8/b9) Every write of an order holds a named lock of the order (OrderSnapshots::lockName) and of the order it is (or
was) a re-send of, in name order, 10 s at most (else 503 busy, retried by the store): a re-send and its first order, and two first snapshots
of one order, never interleave.

**PR40.** (b6) A line id that is a unit of another order's reservation in CW is refused (400, its field). (b7) A line id another order stored
at the same moment is never taken over: the upsert never changes a line's order, and the snapshot is refused whole when a line is another
order's. (b20) An older version is `older_ignored` whatever its content. (b12) A tracking number is kept only when it is one (CONTRACT
change 5: A-Z a-z 0-9, space . / # _ -, at least 4 digits; CW adds: a digit in every word); anything else is kept as null. (a12, b18) The
margin, units and units-without-price columns are BIGINT.

**PR41.** (a9/b17) ERPNext's rows of one order are taken together over every day file it is on (two passes; an order is applied on its last
day). (a10) A variant with a row at a rate of 0 keeps what it had. (b16) A day file with a row that is not whole, or a number that is not
one, is refused whole and named; nothing of it is applied. (b19) The folder is read as it is named (scandir, never a glob pattern).

**PR42.** (a11/b11) The re-cost and the ERPNext import work their costs out under the order's locks from what is stored then (a line an
import fixed meanwhile is no longer of the re-cost's sources; an order no longer paid before the cost start is left).

**PR43.** (b13/b14/b15) A bulk file proves its store before anything is written: its name is snapshots_<store>_<day>.jsonl and names the
store asked for; its .sum is there, whole, of the same store and day; the file is read twice (checked, then stored); a .sum that does not
match (its sha256; its totals when every line could be read) writes nothing. A line longer than the cap is one refused line, drained to
its end.

**PR44.** (c2) Profit by order pages by a cursor (the last row's paid time or margin, store and order ref) on ix_sale_order_paid /
ix_sale_order_store_paid / ix_sale_order_margin: a page reads its own rows. The lowest margin first leaves out orders with no sale.
(c3) The No buying price list reads ix_sale_line_cost (cost_source, day). (c4) Shops are ranked by the figures their rows show (the
order-level refunds taken off). (c5) A website product with no CW item is its own store's row. (c6) A figure with units with no price, or
units waiting for their cost, says "incomplete" (and why); the order's page says it too. (c7) The lists by product, brand and supplier say
how much order-level refund they leave out. (c8) The payment way in words.

**PR45.** Not changed: the lists by product, brand and supplier over a long period still add up every item-day row of it (about a million
rows a year): a year's list takes a second or two; a month-level summary can come later if it is slow on live.
