whose first delivery (ten at £1.00, the supplier's price £3.00) was booked before that time but committed after the run: £1.00 (it was
£3.00: the start folded after the delivery reset it), and the invoice to £2.00 after it: £2.00 (it was £3.00 + £1.00).

**PR73.** (a: late credit, taken-back receipts, overflow, rounding; a5/N1 PARTLY) A credit of an invoice line is "of goods on their way"
as of ITS OWN time: no receipt standing then had taken the line in. When the goods came after it but their receipt was read first (the
credit's booking committed late), the receipt was priced without it: the credit comes off those receipts' units as they came (one
non-deferred credit event at the receipt's time, by what it would have taken off each unit): ten at £4.00, £1.00 a unit credited before
they came, read after their receipt: £3.00 (it stayed £4.00). A receipt taken back no longer takes a credit in, nor counts in its undo:
ten at £4.00 on the shelf, ten more received at £3.00 (a credit of £10.00), taken back, received again, the credit cancelled: £4.00 (it
was £4.50: the taken-back receipt was undone too). The undo of a credit is what it really took off a unit of each receipt: the receipt's
price without it less its price with it, worked out as the receipt worked it out (ProfitMath::receiptPrice; CostEngine::creditShare): a
penny credited on 200 units at £1.00 (the receipt stays at £1.0000, half away from zero) is undone by nothing (it added £0.0001 a unit: £200.02);
100,000 units credited £1.00 each are undone exactly (the old product of four numbers went past a 64-bit integer and stopped the job).

**PR74.** (a: over-delivery; a13 PARTLY) Units a receipt line brought beyond what its invoice lines bill come in at the receipt's own price;
the price of the line = (the invoice lines' landed value of the units they gave - their credits on those units + the units beyond x the
receipt's price) / every unit that came. Two lines of 10 at £4.00 (a credit of £10.00 on line 2), 30 came at £4.00: £110.00 / 30 = £3.6667
(it was £3.50 on all 30: £105.00).

**PR75.** (a: R3/a3 PARTLY) A moment never cuts a stock operation in two: the units on hand at a moment count an operation with a row up to
it whole (its rows booked just after it too, within LAG_SECONDS), and "the fewest on hand since" counts an operation begun before its start
whole at the start and one begun before its end whole (CostEngine::onHandAt, lowestOnHandSince, opRows): 20 on hand, ten moved between two
of our rooms, a moment between the transfer's two rows: 20 (it was 10).

**PR76.** (b: S1, S2; c6/PR54/PR61 PARTLY) An order's page says "not known" exactly when units lack a price: its profit when its OWN units
lack one (whatever it sold for: a free unit with no price is a loss not known, never £0.00), its profit with its re-sends when its own or
a paid re-send's units lack one (never the sum as if known); its own profit is shown when only a re-send's price is missing (ProfitViews::
order: own_incomplete, resends_incomplete). The No buying price page says when units still wait for their cost and never says "every product
sold in these days has a buying price" while they wait (Words PROFIT no_cost_waiting).

**PR77.** (c) bin/import_erp_sales_cost.php ends with exit 1 when a day file was refused (nothing applied), so a go-live step that checks the
exit code stops; bin/seed_item_cost.php run again after the start was written (stopped before its replay) goes on with the replay and the
sales that waited instead of refusing.

**PR78.** Left as they are (said in the README; open questions there): the mark is not held back while documents older than the job's
window are unread (a1/b1: a sale's cost is fixed once, PR16; a booking committed more than an hour late moves the price from its own time on,
and the sales costed meanwhile keep theirs until bin/recost_sales.php); the lists by product, brand and supplier over a long period read every
item-day row of it (PR45, PR56); the staff log-in tool's "all" list is outside the build (it was checked not to name finance).

### The Codex check of 51417a3 (`build/A/codex_r6.txt`, one run): r5's eleven checked (8 FIXED, 3 PARTLY); no HIGH; 3 MEDIUM and 3 LOW new; each shown failing first with Codex's own numbers on 51417a3 (`runs/profit_r6fix_red.log`) and fixed (PR79-PR82)

**PR79.** (M1, M2, M3, L5; r5a 2 PARTLY; the coordinator's direction of 20 Nov) An item's price history in force is ALWAYS in time order. An
event the cost job meets that is older than the item's last one (a booking that committed late, one the look back recovered, the
cancellation of one) is never put in at its place, shifted to a receipt's time or adjusted in place: the item's whole history is written
again from its start, in time order, as its next timeline (item_cost.timeline, item_cost_event.timeline; CostEngine::rebuild): every
delivery, invoice, credit note and cancellation the item had, and the late one, each worked out again by the SAME rules as an event read in
order (its units on hand, whether a credit's goods were still on their way, what a receipt took in, what a cancellation undoes, all as of its
own time). The earlier timeline is kept (append only); the start comes first (moved just before the first event when it was not). An item
has few events since 16 Nov, so writing it again is cheap. The late-credit branch of PR73 is gone (a late credit is a late event). Numbers
(Codex's): a credit and its cancellation before the goods came, read after their receipt: £40.00 (it was £30.00); a credit read late whose
receipt is taken back and made again: £30.00 (it was £40.00); a credit read late on a receipt in two portions gives what reading it in time
gives: £0.9967 (it was £0.9968); a 1p credit read late on 100 units when 100 were on the shelf at £0.9999: £199.98 (it was £200.00). The
`late` flag and the `replay` event of PR36/PR60/PR69 are gone: the price at a moment is the last event up to it in the timeline in force,
one indexed read (FORCE INDEX ix_item_cost_event_item: MySQL took a table scan for a moment after every event).

**PR80.** (r5a 5 PARTLY) Units on hand are read in each item's commit order (stock_value_seq: an item's on-hand rows are numbered in the
order they were made final, all rows of one operation together): the units at a moment = every operation made final by then (its seq rows
are made at its end), whole; "the fewest on hand since" walks the seq rows between two places, looking only between operations; an operation
cut by a place (rows of one operation made by several statements) is carried to its end by its identity (CostEngine::opEnd), never by a
time pad. A delivery's own "units on hand before it" is read at its place in the commit order too (its operation's earlier rows included: a
receipt's second portion averages with its first). A transfer that took six minutes is whole at every moment (20 on hand, never 10). Where a
cancellation of a credit looks "since its receipt came", it starts after that receipt's whole operation (its last portion's place).

**PR81.** (L4) The undo of a credit is worked out against the credits of the line still standing when it is cancelled (those cancelled
before gave their own rounding back already): 400 units at £1.00 with credits of 2p and 1p (£0.9999), the 2p cancelled (£1.0000), the 1p
cancelled: £1.0000, £400.00 (it was £400.04).

**PR82.** (L6) A line waits for its buying price only when it has one to wait for: units that count and not back in stock. A line refunded
in full whose unit came back to stock has a cost of zero, known: its order's profit is £0.00, never "not known" (ProfitViews::order, the
re-sends' figures, the waiting units of every list, and the order's margin in OrderSnapshots::refreshParent).

### The lead's real-data test of 51417a3 on CW staging (a copy of live CW, 50 real Vape and Go day files, 1 Oct - 19 Nov 2026, 65,363 orders): 4 orders refused (PR83)

**PR83.** (CONTRACT.md change 8) The shapes the shop really stores are taken: a line's price may be below 0 down to -£1.00
(SnapshotBody::MAX_NEGATIVE_PRICE: spread remainders of -2p / -3p next to free lines; 10 such lines since ord_id 1,500,000, the lowest -3p),
and its discount below 0 down to minus (its price + £1.00), never below -£100 (change 1; a coupon's remainder of -99p on a 49p line beside
lines discounted 1p each; 1 such line). Before, the 4 orders holding them were refused whole (400 bad_snapshot) and vanished from the
profit. The money stays exact, line by line: goods = price - discount - refund, ex VAT at the order's rate. £12.99 with two free lines and
two lines of -2p: £12.95 inc VAT, £10.79 ex VAT (£10.83 - 2p - 2p); four 49p lines less 1p and one 49p line less -99p: £3.40 inc VAT, £2.83
ex VAT (4 x 40p + £1.23) (ProfitSnapshotShapesTest). A price below -£1.00, or a discount below minus (price + £1.00), is still refused, with
its field. The bulk test's refused example is now a price of -£1.01 (its -5p is a real shape since change 8).

### The lead's look at the screens on real data (51417a3 on a copy of live CW, 50 real days; PR84, PR85)

**PR84.** An order's page shows its lines as one row per product (its CW item, else its website number), cost of one unit, where the cost
came from and state (cancelled, free, back in stock, refunded, no longer on the order): its units counted, goods sold, cost and profit added
up and its margin from those sums (ProfitViews::grouped; Words PROFIT refunded). An order of 20 identical units shows one row of 20, not 20
rows; the rows add up to the order's own units, goods sold and cost exactly (21 units, £24.00, £10.50 in the test: 19 sold, 1 refunded but
not back in stock, 1 cancelled, 1 of another product).

**PR85.** Summed figures (the summary, by day / week / month, by shop / product / brand / supplier) say "incomplete" only when the units with
no buying price or still waiting for one are more than 0.5% of their units (more than 1 in 200: ProfitViews::INCOMPLETE_PER, incomplete());
the No price count column always shows the count. The units rule was chosen over a share of goods because both counts are on every row (no
estimate needed) and it is the one the list's sort can use in SQL: a list by margin ranks a row as incomplete by the same rule (1 unit in
1,000 without a price no longer pushes a 60% product after a 50% one). 5 of 1,000: not said; 6 of 1,000: said; 1 of 400 on a day: the count
1, no "incomplete"; 3 of 400: "incomplete". One order is still incomplete with any unit without a price (its margin is not known).

### The Codex check of 3f1b54e (`build/A/codex_r7.txt`, one run): r6's findings and r5a 2/5 FIXED; no HIGH; 2 MEDIUM new and 1 LOW left; each shown failing first with Codex's numbers on a copy of 1179112 (`runs/profit_r7fix_red.log`) and fixed (PR86-PR88)

**PR86.** (M1) A delivery's time in the price history is when its units were on hand: when its operation was made final (its seq row's
time, stock_value_seq), the same clock "units on hand at a moment" reads; the booking's own time stays in the ledger. A delivery booked at
10:00 and made final at 10:02 with a credit of the earlier ten at 10:01: the credit sees the ten on hand (to £0), then the ten at £3.00
come in: £30.00 for twenty, £1.50 each (it was £1.00: the credit saw ten units while the history already held twenty). The job's mark stops
a microsecond short of the first delivery not read by that same time (PR47).

**PR87.** (M2) A moment long ago is read without the history after it: an item's place in its commit order at a moment is a binary search on
stock_value_seq's primary key (its rows' times only grow; a few point reads), an operation's end is found reading one row and then more,
and the units on hand at a place read each of our warehouses that ever held the item back from the last ledger row booked by then (a row up
to that place was booked before it was made final). On a 300-row history a moment after the 10th row reads under 150 rows (it read 979).
A rebuild's events count against the run's event limit.

**PR88.** (r5a 7 LOW) Credits given while goods were on their way are kept per credit-note line, so one credit note of two lines of the same
invoice line is undone line by line against what still stands: 400 units at £1.00 with one note of 1p and 2p (£0.9999), the note cancelled:
£1.0000, £400.00 (it was £399.96).

### The Codex check of 1179112..e1f075c (`build/A/codex_r8.txt`, one run, the last build round): no HIGH; 5 MEDIUM and 3 LOW new, 3 PARTLY; each shown failing first with Codex's numbers on e1f075c (`runs/profit_r8fix_red.log`, `red2.log`) and fixed (PR89-PR93); what is left is a known limit in the README

**PR89.** (M1; the lead: "the mark must never pass an unread document") The job's mark never passes its cutoff (a delivery is stamped when its
stock was made final, which can be after the cutoff: what came between was not read), and never passes a document not read yet: every run's
look back now reads the documents not read whole since the start (the oldest first, up to UNREAD_PER_RUN; the day bound is gone, the same
index range as the window's own read), and while one is left before the window the mark stays just before it (never going back). Three
deliveries committed after the window passed them, one read a run: the mark waits, then moves on once all are read (£2.00). The look back
waits for the next run once a run has written its limit. Left (a known limit): a booking whose transaction commits more than LAG_SECONDS (5
minutes) after its own time can be passed before it is visible; its item's history is written again when it is read, and the sales costed
meanwhile keep their cost until bin/recost_sales.php.

**PR90.** (M2, M3) Everything that compares a delivery with other events uses when its stock was made final (stock_value_seq): a new item's
first delivery and the priced stock that came in before it (ten at £2.00 made final before a delivery of ten at £3.00 booked earlier: the
item starts at £2.00, £2.50 after the delivery; it was £2.00), and a receipt taken back stops taking credits only when its stock leaves (a
credit between the reversal's booking and its being made final comes off the twenty still on hand: £3.50, then the ten leave at £4.00:
£30.00 for ten; it was £40.00).

**PR91.** (M4, M5, M2 PARTLY) The units on hand at a place of an item's commit order are exact: the sum of our warehouses' on-hand rows of its
seq rows, walked from the nearest place known (nothing before the first; today's balances at the last, read in one consistent statement;
every place worked out before by the engine), never bounded by ledger ids or booking times (ten booked, on hand, whatever the ids: 10, it
read 0). A rebuild reads its events in time order, so its walks add up to the item's history about once. A moment's place takes the rows
just after the binary search's answer whose clock says they were made final by then (a clock stepped back: 30, it read 10). Left (a known
limit): a clock stepped back across more than 64 bookings of one item.

**PR92.** (LOW 1, the multi-line PARTLY) A credit line counts as cancelled only by the cancellation of its own line, so the lines of one note
cancelled one after the other each give back their own part against what still stands (a note of 1p, 3p, 3p and a note of 4p on 400 units
at £1.00, the first note cancelled: £0.9999, £399.96; it gave £400.00). (LOW 2) A rebuild's rows are counted once in the run (5, it said 6).

**PR93.** (LOW 3) Units waiting for their cost are counted on every summed row ("+1 waiting for their cost" beside the No price count), also
when they are too few to say "incomplete" (PR85).

### The final review of 6d59eda (three read-only runs of gpt-6.2-astra: `build/A/codex_final_astra_{a,b,c}.txt`; production safety, security and data, money): 7 HIGH (two the same), each checked in the code; every HIGH and the MEDIUMs below shown failing first with the reviewers' numbers on 6d59eda (`runs/profit_r9fix_red.log`, `red2.log`; the undo on the CW test box with c40c050's own code: `runs/profit_r9_rollback_rehearsal.log`) and fixed (PR94-PR112); what is left is a known limit in the README

**PR94.** (a-HIGH1 / b-HIGH1, the undo) Once 0074 (and 0075, PR95) are recorded, the code of the release before refuses the schema: its CLI
guard (Cli::requireCurrentSchema, every cron job: the reservation expiry stops with exit 3) and its installer's `bin/migrate.php --status`
("schema has migration 0074_profit.sql but no such file exists"), shown with c40c050's own code on a scratch schema of the test box. The guard
stays strict (a schema with migrations the code does not know is refused; accepting "later" migrations would let old code run on a schema it
may not understand). The undo is a ROLLBACK RELEASE prepared before the go-live: c40c050's code with migrations/0074_profit.sql and
migrations/0075_profit_queue.sql added byte for byte, no code: the same schema check then passes (the rehearsal: expiry exit 0, invariants ok,
migrate --status nothing pending), the installer switches to it without --migrate, and its cron file has no profit job. It is made by the
go-live kit (README of build/A, "Undo": the exact commands), as a commit on main whose tree is c40c050's plus the two files, pushed and
installed the normal way, or in an emergency by switching /opt/cw-prod to a release directory built the same way on the box.
`tests/Integration/Profit/RollbackReleaseTest.php` holds the recipe to the branch: every migration this branch adds after 0073 is in its list, and
with exactly those files a schema migrated by this release passes the old guard, without them it is refused.

**PR95.** (a-HIGH2, checkout isolation; b-LOW1) `PUT /v1/orders/{ref}/snapshot` only STORES: OrderSnapshots::accept checks the body, refuses a
line of another order by reads that lock nothing, and in ONE short transaction under the order's own intake lock (`cw_profit_in:`, never the
money work's guard) writes order_snapshot and its row in the new `order_snapshot_queue` (0075: one row per order whose latest snapshot is not
worked out; `seq` moves on with each one stored). No day summary, no cost read, no row of sale_order / sale_line / profit_day is touched, so a
store's checkout, whose stock calls share the ten PHP workers, never waits behind the money work. The money work is the new job
bin/apply_order_snapshots.php (cron every minute; at most 2,000 orders or about 45 seconds a run; one transaction per order under its guards,
as before): it reads the queue row's seq and the stored body in ONE read and takes the row away only while its seq is still that one (a newer
snapshot stored meanwhile keeps it for the next run). A snapshot the work refuses (a line another order stored at the same moment) is marked
on its row (failed, the reason) and never tried again until a newer snapshot of the order comes; `--status` lists the waiting and the refused.
The money work never locks order_snapshot (recompute reads it without FOR UPDATE: the guards keep the money writers apart). OrderSnapshots::store
(the bulk files, the tests) is accept and the order's money work at once (and the money work of a snapshot that waited). The items' cost at
the paid time is read in one statement per 500 items (a dependent indexed read per item, then their prices by id): 1,000 items are about five
statements, not 2,001 (the red log). The 256 KB cap is kept before the body is read (Request::body($max): a declared length over it is refused
unread, never more than 256 KB + 1 byte read). The reviewer's other remedy, workers kept for the stock calls, is the server's pool and left as it
is: nothing of the snapshot holds a worker beyond its milliseconds now.

**PR96.** (b-HIGH2, personal data) No free text is kept from a snapshot. Ids and refs (line, variant, parent, sub order, parcel, the path's
order) are codes (letters, digits and : _ . -, at most 64; anything else is refused: they are keys). The order number is a number with a few
letters before it at most (the real files: "1567469"), else "". The delivery method id is digits, the service code a code with no run of 7
digits, else null / "". The order's and the parcels' status, the payment way and the carrier are words of fixed lists, else "other". A
delivery method or service name is kept only when every word of it is one of the carriers' service words (SnapshotBody::SERVICE_WORDS, from
the real names: "Royal Mail Tracked 48 (2-4 Working Days)", "DPD Pickup (2 day Service)", "In Store Collection Preston", "EVRI International",
"Return label") or a short number, else null / "": a name, an e-mail address, a phone number or a postal address can never be stored, whatever
a connector maps into a field. A parcel gone from a newer snapshot keeps its codes and times and no text (its service name is cleared).

**PR97.** (c-M1) A shop line is ONE unit: the connector sends one orders_items row per unit (`qty: 1` always); any other qty is refused
(400 lines[i].qty), so a restock of one unit of a two-unit line can never erase the whole line's sale and cost.

**PR98.** (a-M4, b-M) bin/import_order_snapshots.php that finds another import holding the job's lock reads nothing and ends with exit 4 (new
Cli::BUSY: "not run, run it again"), never 0. bin/refresh_item_cost.php --reconcile (the night's full read) waits up to 15 minutes for a run of
every ten minutes that holds the lock instead of being skipped; still held: exit 4.

**PR99.** (c-HIGH1, a-M5, b-HIGH3: the start) The start is followed by the replay of every delivery, invoice and credit note since it, so no
starting price may hold one of them. CostEngine::plan takes the start's moment (bin/seed_item_cost.php always gives it): ERPNext's Bin first;
else CW's own average of what came in with a price BEFORE the start (the commit order, stock_value_seq), never today's report_item; else the
supplier's last price known before the start (an ERPNext purchase invoice posted before its day, a supplier item's price or order price dated
before it); else none until the item's first priced delivery. 10 at £1 before the start and 10 at £3 after it: £2.00 (it was £2.50 from a
£2.00 opening). Every input is of before the start, so a seed stopped half way prices its later batches as its first. The Bin file is checked
whole first: a row without the header's columns, or whose quantity or valuation is blank or not a number, is broken; while one is broken and
not named by --allow-skips (its item code, or row:<n>) nothing is written, in the dry run too, and the tool ends with exit 1 naming every row.

**PR100.** (c-HIGH2, a-M6) An invoice moves only the units of the delivery it bills that can still be on hand: at most the fewest units on hand
since that delivery came, in the item's commit order (the receipt's last portion's operation to the invoice's place, as the reversals already
do). A price credit the same, for the delivery its invoice line billed (or the receipts that took goods on their way in). 10 at £1 sold out,
10 at £3, the first ten's invoice at £2: £3.00 (it was £4.00); a 50p credit of the first ten after they sold out, 10 at £4 on hand: £4.00 (it
was £3.50); 4 of the first ten left: only those four move (£2.7143, it was £3.1429). The same rule in an item's history written again.

**PR101.** (b-M, b-LOW) The snapshot's shapes: paid_at must be sent (null when not paid): a body without it is refused, never read as "not
paid" (which took a paid sale off its day); `lines` and `parcels` must be JSON lists and `delivery` an object or null (`"lines": {}` decoded
like `[]` and took every line off the order: SnapshotBody::checkJsonShapes, in the API and the bulk files); a line id (or parcel ref) in
another case is the same line, as the database's key compares (L1 and l1: refused, never two lines in the order and one row); a time must carry
its zone (Z or an offset): a London time without one is never read as UTC.

**PR102.** (c-HIGH3, c-M10) Profit by order shows each order's OWN goods, cost and profit (what the day summaries count: a re-send's cost on
the re-send's row and paid day), so the rows of a period add up to its day summary exactly (a parent £10 and £3, its free re-send £3: rows
£6 cost and £4 profit, as the day; they added up to £9 and £1). A first order also shows its re-sends' cost and its profit with them (the
detail page's own labels), and its margin stays the agreed one, with them (PR10). A profit that is not known (a unit of the order, or of a paid
re-send for the figure with them, has no price or waits for one) is "not known", never a number (£10 shown for an order with an unpriced unit);
a fully refunded parent with an unpriced re-send is incomplete.

**PR103.** (c-M9) Each Profit page reads its figures and its waiting units from ONE moment of the database (ProfitDays::snapshot: CW\Ops\Snapshot's
REPEATABLE READ, CONSISTENT SNAPSHOT, READ ONLY; nested reads join it): a cost fixed between two reads never shows a complete 100% margin.

**PR104.** (c-LOW4, a-M8) bin/rebuild_profit_days.php compares by default (and with --check): every figure of a day or an item whose kept
summary differs from what its orders add up to is printed with both values, nothing is written, exit 1 when one differs; --apply writes (the
nightly cron line has it). The go-live "check" (README step 6) writes nothing.

**PR105.** (c-LOW1) An order-level refund comes off the lines' sale ex VAT in proportion to their own rounded amounts: refunding everything the
lines sold takes their ex-VAT sale off exactly (ten 99p lines: 830p, it left 5p); what is beyond the lines' sale comes off at the order's rate.

**PR106.** (b-M) An import whose .sum file matches but has a refused line says "totals NOT CHECKED" apart from the file's match (it said
".sum matches"); the exit stays 1.

**PR107.** (c-M3) The cost job and the returns sweep read the window by the booking time alone (ix_stock_ledger_created), never from the id of
the window's first row: a row given an earlier id but a later time is read in its own run.

**PR108.** (c-M4) An invoice's charges over goods lines all worth nothing are spread by units (10 free samples and £20 freight: £2 a unit; the
£20 was lost); by value otherwise, as before.

**PR109.** (c-M5) The VAT setting: "5.0000" is 5% when read (trailing zeros after two decimals are the same percent; it fell back to 20%), and
the settings tool checks it as a percent with at most two decimals and keeps it without trailing zeros ("5").

**PR110.** (c-M6, c-M7, c-M8, b-M, a-LOW) ERPNext's cost at the sale: a variant is taken only when CW's lines of it that count hold exactly the
units ERPNext priced (two CW units against one ERPNext unit: reported "units not matching", left as they were; £6 was written for £3 priced);
only for orders paid inside ERPNext's history, from profit.erp_history_from to the start's recorded floor (the setting while there is none),
both bounds checked again under each order's locks; a blank or strange docstatus or is_return is a broken day; a line that already has that
cost from the import is left as it is (its time fixed is not moved). The deliberate re-cost reads the order's paid day again under its lock
and leaves an order no longer paid on a day asked for; a line it re-costed to the same cost before is left as it is.

**PR111.** (a-M7) Finance only looks, whatever the Roles and permissions page says: it is a look-only job (Permissions::LOOK_ONLY: the jobs admin
may hold, and finance) that the page refuses to give a task that changes something (`acting_job`) and whose stored grant of one is dropped
when it is read. Admin still may be combined only with viewer, accountant and auditor (ADMIN_COMPATIBLE, unchanged).

**PR112.** (a-M1, the go-live) The profit cron lines are in deploy/production/cw-prod.cron and deploy/staging/cw-staging.cron (the jobs come
with the release that has their code and go with the undo's: install_cron.sh installs the release's own file; lines added by hand to
/etc/cron.d would be lost at the next install). Before the start every job does nothing harmful: refresh_item_cost says "not started", the
money job works the orders out with their costs waiting (PendingCosts fixes them after the start). 0074 and 0075 go in through
install_cron.sh --migrate, which pauses the public vhost and php-fpm while the schema changes: a short stock-API window, planned with the shops'
quiet hour, with the long imports finished first and the rollback release ready (README of build/A, "At go-live").

### The Codex check of c48683e (`build/A/codex_r9.txt`, one run, the default model): of the final review's HIGHs 3 FIXED and 5 PARTLY; 2 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM and 1 LOW new; fixed (PR113-PR120), each with a test seen failing first on c48683e (`runs/profit_r9b_red.log`: 8 red, `runs/profit_r9b_red2.log`: 5 red, `runs/profit_r9b_red3.log`: 1 red) except four moments of a race or a read that no test can hold still, fixed by reading (named below); what is left is a known limit in the README

Tests (tests/Unit/ProfitFinalReviewUnitTest.php, tests/Integration/Profit/FinalReview{Snapshot,Cost,Tools}Test.php): a refusal never strands the correction
stored meanwhile (new HIGH 1); a batch tool waits while a newer snapshot waits (new HIGH 2); ORD1 and ord1 take the same locks (MEDIUM 1); a line
id that changes case is the same line (b-M2); the opening by the replay's clock, items made after the start left out (MEDIUM 3, 4); a refund
split of £50m (MEDIUM 6); the money job's few-second wait (MEDIUM 7); the check under the rebuild's lock (MEDIUM 8); a kept row of zeros
(LOW 1); a phone number in groups (b-HIGH2); a Bin row with no item code / --rows (b-HIGH3); a credit of a delivery taken
back (c-HIGH2); a cancelled line never stamped by the ERPNext import (c-M6); order_snapshot empty after accept (PR113). Fixed by reading only:
the parent pinned with the seq before the guards (MEDIUM 2: a race between two statements), the credited line's `take` on a receipt of two
invoice lines keyed as one (c-HIGH2's second half), the 3-second row-lock wait of the money job (the session's innodb_lock_wait_timeout), and
the order page read in one snapshot (c-M9).

**PR113.** (new HIGH 1, MEDIUM 1 and 2; a-HIGH2 PARTLY) The queue row holds the snapshot WAITING (its body, version and hash: 0075); order_snapshot
holds the latest snapshot WORKED OUT (the one sale_order, sale_line and sale_parcel say), written by the money job in the transaction that
works it out. accept() compares an incoming snapshot with the newest CW holds (the waiting one, else the worked-out one) and writes only the
queue row: no row of order_snapshot, so no foreign-key lock on `channel` either (the selling-mode relay's lock never makes a PUT wait). A
refused snapshot never reaches order_snapshot and is marked on its queue row only while its seq is the refused one (a corrected snapshot
stored meanwhile was marked failed and stranded). The money job reads the waiting snapshot's seq and parent before it takes the guards and
works it out only if its seq is still that one (a snapshot naming a new parent stored in between is read again, at most three times). The
guards and the intake lock are named without case, as the key compares (ORD1 and ord1 are one order). Any error working an order out marks
that order and the run goes on with the next.

**PR114.** (new HIGH 2; c-M7, c-M8 PARTLY) recompute() works on the snapshot worked out (order_snapshot, FOR UPDATE under the guards), the
version the order's rows say, so a batch tool checks and writes against one version. While a newer snapshot of the order waits for the money
job, a batch tool's costs wait too (the ERPNext import says "waiting for the money job N (run again after it)", the re-cost `deferred`): a
correction moving the payment after the start is worked out first, and the import run again leaves it alone. The re-cost counts what it
wrote, not what it planned.

**PR115.** (b-M2 PARTLY) An order's lines and parcels are matched between snapshots without case, as their keys compare: L1 then l1 is one line,
never one marked removed while the order still counts it.

**PR116.** (b-HIGH2 PARTLY) A delivery method or service name, and a service code, hold at most 6 digits in all (the real ones hold 4 at most):
a phone number written in groups ("0770 0900 123") is never kept.

**PR117.** (new MEDIUM 3, 4, 5; c-HIGH1, a-M5 PARTLY) The opening average takes what was BOOKED before the start, by the ledger's booking time,
the clock the replay chooses its deliveries by (a delivery booked before midnight and made final after it was in neither). An item made at or
after the start is not in the start: the job starts it just before its first delivery (PR65). The start is written in ONE transaction with
its mark, so a start run again is priced from one set of inputs. Left (a known limit): a supplier price changed after the start is not looked
up in history; that item starts with none and its first priced delivery sets it.

**PR118.** (b-HIGH3 PARTLY) A Bin row with no item code is broken; `--rows=<n>` (the export's own count of its rows) refuses a file cut short
between whole rows.

**PR119.** (c-HIGH2 PARTLY) An invoice or a price credit of a delivery taken back by then reaches none of the stock that stays (ten at £4, ten
received at £2 and taken back, a 50p credit of those: £4.00, it was £3.50); a credit of goods that were on their way is capped on each
receipt by the units of the credited invoice line that receipt took, not all its units. The case is real: CW takes back a delivery that is
invoiced (GoodsReceiptHandler::reverse works its invoices out again, PC10) and lets the supplier credit it afterwards (a credit note's line
keeps its invoice line's delivery, whose status is not asked again: SupplierInvoiceHandler::linkProblems); the test does exactly that.

**PR120.** (new MEDIUM 6, 7, 8 and the LOW; c-M6, c-M9 PARTLY) An order-level refund is split with exact arithmetic (bcmath: two amounts of
pence can pass PHP's integers). The money job waits at most 3 seconds for a lock (an order's guards, a day's row a rebuild holds): that order
is left for the next run; `--retry-refused` tries the refused ones again. bin/rebuild_profit_days.php's check takes no lock, so it always
compares (exit 0 only when it did and nothing differs); --apply with the lock held does nothing and ends with exit 4; a day's row of zeros
with no paid order is a difference (--apply removes it). The ERPNext import never stamps a cancelled line. An order's page reads the order,
its lines and its re-sends in one snapshot.

### The Codex check of 2b718e7 (`build/A/codex_r10.txt`, one run, the default model; the last Codex round): of round 9's findings c-HIGH2, b-M2, c-M6, c-M9, new MEDIUM 4, 6, 8 FIXED, the rest PARTLY (MEDIUM 5 NOT FIXED: a known limit); 2 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM and 1 LOW new; each finding checked in the code; the real ones fixed (PR121-PR128), each with a test seen failing first on 2b718e7 (`runs/profit_r10fix_red.log`: 6 red, `runs/profit_r10fix_red2.log`: 1 red) except PR122 and PR128 (a moment between two statements that no test can hold still: fixed by reading); what is left is a known limit in the README

**PR121.** (new HIGH 1) A newer version of the same content moves the queue row's seq on and forgets its refusal, as any newer snapshot does.
It only changed the version before: a money job working the older version out meanwhile took the row away with the newer version on it (CW
had answered "same, 1012"; order_snapshot kept 1010), and a late 1011 with other figures was then taken as newer (£20 of goods in place of
£10). A refused snapshot sent again as a newer version of the same content is tried again.

**PR122.** (round 9's new HIGH 1, PARTLY; new MEDIUM 5) A refusal is written on the queue row while the order's guards are still held, so no
other money writer can work a newer snapshot out and take its row away (and the API then make a new row with seq 1 again, which the late mark
would hit) before the mark. A lock wait of the mark itself counts as busy (the row stays waiting). bin/apply_order_snapshots.php sets its
3-second lock wait before --retry-refused's update too.

**PR123.** (new HIGH 2; c-M7, c-M8 PARTLY) A batch tool's costs (the ERPNext import, the re-cost: recompute() with a function) are checked
again at their commit: after the order is worked out, the order's intake lock is taken without a wait (the API storing a snapshot of that order
right now: the order is left, `deferred`) and the queue is read again under it; a correction the API stored while the tool worked leaves the
costs unwritten (deferred). The API storing a snapshot of that order from then on waits for that commit only, never for the tool's work (it
waits at most INTAKE_WAIT_SEC, then 503 busy, as before). No outer transaction: both tools call recompute() on their own, so the check is at
the real commit.

**PR124.** (new MEDIUM 4) The ERPNext import counts the lines it wrote, not the plan read before the order's locks (an order left waiting
counts none); the run's result has `waiting`, and the tool prints how many orders are left to run it again for.

**PR125.** (new MEDIUM 2) A CW item made after the start that matches an ERPNext Bin row keeps that price as its start (ERPNext held it at £4
at the start: never an unknown cost); an item made after the start without one is still left to the job (PR117).

**PR126.** (new LOW) bin/apply_order_snapshots.php takes the job's lock itself: --status reads without it (it never says "skipped" while the
minute job runs); an asked-for --retry-refused that finds it held does nothing and ends with exit 4; the minute job's own run is skipped as
before (exit 0).

**PR127.** (round 9's LOW 1, PARTLY) The day check also reports an item's row of zeros kept on a day with no sale of it (its only sale moved
to another day), which --apply removes; a day's row of zeros was reported already (PR120).

**PR128.** (new MEDIUM 3) store() (the bulk files) reports a refusal of what it stored when the money job, running in between, refused it:
never counted "stored" by the file.

Not fixed, known limits (README): MEDIUM 1, a receipt booked in the milliseconds before the start whose value sequence is written just after
it (the same transaction) is in the opening from the start's moment; MEDIUM 6, 0075 changed after c48683e: no database outside the test
box ever had it (a test schema is made again each run); round 9's b-HIGH2 (a service code is a shape, not a carrier's list), b-HIGH3 (--rows
is given by the go-live step, not required), c-HIGH1 / MEDIUM 3 with a Bin opening (known limit 4), a-HIGH2 (a PUT waits for the money job's
last commit of that order, milliseconds), MEDIUM 2 (a parent order whose ref is the word "null"), MEDIUM 7 (the 45-second budget is checked
before each order; one order's lock waits add a few times 3 seconds).

### The owner's rule for clones (21 Nov 2026 ~01:58 UK, "Yes, that's right"; README open question 5): a clone's price is never money in

**PR129.** Every order with parent_ref (the shop's clone link) is a re-send, a replacement, whatever price staff left on it (as built). New:
nothing on it counts as money in. Its lines sell nothing (sale_inc, sale_ex 0), its refunds take nothing off (never below 0), its delivery
charge is none (delivery_ex 0), so its own row, its margin (none: no sale to measure against), the day and item-day summaries, Profit by order
and the summary count no money from it; what the shop sent stays in the `_inc` fields as it sent it (goods_inc, discount_inc, refund_inc,
delivery_charged_inc). Its goods cost is as built: on its first order (resends, resend_cost, that order's margin) and in the day's cost on the
clone's own day; never counted as an order. The clone's page says so when the shop has a price on it ("not counted as money in"). A snapshot
that takes the link away makes it the order's own sale again (and its first order's figures follow, as any change of parent did); one that
puts it back, no money again. Why (the owner): staff often forget to set a replacement's price to 0, and a real payment for a replacement
(postage) is a Viva link outside the shop, so a price on a clone is not money received; who pays comes with the Resend button (CW-1147). Real
month (cw_realcopy, 20 Oct - 18 Nov): 143 paid clones, 66 with a price (GBP 1,534 ex VAT goods, about GBP 148 delivery) that no longer count.
Left as built: a clone of a clone puts its cost on the clone it names (parent_ref is not followed up a chain); the ERPNext import's day
reconciliation line compares CW's goods (now without the clones' prices) with ERPNext's invoices, which may hold them (printed only).
Tests: tests/Integration/Profit/CloneNeverMoneyInTest.php, tests/Integration/UiKernel/ProfitScreensTest.php (red on 24e2017:
`runs/profit_clone_red.log`; green `runs/profit_clone_green.log`).

### The second final review of 3c31d94 (three read-only runs of gpt-6.2-astra: `build/A/codex_final2_astra_{a,b,c}.txt`, production safety, security and data, money; the lead's fix brief `final2/FIX_BRIEF.md` F1-F21): every finding checked in the code first, each code fix shown failing first on 3c31d94 (`runs/profit_r11_red.log`: 26 + 5 red; `runs/profit_r11_red2.log`: 3 red) and then green (`runs/profit_r11_green1.log`, `green2.log`, `green3.log`); F4 and F21 are the go-live kit's (README of build/A), F4 rehearsed on the CW test box (`runs/profit_r11_rollback_rehearsal.log`)

**PR130.** (F1: a-HIGH2 = c-HIGH1) A delivery line's units take ONE invoice's price. An invoice line naming a delivery moves at most the units
of it that can still be here LESS the units the invoice lines of the same delivery line posted before it moved (still standing: not
cancelled by then), in posting order; a price credit of an invoice line of it reaches only that line's share of what is left (the shares
filled in posting order, each at most the units its line moved); a cancellation the same, as of its own time. 100 in at £2, 80 sold, two
invoices of 50 at £3: the 20 left are £3 (it said £4: each invoice moved the same 20 from £2). THE RULE CHOSEN for two prices (the brief
left it to the builder): the units left go to the invoice lines in the order they were posted, each at most its own billed units: 50 at £3
then 50 at £3.50 with 20 left: £3 (the 20 are the first invoice's), and a credit of the second reaches none of them. A history written again
(rebuild) applies the same rule as it writes the events in time order. Left (a known limit): a claim is fixed at its invoice's time: an
earlier invoice of the line cancelled after a later one gives its units back to the delivery's own price (not to the later invoice); the
usual re-posting of the corrected invoice claims them again.

**PR131.** (F2: a-HIGH3 = c-HIGH2, b-M8) A delivery taken back leaves at the price its units carry: the price it came in at plus the moves
standing on that delivery line's units that can still be here just before (its invoices' shares with their credits; for goods that were on
their way, its price worked out again with the credits standing then, so a deferred credit cancelled since gives its part back, and the
credits given since they came), spread over every unit the line brought. Ten at £4, ten at £2 invoiced at £3 (£70), the second ten taken
back: £40 for the ten that stay (it said £50); b-M8's ten at £4, ten at £3 after a deferred £1 credit, the credit cancelled (£80), then taken
back: £40 (it said £50). An invoice or credit of that delivery cancelled afterwards finds none of its units here and takes nothing off again
(exactly once). The round-8 test CostEngineReviewR8Test::testAReceiptTakenBackStopsTakingCreditsWhenItsStockLeaves expected the old rule
(the ten leaving at £4.00 and the ten that stay taking the credit: £30.00); it now expects £40.00 (they leave at the £3.00 they carry).

**PR132.** (F3: a-HIGH4, b-M3, c-M7, a-M8) An order's ref is compared without case everywhere PHP compares it, as the database does: the
ownership check of a line's unit (a reservation of vpg42 is order VPG42's; it threw "a unit of another order" on every run), every row
written under the order's ref as stored (a snapshot sent as ord1 of ORD1 writes its new lines under ORD1), the day rebuild groups each line
by the ref of the order it joins (it lost the line: the day said £15, its products £10), the ERPNext import and the returns sweep look
orders up without case. One order whose work fails never stops the others: PendingCosts, the returns sweep (its run and the nightly check)
and bin/rebuild_profit_days.php catch an error per order (per store-day for the rebuild, whose row wait is 10 s), count it, name the order
(the first 20) in the run's summary kept on its profit_job row (`pending_costs`, `returns`, `returns_check`; `bin/refresh_item_cost.php
--status` prints them) and in the job's log, and go on; bin/refresh_item_cost.php runs each phase whatever the one before did and ends with
exit 1 when an order or a phase failed. The returns sweep's mark still moves on past a failed order (its nightly check reads every returned
unit again).

**PR133.** (F4: a-HIGH1, a-M10, a-L1, a-L2, Fable M1, L4, L5) The go-live and undo steps (README of build/A, "At go-live" and "Undo"):
the rollback release B is built and checked BEFORE step 1 (c40c050 + the final 0074 and 0075 files, sha256 checked); a step 1 stopped half
way (the installer's exit with the writers paused: its pause markers /etc/cw/cw-prod.cron.paused, cw-https.paused, cw-fpm.stopped) is
recovered with the PROFIT release's own `install_cron.sh --migrate` (it converges and resumes), never with an undo (B and A both refuse a
schema with 0075 pending, and A's installer refuses while the markers are there); B brings the web back on if it is off (php-fpm started,
the vhost enabled, the markers removed) and stops the profit jobs (the cron file first, then the running jobs waited for by name, at most 6
minutes, any left listed and stopped by pid); A's check line is `git diff --cached --name-status c40c050` before its commit and a byte
compare of both migration files after; the old People screen REVOKES Finance when a Finance holder's jobs are saved on c40c050 (README
corrected: check and grant Finance again after a roll-forward); a roll-forward after an undo on which --migrate ran is installed with
--migrate. Rehearsed on the CW test box with the final files (the normal undo and a step 1 stopped at 0075).

**PR134.** (F5: a-M1, b-M10) The snapshot API's waits are bounded for the web request only: its intake lock about 1 s
(OrderSnapshots::API_INTAKE_WAIT_SEC; it was 5), the order's queue row 2 s (the request's session innodb_lock_wait_timeout, put back after;
API_ROW_WAIT_SEC), each then 503 `busy` (retryable). A PHP worker is held by a snapshot at most about 3 s of waits. The bulk files keep the
longer waits.

**PR135.** (F6: a-M5, b-M1, c-M8, Fable L2) bin/seed_item_cost.php, bin/import_erp_sales_cost.php and bin/recost_sales.php (and so every
one-time tool that shares a job's lock) end with exit 4 "busy: ... nothing done" when another run holds the lock (they ended 0 with
"skipped"); seed --apply reads the job's mark and floor back after writing the start and ends with exit 1 when they are not there; the go-live
step 2 output must say "started N items".

**PR136.** (F7: a-M6, b-M7, c-M4, Fable L1) The re-cost counts an order only when recompute() says it committed; any other end of a batch
order counts `deferred` when the money job's queue or the API held it (a change rolled back at its commit was counted re-costed). Known limit
2's recovery is the re-cost of the source that was costed (`--source=cw_cost`, or erp_at_sale / estimate) as a dry run, then with --apply.

**PR137.** (F8: a-M7, Fable L3) A bulk file's snapshot of an order whose queue row is refused is refused (exit 1), also when CW answers
"same" (the same snapshot sent again); an order whose guards the minute job holds is tried again 3 times a second apart before it is said busy.

**PR138.** (F9: a-L3, b-M5) A day file holds each order once, each placed on the file's own London day (the connector's export: one file per
UK day the orders were PLACED, ord_date in London time, CONTRACT change 7): checked in the first pass, else nothing is written and every such
line is named (two copies of a £12 order with a .sum of two orders and £24 passed and stored £12). Two earlier tests sent an order twice in
one file (an older version) or orders of another day: ProfitImportsTest reads the older version from a file of its own,
ProfitImportsReviewR1Test places its second file's orders on that file's day.

**PR139.** (F10: a-M4, b-M4, c-M3) ERPNext's reconciliation line of a day also compares CW's own orders of the store paid that UK day inside
ERPNext's history with the whole export: those no day file holds ("cw orders paid that day not in the export N (GBP x)": their cost stays an
estimate) apart from those on an invoice of another day; the days of the export's span (or the days asked for) with CW orders and no day
file at all are one line. A folder with no day file in the days asked for is refused (exit 1; it finished with zero days).

**PR140.** (F11: b-HIGH2) The ERPNext export carries no shop of its own: its header (name, posting_date, creation, custom_order_id,
is_return, return_against, docstatus, net_total, total_taxes_and_charges, grand_total, discount_amount, idx, item_code, qty, rate, net_rate,
net_amount, incoming_rate, warehouse) names no company, customer group or store, and its rows were not looked at. ERPNext is Vape and Go's:
its item codes are "P" + a variant of the store erp_opening.listing_store names (the opening import's rule) and custom_order_id is that
store's order id, so the import is bound to that store: any other --channel is refused before a file is read (exit 2). A --series would not
bind it (a prefix the operator types says nothing of the store); a manifest of the export is a change of the export for later.

**PR141.** (F12: b-HIGH1) A parcel ref is only the shop's own shapes, odl:<number> or orl:<number> (CONTRACT change 4; any case), else the
snapshot is refused (400 parcels[i].parcel_ref): "Jane.Smith" is never stored (it stayed after the parcel was gone). A delivery method or
service name is kept only when every word is a service word AND one of them is a carrier's or a service's (SERVICE_ANCHORS: royal, mail, dpd,
evri, tracked, delivery, collection, return, label, ...): "12 Preston Road" and "12 Preston" are never stored; "road" is no service word any

the listings' variant ids, stored by the stock API's rules for every reserved order), which the connector builds from integers
(cw_snapshot_ref, (int) ordi_id); a digits-only shape here would refuse snapshots of keys CW's stock API holds and every test fixture's
ids. A service code stays a shape (known limit 19).

**PR143.** (F14: a-M9, c-M6, Fable L6; the owner: the cost goes on the first order) A replacement of a replacement puts its cost and its

## CW-1155 "Receive the rest": the rest of a short line received on the same invoice (branch `receive-rest`, 22 Nov 2026; RR1-RR20; migration 0076)

<!-- ---- CW-1155 (0076): RR1-RR20. ---- -->
The owner's words (22 Nov 2026, the CW chat): "until on goods received we keep it the same way as it is now. all stores take the 5 out as well.
then it just stays on accept the difference section. then when the rest actually comes we should be able to add it on the same invoice and on
booking it give the shops back that number to sell again ... if [the supplier says] it is not going to come ... then we do like what we do
today like file a missing, credit note whatever it is." The real case: SINV-000632 line 19 (5 x CW-004020 at £1.00) booked 0 of 5 on
GRN-000026. Plans: `cw_work/receive_rest_20261122/PLAN_fable.md` (built, flows B1-B6, same item only) and `PLAN_astra.md`; the lead's ten
decisions in `BRIEF_BUILD.md` win where they differ. Code: `src/Arrivals/ArrivalRest.php` (new); changed `Arrivals`, `ArrivalBooking`,
`ArrivalInvariants`, `Invoices/{InvoiceMatch, SupplierInvoices, SupplierInvoiceHandler}`, `Receiving/{GoodsReceipts, GoodsReceiptHandler,
ReceiptPlan}`, `Profit/CostEngine` (one lookup), the receipt, invoice and To match screens, one marked block each in `Words`, `Settings`, `Grants`.

**RR1. One append-only table of facts, `invoice_arrival_rest` (0076).** Per invoice line counted on arrival whose first receipt (the one its
arrival row names) did not bring all of it: one row per later fact with its units: `rest` (a later receipt line of the same item brought them;
written by that receipt's posting; counts while it is posted), `claim` (claimed from the supplier by "Claim what did not come"; counts while
the claim is draft, waiting or posted), `waive` (a person accepted the invoice's difference while they were waited for; counts for good).
Every row names the first receipt (and its line) it is about: rows of a first receipt taken back count no more. Never changed or removed
(Grants: SELECT, INSERT); a cancellation or reversal changes the documents' status and every reader counts by it. No FK on the first receipt
(a receipt of the rest is posted without that row's lock: an FK check would S-lock it and meet a claim holding it, a deadlock seen in
ReceiveRestRaceTest; J5 checks it). The arrival rows are NEVER reopened: `open` means Incoming, and owed units are never sellable (the owner's rule).

**RR2. "Still owed" is derived, never stored (the lead's decision 1).** owed = line units - units credited on the line (posted credit notes)
- what the first receipt brought (accepted + set aside + quarantined, a receipt line shared by two invoice lines given to them in line order,
Arrivals::missingOf's rule) - posted `rest` - live `claim` - `waive`, never below 0 (`ArrivalRest::lines`). A live claim of the first receipt
with no rows (made before 0076, or by hand) claims everything. "What did not come" (the claim) is the same without the claims: ONE rule for
the claim and the rest, so a claim never claims what came later, was credited or given up. So SINV-000632 shows "Waiting for the rest: 5
(£5.00)" the moment the code is live, no data fix.

**RR3. "Receive the rest" (`Arrivals::receiveRest`, doc.GRN.post).** A draft receipt of only the owed units, from the SAME invoice: its
supplier number as the next part (RR4), its date, its order when every owed line comes from one still receivable (against the same order
line: the order fills up), one line per owed invoice line (the line's packs and pack price when the owed units are whole packs, else single
units at its unit price, 4 decimals), the invoice's copy, the link goods_receipt_invoice (auto 0), audit `arrival.receive_rest`. A live
receipt made from the invoice already: that one (pressed twice, two people at once: the same draft). 409 `claimed` when what is missing is
claimed, 409 `nothing_owed`. The person lands on the normal receipt page: bench, stamp, post as any receipt.

**RR4. The duplicate-invoice guards widened for this proven link only.** A supplier invoice number is on one live receipt (PO10, I171):
`GoodsReceipts::invoicePart` (with `$restOf`), `ReceiptPlan` `invoice_shared` and `invoice_copy_elsewhere`, and `GoodsReceipts::attach`
let the receipts made from ONE CW invoice (both in goods_receipt_invoice with the same invoice) share its number and its copy; every other
receipt is refused as before (tested: a receipt keyed by hand with the number, the copy on an unrelated receipt).

**RR5. Posting a receipt of the rest (ArrivalBooking::receiptPosted, a new branch where it returned early).** A receipt made from an invoice
with no open arrival row and rows received by another receipt is a receipt of the rest. Under the invoice's arrival rows' lock: every line's
item is owed and the units on the paperwork per item are at most what is owed, else 422 `not_owed` (or 409 `claimed` when it was claimed;
the receipt page lists the same as problems before posting: `ArrivalRest::problems` in ReceiptPlan); each line's units that came (accepted +
set aside + quarantined) are given to the owed invoice lines of its item in line order, at most what each is owed, as `rest` rows; audit
`arrival.rest_received`; the invoice's match is worked out again and the receipt's "not invoiced yet" stored (0). NO movement of Incoming
(the owed units were never there): the receipt's own goods_in puts what came on hand in MAIN and its selling mode puts the item back on sale
(an ordinary receipt for the shops' stock feed). Part arrivals: what did not come stays owed (its own short incident too).

**RR6. The match and "Not invoiced yet".** InvoiceMatch::compute: a received line is "there" also in what posted rest rows brought (each
rest receipt line's accepted units less returned and billed elsewhere, given to its rows in order); receiptFacts: a rest receipt line is
billed by its invoice (its rows' units, at most what the line bills net of credits) so it has nothing left to invoice; invoicesOnReceipts and
SupplierInvoiceHandler::receiptIds know the rest receipts (locks of an acceptance or a credit note, and a reversal's refresh). With no rows
(every invoice on day one) every figure is what it was; V4 and V7 work them out with the same functions.

**RR7. The short incident.** When nothing is owed any more for every invoice line a short incident's receipt line is about (the first
receipt's line, and each rest receipt's line that brought some), the posting of the rest resolves it: "The rest came on GRN-x.", resolved
by the poster, audit `incident.rest_resolved` (auto). A part arrival leaves it open. A rest receipt taken back opens again every incident the
rest resolved by itself (its last close is `incident.rest_resolved`) whose lines are owed again (audit `incident.rest_reopened`); a person's
own resolution stays.

**RR8. A claim and the rest exclude each other (the lead's decision 4).** claimMissing: refused 409 `rest_being_received` while a draft of the
rest is live; it writes one `claim` row per line it claims (its units), so those units are not waited for while it is live; cancelling or
taking back the claim releases them. receiveRest offers only units not claimed (409 `claimed` when nothing else is owed); the posting
checks again under the arrival rows' lock.

**RR9. Accepting the difference while units are waited for (the lead's decision 3).** Allowed (invoices.accept, the note, the fingerprint);
in the same transaction a `waive` row per owed line with exactly its units: we stop waiting (the reminder goes), for good (a later match that
drops the acceptance does not bring them back). Units owed again later (a part of the rest taken back) can still be received. Refused
409 `rest_being_received` while a draft of the rest is live (book it in or cancel it first: the waiver would take units the draft brings).

**RR10. The rest taken back.** Its stock negated as any receipt; its rows count no more (owed again); the incidents as RR7; the invoice's match
worked out again (InvoiceMatch::afterReceiptReversed through invoicesOnReceipts). Nothing goes to Incoming.

**RR11. The first receipt is not taken back while a receipt of the rest stands** (posted, or a draft): 409 `rest_received` "GRN-y took in the
rest of this invoice: cancel that receipt first", read before anything of the reversal is written. Without it the arrival rows would reopen
(units on their way again) while the rest is on hand: double stock.

**RR12. Locks (no cycle).** receiveRest, claimMissing and SupplierInvoices::accept take the invoice's document row first, then the first
receipt's (accept: the receipts, lockReceipts), then (claim, accept) the invoice's arrival rows, then supplier_invoice rows: one of them at a
time per invoice. A receipt's posting takes its own rows, its order's, then the arrival rows, then other receipts' incidents, then
supplier_invoice; a receipt's reversal now takes the arrival rows after its order's rows and before its incidents (`ArrivalBooking::lockFor`)
so a reversal and a posting of the rest wait in one order. ReceiveRestRaceTest: two receiveRest (one draft), receiveRest against a claim
(exactly one), the posting of the rest against a claim, an acceptance and the first receipt's reversal (the posting books, the other is
refused), held and at the same moment, no deadlock.

**RR13. The screens (plain words; Words::REST).** Purchases › To match: under the match pill "Waiting for the rest: 5 (£5.00)" and "3 days
waiting" / "Late · 15 days waiting" (red from arrivals.rest_late_days). The invoice page: the same line, per owed line, "Receive the rest"
(doc.GRN.post) and the receipts of the rest ("Received on GRN-…: 3"). The first receipt's page ("What did not come"): the same, "Receive the
rest" beside "Claim what did not come". A receipt of the rest: "This receipt takes in the rest of SINV-… (first part: GRN-…)". Every POST
carries the CSRF token; the service checks the person again. No e-mail, no badge, no Arriving-board group (cheaper: cut first by the plan).

**RR14. The buying price (the lead's decision 7).** CostEngine::invoiceLineOf: a receipt with `rest` rows takes the invoice lines its rows
name, each at most the units the row settled (receiptBasis), never the n-th line of the item; the existing lookup stays for every other
receipt. One item on two invoice lines at two prices, only the second short: the rest comes at the second's landed price (it gave the first's:
ReceiveRestCostTest, red first). Each part is its own FIFO layer at that price (£1.00 in the real case); taken back, it leaves at that price.

**RR15. The nightly checks.** J5: every row is about a first receipt made from that invoice; a `rest` row names a line of another receipt of
the same invoice, supplier and item; a `claim` row a return about that first receipt and invoice. J6: per invoice line, posted rest + live
claims + waivers of its first receipt never exceed what that receipt did not bring (the newest 2000 invoices with rows). J1-J4, G1-G8,
V1-V8 unchanged and holding.

**RR16. The reminder, `arrivals.rest_late_days` (14, 1-365, provisional; the lead's decision 6).** Days waiting = UK calendar days since the
first receipt was posted; late from that many days.

**RR17. Known limits (for the owner).** "Not invoiced yet": a part of the rest is billed for the units it settled (RR23), so a credit of
units of a line given AFTER its rest came is billed against the first receipt only and the list shows fewer units left to invoice than
there are (10 came, 5 billed: it shows 1 left instead of 5); the nightly checks (V7, J1-J6) stay clean on it (they work it out the same
way: ReceiveRestReviewR1Test). Accepted by the lead, 22 Nov 2026. A wrong item set aside at the bench (VERIFY) counts as come for what is owed and for the claim, as today's "Claim what did not come"
(RR31; the workaround: the usual return and credit of the wrong item; how it relates to the owed units is the replacement's, step 2).
A credit note line credits units in the match's eyes: a PRICE credit typed as units on an owed line
lowers what is waited for (as the match bills it). Claim rows say what was claimed when it was made (a claim's lines edited by hand later are
not read). A part arrival with a price credit of that line given between the parts: the credit reaches the units already here (CostEngine's
rule for any credit); the rest comes at the uncredited landed price. "Over" units on a rest receipt go to VERIFY as on any receipt.

**RR18. Not in this build: a replacement (another item instead).** The seam: `kind` gains 'replacement' at the END of its ENUM (instant), a
draft-time link of the replacing line, `ArrivalRest::posted` takes declared replacements, CostEngine prices them at their own typed price.

**RR19. Not changed.** The first receipt's posting (same stock, incident, match), Goods In's Receive, the bench, the stamp rules, book as
received, the receipt's posting order (the arrival step 5b before the stock), the shops' stock feed.

**RR20. Go-live and rollback.** 0076: one CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + one setting with its baseline (seconds; nothing locked), Grants, the
release. Rollback: NOT a bare symlink back to b35949d: once 0076 is recorded in schema_migrations, b35949d's CLI guard
(Cli::requireCurrentSchema: every cron job, the expiry of unpaid holds too) and its installer refuse the schema ("migrations this code does
not have"). The rollback release is b35949d's code with `migrations/0076_receive_rest.sql` added byte for byte (profit step 1's recipe,
PR94; RollbackReleaseTest holds it: BEFORE_LAST 0075, ROLLBACK_FILES [0076]); the empty table and setting stay. Once a receipt of the rest is posted, the old code shows its
invoice as "needs review" and the receipt in "Not invoiced yet" and the nightly V4 / V7 report them (no stock is wrong): take the rest
receipt back under the new code first, or fix forward. Before any rollback: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_arrival_rest`.

**RR21. The Codex check of a0d33a2 (`cw_work/receive_rest_20261122/codex_r1.txt`, default model: HOLD, 3 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW), each point

claim settles: counted once. (M3) invoicePart locks only the other receipts' own rows (`FOR UPDATE OF g`), never their documents and
keyers (a new part against the reversal of an earlier part by the same person; the race test runs it, no deadlock seen either way).

(M5) The rest of one line resolves only incidents about the lines it brought (a line credited instead is never "came"). (LOW) J5: a fact

**Accepted by the lead (22 Nov) as known limits or for the go-live kit, not changed:** (a) a claim's debit note with a damaged item added

accepted (Accept shows only for one that needs review): its units wait until they come or are claimed or credited; (e) a supplier
