## Expenses (CW-1150): expenses, regular costs and the real profit (branch `expenses`, 24 Nov 2026; EX1-EX20; migration 0079)

<!-- ---- CW-1150 (0079): EX1-EX20. Brief: cw_work/runs/expenses_brief.txt; drawings: cw_work/expenses_design_20261124/project/ ---- -->
The owner's words (CW chat), kept as he wrote them:
- 21 Nov 2026: NO Sage at all (never read, check or connect Sage). CW holds the costs itself. He uploads expense invoices with the PDF and
  enters every purchase invoice from 1 November; Global Payments' fees are its monthly invoice entered as an expense.
- 24 Nov ~11:50: "no i will add it seperate like vape and go expense vapebig eexpense alectrofag expense like that".
- 24 Nov ~12:05 (his weekly list, from the business owner, no invoices): "thesee all aree weekly ... i wont be able to give invoice. it is
  from the owner. startlink dont worry i can add invoice monthly ... then theree are some like cloudflare that wee do yearly".
- 24 Nov ~12:10: "Yes, per day".
- 24 Nov 12:15: "Yes, build it" on the drawings (Main = the expenses list, AddExpense, MonthlyCosts = Regular costs, ProfitMonth = the real
  profit). The drawings are the spec for the parts, their order and their words; CW's own look (app.css) is the style.
Code: `src/Expenses/{ExpenseMoney, RegularCostMath, ExpenseHistory, ExpenseAccess, ExpenseFiles, Expenses, ExpenseTypes, RegularCosts,
ExpenseViews}.php` (new), `Ui/Controller/{ExpensesController, RegularCostsController, ExpenseTypesController}.php` (new),
`ProfitController::real`, the views `profit_expense*`, `expense_*`, `profit_regular*`, `profit_real`, `bin/seed_regular_costs.php` (new), and
one marked block each in `Permissions`, `Grants`, `FileStore::KINDS`, `FilesController::show`, `Words`, `Sections`, `Kernel`,
`ReferenceController::SETTINGS_SECTIONS`, app.css and app.js. Every test file is made up (no real invoice, no customer data).

**EX1. Each expense belongs to ONE shop, the one the person picks (the owner, 24 Nov).** Vape and Go, Electrofag or Vape Big: three big
buttons on the form, NONE picked for you (the form never fills it, not even after "Save and add another"); no shared cost is split by CW.

**EX2. An expense (`expense`, 0079).** Its shop, supplier (EX11), type (EX10), invoice date (the day it counts), invoice number (as printed;
empty allowed when a bill has none), the amount without VAT and the VAT as printed, the total = net + VAT (a CHECK), a note, its file (EX9).
The amount without VAT is above 0 (an expense of nothing is refused), the VAT 0 or more; both at most £9,999,999.99. A bill in dollars is
typed as the pounds the card was charged (the form says so; CW keeps no currency). A credit note (a negative amount) is NOT taken in this
version: the open question Q1. The invoice date is a real day from 1 Jan 2020 to a year after today (a typo guard only).

**EX3. The VAT of an expense is never worked out by CW.** (A regular cost's is: EX38. Amended by EX65, the owner's word of 25 Nov 2026: the
form's script fills it in from a total typed with VAT; the server still saves exactly what the boxes say.) It is typed as printed, 0 when none; the total is net + VAT. The profit counts the amount WITHOUT
VAT (every Profit page is without VAT; the drawing's tiles and the ProfitMonth Expenses line show the net).

**EX4. Money in whole pence (BIGINT), never a float.** Typed as pounds and pence ("64.20", "£1,234.56", "12.5", "200"; at most two decimals;
`ExpenseMoney::pence`), shown by integer arithmetic (`ExpenseMoney::gbp`). app.js shows the total as it is typed (whole pence too); the server
works it out again on save.

**EX5. A regular cost (`regular_cost`, 0079; the owner, 24 Nov: "Yes, per day").** Its name, shop (one of the three, picked each time), group
(EX10), how often (every week, every month, every year), the amount as given (since the owner's answer of 24 Nov, with its VAT choice: only
the cost without VAT counts, EX38), its first day
and its last day (none: no end; both days count). Per day: a weekly amount / 7; a monthly amount / the days of THAT calendar month (28-31); a
yearly amount / the days of THAT calendar year (365 or 366). The brief's example holds: Unit 1 £207.69 a week = £29.67 a day, November
(30 days) £890.10.

**EX6. The rounding rule: cumulative, once per line and period (`RegularCostMath`).** What a line accrued from its first day to the end of
day D is an exact fraction A(D) (integers: whole pence + numerator / denominator, never a float); its share of days a..b is round(A(b)) -
round(A(a - 1)), half up. Therefore: the days of a month add up to the month EXACTLY, the months to the year, any two following periods to
the whole; 7 days of a weekly line are its amount exactly (any 28 days of £207.69 a week = £830.76, wherever they start); a whole calendar
month of a monthly line is its amount, a whole calendar year of a yearly one too; a period's share is within a penny of its own exact value
(March 2027 of Unit 3, £923.08 a week from 1 Nov 2026, is £4,087.92: 31 x 923.08 / 7 = 4,087.926, the penny went to the earlier days). A
shop's figure is the SUM of its lines' shares, so the lines shown always add up to the shop's line: the owner's weekly list in November is
£41,879.73 (each line rounded once; rounding the week's total once, as the drawing did, gives £41,879.74). Tests:
`tests/Unit/RegularCostMathTest.php`.

**EX7. A new amount ends the line and starts a new one (the brief: "old days keep the old amount").** "The amount changes" on a line's page
takes the new amount and its first day (after the line's own first day, on or before its last day): the line ends the day before and a new
line starts that day with the rest of the old one (name, shop, group, how often, note, last day), naming it (`replaces_id`). A line's amount,
shop, how often and first day never change in place (Grants: no UPDATE of those columns); its name, group, note and last day do (an end put
on, moved or taken off). A line put in by mistake is deleted by a mark with a reason: out of the profit on every day.

**EX8. Every change and delete keeps who, when, old -> new (`expense_history`, append-only; and audit_log).** One row per version of an
expense, a regular cost, a supplier or a type: what it was before and after (with the shop's, supplier's and type's names beside their ids,
so the trail reads in words), the reason when one is asked for (a delete, a type's change), who and when; the row's own `version` is the
trail's latest, and a form drawn before another person's change is refused ("changed meanwhile"). A delete is a MARK with a reason (deleted
at, by, why): out of every list and of the profit, kept with its history and file, never removed (Grants: no DELETE on any of the five
tables; the creation columns frozen). The expense page and the regular cost page show the history ("Without VAT: £64.20 → £65.00; Shop:
Vape and Go → Electrofag").

**EX9. The invoice file: a PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 10 MB, checked by its FIRST BYTES (`ExpenseFiles`).** `%PDF-`, `FF D8 FF`, `89 PNG
0D 0A 1A 0A`, and the content sniffer (finfo) must agree; the name and what the browser said play no part (a text file named .pdf, HTML, SVG,
GIF, a ZIP: refused, "nothing was saved"). The bytes are read once (at most 10 MB + 1) and stored from a private copy of exactly those bytes.
WHERE: CW's existing document store (`FileStore`, I23, I36), not a new folder: app.env `file_store_dir`, which is `/srv/cw-docs` on the CW
servers (`deploy/production/install_file_store.sh`): outside every web directory and every code directory (LocalFileStorage refuses
otherwise), file name = its sha256, mode 0440 and immutable once the minute's seal has run (stricter than the brief's 0640), kept 7 years,
re-hashed on every read; kind `expense_invoice`. The brief's own example (a new /var/lib/cw/expense_files/) would have been a second store
without the seal, the re-hash or the retention: the house store already does all of it. Served only by `GET /ui/profit/expenses/{id}/file`
(signed in, expenses.view: Finance and the Expenses job) as an ATTACHMENT of its sniffed type with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`,
nosniff and no-store (FilesController::download); never listed, never run. The general `/ui/files/{id}` refuses a file an expense names (or
of kind expense_invoice) to anyone without expenses.view, whatever else they may read. **BACKUPS (CW-701):** `/srv/cw-docs` on the
production box must be in the server's backups; the expense PDFs are the only copy CW keeps (the owner is told; it was already true for the
supplier invoice copies and the purchase orders' PDFs).

**EX10. The types: a settable list, Settings > Expense types (`expense_type`, 0079).** Changed like CW's other settable lists: an admin or a
reviewer (settings.manage, re-read inside the write: ConfigHistory::authorise), each change with its reason (3-500 characters) and kept in
expense_history; renamed or switched off, never deleted (what names it keeps it). Start list (the brief): Stationery and packaging, Software
and AI, Developer, Fees, Other. The regular costs' groups are the SAME list, kind `regular` ("keep it simple": one list, one page): Rent,

whole, as built.

**EX37. A credit note (the owner's Q1).** "Add an expense" and "Change this expense" have a "This is a credit note" tick (never ticked for
you). Its amounts are typed as printed, without a minus (a minus typed is refused, as for an invoice), and kept and counted as minus: net
and VAT both minus (the CHECK: net -£9,999,999.99 to -£0.01 with VAT -£9,999,999.99 to £0; an invoice stays net £0.01 up and VAT £0 up),
total = net + VAT. It takes that much off its shop's expenses on its date: the list, the tiles, Real profit and Profit by shop simply add
the minus. Example: Viking Direct's credit £10.42 + £2.08 VAT on 20 Nov: Vape and Go's November expenses £64.20 - £10.42 = £53.78 without
VAT. Its PDF is kept as an invoice's. The list marks it "Credit note" with minus amounts; its page says it is one; its change form shows the
amounts as printed with the tick on, and taking the tick off makes it an invoice again (kept in its history, before and after). The same
duplicate guard as an invoice, within its kind: the same supplier, shop and number as a credit note not deleted asks first (with no number:
the same supplier, shop, day and total); an invoice of the same number as a credit note is not "the same one twice" (a credit note often
names the invoice it credits). The safest reading of "duplicate guard as for invoices": a second credit note of one number still asks, and
a credit note never blocks its own invoice.

**EX38. A regular cost's VAT (the owner's Q4: "all of them i gave you is 20% inc vat").** Every line has a VAT choice: "Includes 20% VAT"
(picked for you on Add a regular cost) or "No VAT", set on the line (Change) and kept in its history. The rate is the CW setting
profit.vat_rate_pct (the shops' VAT, 20%; not a constant) and is kept on the line when it is set (`vat_rate_bp`, basis points; 0 = no
VAT), so a later change of the setting changes no past day: a line keeps its own rate while it includes VAT; a new line, a new amount, or a
line switched from "No VAT" to including VAT takes the rate of that day. VAT = amount x rate / (100% + rate) to the penny, half up (at 20%:
the amount / 6); the cost without VAT = amount - VAT (Unit 1 £207.69: VAT £34.62, cost £173.07; Novos £2,769.00: £461.50, £2,307.50).
Only the cost without VAT is shared per day (each line's cost rounded once per period, as EX6) and taken off the real profit; the expenses
list's "Regular costs" row is without VAT too. Profit > Regular costs shows Amount (with VAT), VAT and Cost without VAT, and "Every week in
all" sums each (the owner's list: £9,771.94, £1,628.66, £8,143.28); a line's page shows them and its day's and month's share of the cost.
The seed marks all 16 lines as including the setting's rate (20%), and treats a line of the same name with another VAT choice as other
figures (the whole run refused, as r1 H3: EX26). November 2026 for the whole list from 1 Nov: £34,899.77 without VAT (was £41,879.73 with it). A
row put in around CW without the column gets 0: counted in full, never less (the nightly check EX-I2 compares the rate with the history).

`sandbox` and the pages' own policy are both enforced (before, header() replaced the first); HtmlResponse::emitted() is what a client gets.

**EX51. Exact days on Profit > Expenses and Regular costs at most reports.sales_max_days (Fable L2).** As Real profit: a longer span keeps
its last day, is cut at the front, and the page says "At most 366 days at once: shown from ...".

**EX52. A download's name keeps its extension (astra MEDIUM).** Supplier + number (or date), cleaned, cut to leave room for the sniffed
type's extension: at most 255 bytes with it, so the disposition's clean keeps ".pdf" in both of its names.

**EX53. The help texts say the shops' VAT rate of the setting (Fable L3).** "includes VAT at the shops' rate (now 20%)" and "How it is
shared out" with its example worked out at that rate; never a fixed 20% or "/ 6".

**EX54. A regular cost's VAT choice is kept apart from its rate (astra MEDIUM).** `regular_cost.vat_included` (0/1; a CHECK: no VAT has rate
0): a line including VAT while the shops' rate is 0% stays one; at 20% again a new amount of £120 includes £20 VAT (£100 counts, never £120).
The history shows "VAT: Includes VAT → No VAT; VAT rate: 20% → 0%"; nightly EX-I2 compares both.

**EX55. The rest (Fable M1, L1, L4; astra LOW x2).** M1: deleting a "new amount" line says, on its delete form and after, that the line before

"new amount" is the next live line by date in its WHOLE chain (a backdated new amount links the later one); a monthly or yearly share is
worked out directly (first and last calendar month or year, the whole ones between counted at once), the same fraction as day by day (20,000
random cases checked against the loop it replaces), so a one-day report years after a line's first day costs no more than one in its first month.

**EX56. Profit by shop's three columns are Real profit's own figures of the shop (astra MEDIUM).** Read in the row's snapshot from

for it (one unpriced unit of 1,000 is marked, below the margin pages' 0.5%).

**Fix round 2 (the Codex re-check of 8dbee81, `runs/expenses_recheck_astra_report.txt`, C1-C7, and the Fable re-check F-A, F-B): each first as a
failing test (`tests/Integration/Expenses/ExpensesFix2Test.php`, `runs/expenses_fix2_red.log`: 9 of 9 red on 8dbee81), then fixed (EX57-EX63).**

**EX57. Days are strict, a share is never minus (C4).** A day a person or a link asks for is YYYY-MM-DD in the years 2000-2099

**EX58. A "same one" question lists every record it met and its confirmation covers exactly them (C1, F-B).** No cap of 20: the check reads

**EX64. The expense and regular-cost forms are one card whose boxes line up (the owner, 25 Nov 2026: "the adding expense part ... It's so

**EX65. An expense's total with VAT fills the amount without VAT and the VAT (the owner, 25 Nov 2026, of Add an expense: "When I type in
price including VAT, why the non-VAT is not automatically calculated and shown? If it is right, then I don't have to type it again.";
amends EX3).** Add an expense and an expense's Change have "Total with VAT (£)" and a VAT choice like a regular cost's (EX38): "Includes 20%
VAT" (the shops' rate, profit.vat_rate_pct; picked for you on Add), "No VAT", "Different VAT (type it)", then one row Total with VAT | Amount
without VAT | VAT. The page's script fills the two boxes as the total is typed: at the rate, without VAT = total x 10000 / (10000 + rate) to
the penny, half up, in whole pence, and VAT = the total minus that, so the two always add up to the total (the owner's Amazon invoice:
£8.47 = £7.06 + £1.41, as it prints); No VAT: without VAT = the total, VAT £0; Different VAT: the VAT stays as typed, without VAT = the total
minus it. The total leads once the person has typed it (or sent it back on a refusal); until then (an empty Add form; an expense's Change
showing its saved total) typing the amount or the VAT works the old way and the total box shows their sum, so fixing a saved VAT by a penny
moves the total, never the amount without VAT. A box typed by hand is never overwritten: typing the VAT (or the amount) yourself while the
total leads picks "Different VAT" and the other box follows the total (an invoice's VAT a penny off the rounding is typed once); with both typed by hand neither moves, and a
line under them says when they do not add up to the total; pressing "Includes" or "No VAT" (again) works both out afresh. The old way
(without VAT + VAT, the total left empty) still works, and so does a page whose script never ran. WHAT IS SHOWN IS WHAT IS SAVED: the server
keeps the amount without VAT and the VAT exactly as in the boxes and works nothing out; a total typed must be their sum, else it is refused
with both sums named and nothing saved (a credit note's total is typed as printed, without a minus, like its amounts: EX37). The VAT choice
is not saved: an expense's Change picks the choice its figures match (no VAT; the rate's split; else Different) and its script shows the
total (net + VAT) in the box, which the page itself leaves empty, so the amounts changed without the script never meet a stale total. No database change. The page is told which form it answers (Change, Delete) as a regular cost's page is, so a refusal of
either, even an incomplete form, opens that fold and is said there. The final reviews of 1f18763 (Codex, Fable): the script keeps a hidden
"hand" (which boxes were typed by hand: net, vat; and sum when the total box holds the sum it wrote), given back with a refusal so the page
carries on as it was typed (a total the person typed leads again, a sum the script wrote does not; a box typed by hand stays kept); a box
typed by hand before the total shows "Different VAT"; the old way's two amounts pick the choice their split matches (as a saved expense's
Change does), and the sum goes only into an empty total box or over the sum written before; a total that is not an amount ("8,47") is said
so under the boxes and never written over. One money rule for the three boxes in the script and on the server (spaces, tabs and the no-break
spaces U+00A0, U+202F, U+2007 around and after the £; nothing else trimmed; a box at most £9,999,999.99, a total at most two boxes' worth).
The one-effect key (FormOnce) checks the fields and a typed total, never the choice or the record of hand typing, so an Add sent from the
page live before keeps its fingerprint and is replayed. The page reads the shops' rate once for the label and the script. CW-1176 (the
lead's browser test of the live 27dea71): a total still being typed (an amount and its point, "8.", whose lowest end is within two
boxes' worth, or the £ alone; "8.4" is an amount already: 840p, £7.00 + £1.40 at 20%) says nothing and leaves the boxes; one that cannot
become an amount ("8,47", "8,", three decimals, a letter, "20,000,000.") says so and empties the boxes the script filled from the total,
never one typed by hand; which boxes it filled goes with the form in the hidden "hand" (fnet, fvat), so a refused form empties them too
(Codex's final of 332aba7). A comma is read only as a thousands mark of three figures, so "8,4" says "not an
amount" at once (a total is seldom typed with thousands commas). The server refuses both on save, as before.

## PayPal's payment fees in the profit (CW-1172): read every night from PayPal's own API (branch `paypal-fees`, 25 Nov 2026; PPF1-PPF22: the prefix PF is pack F's; migration 0080)

<!-- ---- CW-1172 (0080): PPF1-PPF22. Brief: cw_work/runs/paypal_fees_brief.txt; state: cw_work/runs/PAYPAL_FEES_STATE.md ---- -->
The owner's rules (24 Nov 2026 23:58, agreed with the lead), kept as the brief gives them: 1. the PayPal fee of each sale goes on THAT
order, on the order's profit day; 2. a refund: the part of the fee PayPal gives back goes back on the same order, on the refund's day;
3. a chargeback: the money taken back PLUS PayPal's chargeback fee and any dispute fee are a cost on that order, on the chargeback's day;
4. anything with no order number (or no CW order for it) goes on the shop's "not on an order" line; 5. holds and their releases, money moved
to the bank, payments sent or received are NOT costs (read, kept, never counted). The owner, 25 Nov ~00:50 (through the lead): there is ONE
PayPal account, used by Vape and Go, Electrofag AND Hayati Vapes (hayativapes.uk, WooCommerce, not a CW shop); each row goes to the shop whose
order-number form its invoice matches; a shop not switched on keeps its rows as facts and NEVER lands on Vape and Go's lines; only rows with
no or an unrecognised invoice go on the account's main shop (Vape and Go). CW uses the shop's existing PayPal REST key (his choice), and only
ever calls POST /v1/oauth2/token and GET /v1/reporting/transactions with it. Global Payments is out of scope (its monthly invoice is an
expense).
Code: `src/Profit/{PaypalCodes, PaypalRow, PaypalKey, PaypalHttp, PaypalHttpFailed, CurlPaypalHttp, PaypalApi, PaypalFees,
PaypalInvariants}.php` (new), `bin/paypal_fees.php` (new), one marked block each in `ProfitDays` (DAY_FIELDS, orderShare, compute),
`OrderSnapshots::apply`, `ProfitViews` (SUMS, figures, order), `DeliveryBills` (a fact's `field`, tidy), `ExpenseViews::realProfit`, the views
`profit_real` and `profit_order`, `Alerts`, `AlertDispatch`, `Invariants`, `Grants`, `Settings::RULES`, `Words`. Tests: `tests/Unit/
PaypalReadTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Profit/{PaypalFeesTest, PaypalReplayTest}.php`, `tests/Support/{FakePaypalHttp, PaypalTx}.php`; every
fixture is made up; the real rows are read only by the replay, from a reduced copy outside git (PPF19).

**PPF1. What is built.** The nightly job reads PayPal's Transaction Search (transaction_info only) for the last few days, stores every
transaction, decides where its money counts, and keeps two new profit_day figures: `fee_cost` (PayPal money on orders) and `fee_other`
(PayPal money on no CW order). Profit › Real profit's "Payment fees" line shows them for a shop switched on (its first fee day set); an
order's page lists its PayPal rows. Nothing else of the profit changes.

**PPF2. One row per transaction AND event code, changed in place.** paypal_txn's key is (account, PayPal's transaction_id, event code):
PayPal gives a dispute hold (T1110, status P) and its release (T1111, status D) the SAME id (12 such pairs in the real rows of 1 Oct - 24 Nov),
so the id alone would make the release overwrite the hold. A re-read that brings another status, amount, fee, date or reference changes the
row in place (version + 1; paypal_txn_history keeps before and after, PPF8) and marks it due; the same row read again changes nothing (its
last_run only). The same (id, code) twice in one window with different content refuses the window (it moved while read: the next run reads it
again). A row whose stored kind or cost is not what the rules of the running code make of it (a release that classes a code anew) is a
change too, when it is read again (PP3 says the others every night). Nothing personal is read or kept: no payer, e-mail, name, item text, note, balance or instrument; the invoice and custom fields are kept
as written only when they are a reference (letters, digits and . _ : | = / + - only, at most 127: the shops write their order number there);
one with a space or an @ (it could be a name or an e-mail) is never kept, only that there was one (`dropped`).

**PPF3. Every event code classified (PaypalCodes::TABLE).** sale: T0005 (Direct payment API), T0006 (PayPal Checkout): the FEE counts.
refund: T1107: the fee given back counts. chargeback: T1106 (payment reversal by PayPal), T1201 (chargeback), T1202 (chargeback reversal: the
money back): the money AND its fee count. fee: T0106 (chargeback processing fee), T0114 (dispute fee): the money and its fee count. ignore
(rule 5): holds and releases (T1105, T1110, T1111, T1300-T1302, T1500-T1503, T2101-T2108, T2111, T2112), the bank (T0300-T0303, T0400,
T0401, T0403), currency conversion (T0200-T0202), the PayPal card (T0500-T0505), the card's cash-back bonus (T0801: +£105.03 in the real rows,
an owner question: not a payment fee), and every payment code T0000-T0019 when the money went OUT (a payment sent: T0003 pre-approved
payments to other merchants, T0000, T0011 in the real rows). unknown: every other code, and a payment code other than T0005 / T0006 with money
coming IN: kept, never guessed into money, shown (PPF14). A costed kind with an amount of the wrong sign (a sale not above 0, a refund not
below 0), a currency other than GBP (amount or fee), an ignored row with a fee, or a status other than S, V, P, D is "needs a look" (never
counted). In the real rows every code is understood (0 needs a look).

**PPF4. What a row costs, in pence, one rule.** sale and refund: minus the fee (PayPal signs a fee taken below 0: a cost above 0; a fee
given back: a cost below 0); chargeback and fee: minus (amount + fee) (money taken from the balance below 0: a cost above 0; a chargeback
reversal: money back, a cost below 0). PayPal's amounts are whole pence: no rounding anywhere (checklist 4), so a month is exactly the sum of
its days. Credits (checklist 1): a refund's fee back and a chargeback reversal are negative costs on their order on their own day; they never
set a price and never touch an order's goods or buying cost.

**PPF5. Whether it counts, in this order.** look (PPF3) → not_counted (ignored kind, status D) → outside (a shop CW does not hold: Hayati
Vapes, PPF21) → before_start (its shop not switched on, or its UK day before the shop's first fee day) → pending (status P: read again: the
nightly reads back to the oldest pending row, at most 31 days) → counts (S, and V: a reversed sale happened; its reversal is a row of its
own). The UK day is the day of transaction_initiation_date in Europe/London (the owner's Balance report ties on UK days; the lead's counts by
form were on UTC days: both shown in PPF19).

**PPF6. Its order.** The shop comes from the form (PPF21); then exactly ONE order of that shop whose sale_order.order_no is the number:
`order`; none: `no_order`; two or more: `ambiguous`; no shop's form: `no_number`. The lookup is made in the plan and made AGAIN right before
the commit under the write's guards (the guarded write's verify, checklist 11): an order of the number stored meanwhile makes the plan old
(made again). A row on no order is tried again every night (rematch: a no_order or ambiguous row whose number now has an order of its shop is
marked due): an order reaching CW late takes its fee (owner rule 1).

**PPF7. Where its money counts.** On an order: a sale's fee with no day of its own (alloc_day NULL) counts on the order's paid day
(sale_order.day): OrderSnapshots passes PaypalFees::orderFee to ProfitDays::orderShare, so an order paid later, or moved to another day, takes
it along; a refund's fee back, a chargeback's money and fees count on their own UK day (alloc_day). On no order: the shop's "not on an order"
line (fee_other) on its own UK day. An order not paid in CW (day NULL) holds its sale fee but counts it nowhere until it is paid (as its goods
and its delivery: --status says how many and how much). Every write of these figures goes through DeliveryBills::guardedWrite (THE guarded
write of the profit days: the order guards in name order, the day rows in key order without waiting, the orders' days read again, then the
rows and the figures by the difference, then verify): a fact may now name its profit_day figure (`field`: fee_cost or fee_other; the carriers'
by default; only the four figures, as it is written into SQL), and DeliveryBills::tidy keeps a day row that PayPal money counts on.
ProfitDays::compute works both figures out from scratch (PaypalFees::dayFigures), so the rebuild check holds them to their rows.

**PPF8. History.** paypal_txn_history (append-only: Grants): `changed` (what PayPal says: before and after) and `allocated` (where its money
counts: before and after), with the run and the actor; the row's version is its history's last.

**PPF9. The run, durable due marks, nothing half-written.** bin/paypal_fees.php --account=<name>: the job lock (Cli: one run of the job per
schema) and the account's own lock (GET_LOCK, 10 s). A run row (paypal_run) is written first. The days are read in windows of WINDOW_DAYS = 7
(PayPal allows 31; a week is about 2,000 rows); each window is read whole (every page) or refused whole, then stored in ONE transaction, its
new and changed rows marked `due` in that same transaction (checklist 14: durable before acting). Then every due row is decided, CHUNK = 200 a
guarded write, its due mark cleared in that write. A window that fails ends the run as failed; the windows before it stay stored, their rows
due; a decision that cannot be made now (an order busy) leaves its rows due; the next run decides them. A run that died is closed as failed
by the next one (it holds the account's lock). Nightly: the last profit.paypal_reread_days days (7) again, earlier to the oldest pending row,
never before the first fee day. Backfill: --from=YYYY-MM-DD [--to]. --decide: no PayPal call, the due rows decided. --status: read only.
Cron 05:20 UTC (05:20 UK in winter, 06:20 in summer: after PayPal's ~3 hour lag), before nothing that depends on it (the 03:40 rebuild of the
last 3 days re-checks the figures the next night).

**PPF10. PayPal's API, read only.** PaypalApi::PATHS: POST /v1/oauth2/token and GET /v1/reporting/transactions, nothing else (refused before
any request). fields=transaction_info, page_size 500, page 1..total_pages (at most 100 pages a window). Every request: 60 s timeout, 15 s to
connect, HTTPS only with the certificate checked, no redirect; a lost connection, 429 or 5xx is tried 4 times (waiting 2, 4, 8 s); a 401 on a
page asks for a new token once; any other status, an answer not in PayPal's shape, a page count that changes between pages, or rows that do
not add up to total_items refuses the whole window. A refusal says the call, the page and the HTTP status: never PayPal's text, the key or the
token. The token lives in the PaypalApi object for the run only. PayPal serves a row in the window of its last update too (a September dispute
hold's release came in October's read): the same row read again in another window is the same row (PPF2).

**PPF11. The key.** The account's key file: app.env `paypal_key_file_<account>` (CW_PAYPAL_KEY_FILE_<ACCOUNT>), a JSON object of exactly
client_id, client_secret, api_base (PayPal's live or sandbox host only), shop (the account's main shop) and account. Refused (the run does
not start, a failed run is recorded so the alert says it at once: paypal_failed) when the path is not set, the file is missing, a link or not
a plain file, not owned by root, readable by others, writable by its group, executable, larger than 4 KB, not that JSON, for another account,
or its shop is not the account's main shop. Never printed, never logged; PaypalKey hides the secret from dumps; the refusal names what is
wrong, never what the file holds. The go-live kit places it from the shop's config (Website/ajax/paypal/config.php live block) without
printing it, root:www-data 0640.

**PPF12. Who writes.** Only a server job (Caller::system): no person, no store, never through the web (no screen writes PayPal's rows).

**PPF13. Settings (Settings › Profit, each change kept with its history).** profit.paypal_from_<shop> (date; empty = not switched on):
all three empty from 0080; the go-live kit sets Vape and Go's to 2026-11-01 once its key file is placed, right before the backfill (no
"never read" alert in between); Electrofag and Vape Big later. profit.paypal_shops_vapeandgo: the shops of the account, the main shop first
(`vapeandgo,electrofag,hayati`). profit.paypal_form_<shop>: how the shop's order number looks in a PayPal invoice, a pattern from ^ to $ with
ONE (part), the number: Vape and Go `^([0-9]{7})-[0-9]{10}$`, Electrofag `^([0-9]{4,6})-[0-9]{10}$` (5,6xx now: 4 digits until 9,999, then 5),
Hayati Vapes `^faaeeb-([0-9]{1,6})$` (all 321 of its rows in the real data have the letters `faaeeb`). profit.paypal_reread_days (7, 1 to
31). profit.paypal_not_on_order_alarm (£50 a day: Vape and Go's own rows on no order are a few pounds a day; the other shops' rows never land
there).

**PPF14. The health alert.** Per account with a shop switched on, said in its main shop: paypal_not_read (no ok run for 26 hours, or none
ever), paypal_failed (the newest run failed: its reason in CW's words; also a key refused, or the account's shops or forms set wrong),
paypal_needs_look (rows not understood since the first fee day: never counted until a person looks; bin/paypal_fees.php --status lists them),
paypal_not_on_order (a day of the last re-read days whose money on no CW order is above the setting).

**PPF15. Full size, timed (the replay, PPF19, on the CW test box).** 14,302 real rows (1 Oct - 24 Nov): the backfill read + store + decide
in 17.6 s (PayPal's pages served 0.3 s, parse 0.9 s, store 3.5 s in 8 windows, decide 12.8 s in 72 guarded writes of 200: 0.15 s each on
average, 0.19 s the longest), peak memory 74 MB; the same days again 2.8 s (nothing new, changed or decided); a nightly of 7 days (1,851 rows)
0.4 s; Electrofag switched on (1,205 rows decided again) 1.2 s; 57 days rebuilt from scratch 2.6 s; the PayPal invariants 0.2 s. A guarded
write holds its order guards for well under the 3 s a snapshot waits (0.19 s at most, every row of a chunk in ONE update and ONE history
insert). The rematch reads plain indexed rows and marks by id: MySQL planned the first version (an UPDATE with a correlated EXISTS) row by row,
12 s at this size.

**PPF16. An order's page.** A "PayPal" table: each row on the order (its day, what it is, the day it counts on, what it costs) and the total.

**PPF17. Profit › Real profit.** "− Payment fees" is a shop's fee_cost + fee_other of the days (from its first fee day; 0 before it and for a
shop not switched on, whose "not built yet" note stays); the real profit takes it off. Global Payments' fees stay an expense.

**PPF18. The nightly checks (CW\Invariants: PaypalInvariants).** PP1 a decided row counts its whole cost in exactly one place or nowhere;
PP2 only in its own shop (never another shop's line), on an order of that shop with its number, a sale's fee on the order's day and the rest on
their own day; PP3 kind and cost are what the rules say; PP4 nothing due for 26 hours; PP5 no run "running" for 26 hours. Their cost: PP3 reads
every row 5,000 at a time (a year is about 100,000: well inside the 1 GB of bin/invariants.php).

**PPF19. The real-data replay (tests/Integration/Profit/PaypalReplayTest.php).** The lead's 14,302 rows reduced to the fields CW reads (no
payer, name, item text, balance; an invoice or custom field that is not a reference dropped), copied to the test box only for the run (removed
by a trap arranged before the copy, its absence checked after; cw_work/runs/paypal_replay_run.sh), served by the fake PayPal page by page.
It holds: the account's October on UK days to the owner's Balance report (sales' fees 6,449.95 = 2,584.30 + 3,865.65; refunds' fees back
81.16; chargebacks 288.79 less the 0.68 fee back on a reversal; chargeback fees 56.00; dispute fees 36.00); each shop's October by its form on
UTC days as the lead counted (Vape and Go 6,575 sales, fees 5,699.03; Electrofag 603, 611.90; Hayati Vapes 131, 108.71; no invoice 50,
21.08) and Vape and Go's on UK days (5,708.26); 0 rows not understood; Electrofag (not switched on) and Hayati Vapes never on Vape and Go's
lines; every penny once (Vape and Go's days = its counted rows); each day's figures = its rows'; a second run changes nothing; a rebuild of
every day gives the same pence; Electrofag switched on puts its October sales' fees (611.90) on its own orders, Vape and Go's days unchanged.

**PPF20. No undo release.** The owner (24 Nov 2026): CW is fixed forward. RollbackReleaseTest keeps the recipe's check (0e3db2a with 0080
added byte for byte); the release before never reads the new tables, and its rebuild of a day writes the columns it knows and leaves fee_cost
and fee_other at 0 on that day. (25 Nov 09:49: live moved to f044e2f, the expense page layout, no migration; 25 Nov 12:31: to 27dea71, the expense total with VAT, no migration; 25 Nov 13:31: to 04dbab6, its typing (CW-1176), no migration; 25 Nov 20:34: to 86c21af, CW-1180 "don't restock" with migration 0081; the

RollbackReleaseTest's BEFORE_ALSO names 0081 as the release before's own. 25 Nov 22:13: to 19980e0, CW-1182 "Claude reads uploads" with
migration 0082; the branch merged it (round 6) and the recipe is 19980e0 + 0080; BEFORE_ALSO names 0081 and 0082.)

**PPF21. One account, several shops, by the invoice's form.** A row's shop is the ONE shop of the account whose form its invoice matches
(else its custom field's); none, or two shops' forms: no shop (the main shop's "not on an order" line, match `no_number`). A shop CW does not
hold (Hayati Vapes) is `outside`: kept, never counted, never on another shop's line. A CW shop not switched on (Electrofag until its first fee
day) keeps its rows `before_start` with their shop: switched on, the next run counts them on its own orders and its own line (rematch marks
them due). The account's shops and forms are fingerprinted (PaypalFees::formsSig; each row keeps the fingerprint it was read under, read_sig,
and decided by, decided_sig): a change of them decides every row of the
account again, once. A shop or form setting that is not what PPF13 says refuses the run (paypal_bad_shops, paypal_bad_form) and the alert says
it.

**PPF22. Not built / owner questions.** (a) T0801 (the PayPal card's cash back, +£105.03 in the real rows): ignored as not a payment fee.
(b) Hayati Vapes' PayPal money (Oct 108.71 of sales' fees) is kept as facts only; it becomes counted if Hayati Vapes ever is a CW shop.
(c) A chargeback the shop ALSO refunds in its admin would count twice (the refund in the sales, the chargeback here): never seen in the real
rows; to watch. (d) No screen lists the PayPal rows (bin/paypal_fees.php --status does); a "PayPal" page under Profit is a later step.

### Fix round 1: the Codex review of dd93337 (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_r1_final.md`: 7 HIGH, 13 MEDIUM, 2 LOW) and the lead's decisions 1-8 (25 Nov 2026), each shown failing first on dd93337 (`runs/paypal_r1_red.log`: 14 of 14 red) and then green (PPF23-PPF33)

**PPF23. A chargeback's money counts only beyond what CW already holds as a refund on that order (the lead's decision 1; Codex HIGH).** For
each order, its chargebacks in time order use up its refunds in CW (sale_order.line_refund_inc + order_refund_inc + delivery_refund_inc, inc
VAT: the money a customer was given back), each at most its own money taken back; that part is `refund_offset_pence` and is not counted again.
The PayPal chargeback fee and dispute fees always count; a chargeback reversal (money back) counts whole. Every chargeback on the order is
decided in the same write (its siblings join the chunk), and decided again when the order's refunds in CW change (`refund_seen_pence`: the
nightly rematch compares). Example: £30 taken back, £10 refunded in the shop's admin: £20 + the £14 fee count; the rest refunded later: only
the £14 fee.

**PPF24. Refunds, chargebacks and fees follow PayPal's reference to their sale first (the lead's decision 3; Codex HIGH).** The row a
refund, chargeback or fee refers to (paypal_reference_id: its sale; a chargeback fee's chargeback, then its sale, three steps at most) gives
its shop and order number when that row has a shop; else its invoice, then its custom field (`matched_by`). A reference and an invoice that
disagree (another shop or number): needs a look (`ref_conflict`), never guessed. A row whose referred row is read later (another window) is
decided again then (the nightly rematch, and the run decides twice: a sale read now and the refund that refers to it).

**PPF25. A shop's form edited never moves money to another shop (the lead's decision 2; Codex HIGH).** A row that had a shop keeps it unless
the new settings positively match another shop: matching no shop now = needs a look (`form_lost`, its shop and number kept, never the main
shop's line); two shops' forms = needs a look (`form_overlap`). Only a row that never had a shop and matches none (no or an unrecognised
invoice) goes on the main shop's "not on an order" line.

**PPF26. Every decision keeps the forms it was made by (Codex MEDIUM).** `decided_sig` (the account's shops and forms) on each row, written by
every decision, --decide too; a row decided by other forms than now is decided again (replaces the run-level fingerprint).

**PPF27. A renumbered or doubled order is matched again (Codex MEDIUM).** The nightly rematch looks up every row on an order (its
`match_order_ref`, kept also when nothing counts) with its shop and number: another order, none, or two now: decided again; an ambiguous row
when the count of its orders changed.

**PPF28. Switching off needs no PayPal read; the pages show what the days hold (Codex MEDIUM x2).** bin/paypal_fees.php makes the local
decisions first (no PayPal call) on every run, so a shop switched off, forms changed or orders that reached CW are decided even when the key or
PayPal fails. Profit > Real profit's payment fees are the profit days' fee figures of the days asked for, always (the same figures as the order
pages and the rebuild: a month plus the next = the two months; a sale fee follows its order to its paid day); `fees_from` only says whether a
shop's fees are read. Under "− Payment fees" a line "of which: PayPal money on no order" shows fee_other (the lead's decision 8; Codex LOW).

**PPF29. The key names its merchant, every page must be that merchant's (the lead's decision 4; Codex HIGH + MEDIUM x2).** The key file
holds a 6th field `merchant_id` (PayPal's account number of the merchant); every page whose `account_number` is not it is refused
(`paypal_wrong_account`, nothing stored). A key file readable by its group must be root:www-data (or root:root); the checks are made on the
opened file's descriptor (fstat: the same inode as the path). The kit: production's key must be PayPal's live host; its shop is checked
before the file is replaced; the key goes over `ssh -T` (no terminal, nothing echoed).

**PPF30. A long outage is read back; the alert waits for it (the lead's decision 5; Codex HIGH).** The nightly reads from the earlier of the
re-read days and the day before the last day read without a gap (coveredUntil: the ok runs' from_day..to_day joined from the first fee day),
never before the first fee day. The "not read" alert stays until the reads have no gap up to yesterday.

**PPF31. PayPal's pages, refresh time and deadline (Codex MEDIUM x3).** A row twice in one window (its id and code: PayPal's pages moved) reads
the whole window again, 3 times, then refuses it. last_refreshed_datetime is read strictly into CW's UTC time (else none) and never logged as
PayPal wrote it; PayPal's data not refreshed for 26 hours is an alert (`paypal_stale`). The job has an overall deadline (nightly 240 s, a
backfill 20 min): no request starts after it and none lasts beyond it; the cron line adds `timeout 300` (the installer drains for 6 minutes).

**PPF32. The "not on an order" alarm is per shop, its setting in pence (Codex MEDIUM).** One alert per shop (its own line); the setting takes
pounds with at most two decimals (Settings rule `pence`). A due row is timed from `due_since` (when it became due), not its last change
(PP4; Codex LOW).

**PPF33. Only order numbers are kept of the invoice and custom fields (the lead's decision 7; Codex MEDIUM).** Kept as written only when the
text is an order number in the form of one of the account's shops; anything else (a phone number, free text) is never stored, only that
there was one (`dropped`).

Also (the kit; Codex HIGH x2, MEDIUM x2): a backfill asked by hand that finds the job's lock held is BUSY (exit 4), never a skipped success;
the kit's gate is bound to ITS run (the id its own line prints, RUN=<id> ok: an ok backfill of the account from the pinned first day to the
day asked) and reconciles every shop's PayPal allocations, worked out on their own, against its profit days day by day; `golive.sh apply`
checks the exact start again (or, after a stopped apply of the same tip, only the states its own install leaves); the switch-on step sets
Electrofag's first fee day too (2026-12-01, its first real-profit day; tested: the day before out, the day itself in).

### Final review: Codex astra on 5f197ca (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_final_astra_final.md`: 13 HIGH, 9 MEDIUM, 3 LOW), each shown failing first on 5f197ca (`runs/paypal_r2_red.log`: 8 of 8 red) and then green (PPF34-PPF40)

**PPF34. A chargeback's refund offset: only from chargebacks that count, only from refunds CW counts, never from PayPal's own refunds (a1, a3, a4; HIGH x3).**
The order's budget is the refunds CW counts in profit on it (lines, order level, delivery, inc VAT; none while the order is not paid in CW,
none on a re-send: its refunds take nothing off) LESS PayPal's own refunds of that order (T1107, done or reversed, counted or before the first
fee day: PayPal paid that money out, so it is real money out beside the chargeback). Only the chargebacks that COUNT on that order (not
pending, denied, not understood, before the first fee day, of two forms, another currency) use the budget, in time order, each at most its own
money taken back. The budget a decision used is kept (`refund_seen_pence`); the nightly rematch works it out again (paid, unpaid, a re-send, a
refund in CW, a PayPal refund read) and decides the chargeback again when it differs. Example (a3): a £20 refund PayPal paid out that CW
holds, then an £80 chargeback: both count (£20 + £80). Example (a4): £30 refunded in CW on an order CW does not count yet, a £30 chargeback:
£30 counts now; the order paid in CW later: the chargeback is decided again and counts £0 (its refund counts instead). **The lead's question
(a3):** PayPal's refund rows have no "this refund is a dispute's" mark, so CW tells the two apart by whether PayPal paid the refund out (a
T1107 on the order). My pick: the rule above (a CW refund PayPal did not pay out is taken as the chargeback's own, e.g. staff marking the
order refunded after the chargeback; one PayPal paid out never offsets). The other way would be no offset at all (every chargeback counts
whole, and a CW refund recorded because of the chargeback counts twice). Decide before the go-live if the pick is not right.

**PPF35. A moved chargeback re-decides its old order's others; children follow their parent; an unresolved parent holds its child; the main
shop is pinned (a2, a5, a6, a8; HIGH x4).** A refund or chargeback decided brings into the same guarded write every refund and chargeback on
the same order number of its shop, as resolved now AND as stored (so a chargeback moved from A to B gives A's budget back to A's other
chargebacks at once). A row whose shop, number, order or state changes marks due, in the same write, every row whose PayPal reference names
it (its refunds, chargebacks, fees: fee -> chargeback -> sale), decided in the same decideAll (up to four rounds; a row decided more than
eight times is a loop: refused). A row whose referred row has no clear shop (a conflict, two forms, a shop lost, unresolved itself) needs a
look (`ref_unresolved`); a row whose PayPal reference (a transaction) is not held by CW and whose own fields name no shop needs a look
(`ref_missing`; checked on the real rows: every refund, chargeback and fee of Oct-Nov carries its own invoice, so none is held). Neither is
ever put on the main shop's line. `profit.paypal_main_<account>` pins the main shop (vapeandgo): a shops list that does not start with it is
refused (`paypal_bad_shops`) before any decision or read, --decide included.

**PPF36. Of the invoice and custom fields only a form's capture is kept, and the evidence is never lost to a re-read (a7, e1; HIGH +
MEDIUM).** The store keeps `invoice_state` (none, order, dropped, overlap) with `invoice_shop` and `invoice_no` (the shop whose form captured
it and the number: never the text, so a form like ^([0-9]{7})-.+$ never keeps the phone number after it), the same for the custom field. A
capture kept before stays when a later read's forms capture nothing (a form narrowed meanwhile); a capture of a later read replaces it. A
decision uses the captures (a form edit takes effect at a row's next read, never by --decide alone). Every row of a window's days is marked
read with the account's shops and forms (`read_sig`); the nightly reads back from the oldest day of rows read under other forms (never
before the first fee day), so a form put back recovers the rows first read under the narrowed one.

**PPF37. The newer PayPal version wins (a9; MEDIUM).** transaction_updated_date to the microsecond: an older version than the one kept changes
nothing; the same time with other facts keeps the facts, marks the row `pp_conflict` (needs a look, never counted; the history keeps both)
until a newer version says which; a newer one replaces them and clears the mark.

**PPF38. Coverage only with fresh data, window by window; the stale alert at the read (c1, c2, c3; HIGH x2 + MEDIUM).** Each window stored
proves its days only up to the last whole UK day before PayPal's last_refreshed_datetime (none given: nothing proven); the run's
`covered_to` moves on window by window and is kept when a later window fails or the deadline ends the run, so a catch-up longer than one
night resumes where it stopped. coveredUntil joins every run's from_day..covered_to (any state). The "not read" alert wants the coverage to
reach the day before yesterday (the 05:20 nightly proves yesterday); `paypal_stale` is PayPal's data more than 12 hours old WHEN CW READ IT
(or no refresh time given), by the newest ok run: never against the clock between two nightlies.

**PPF39. The merchant and the live host are CW's own settings, checked at every run; a refusal is a failed run (b1, b2; HIGH + MEDIUM).**
`profit.paypal_merchant_<account>` (PayPal's account number of the merchant; the go-live kit sets it) must equal the key's merchant_id (and
every page's account_number, PPF29); `profit.paypal_live_<account>` (true) requires the live host. Not set, another merchant, or a sandbox key:
refused before reading, recorded as a failed run (`paypal_failed` at once), exit 3.

**PPF40. The rest (c4, e2, e3, d6; LOW x3 + MEDIUM).** PP1 and PP2 judge decided rows only (a row due keeps its old place against its new facts
until decided; PP4 times it); an offset only on a row that counts. An unknown status needs a look before an ignored row is let go.
--status counts every row that needs a look and shows the newest 50 with CW's own row id. The job reads PayPal only when a shop of the account
has its first fee day set AND reached (the quick stop clears every shop's day of the shared account; Electrofag's day to come reads nothing).

Also (the kit; d1-d7): the apply gate accepts a part-applied 0080 (its tables empty and of the migration's shape, no migration record) and
the installer finishes it under its lock; `install_cron.sh --expect-revision=<tip> --expect-active=<release>` checks the pinned tip and the
starting release under the installer's own lock; the backfill gate reconciles gross, offsets and net (net = gross − offsets; the days hold
the net, less sale fees on orders not paid in CW) and the day figures in ONE consistent read; a row needing a look, a row still due or money
counted nowhere in the pinned days fails the gate; the RUNBOOK's quick stop clears every shop of the shared account; returning from the
rollback release rebuilds every day from the first fee day and reconciles them.

### Round 3: the Codex astra re-check of 20faffa (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_verify_astra_final.md`: NO GO; 10 findings PARTLY fixed, 8 new) and the lead's decisions (25 Nov 2026), each shown failing first on 20faffa (`runs/paypal_r3_red.log`) and then green (PPF41-PPF46)

The lead's design rule for this round: **when CW cannot be sure, the row needs a look (with its reason), never a guessed shop or a guessed
offset.** A look costs staff one click; a guessed shop silently mis-states a partner's profit.

**PPF41. Coverage is only what PayPal's answer proves (c1; HIGH).** A window proves its days only up to the last whole UK day before the
LEAST fresh `last_refreshed_datetime` of its pages (a page without one: nothing of the window is proven), and never past the end of the
interval its pages say they cover (an `end_date` more than a minute before the end asked for: proven to the last whole UK day before it; a
`start_date` later than asked: nothing), at most its own last day; a page that says it is another page than the one asked for refuses the
window whole (`paypal_moved`). The run's covered_to moves on only while each window proved all of its days; the rest of the days stay to be
read (the nightly starts from the day before the last day proven) and the "not read" alert stays until they are. Example: a 1-7 Nov request
answered for 1-4 Nov with a fresh refresh time: covered to 4 Nov, the next night reads from 3 Nov, the alert clears once the days are read
whole. (A 60 s slack is PayPal's own rounding of the times asked for; production's answers have not been seen with their start/end dates:
if they differ, the backfill gate STOPs, never certifies.)

**PPF42. Which version wins, and what its captures are (a9, a7, NEW correction, NEW equal time; HIGH x3 + MEDIUM).** A version with no
update time is OLDER than any dated one (it never overwrites a dated version, never erases its time); two of none are the same unknown time.
A NEWER version is what PayPal says now: its facts AND its captures, whatever they are (an invoice cleared with a Hayati Vapes order in the
custom field: Hayati's, off Vape and Go; an invoice two shops' forms take: a look, `form_overlap`), never an old capture put back over it.
The SAME version (the same time) read under the same forms with other facts OR other captures (another shop, another number) is PayPal
saying two things of one version: the kept facts and captures stay and the row needs a look (`pp_conflict`) until a newer version says
which, never "the last read wins". Read under OTHER forms (a form edited), its captures are the forms' of now, except that a capture a
narrowed form no longer makes is kept together with the forms it was made by (`read_sig`), and two shops' forms now is a positive overlap
held for a look even for a row recognised before. `read_sig` is set only on a row a read gave and applied: never on a row PayPal left out of
the read of its day (it keeps the forms it was read by and is read again), never from an older version.

**PPF43. A chargeback counts in full only when PayPal's own refunds account for its order's refunds in CW; else a look (the lead's
decision a3 with his correction of 25 Nov ~11:20; a4; HIGH x2; it replaces PPF23's and PPF34's offset).** For a chargeback (T1106, T1201,
and its reversal T1202) that would count on an order, the order's refund budget = the refunds CW counts in profit on it (by the profit's own
line rules, ProfitMath::line: a line's sale with its refund against without it, so a refund on a cancelled or free line, or beyond a
restocked line's sale, counts nothing; the order-level and delivery refunds; none while the order is not paid in CW or is a re-send) MINUS
PayPal's own refunds of that order that CW has read and matched to it (T1107, done or reversed, counted or before the first fee day): a
refund PayPal paid out never offsets a chargeback (PPF34). Budget above 0 (CW holds refund money that did not go out through PayPal: staff
recorded it because of the chargeback, or paid it by bank; CW cannot tell which): the chargeback needs a look (`refund_not_on_paypal`, the
budget kept in `refund_seen_pence`; the nightly rematch decides it again when the order's refunds or PayPal's refunds of it change), nothing
of it counted, never an offset by guess. Budget 0: the chargeback counts in full. An order PAID BEFORE the account's first day read from
PayPal (its earliest first fee day, where the backfill starts: its PayPal refunds before it were never read): a chargeback on it with ANY
refund in CW needs a look, whatever PayPal refunds of it were read. The chargeback and dispute fees always count (they are certain);
`refund_offset_pence` stays 0. Chargebacks are rare (1 in 1-23 Nov), so a look each time is cheap. Examples: a £100 order, £20 refunded
through PayPal (T1107) and in CW, then an £80 chargeback: budget 0, both count (£100 out); £30 refunded in CW with no PayPal refund, a £30
chargeback: budget £30, a look (its £14 fee counts); PayPal's £30 refund of that order read later: budget 0, the chargeback counts £30; £30
refunded only on a cancelled line: budget 0 (it counts nothing in profit), the chargeback counts; an order paid 28 Oct with £15 refunded in CW
and PayPal's £15 refund of it read on 2 Nov, a chargeback: a look (PayPal's refunds of it before 1 Nov were never read); paid 28 Oct with no
refund in CW: counts in full. (The real rows hold one chargeback with a PayPal refund of the same sale: a 20 Oct T1106 of £29.08 and a 22 Oct
T1107 of £15.99, both money out.)

**PPF44. The old days in their own windows; forward progress every night (c2; HIGH).** The nightly reads FORWARD first, from the earlier of
the re-read days and the day before the last day proven (nightlyFrom), so old pending rows never move the start back; then the old days in
their own windows (nightlyExtra: the days before the forward start of rows still pending and of rows last read under other forms with an
invoice or custom field, at most PENDING_DAYS = 31 days back, never before the first fee day, as ranges of at most a window); they never
move covered_to. What the forward days brought is decided before any old day is read, and when a window fails (or the deadline ends the run)
what was stored before it is decided at once, the run failed all the same (a catch-up longer than a night goes on night by night: the test
reads two windows a night and finishes in two). A row last read under other forms whose shop the forms of now might make otherwise (its
shop's field captured by none or two of the forms then) that is older than the days read again needs a look (`form_unread`), never a shop
guessed from the forms of then; once a read under the forms of now gives it (a backfill of its day), it is decided again (released), also
when nothing about it changed.

**PPF45. Followed to the end, held with its parent, conflict first, every chargeback's order guarded (a2, a6, NEW ignored, NEW fully offset;
HIGH x2 + MEDIUM x2).** A decision follows the refunds and chargebacks of the same order numbers (as resolved now and as stored) until no
new one comes, up to SIBLING_PASSES = 64 steps; beyond, the write is refused and the run fails with that reason (`paypal_siblings`), never a
silent stop half-way. A row whose referred row has two PayPal versions at one time (`pp_conflict`) gets no shop from it (`ref_unresolved`),
through every step of the chain, and follows it again once a newer version settles it. Two versions at one time are checked BEFORE an
ignored row is let go (a fee-free T0801 read again with a £14 fee: a look, the alert on). Every order a chargeback is on, as resolved now and
as stored, is guarded in its guarded write whatever its money (£0 before and after included), so no snapshot changes the refunds it was
decided by between its last look and its commit.

**PPF46. The kit (d1, NEW backfill gate, d7; HIGH x2 + MEDIUM).** `golive.sh check` (any day: after midnight too) recognises the kit's own
stopped install of this tip (its durable marker) as the resumable state and says so; a part-applied 0080's tables must be empty and of the
tip's shape: columns, each column's type and NULL, primary and unique keys (`tables.shape` from the tip's SQL). backfill-check needs the
backfill's run proven read (covered_to) to its last day, a finished UK day (golive.sh backfill: yesterday by default). The return from the
rollback release rebuilds from the earliest day any PayPal money counts on (`box.sh rebuild-from`) and reconciles every shop against the
release live then (`box.sh reconcile-days --release=<commit>`).

### Round 4, the last fix round: the Codex astra final of df9b8d3 (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_final2_astra_final.md`: NO GO, 8 High + 5 Medium) and the Fable final review (GO with Mediums and Lows), with the lead's decisions (25 Nov 2026), each shown failing first on df9b8d3 (`runs/paypal_r4_red.log`: 15 of 15 red) and then green (PPF47-PPF57)

The lead's design rule still holds: **when CW cannot be sure, the row needs a look (with its reason), never a guessed shop or offset.**

**PPF47. The sales no shop's form takes stay on Vape and Go's "not on an order" line (H1; the owner, 25 Nov ~04:25).** A PayPal row whose
invoice and custom field no shop's form takes (no invoice, or one no form takes: 17 sales, £6.18 of fees in 1-23 Nov) counts on the account's
main shop's "not on an order" line, as the owner approved. The kit prints their count and pence on their own line in backfill-check (never
hidden in the pin) and STOPs when they are not the pinned ones. An Electrofag sale read while its form was narrowed is such a row under the
forms of then; once the form is put back it is held (PPF48) until a read under the forms of now gives it to Electrofag.

**PPF48. A form change holds every row read under other forms, whatever its age, and its children (H3; HIGH).** CW keeps no invoice text
(PPF36), so a capture made under other shops or forms than now (read_sig not the forms of now) is no more certain than none: such a row with an
invoice or custom field captured (by one shop, none or two) needs a look (`form_unread`) at once, whatever its age, until a read under the
forms of now gives it (the nightly reads the last PENDING_DAYS = 31 days of such rows again in their own windows; older ones need a backfill
of their days, `bin/paypal_fees.php --from --to`). A row whose parent (the row its PayPal reference names) is so held, or of two PayPal
versions, gets no shop from it (`ref_unresolved`): an invoice-less £14 fee never falls to Vape and Go while its sale is held. When a row's
facts, captures or forms change at a read, or its place moves at a decision, the rows that refer to it, and those that refer to them (three
steps, as the shop is followed), are due again in the same transaction: a fee whose chargeback is denied (its own place unchanged) still
follows its sale once the sale is read under the forms of now. This replaces PPF44's "older than the days read again" and PPF42's "a capture
a narrowed form no longer makes is kept" as a place to count (the capture is still kept, as evidence, with the forms that made it).

**PPF49. A row's own fields first: two shops are a look, never "the first field wins" (H2; HIGH).** A row whose invoice and custom field are
captured by two different shops' forms is a look (`field_conflict`), and so is a row of two shops' forms on either field (`form_overlap`):
whatever its PayPal reference says (a referenced sale never overrides a fee's own overlapping invoice), and its children wait with it
(`ref_unresolved`). The order NUMBERS of the invoice and the custom field are NOT compared: on every real row with both (13,238 of the lead's
14,302), the custom field carries another number of the same shop (Vape and Go's own id, 188,379 above the order number, with the invoice's
10-digit tail; Electrofag's about 1,059 above), so comparing them would hold every row. For the same reason a row whose shop comes from its
custom field alone gets that shop but NO order number: its shop's "not on an order" line, never an order found by the custom field's number
(no real row has a custom field without an invoice; the number would one day be a real order's). Its reference vs its own invoice: a
different shop, or a different number of its invoice, is `ref_conflict` as before. QUESTION FOR THE LEAD (my pick built): the custom-only
row on its shop's line (a) rather than a look (b).

**PPF50. A chargeback's money held, its fee counted (H4, H5; HIGH x2).** A chargeback (T1106, T1201, T1202) whose MONEY CW cannot place surely
is a look whose FEE on the same row is certain and counts on its own day: `refund_not_on_paypal` (its order's refunds in CW that PayPal's own
refunds of it do not cover, PPF43; the fee on that order), `order_ambiguous` (its order number has two or more orders of its shop: which
order's refunds? the fee on the shop's "not on an order" line; held until one order has the number, then decided by PPF43). Both parts are
reconciled on their own: PP1 holds such a row's allocation to exactly its fee (-fee_pence) and its money to nowhere; 0080's checks allow an
allocation on a look only for these two reasons on a chargeback. Example: £30 back and a £14 fee on one T1201, £30 refunded in CW not on
PayPal: a look, £14 on the order on its day; PayPal's own £30 refund of the order read later: the row counts £44 whole.

**PPF51. An order paid before the first day read: ANY refund recorded in CW makes its chargeback a look (H6; HIGH).** CW tracks the refunds
recorded on the order (every line's refund, a cancelled, free or removed line's too, the order-level and delivery refunds, as recorded)
apart from the refunds the profit counts (PPF43); for an order paid before the account's first day read from PayPal, any recorded refund is
a look (`refund_not_on_paypal`, the recorded pence kept in refund_seen_pence). Paid in November, a cancelled line's refund still counts
nothing and the chargeback counts whole (a4).

**PPF52. A day is proven only by pages that say their whole interval; the catch-up resumes on the first day not proven (H7, H8; HIGH x2).**
EVERY page must give its start_date and end_date (one that does not: nothing of its window proven); a start later than asked proves nothing; an
end earlier than asked by even a second proves only up to the last whole UK day before it (no slack below the end asked for; PayPal printing a
LATER end proves the whole); a row PayPal repeats in its answer (PPF55) proves nothing of its window. The forward read is window by window:
a window whose answer's own interval ended early is followed by one from its FIRST DAY NOT PROVEN (split), so a 1-7 Nov request answered for
1-2 Nov is followed by 3 Nov, never 1 Nov again; the run's covered_to moves only while the windows join without a gap; a window that proves
nothing leaves a gap (its rows stored all the same). The nightly starts from the first day not proven (or the re-read days, the earlier).
The run's summary (and bin/paypal_fees.php's line, which the go-live kit prints) says why windows proved less than their days ("a page without
its start or end", "a page without its refresh time", "a page starting later than asked", "a row given twice", "its answer ended early",
"PayPal's data not finished past <day>"), so a gate that STOPs on coverage says why. (This replaces PPF41's 60 s slack.)

**PPF53. The key file is root's alone; PayPal reached before the key (Fable F-M1, F-check).** The key file is root:root 0600 (0400 passes):
PaypalKey refuses any group or other read, so nothing the web app runs as (www-data) can read it; only bin/paypal_fees.php reads it, run by
root's cron (`grep -rln "PaypalKey::load\|paypal_key_file" src public bin`: PaypalKey itself and bin/paypal_fees.php). The kit's key-place
writes 0600, key-check wants it, and before the key `box.sh paypal-reach` wants PayPal's API host to answer 401 to a request with no key
(outbound HTTPS from the CW box works), else STOP.

**PPF54. An order snapshot decides its chargebacks again at once (M1; MEDIUM; Codex's earlier a4 second half).** OrderSnapshots::apply marks
the PayPal chargebacks of the order (of its shop with its number, now or before, and those on it) due IN ITS OWN TRANSACTION, and right after
the commit decides them (PaypalFees::decideRows: the guarded write takes the order's guard, then the rows that follow them): a refund recorded
in CW never counts beside the chargeback's money until the nightly. A decision that cannot be made then (an order busy, the account's settings
wrong) leaves them due, durable, for the next PayPal run; the snapshot is never refused for it. One indexed read per snapshot
(ix_paypal_txn_shop_no).

**PPF55. The run's time and PayPal's repeats (M2, F-L5; MEDIUM + LOW).** Each window stored is decided at once; a window is started only
before the run's deadline less DECIDE_RESERVE_SEC (60 s; PaypalApi's own deadline is the same, bin/paypal_fees.php), so the decisions of what
was stored always have their time, and a deadline that comes right after a window is stored still decides it (the run is failed all the
same, covered_to kept). A row PayPal gives twice in one answer (its id AND event code): the window is read again (READS = 3 in all), then taken
as it stands: the same content twice is kept once (counted in the run's summary and the CLI's line), two contents of one row keep the newer
and the row is a look (`pp_conflict`) until a later read gives one; never the whole window refused night after night; the window proves
none of its days (a repeat may stand for a row its moving pages left out), so the next run reads them again.

**PPF56. The alerts (F-M2, F-L7; MEDIUM + LOW).** The rows that need a look are said at most ONCE A DAY (the problem's repeat_seconds, which
AlertDispatch takes when longer than alerts.repeat_minutes), in words that say what they are: "N PayPal rows that need a look (reason count,
...; the newest day). The money in doubt is not counted until the CW team looks at them." (never "does not understand"; staff closing a look
is a later step, CW-1177). No "never read" alert while the account's newest run is still running within its time and a margin (the first
backfill right after the switch-on); a run still "running" past its time (nightly 240 s, backfill 1,200 s) and RUN_MARGIN_SEC (10 min) died:
the "failed" alert says so at once, not 26 hours later.

**PPF57. The kit (M3, M4, M5, F-M3, F-L1, F-L8).** backfill-check compares the pins with the rows THE CERTIFIED RUN returned (last_run of it or
later) and STOPs on any row of the backfill's days only an earlier run returned (a proven re-read no longer gives it); no refund offset may
stand anywhere (0080's check: refund_offset_pence = 0; PP1; the gate) and Vape and Go's net must equal its gross; a part-applied 0080 is
resumed only when its tables match the tip's SQL in column defaults and AUTO_INCREMENT too, and profit_day's two columns (when there) are the
tip's signed BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; the RUNBOOK says what to do when the gate STOPs for an honest reason after the switch-on (nothing is
undone: the nightly keeps reading; PIN_EXPECT changed with its reason, make_kit_sha.sh, golive.sh check, golive.sh backfill again); the What's
new draft says Electrofag's fees start by themselves on 1 December 2026, names no command in the staff text and takes its figure from the
gate's "on its profit days of 1-23 Nov" line; the backfill's outer limits are above its own deadline (timeout 1500 > 1,200 s);
`--apply-gate` (never read) is gone; the UNDO_INDEX line gives the undo order (this one first, then #622, #620, #619, #615, #614, #606).

### Round 5: the Codex astra final of 66b62d5 and the kit (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_r4_final_astra_final.md`: NO GO, 3 High + Mediums + Lows), with the lead's 16 decisions (`runs/paypal_round5_brief.md`, 25 Nov 2026), each shown failing first on 66b62d5 (`runs/paypal_r5_red.log`) and then green (PPF58-PPF69)

**PPF58. The looks alert: once a day across episodes, in staff words (the lead's decision 2).** The rows that need a look are said at most once a
day (LOOK_REPEAT_SEC) and the account's last time is KEPT across episodes: a look said at 06:00 that clears at 07:00 and comes back at 08:00 is
not said again before 06:00 the next day (AlertDispatch keeps last_sent_at of a problem that has its own repeat_seconds when it comes back; a
"back to normal" for the cleared one is still sent). The reasons are said in staff words (Ui\Words::PAYPAL_LOOK, one for every look reason of
PaypalFees::LOOK_REASONS; WordsTest holds every code to a word), never a code: "a chargeback on an order refunded outside PayPal (its fee is
counted): 1". The health problem carries the reasons as data (reason => rows); its detail (the job's log) names none.

**PPF59. An order snapshot queues its order; its chargebacks are decided after the OUTERMOST commit (the lead's decisions 7 and 13; Codex M1 and
the PayPal row lock).** The snapshot writes no PayPal row: when the order has PayPal chargebacks (two plain indexed reads, nothing locked) it
inserts one row of its own into paypal_order_due (0080's fourth table, keyed by an id with an index on the order; no unique key, no foreign
key: an insert that waits for nobody) IN its transaction, so it never waits for a chargeback row a PayPal read or decision holds while it holds
the order's guard and its profit days (proved: a test holds the chargeback's row FOR UPDATE while the snapshot of its order commits in well
under the row wait). Right after the OUTERMOST commit (Db::afterCommit: at once when the snapshot's own transaction was the outermost, after
its guards are let go; else after the caller's transaction commits, never before it, dropped on its rollback) PaypalFees::afterSnapshot takes
the queue rows of that order (its chargebacks found again and marked due and the queue rows taken away in ONE short transaction, with NOWAIT:
a row a PayPal read holds is never waited for) and decides them (decideRows, the orders' guards); what cannot be done then stays queued or
due, durable: every decideAll (each PayPal run, `--decide`, the switch-off) takes the account's queue FIRST. A caller's transaction begun
outside Db::transaction() is not seen (afterCommit returns false): the queue row stands for it. PP6: a queued order waiting 26 hours is a
finding. `--status` says how many orders are queued.

**PPF60. Two contents of a row in ONE answer, and repeats found before PayPal's count (the lead's decisions 11 and 12).** pp_conflict 2 is a row
one answer gave two contents of (the newer kept, a look) apart from 1, two reads that disagree on one version (a look until a newer version):
a later read that gives the row once says which version PayPal has (taken as a newer version would be: its facts, its captures; the look
cleared), so £20 and £30 in one answer followed by £30 alone counts £30; an answer giving the two contents again (in any order) is still 2,
never taken for a contradiction between reads. PaypalApi counts the repeats of an answer BEFORE comparing its rows
with PayPal's total_items: A, A, B for two declared rows is a repeat (read again, READS times, then given back as it stands: B's £60 fee is
stored and counted, the window proves nothing); a count the rows do not make with no repeat at all is still refused (after the reads again).

**PPF61. An older version with other money is said on its row (the lead's decision 9; Codex M3).** A run that reads an OLDER version of a row
(by PayPal's update time) than the one kept keeps the newer, and when the older one says other money or another place (any of PayPal's facts
but its update time; its captures when read under the forms of the kept ones) the row says so: older_run = that run (cleared by the next read
that gives the kept version or one of the same money). The go-live gate STOPs on any row of the backfill's days whose older_run is the
certified run or later (its pins are what that run returned, never a newer version it did not).

**PPF62. A fee's own invoice number stands when its reference gives the same shop and no number (the lead's decision 4; H2).** The order numbers
of a row and of the row its reference names are compared only when BOTH have one; a reference that gives the same shop and no number (a sale
known by its custom field alone) leaves the row its own invoice number: the £14 dispute fee whose invoice is Vape and Go's order 1312001 counts
on that order, never a conflict (matched_by stays `reference`: it was found through it).

**PPF63. Captures of two forms are never mixed (the lead's decision 5; H3).** CW keeps no text, so a capture's forms are known only for a whole
read. When the same version is read under other forms and a narrowed form no longer makes a capture the forms it was read by made, the row
keeps ALL its captures with the forms that made them (never the old custom field's capture beside the invoice's of now): it is held
(form_unread) until one read under the forms of now gives all of its captures, or those forms are put back. Codex's sequence: a form taking
15... puts a custom-only £1.20 sale on Vape and Go's line; changed to 13... and read again: held, its captures the 15... form's; the 15... form
put back: its line again, never order 1312001.

**PPF64. A page's interval at PayPal's own precision (the lead's decision 6; H7).** PaypalApi::time keeps the fraction of a second PayPal gives
(last_refreshed_datetime, start_date, end_date: CW's UTC time to the microsecond) and a page's start and end are compared with the bounds asked
for (whole seconds, as sent) at that precision: a start of 00:00:00.900 is later than 00:00:00 (nothing proven), an end of 23:59:58.900 ends
early. PayPal's real shapes (the lead's probe of 25 Nov: 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z .. 2026-11-24T23:59:59Z exact; today's end = its refresh time)
prove as before.

**PPF65. What a run could not decide by its deadline gets a budget of its own (the lead's decision 8; Codex M2).** When the deadline (or an order
busy) stops the decisions of a window the run stored, the run decides what is left at once with LOCAL_DECIDE_SEC (30 s) of its own and no
PayPal call, never with the deadline that has just run out (the nightly's 240 s + 30 s stays inside the cron's `timeout 300`; a backfill's
1,200 + 30 s inside the kit's 1,500 s); the run is failed all the same and what is still left is decided by the next run first.

**PPF66. A shop switched off takes its held chargebacks' fees with it (the lead's decision 10; HIGH).** A shop's first fee day set, moved or
cleared re-decides, besides its rows that count, its chargebacks held for a look whose FEE counts (refund_not_on_paypal, order_ambiguous), so
their fee leaves the profit with the switch-off (before_start); `--decide` and a rebuild of the days agree.

**PPF67. A row that counts nothing whatever its shop is not marked again and again (the lead's decision 14).** An ignored or denied row
(not_counted) whose captures were read under other forms is decided again once (its decided_sig differs) and then never marked again at every
pass (beyond the days read again it would never be read again: a backlog decided four times a pass); the rows that refer to it are still due
again whenever it is read (store) or moves (decide), so a fee follows its denied chargeback's sale once it is read under the forms of now.

**PPF68. The key file root:root, mode 0600 or 0400 exactly (the lead's decision 1).** PaypalKey refuses a key file that is not owned by root,
whose group is not root, or whose mode is anything but 0600 or 0400 (a write-only, a run bit, set-id or sticky: refused), the go-live gate's
own rule, so the nightly never takes a key the gate refuses. The kit's key-place writes its temporary file in the key's own folder (one
mount: the rename is atomic).
