**PPF69. The kit (the lead's decisions 3, 9, 15, 16).** A later day's backfill (the gate STOPped for an honest reason, the pins changed: RUNBOOK)
needs no same-day key marker: `golive.sh check` of that day, then `golive.sh backfill` verifies the live release (the tip, 0080 whole, its cron)
and the key (key-check) itself (box.sh resume-backfill). The gate says a held chargeback's money ("held for a look") and its fee ("counted")
apart from the rows never counted, and STOPs on a row of the backfill's days the certified run returned in an older version with other money
(PPF61). A part-applied 0080 is resumed only when its tables' CHECK constraints (as MySQL states them, compared after one normalisation on
both sides) and ALL their indexes (the snapshot lookup index too) are the tip's, and paypal_order_due is one of its four tables. TARGET=test
runs offline: the trial gives paypal-reach's answer itself (PPKIT_TRIAL_REACH, 401 by default; production keeps the real request).

### Round 6: the Codex astra final of 9b46fe0 and the kit (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_r5_final_astra_final.md`: NO GO), with the lead's 14 decisions (25 Nov 2026 ~22:05), each shown failing first on 9b46fe0 (`runs/paypal_r6_red.log`, `runs/paypal_r6_red2.log`) and then green (PPF70-PPF78)

**PPF70. A UK day is complete only when PayPal's answer reaches the next day's start (the lead's decision 3; H7).** A window whose answer ends
before the end asked for proves its days only up to the day BEFORE the UK day of that end, at the precision PayPal gives it: an answer of
1-7 Nov ending at 4 Nov 23:59:59.250 proves 1-3 Nov (the 4th's last 0.75 s were not answered for: a £60 fee at .750 would be skipped), and
the next window starts on the 4th (PPF52); an answer ending at 5 Nov 00:00:00 proves 1-4 Nov. An end at or after the one asked for (full
precision) proves the whole window, as before.

**PPF71. The order queue is taken in bounded batches within the run's time (the lead's decision 4; M2).** decideAll takes paypal_order_due
TAKE_BATCH (200) orders at a time in the queue's order, each batch its own short transaction (its chargebacks marked due and its queue rows
taken away together, PPF59), up to the newest order queued when it starts. The run's deadline is checked before each batch and bounds every
row wait inside one (Db::waitsUntil: the session's innodb_lock_wait_timeout never more than the whole seconds left; less than a second left:
no statement is started): a batch that runs out of time or waits for a PayPal row held elsewhere is rolled back whole and stays queued with
the rest (paypal_deadline, busy: the run fails with it, the next run takes them first). A long queue never holds one transaction past the
cron's limit; what was taken stays taken.

**PPF72. The go-live gate certifies only the account's last run: older_run is never cleared, an older version of another shop or order is
said, the kit holds the nightly (the lead's decisions 5 and 11; M3, NEW High).** A run that returns an OLDER version than kept with other
money, OR other captures (the invoice or custom field there or not, its shop or number taken: compared whatever forms made them, since CW
cannot tell whether the version or a form change makes the difference) sets older_run to its id; no later run clears it (a read of the kept
version, a newer version: the mark stays), so the gate always sees it. The gate also refuses certification when any other run of the account
started after the certified one (PPF78), and the nightly does nothing while the go-live kit's hold is in force: `<key file>.hold` holding
"until=<unix time>" (PaypalFees::nightlyHold: its time still ahead and at most HOLD_MAX_SEC, 2 hours, ahead; one run out, further ahead or
not in that form holds nothing, so a kit that dies never stops the nightly for long; a backfill or --decide by hand is never held).

**PPF73. A row one answer gave two contents of is settled only by an answer giving it exactly once in a window that proves its day (the
lead's decision 6).** store() counts every copy of a row in the answer BEFORE identical copies are let go: the same content twice, or once in
a window that proves nothing of the row's day (a page without its refresh time, a repeat, a short start, an end before the row's day ends:
PPF52, PPF70; proven() is worked out before the rows are stored), never settles pp_conflict 2, nor does a newer version given so; a clean
read once in a proven window takes that version (PPF60) and counts it. Two reads disagreeing (1) are settled by a newer version as before.

**PPF74. A row that counts nothing whatever its shop is not marked again by the reference rule either (the lead's decision 7).** The rematch
of rows whose referred row was read since skips rows not counted whatever their shop (denied, ignored: not_counted; those decided under other
forms are marked by the forms rule once, PPF67): a denied chargeback with its own invoice whose sale is held for form_unread is decided once,
then never again at every pass; it still follows its sale whenever the sale is read (store) or moves (decide).

**PPF75. A reference shared by several rows: all of them, never the first one read (the lead's decision 10; NEW High).** One PayPal id may
have several event codes (two chargebacks). resolveForms loads EVERY row of each id referred to (the rows decided now as they are, the others
from the table: never only those among the rows of this decision), takes the rows of the best rank (sale, chargeback, fee, refund), and
holds the referring row (ref_conflict) when they name two shops or two orders, or one a shop and another none; whichever is read first, in
either order, also when one of them was decided by an earlier run. Rows of one rank that agree are one answer (counted there).

**PPF76. A batch recost lets the intake lock go before its PayPal work (the lead's decision 12).** OrderSnapshots::recompute (a batch tool's
costs) dispatches the PayPal work of the orders it queued (afterSnapshot) only after the finally that releases the order's intake lock: the
API storing a snapshot of that order waits about a second for that lock, never for a chargeback's decision.

**PPF77. "Back to normal" only for an episode whose alert was said; the held refund's words (the lead's decisions 2 and 14).** A cleared
alert gets its "back to normal" only when its last send belongs to the episode that cleared (last_sent_at at or after its first_seen_at): the
looks alert keeps its last send across episodes (PPF58), so a recurrence kept quiet never sends a recovery. The held chargeback's look says
"CW could not verify this refund against PayPal" (the refund recorded in CW may have been made through PayPal before the days read), its fee
counted as before; ref_conflict's words also cover a payment naming two orders (PPF75).

**PPF78. The kit (the lead's decisions 1, 5, 8, 9, 13).** key-check takes root:root 0600 or 0400 (PPF68). backfill-check STOPs on a run of
the account started after the certified one and on any order queued for its chargebacks (read in the same consistent read as the due rows
and the totals); `golive.sh backfill` holds the nightly before the switch-on (`box.sh hold-nightly`, checked with the tip's own code), drains
the queue just before the gate (`box.sh decide`) and takes the hold away whatever the verdict (`box.sh release-nightly`, by a trap). A
part-applied 0080's indexes are compared with their uniqueness, and each of its tables with what MySQL itself makes of the pinned 0080 file
(pp_state.php --ddl: a TEMPORARY table of its own session, foreign keys aside; SHOW CREATE TABLE of both line by line: a CHECK's literal case
and grouping never hidden by a normalisation). Back from the rollback release: `box.sh return-decide` records the earliest affected day
before `--decide`, runs it on the restored release, then the rebuild from the earliest day and the reconcile (RUNBOOK).

### Round 6b: the Codex astra review of 5784c00 (`runs/codex_25nov/paypal_r6_astra_final.md`), with the lead's decisions (25 Nov 2026 ~22:55), each shown failing first on 5784c00 (`runs/paypal_r6b_red.log`) and then green (PPF79-PPF80)

**PPF79. A fraction of a second between two windows: a known limit (the lead; Codex H7 of 5784c00).** Each window asks PayPal for whole
seconds, from 00:00:00 of its first UK day to 23:59:59 of its last, and the next window starts at 00:00:00: a row at 23:59:59.750 would fall
in neither. PayPal's times are whole seconds: none of the 14,302 real rows of the lead's read (24 Nov) carries a fraction, so no row falls
there. Not changed now (the lead, 25 Nov ~22:55): on the tracker. An answer that ENDS short of its asked end is still never taken for the
whole day (PPF70).

**PPF80. Round 6b (the lead's decisions; Codex High x2, Medium x5, Low).**
- A reference's rows of one rank are compared by their KNOWN shops and KNOWN order numbers apart: one with no number agrees with one that
  has it, one that names no shop with one that names it; only two known shops, or two known numbers, that differ hold the row (ref_conflict,
  PPF75); otherwise the one shop with the one known number (or none) is the reference's, and the row's own invoice number is taken when every
  known value agrees (PPF62). A row of them that names two shops' forms, or lost its shop, is held as before (ref_unresolved). Codex's case
  (Vape and Go's 1312001 and Vape and Go with no number; the fee's own invoice 1312001) counts on 1312001, read in either order.
- A NEW row of a PayPal id other rows refer to marks those rows due in the same store (markFollowers): they are decided again with it,
  whatever its own first decision moves (a denied row of no clear shop moves none of its own fields, so its decision alone never would).
- A row one answer gave two contents of is settled only when its day is within the answer's proven days at BOTH ends: from the window's
  first day (an answer starting earlier than asked proves nothing of the day before) to its last day proven (PPF73).
- rematch()'s marks wait for a row no longer than the run's time, as the queue's batches (PPF71): the same bounded wait (Db::waitsUntil;
  paypal_deadline, busy), never a full session lock wait with a second left.
- The kit: `box.sh reconcile-days` requires no order queued and no row due in the SAME consistent read as its day-by-day comparison (a refund
  recorded during the rebuild while its chargeback's row was held leaves the order queued: `box.sh decide` first); the gate refuses EVERY
  older_run mark of the certified account at or after the certified run, whatever the row's stored day; a resumed part of 0080 must be
  InnoDB (an otherwise identical MyISAM queue would keep its deletion when a transaction rolls back); `box.sh hold-nightly` and `box.sh
  decide` take `--release=<commit>` as return-decide does (a return from the rollback release to a later fixed release); golive.sh takes
  the hold away BEFORE it writes the success markers (the EXIT trap stays for a failure).

## CW-1180 "don't restock" = written off at once (branch `no-restock`, 25 Nov 2026; NR1-NR8; migration 0081)

The owner (CW chat, 25 Nov 2026 ~15:15-16:45 UK): "if the staff said dont restock then dont reestock", then "Yes, build it" (a test copy;
live only on his word, never on Black Friday). Until now a paid unit a store cancelled and marked not restockable went to VERIFY ("Doubtful
cancels awaiting recount") with a recount task (D37) that nobody did: 1,238 units, £2,435, piled up from 28 Oct to 25 Nov and were cleared by
hand (What's new #625). Code: `src/Reservations.php` (cancel, uncancel, uncancelFromWriteOff, lastCancels, notRestockableMode),
`src/Invariants.php` (12-13), `src/Ui/SalesViews.php`, the Sales returns, order and movements pages, `Ui\Words` (SALE_RESTOCK_TEXT,
SALE_ORDER, SETTING_CHOICE, LEDGER_NOTE). Tests: `tests/Integration/Stock/CancelWriteOffTest.php`, `CancelWriteOffInvariantsTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/NoRestockScreensTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Migration0081Test.php`.

**NR1. A setting, `stock.cancel_not_restockable` (amends D37).** Two choices, shown in words on Settings > Stock records ("Write it off at
once (at its cost)", "Move it to Doubtful cancels for a recount (the way before)"), changed with a reason and kept in the setting's History
by those words, like every setting (config_change version, audit row). 0081 seeds `write_off`, the owner's rule (provisional, as every new
setting, until he ticks "agreed"). The cancel reads it in its transaction, once per call, so a change applies to the next cancel. While the
row is missing (a release running a moment before 0081) or holds anything else (only by hand in the database), CW keeps the way before
(`verify`): a release alone changes nothing; 0081 switches it on.

**NR2. The write-off.** Under `write_off`, a cancel with `restockable = false` of an ALLOCATED unit books allocated −u (the `cancel` row, as
before), then ONE `write_off` row of on_hand −u at the unit's sale warehouse (its snapshot, D44), noted `cancel_not_restockable` (the same
system note as the VERIFY move of the way before: one name for "not restockable"; the movement type tells the two apart), with the channel,
order ref and unit id on it, at booking time (D45), in the same transaction under the same locks (reservation → the unit's balances, sorted →
value clock → feed clock: today's order, the VERIFY balance simply not locked). Answer: result `cancelled`, outcome `written_off` (NR10). No VERIFY move, no recount,
no document: the order flow's own movements (cancel, ship, return, the VERIFY move) never had one, and a document (number series, approvals,
reviews) inside an order's transaction would break its lock order (I21) for nothing a person decides. A held unit (never paid, never
picked) is only freed, as before; a restockable cancel is unchanged. allocated −u and on_hand −u together leave availability where it was:
no feed row, never an oversell; a shelf already below zero opens the usual negative_on_hand review.
- *Example:* an Elf Bar, 10 on the shelf, 2 paid (available 8). One cancelled not restockable: shelf 9, allocated 1, available still 8; one
  write-off of £2.04 at MAIN. Before: shelf 9, VERIFY 1, an open recount.

**NR3. "At its cost" = the item's average cost so far.** The write-off row carries `unit_cost` = CostHints::average (every unit that came in
with a cost, weighted: the stock value's own rule, the same figure Reports values the unit at), `cost_source` `estimate` (a cost CW worked
out itself, as the opening loads' are; 0006's ENUM has no other fitting value and widening it would copy the whole ledger table). None
when no unit of the item ever came in with a cost (the stock value already counts that item at £0). The average is read under the item's
value clock, taken right after the balance locks (Stock::lockValueClocks, as a document posting does; NR11 M1), or read before the locks and
kept only when that clock did not move meanwhile (NR12). A cost on a fall moves no average: every average CW keeps (CostHints, report_item,
CostEngine's start price) counts only rises with a cost. So the stored cost is the record of what left (the pages show it), never an input.
- *Example:* 10 in at £2.00 and 10 at £3.00: average £2.50; a pack of two cancelled not restockable: one write-off of 2 at £2.50 = £5.00.

**NR4. Uncancel of a written-off unit: the exact inverse (amends D46).** A unit whose LAST cancel wrote it off (lastCancels: the newest
`cancel` row and a `write_off` of on_hand down noted cancel_not_restockable after it) comes back with on_hand +u at the same warehouse, a
`write_off` row noted `uncancel_from_write_off`, at booking time, then allocated +u: availability does not move (never an oversell). Answer:
result `uncancelled`, outcome `write_off_taken_back` (NR10). The take-back carries NO cost of its own: a rise with a cost is a purchase to every average (NR3), so a
take-back at £2.04 would move the average the cancel never moved; without one the unit comes back at exactly the value it left at (on hand ×
the same average), and the record pairs it with the write-off (same unit, the uncancel's key, invariants 12-13). What the last cancel did
decides, whatever the setting says now: a unit parked under `verify` comes back from VERIFY (D46) after a switch to `write_off`, and the
other way round.
- *Example:* the Elf Bar above taken back: shelf 10, allocated 2, available 8, average still £2.04: as before the cancel.

**NR5. Counted since: allocated and a review, never a guess.** When the item was counted at that warehouse after the write-off (a `count`
row of the balance booked after it, whatever its counted_at: the count replaced the figure the write-off was part of, as D46's
verify_counted; ledger ids of one balance follow its lock), or the write-off is not the unit's own figure (another balance or size than its
snapshot), CW leaves on_hand alone, allocates +u and opens a count_review `uncancel_after_write_off` at the unit's warehouse (dedupe
`uncancel_write_off:<channel>:<cancel id>`; detail: the reason `counted_since` / `not_its_figure`, the write-off's ledger id and cost, the
count's ledger id). Availability is then lower than the shelf until a person acts, never higher; a strict/stopped item left below zero gets
`uncancel_short` (D46). Answer: result `uncancelled_after_verify`, outcome `after_write_off` (NR10). A hand correction (an adjustment) of the item since is not such a signal: at a
selling warehouse stock moves all day, and CW cannot tell whose unit a correction was about (at VERIFY it could: D46). Like
`uncancel_after_verify`, no page lists this review source yet (an existing gap: the review is in count_review for a person; tracker).
- *Example:* written off (shelf 9), the shelf counted at 9, the cancel taken back: shelf 9, allocated 2, available 7 and a review.

**NR6. Invariants 12-13.** 12: each write-off by a not-restockable cancel and each take-back is ONE on_hand row of the unit's own item,
warehouse and size (−u / +u), under the key of that same cancel / uncancel of the unit (its allocated row −u / +u), and a take-back has no
cost. 13: per unit and item those rows never net above 0 (only what was written off is taken back; below −u is right after NR5 and a later
cancel). Read from the channels' write_off rows through ix_stock_ledger_store_type (staff write-offs have no channel).

**NR7. Words and pages.** Sales returns: "Written off at Main warehouse: not restockable (£2.04)" (what the unit's write-off was worth, its
units × the cost it took, to the penny; "(no cost known)" when none); a unit parked the way before keeps "Not on sale: moved to Doubtful
cancels awaiting recount, waiting for a recount" and its recount's words; the CSV says the same. The order page's steps: "Written off: not
restockable (£2.04)" and "Write-off taken back: the cancel was undone". Stock movements: the system notes in words ("Cancelled by the store,
not restockable", ...), never their codes. No new page.

**NR8. Profit and the reports (no rule changed).** An Elf Bar cancelled not restockable: stock value −£2.04 (on hand −1 at the average; the
VERIFY park kept it in our stock until the hand clear); order profit unchanged (a cancelled line counts no units, sale or cost: PR4); Real
profit unchanged (it never held stock losses); the stock movement reports show one write-off; the moving buying price (CostEngine, PR13)
weighs the next delivery against one unit fewer on hand (100 at £2.00 and 100 more at £2.20 give £2.1000 a unit; with the unit written off,
99 + 100 give £2.1005); the report job's sales figures (cancel/uncancel of the allocated figure) are unchanged; the ERPNext way-back file
leaves it out like every row a website booked (RB2: `from_website`). 0081 does not need 0080: the Migrator applies whatever file is pending in
name order, so either may go live first (Migration0081Test); but a release must hold every file its schema has applied, so whichever goes
second is built on the first (the kit's re-pin).

**NR9. The shops' connectors must know the three new answers first (amends SC3). SUPERSEDED by NR10 (no connector release).** A cancel now answers `cancelled_written_off` per
unit, and an uncancel `uncancelled_from_write_off` or `uncancelled_after_write_off`. The connector's unit sweep (unit_sweep.php,
`CW_US_EXPECTED_RESULTS`) logs any answer not in its list as `unit_event_anomaly`, and for an uncancel raises the alert
`unit_sweep_uncancelled` ("CW did not put the units back"), which would be false. So each shop's connector release adds `cancelled_written_off`
to its cancel list and the two others to its uncancel list (`uncancelled_after_write_off` logged as a warning, like
`uncancelled_after_verify`: CW opened a count review) BEFORE this release goes live; the go-live kit's check STOPs while a connector it can
read lacks them, and until the lead has looked at the others (`CONNECTORS_SEEN`). CW's answers stay honest (no old name reused for a new
outcome). Until the connectors are ready, the release could also go live with the setting at `verify` (no new answer is ever given), but
0081 seeds `write_off` (the owner's rule), so the kit orders it: connectors first, then CW.

**NR10. Answers the connectors already know, the precise outcome beside them (the lead, 25 Nov 2026; supersedes NR9's "connectors first").**
No connector release: the shops' connectors (0.4.17 on all 3 shops) use a unit's `result` only to spot anomalies (unit_sweep.php
`CW_US_EXPECTED_RESULTS`, and the `uncancelled_after_verify` warning), and a release on 3 shops in Black Friday week would hold the rule back
while 30-60 units a day still pile into VERIFY. So the write-off way answers with results those connectors know, and says what CW did in an
ADDITIVE per-unit field `outcome` that they ignore:
- a cancel written off: result `cancelled` (as a restockable cancel), outcome `written_off`;
- an uncancel that takes the write-off back exactly: result `uncancelled`, outcome `write_off_taken_back`;
- an uncancel after a count (NR5): result `uncancelled_after_verify` (the shops' "a person should look" warning: the intent is the same, CW
  opened a review), outcome `after_write_off`.
The way before (VERIFY) and every other unit answer exactly as before, with no `outcome` (`cancelled_to_verify`, `uncancelled_from_verify`,
`uncancelled_after_verify`, a restockable `cancelled`, `already_cancelled`, ...), so their stored answers and replays are unchanged. The
outcome is part of the stored answer: a replay under the same key returns it byte for byte (WriteOffAnswersRouteTest). Nothing personal is in
it. No page reads `result` (Sales returns, the order page and Stock movements read the ledger: NR7). The go-live kit's check reads the live
connector files it can see and STOPs if their expected lists no longer hold the three old results CW now gives (`cancelled`, `uncancelled`,
`uncancelled_after_verify`).

**NR11. The final review of f3a7ed0 (Codex astra, NO GO: 2 High, 7 Medium), each fixed test-first.**
- *M1, the cost:* a delivery committing between the cancel's start and its write-off could leave the write-off at the stale average (10 at
  £2 then 10 at £4 booked meanwhile: written off at £2 while the stock value falls £3). The house pattern of a posting whose costs depend on
  the item's value stream is used: after the balance locks, `Stock::lockValueClocks` on the written-off items, THEN the average. No other
  on-hand change of the item can take a place in its value sequence until the cancel commits, so the cost is the average of exactly what
  precedes the write-off (CancelWriteOffLocksTest: the delivery booked at the hook is in it: £3.00). No retry is needed. The read now runs
  under the item's locks: the go-live kit times it at production size before the go-live (box.sh before; above 500 ms a STOP to look).
- *M5, counted since:* the balance's latest count after the call's earliest write-off is read ONCE per locked balance, and each unit is judged
  against it (latest count id > its write-off id = counted since). 100 units of one item: one read, not 100.
- *M6, invariant 12:* the cancel / uncancel under the same key must have EXACTLY ONE allocated row, on the write-off's own item and warehouse,
  of the expected signed units; a sum that matches across warehouses no longer passes.
- *M7, invariant 13:* the running balance in ledger order per channel, unit and item (a window sum) must never be above 0: a take-back
  booked before its write-off is flagged even when they net to zero. Both read only the channels' write_off rows (ix_stock_ledger_store_type,
  ~30-60 a day): the kit prints the invariants' time and memory on production after the switch (1G).
- *H1, the code undo:* the PRIMARY undo is the quick stop (the setting back to `verify`; no code change). The code undo (the rollback release,
  which does not know write-offs) STOPs while any unit written off by its last cancel is still cancelled (an uncancel of it under the rollback
  would allocate it without its write-off taken back); the kit lists each with its pack size (units_per_item) and whether its item was
  counted at that warehouse since, and the switch goes on only with `NRKIT_UNDO_ACK=<that number>`. After such an undo `undo.sh corrections`
  says, per unit taken back under the rollback, what to book: its pack size, never "+1" (a 6-pack written off at £2 a unit: +6, £12), and
  NOTHING when the item was counted at that warehouse after the write-off (the count already holds the shelf as it is).
- *H2, the undo switch:* under the install lock, before the symlink or the cron is touched, the rollback release's migration files must be
  exactly the applied ones (a 0080 applied by another install after undo-check: STOP) and no installer pause marker may be there.
- *M2:* the scripted quick stop checks only what it needs (live = the tip, the schema's migrations = the tip's files, the setting row); the
  rollback folder is checked on the code-switch path only. *M3:* `golive.sh check` removes the earlier success first and writes it only at its
  end; `apply` runs the connector check again itself. *M4:* the install marker is retired on success; a resume accepts only the setting /
  history states a real run of 0081 can leave (nothing; the row without its baseline; the row and its baseline before the migration record).

**NR12. Round 3 (the lead's narrow re-check of fa9cd43; the owner's standing rule "we dont undo we fix them"): the undo is the quick stop.**
- *The undo of this release* is the quick stop (stock.cancel_not_restockable back to `verify`, on the Settings page or the kit's
  `undo.sh quickstop`) and fixing forward. The code switch back to the rollback release stays only for a release that breaks (minutes after
  the go-live) and only while NO unit written off by its last cancel is still cancelled: the kit pauses the writers as the installer does
  (cron aside and its running jobs waited for, the public vhost off, php-fpm stopped after its requests: the installer's own markers), counts
  those units with the writers drained, and keeps them paused through the switch; a count above 0 brings the writers back and STOPs with "fix
  forward (quick stop first)". There is no acknowledgement to go on anyway and no correction tool (both removed): after the first such unit,
  no code undo.
- *The quick stop* reads only what it needs, with a short timeout (the schema's migrations = the tip's files, the setting row, its mode),
  and changes the setting.
- *The cost read:* the averages AND the items' value-clock versions (read first) are read BEFORE any lock; under the balance locks and the
  value clocks the versions are read again: unchanged = the costs stand (no scan of value rows under a lock: a 100-item cancel scans before
  it locks), changed = read again there, once (CancelWriteOffLocksTest: the read happens before the balance lock when nothing moved; a
  delivery between the read and the lock gives the re-read £3.00).
- *The kit:* the connector files checked are pinned and apply checks the same list; a resume needs the seeded row exactly (type string, value
  "write_off", provisional, NR1, set up by the migration) and the baseline's JSON exactly; every marker is written to a temporary name and
  renamed (atomic), every write and removal checked.

## Claude reads the upload, phase 1 (CW-1182) and the Mac copy of a Royal Mail bill (CW-1181) (branch `ai-reader`, 25 Nov 2026; AI1-AI20; migration 0082)

The owner (CW chat, 25 Nov 2026 ~17:25 UK), after the Royal Mail bill of 23 Nov could not be pasted: "whatever we doing is wrong. wrong way to
add an invoice you should focus on the claude api connected on all upload places as soon as posssible"; then "I'll create one" (an Anthropic
API key for CW). Staff drop a PDF or a photo where they upload today; CW sends it to the Claude API and fills the SAME check page or form; CW's
own checks still decide and a person always presses Store or Save. Phase 1 = Profit > Delivery bills (a Royal Mail bill) and Profit > Expenses
(an invoice). Nothing goes live without the owner's word.

**AI1. One service, a small class per kind of document (`CW\Ai\DocumentReader`, `CW\Ai\Kind`).** A kind says what Claude is told
(instructions), the fixed JSON answer (schema, sent as structured outputs: every object closed with `additionalProperties: false`, every field
required; only what structured outputs take: no lengths, patterns or bounds, CW checks those itself), the answer's limit in tokens, and CW's
strict reading of the answer (`shape()`: every field in its form or the whole answer refused, naming the field and the line, never what it
holds). Phase 1 kinds: `royal_mail_bill`, `expense_invoice`. A later kind (a supplier invoice with lines, a goods-in, return, PO or count
file) is one more class and one more place in `DocumentReader::PLACES`.

**AI2. Anthropic's own PHP SDK, with a PSR-18 client as the seam (`CW\Ai\Claude`).** `anthropic-ai/sdk` v1.14.0 (PHP ^8.1) and
`guzzlehttp/guzzle` 7.17 (its PSR-18 client) are production packages; `php-http/discovery`'s Composer plugin is not allowed (push_code.sh
installs with --no-plugins anyway). The call: beta messages, streamed (a five-page bill is minutes of output) and folded with the SDK's
`MessageAccumulator`; the document as a `document` block (a photo as an `image` block), base64, BEFORE the text; the model and the effort
from the settings (claude-opus-5-5, medium: set explicitly, its default); no `thinking` (always on for that model; disabling it is a 400);
the server-side refusal fallback opted in (beta `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01`, `fallbacks: "default"`); the base URL fixed (an
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the environment never redirects the key), OpenTelemetry off, the key passed in (never read from the environment).
`stop_reason` is read before any content: `refusal` and `max_tokens` are failures, never half an answer; the text read is the one after the
last `fallback` block; every attempt's tokens counted (usage.iterations). The SDK's errors, most specific first, become reason codes (auth,
forbidden, billing, spend_limit, rate_limited, overloaded, server, timeout, connection, bad_request, too_large, other). Tests never call the
API: the SDK sends through a fake PSR-18 client (`tests/Support/FakeClaude`) that answers with recorded, MADE-UP streams, so the real SDK
builds the request and reads the answer in every test.

**AI3. Read in the background, never in a web worker.** php-fpm stops a request after 150 s and has 10 workers; a 160-line week is about
11,000 tokens of answer (2-4 minutes). So the upload only keeps the file and makes a job (`ai_read`, `waiting`) and the page waits on its
own address (`/ui/profit/delivery/read/{id}`, `/ui/profit/expenses/read/{id}`), looking again every 3 seconds by the Refresh header (no
script); `bin/ai_read.php` (cron, every minute, one run at a time by its lock, about 55 s a run, looking every 2 s) reads the jobs one at a
time with no time limit of the web's (its own deadline: 600 s a call). Once read, the person's own page takes the answer and runs the place's
own checks as the person. A job is its person's only (another person: 404); the routes are the places' own permissions (delivery.upload,
expenses.edit), checked again by the service, and again by the runner when it reads (a job taken away meanwhile: `not_allowed`). One effect
per form (checklist 10): the same file sent again from the same place by the same person, with the same typed fields, while its reading
waits, goes or is not shown yet, is that reading (a double click never pays twice; under the person's own lock). Whatever breaks inside a
read ends its job at once (failed, `error`, the exception's class kept on the job, never its message; staff read "something went wrong in CW
while it was being read"); a stream that breaks while read is `connection`.

**AI4. A Royal Mail bill: Claude copies, CW's own reader decides.** Claude copies the top block (account, invoice number, date, net, VAT,
gross, currency), EVERY line (service date, product code, quantity, description, the reference cell as printed with its sales order,
net, gross, VAT code), its own count of the lines, the VAT summary rows and the "Surcharge included" amount. CW writes the bill out as the
page reader's text (`RoyalMailBillKind::render`: the shape of the owner's pasted bills, each line on two lines, no tab) and runs
`RoyalMailBills::check` on it, so EVERY check of a pasted bill applies unchanged (the lines tie to the net and gross to the penny, the VAT
follows from the codes, an unknown product refuses the bill, the account is the one chosen, the same bill twice ...). The check page is the
same (a line says Claude read it: "compare a few lines with the PDF before you press Store"); Store is the same; the check's audit row says
`read_by: claude` and the job. A reading that does not add up is refused and says so ("CW's reading of the PDF does not add up to the bill's
total: try the bill page's own text or send it to the CW team"), never corrected; the bills busy just now (another Store, the kit's hold):
the reading is given back to its job for the same page to try again in a minute, never read a second time. Before that, a count of the lines that is not Claude's own
count refuses the answer (a reading that lost or doubled lines). £ example: the synthetic week of the tests (AiKindsTest), 12 lines, £2,284.45 net: read
from the PDF it is the SAME bill as its saved page (the same rows and fingerprint: "the same file" if both are uploaded).

**AI5. An expense's invoice fills the form, Save decides.** The add form (and an expense's Change) has "Fill from the file with Claude"
while reading is on: the form is sent with its file; once read, the form comes back with the boxes Claude read filled over what was typed, and
a note saying which. Only what holds together is filled: net + VAT = total (a missing one worked out only from the other two when they are
printed, never a VAT CW works out), in pounds; the VAT choice the figures match (the server's own rule). A supplier only when it is exactly
one of CW's (name, any case and spacing: CW keeps no VAT number of an expense supplier), else left to staff with the printed name said; a
shop only when its exact name is printed as the one billed (the owner's rule: never a shop picked for you); a credit note ticked with its
amounts as printed. Never a confidence number. £ example: an invoice of £70.60 + £14.12 VAT = £84.72 fills 70.60 / 14.12 / 84.72 and
"Includes 20% VAT" (£84.72 x 10000 / 12000 = £70.60); one whose boxes say £70.60 + £14.12 but whose total says £90.00 fills no amount and
says "add up to £84.72, not to its total £90.00". The copy Claude read is deleted: the form asks for the file again (or "Save without a file").

**AI6. DPD stays the CSV.** DPD's weekly PDF is 55-61 pages for 2,300-2,600 parcels (page counts read with pdfinfo; the files were never
opened: they hold delivery addresses and, on page 1, payment details): copying every parcel would be about 150,000 tokens of answer (over
the 128,000 one answer may hold, about £2.50 a bill and half an hour), and the CSV DPD sends with it is the exact list. A PDF chosen with DPD
is refused in words ("upload the CSV file DPD sends with each bill"), nothing sent.

**AI7. Settings, all on the Settings screen ("Claude reads uploads"), audited, with history (0082).** `ai.read_uploads` (Off as installed),
`ai.anthropic_api_key` (a SECRET: never shown back, never logged; the history and the audit keep a fingerprint; a password box holding only
"(set: hidden)" while set, sent back as it is the key stays; a key typed into a refused form is never drawn back; a key of the wrong form is
refused: `sk-ant-...`), `ai.model` (claude-opus-5-5), `ai.effort` (low, medium, high, xhigh, max; medium), `ai.monthly_limit_gbp` (30).
Reading is on only with the switch on AND a key.

**AI8. The month's limit counts real money, rounded up.** Each call's tokens at the model's prices, two settings in pounds per million tokens
(`ai.price_input_gbp_per_mtok` 3.20, `ai.price_output_gbp_per_mtok` 16.00: Claude Opus 5.5's $4 / $20 at $1 = £0.80; change both with the
model), in thousandths of a penny on the log row, rounded UP; the UK month's sum in pence rounded up. At the limit no new reading starts (the
upload as before still works) and a job waiting is not read. £ example: a week's bill of 15,000 tokens in and 13,000 out costs 4,800 + 20,800
= 25,600 thousandths = 25.6p; 100 of them a month = £25.60.

**AI9. The log of calls, without content (`ai_call`).** When, who, place, kind, the model asked and the one that answered, the file's type
and size, tokens in and out, the cost, the result (ok / refused / failed) and its reason code, a refusal's category, the API's request id,
seconds; and later what CW's own checks made of it (passed / refused + the refusal's code: how often Claude's reading of a bill does not add
up). Never the key, the document, a field of it or Claude's text. Never removed by the app login; its row is written before the request and
finished once after it (AI16: only the call's outcome and those three columns are written later). Settings > Rules and numbers says "This
month: N documents read, £x of the £30.00 limit".

**AI10. Privacy: business papers only.** What leaves the server: the document (base64) with CW's fixed instructions and the answer's shape,
to api.anthropic.com over HTTPS, nothing else of CW (no supplier list, no shop name, no order). The Click & Drop report (customer addresses)
is never offered to Claude; DPD's PDF is never sent (AI6).

**AI11. Kept only as long as needed.** The file in the spool folder (app.env `ai_spool_dir`, else /var/lib/cw/ai-read, 0700 www-data; the
file 0600 under a random name) until it is read: deleted right after the call, read or not (a Royal Mail bill's; an invoice's is kept for its
expense's Save: AI15 supersedes this part for the Expenses places); the answer in CW's form until its person's page
takes it (once: `taken`); every minute, whatever the switch, the runner's clean-up: a job left `reading` by a run that stopped (failed,
`stopped`), a job waiting more than an hour (`too_old`), an answer not taken within an hour (`expired`), any file of the folder no job names
that is older than an hour (a crash; only CW's own 32-hex names are touched), a job row's typed fields a day after it finishes (the row
stays, emptied: AI19; the log rows stay).

**AI12. Every failure in the staff's words, with what to do next** (`Ui\AiReadWords`): "CW could not read this document: <why>" and, for a
bill, "Upload the bill's saved page or paste its text, or send the PDF to the CW team"; the key wrong: "a person who manages settings
changes it in Settings > Rules and numbers"; busy: "try again in a minute"; an iPhone's HEIC photo told apart by its own bytes.

**AI13. CW-1181: a tabbed copy whose bill lines come on two lines is read (`RoyalMailBillPage::joinTabbed`).** Chrome on a Mac breaks each

**AI15. The invoice Claude read is the expense's file: kept for its Save, never asked for again (the lead's pick, 25 Nov 2026 ~20:00 UK;

from THAT expense's Change); only while it is kept; its size and sha256 checked again against what was sent (a file changed in the spool is

Save still attaches it), except when its person may no longer use it, it waited too long, or it was gone. A form naming a reading that is

form ...: choose the file again, or tick Save without a file". The form sent again (a lost answer) lands where the first did (its one-effect
key holds the reading, not the file, which is gone by then). Since the file becomes the expense's, an expense's reading takes only what an

deleted right after the reading (CW never keeps bill files). £ example: an invoice of £84.72 read at 2:00 pm, its form saved at 2:20 pm: the
expense of £84.72 has the PDF the person dropped, and nothing is left in the spool; not saved by 3:00 pm (its page took it at 2:00), the
copy is deleted at the runner's next minute and a Save at 3:05 asks for the file again.

**AI16. A call is counted at its most BEFORE it is sent, so a reader that dies mid-call still counts (the lead, 25 Nov 2026 ~20:00 UK).**
Before, a call's log row was written after the answer: a reader killed mid-call (out of memory, a restart) left a call Anthropic may bill
that the month's limit never saw. Now its row is written first: result `started`, counted at the most it may cost (`max_millipence`, kept:
`Claude::maxInputTokens` = the request's own words at two characters a token + 2,000 tokens of framing + 10,000 tokens a page (a page's
text and its picture; the high-resolution models take at most 4,784 visual tokens a page), a PDF's pages counted from its page objects, else
its page tree's /Count, else 100; a photo one page; plus the kind's max_tokens of output) at the settings' prices; the month (and so the
limit) counts it while it goes. After the call the row is finished once (`WHERE result = 'started'`): what its answer said it used; no usage
came back and Claude may have worked (`timeout`, `connection`, an answer CW could not read, `other`): its most; refused before Claude worked
(the key, the account, its limits, busy, the request): nothing (`AiUsage::charged`). A row left `started` is closed as `crashed` (reason
`stopped`) at its most: by the next run (the runner's lock held: its job was `reading`, so its reader stopped) or, whatever the lock, an hour
after it was written (no call lasts that long: 300 seconds, no retry: AI18 M4). The app login may write only the call's outcome
(model that answered, tokens, cost, result, reason, refusal's category, request id, fallback, seconds) and the check's three columns; who,
where, when, the model asked, the file and its most are frozen; a row is never removed. £ example: a 5-page Royal Mail bill's most is about
£1.20 an attempt (54,000 tokens in at £3.20 a million = 17p, 64,000 out at £16.00 = £1.02), reserved twice (the request and the server-side
fallback's: AI18 M2), about £2.39; while it is read the month counts that; read, it is counted at what it used (about 25.6p); its reader
killed mid-call, £2.39 stays (crashed). The limit is a hard cap (AI18 M3): a call starts only when the month's spend plus its most stays
within it.

**AI17. bin/health_alert.php says when the reading is stuck (the lead, 25 Nov 2026 ~20:00 UK).** Two alerts of CW's own, in the same style
as the others (a line in the log, the words sent once per window, "back to normal" when they clear), only while reading is switched on
(`ai.read_uploads`; quiet while it is off, whatever is left): `ai_waiting` "Claude reads uploads: N document(s) have waited more than 10
minutes to be read (the oldest X). The reader runs every minute from cron: tell the CW team." (bin/ai_read.php is not running, or is
stuck on a call) and `ai_reader_failed` "Claude reads uploads: the reader's last run failed X ago (why). Documents sent to be read wait until a
run ends well: tell the CW team." Each run records itself on `ai_reader`'s one row (began; ended well; failed with the error's class, never
its message); a run that began and never ended (its process killed) is found by the next run (it holds the lock, so the last one is not
running) and recorded as failed ("did not end"). The alert holds from the failure until a run ends well, so a run starting meanwhile never
makes it flap.

**AI19. The last round (the Codex re-check of ca8987b; the lead, 25 Nov 2026 ~21:42 UK): the undo is the quick stop; the rest fixed.** The
owner's standing rule (fix forward, as CW-1180): the undo of this release is the QUICK STOP (reading off, the key emptied: no code change).
The code goes back ONLY if reading was never used since the go-live (no job row, no call row, and the key's history never held a value),
checked with the writers paused; otherwise the kit STOPs "fix forward (the quick stop is on)" and puts the writers back. So the undo never
deletes a job or a file (AI18 H8's purge is gone). The kit records the undo's phase BEFORE it pauses the writers and holds the install lock
from its first check to its last, so a run that dies anywhere is resumed by running it again (the writers are never left paused). A later
go-live of this release after such an undo needs no hand step: its own bin/migrate.php, which the installer runs with the writers paused,
types the key's row back to text (AiSettings::restoreKeyRow), and the kit recognises 0082 already applied. Code: a date read is a day after
its blanks are trimmed (a date of blanks refuses the reading, so amounts never land beside a date the form held before); Save stores the
VERIFIED bytes of the invoice Claude read, from a private copy, and the stored file's sha256 must be the job's before the expense commits;
words before the amounts after a complete reference in a Mac copy are refused; [superseded by AI20: the input is the API's own count] a
PDF counted at least one page for every 2,000 bytes, the request's own words at a token a byte; ONE named fallback model (claude-opus-4-8,
the same output limit) instead of the server's default list, so every billable attempt is known (x2); the cap
compares the month's spend and the call's most to the thousandth of a penny; one wall clock over the whole call (a request after it is never
sent; the HTTP client's timeout ends the transfer at it; curl replays nothing); a job is seen and taken only when its kind is its place's;
the app login never removes a job row (no DELETE: a job can never be replaced), a finished job's typed fields emptied in place a day after.
(That byte rule reserved about £24.30 for the real 694 KB 5-page bill of 23 Nov, so a bill could be sent only while the month's spend was
at most about £5.70: AI20 replaces it.)

**AI20. The reservation is the API's EXACT count of the input (the lead, 25 Nov 2026 ~22:15 UK: the byte rule of AI19 M2 was wrong).**
Before each call the reader asks the API's token-counting endpoint (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`, the SDK's
`$client->beta->messages->countTokens()`) for the very request it will send: the same document block, the kind's instructions, the system
prompt, the model and the output schema with its effort; through the same guard (AnthropicOnly: https://api.anthropic.com:443, no redirect)
and within the same wall clock of 300 seconds as the call that follows (one clock over both). Counting is free and reads nothing. The
reservation (the call's row before the request, `max_millipence`) is then: (counted input x the input price + the kind's max_tokens x the
output price) x 2 (the request and the one named fallback, claude-opus-4-8), rounded up to the thousandth of a penny; the hard cap compares
the month's spend plus that. A count that fails, times out, is refused elsewhere or answers anything but a whole number: the document is NOT
sent (the job fails `count_failed`: "Anthropic could not say how large the document is, so it was not sent (nothing was spent): try again
in a minute"), and nothing is reserved (no call row). A PDF's page objects and page-tree count are kept only as a note in the runner's log
("input counted N tokens, P page(s) shown"), never as the bound. £ example: a 5-page Royal Mail bill counted at about 54,000 tokens in
reserves 2 x (54,000 at £3.20 + 64,000 at £16.00 a million) = about £2.40 while it is read (the byte rule reserved about £24); read, it counts
what it used (about 25p); with the £30 limit a bill is sent while the month's spend is at most about £27.60.
